body:
## Batch

P05 — Implement P05: Close a Loop with Proportional Control

## Governed scope

Implemented from `contracts/active-batch.yaml` through the repository-local
agent harness. Deterministic CI remains authoritative.

## Retained evidence

# P05 retained implementation evidence — 2026-08-14

## Result and claim boundary

P05, **Close a Loop with Proportional Control**, is implemented as a complete
deterministic learning slice in the `agent/p05` worktree at base commit
`a966ca7f9c8b8d28330fefa7a58ba11e6548bbed`. The module closes a transparent
first-order plant around `u = Kp*(r-y)`, exposes the pole, proportional offset,
response speed, and effort tradeoff, and reverses feedback polarity as its broken
case before restoring subtraction as recovery.

No MATLAB or Octave executable was available on `PATH`. The MATLAB model, exact
interval propagation, assertions, figures, and UI were authored and statically
inspected but did not execute in a MATLAB runtime. The manifest's `simulated`
evidence level describes deterministic simulation content; it is not a MATLAB
execution or numerical-fidelity claim. This evidence does not establish MATLAB
runtime behavior, rendered UI behavior, MATLAB numerical fidelity, instructional
efficacy, bench, physical hardware, HIL, RT1/RT2, Unreal, field, playtest, staging,
signing, release, deployment, or production validation.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance item | Result | Retained evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preserve the canonical guiding question | pass (static) | Manifest and every learner/tutor artifact retain the exact question; permanent identity test passes. |
| Visible read → baseline → one lever → changed view → mechanism explanation | pass (static) | Sectioned lesson/experiment and ordered walkthrough enforce one prediction, baseline output, error/effort view, isolated lever changes, and mechanism notes. Runtime presentation remains unverified. |
| Deterministic baseline, labeled plots and metrics, two independent sweeps, one broken case | pass (static/reference arithmetic) | `Kp` and plant-time-constant sweeps use a shared interval and preserve all other inputs; reversed feedback sign yields a positive-pole broken case and negative-feedback recovery; label, unit, metric, and marker tests pass. MATLAB rendering remains unverified. |
| Separate deterministic model and meaningful interactive controls | pass (static) | Presentation-free exact-interval `model.m`; bounded `Kp` and `tau` sliders, dynamic view interval, reset, output view, command view, and a callback-retained P05 model handle; separation/control tests pass. UI execution remains unverified. |
| Connect lesson and walkthrough to P04 without syntax-first teaching | pass (static) | P04 model-assumption bridge, visible feedback mechanism, misconceptions, and observation prompts precede MATLAB mechanics. |
| Independent invariants, limits, interpretation questions, and teach-back | pass (static/reference arithmetic) | `run_checks.m`, independent Python arithmetic, five interpretation questions, and a two-sentence teach-back cover equations, poles, offset, combined initial-state/forced response, lever isolation, zero/ramp/near-marginal limits, malformed inputs, recovery, resolution, and resource bounds. MATLAB assertions remain unexecuted. |
| Change manifest only after focused and repository-wide verification | pass (process/static) | Seven content tests passed while P05 remained scaffolded. A disposable candidate with the exact manifest transition passed all required commands and 45 tests before the live manifest changed. |
| Distinguish evidence categories | pass | This file separates static/reference arithmetic and simulated content from MATLAB runtime, UI, numerical fidelity, protocol, bench, HIL, field, and production evidence. |

## Validation commands and exact results

Environment: Linux worktree; Python `3.11.2`; `matlab` and `octave` were not found
on `PATH`. The base commit's GitHub Quality run `31850829094` completed successfully
before editing. No remote CI ran against the uncommitted P05 changes.

author: rebekah-create
body:
## Why

`next` 16.3.0, merged in #104, has an intermittent Turbopack failure evaluating `postcss.config.js`:

```
Error: Turbopack build failed with 1 error:
./apps/web/app/aeonikfont_cc346eda.module.css
TypeError: __turbopack_context__.a is not a function
    at mod (apps/web/postcss.config.js_.loader.mjs:11:31)
```

It broke roughly half of all builds — twice on x64 CI, once on the arm64 Docker build, passing on retry in between. That blocked the deploy of #104, leaving `main` red and production still on the old, vulnerable image.

## Why 16.2.11 loses nothing

Every open `next` advisory has a vulnerable range of `>=16.0.0, <16.2.11`. 16.2.11 is the highest fix version any of them requires:

| Severity | Vulnerable range | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| high | `>= 16.0.0, < 16.2.11` | 16.2.11 |
| medium | `>= 16.0.0, < 16.2.11` | 16.2.11 |
| high | `>= 16.0.0, < 16.2.6` | 16.2.6 |
| high, low, medium | `>= 16.0.0, < 16.2.5` | 16.2.5 |

16.3.0 was chosen only to match upstream, not for security. Parity is the sole thing given up here.

## Changes

- `apps/web/package.json` and the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` override both pinned to 16.2.11, in lockstep
- Lockfile regenerated — nets out to exactly two changes: `next` 16.3.0 → 16.2.11, and `sharp@0.35.3` dropping away (it was only pulled in by 16.3.0)
- Rationale recorded inline in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` so a future "match upstream" bump doesn't silently reintroduce the breakage
- The overrides guard from #104 passes: 8 pairs checked, none clamping

`tsconfig.build.json` is deliberately **kept**. It's inert on 16.2.x — that line doesn't type-check test files — but removing it would mean the next upgrade attempt walks into the ~500 pre-existing test type errors with no warning.

## Follow-up

The 16.3.0 upgrade is worth retrying once the Turbopack/PostCSS issue is fixed upstream. First suspect is the CJS `postcss.config.js`; converting it to ESM (`postcss.config.mjs`) may sidestep the generated interop wrapper, but that's an untested hypothesis.

body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/model/info` silently drops built-in pricing after traffic
- Each worker loses prices for models it served
- Deployment pricing defaults overwrite the shared cost cache

How it solves it:

- Merge deployment `model_info` into a copy, not the cached dict
- Drop unset (`None`) deployment values before merging
- Regression tests pin both, and fail without the fix

## User Flow

Before: an admin who opens the models page after the proxy has served traffic sees pricing vanish for exactly the models people used, and repeated reads disagree with each other

1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read real `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token` and `cache_read_input_token_cost` values for every model
2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back
3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and those three pricing fields are now missing from the model they just used
4. With more than one worker, refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models flips between prices shown and prices missing, depending on which worker answers, and restarting the pods only hides it until traffic returns

After: the models page keeps reporting the same prices no matter how much traffic has gone through, or which worker answers

1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/model/info with their key and read the same three pricing fields
2. Someone sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and gets a normal 200 back
3. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/model/info again and the pricing fields are unchanged
4. Refreshing https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models gives one consistent answer across workers and pods

Fixes #36980

author: mc-nv
body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs

author: dealako
body:
## What & why

Follow-up from @bramwelt's review of #126. Moves schema migrations **out of pod boot** into
an ArgoCD **PreSync hook Job**, so migrations run *before* each rollout. A failed migration
becomes a **failed Job with logs** and halts the sync — the previous ReplicaSet keeps serving
— instead of crash-looping a new pod. This is the change that later lets #1544 drop
`Recreate` + `Replace=true`.

## Change

- **`migrate` subcommand** (`cmd/campaign-service/migrate.go`, wired into `runCommand`
  beside `bootstrap-system-account`). A subcommand rather than a `cmd/migrate` binary because
  **ko publishes only `cmd/campaign-service`** — a Job runs this image with `args: ["migrate"]`.
  Resolves the DSN via `config.ResolveDatabaseURL()` (password never in the pod spec),
  fails fast via `ValidateMigrationDSN`, runs `postgres.Migrate`.
- **Boot verifies, never mutates.** New `postgres.VerifySchema` exposes the existing
  required/invalid-index guard (`checkNoInvalidIndexes`) without `Up()`. `initDatabase` swaps
  `Migrate → VerifySchema`; `migrateMu` is gone (verification is read-only/idempotent).
  `IsPermanentMigrationErr` classification is unchanged, so `/readyz` still fails closed on a
  missing/invalid required index.
- **Chart PreSync Job** (`templates/migrate-job.yaml`): `argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync`,
  `hook-delete-policy: BeforeHookCreation`, `restartPolicy: Never`, small `backoffLimit`,
  bounded `activeDeadlineSeconds`; renders the same `.Values.app.environment` DB secret refs
  the Deployment uses. New `migrateJob` values.
- **Tests**: `parity_test` pins the Job (PreSync hook, `migrate` args, DB secret);
  `migrate_test` pins subcommand dispatch + stray-arg refusal (DB-free).
- **Docs**: new `kubernetes/migrate-job.md` concept (+ index bullet); the deployment,
  internal-container, and internal-infrastructure-postgres concepts and the migrations README
  corrected off their "migrations run at boot" framing; dated log entry.

## Safety boundary (important)

PreSync migrates while the **previous release's pods are still serving**, so `Recreate` does
**not** cover a backward-incompatible migration — only **expand/contract** (#1542) keeping
every migration N-1-safe does, and a genuinely unstageable change needs explicit old-pod
shutdown (scale to zero) or a maintenance window. `Recreate` + `Replace=true` are therefore
no longer load-bearing; they are kept for one release so #1543 and #1544 stay independently
verifiable (#1544 returns to RollingUpdate and drops the annotation).

## Release & validation — REQUIRED (highest-risk change)

New chart version **and** image. Promote **dev → staging → prod**, validating each gate:

- **Dev:** with ≥1 pending migration, confirm the PreSync Job applies it and completes
  **before** the Deployment rolls; the app pod applies no schema change at boot; `/readyz`
  still gates on required indexes; force a failing migration and confirm it surfaces as a
  **failed Job with logs**, halts the sync, and leaves the prior pods serving (no crash-loop).
- **Staging:** repeat on staging data volume.
- **Prod:** only after dev + staging are clean.

## Testing

`go test ./...` green, `go vet ./...` clean, `helm lint` + `helm template` clean,
`go run ./cmd/okfvalidate ./docs/knowledge` conformant. Local pre-PR review trio: clean.

## Issue

Fixes linuxfoundation/lfx-self-serve#1543
Part of epic linuxfoundation/lfx-self-serve#1294

author: mc-nv
body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.

author: dgarnier
body:
`Release` and `Tests` both triggered on push to `main`, so they raced — a package could reach PyPI while the matrix that would have caught the problem was still running. There was no gate at all, only the appearance of one.

## Approach

Rather than duplicating a test step inside `release.yml`, key `Release` off the `Tests` run:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Tests]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  release:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
      && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push'
```

The matrix stays defined in exactly one place, still runs once per push, and `Release` starts only after it finishes green. An inline test step would have meant either duplicating the matrix or gating on a narrower subset of it; a reusable `workflow_call` workflow would have either run the matrix twice per push or hollowed out the `Tests` badge, which reports runs of that workflow on the default branch.

Two details worth flagging:

- **`ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}`** on the checkout. A `workflow_run` job checks out the tip of the default branch by default, which may have moved on by the time the matrix finished; this pins it to the commit that was actually tested.
- **`workflow_run.event == 'push'`** so that manually dispatching `Tests` on `main` doesn't kick off a release.

The 3.15 job is `continue-on-error`, so an rc regression reports without blocking a release.

Trusted publishing is unaffected — PyPI matches on repository, workflow filename and environment, all unchanged.

## Verification

Honest limitation: this one can't be proven before merge. `workflow_run` always uses the copy of the workflow on the default branch, so the new trigger cannot fire from a branch and this PR's own CI does not exercise it. I validated the YAML parses to the intended trigger, condition and checkout ref; the real proof is the first push to `main` after this merges, where `Release` should appear only after `Tests` completes.

## Also done

The repo setting that blocked *Prepare release* from opening a PR is now on:

```
before: {"default_workflow_permissions":"write","can_approve_pull_request_reviews":false}
after:  {"default_workflow_permissions":"write","can_approve_pull_request_reviews":true}
```

So the next dispatch should open its PR unaided. That PR won't carry check runs, since PRs created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't trigger workflows — which is now harmless, because publishing waits for `Tests` on the merge commit instead.

## Interaction with `release/v0.2.0`

Either merge order works. Merge the release first and the current push-triggered `Release` publishes as it does today; merge this first and the v0.2.0 merge goes through the gate instead.

author: silentpixel-git
body:
## Summary

Reported bug: after Act 0's door-answering story event narrates Mrs Hudson (their landlady) admitting Mrs Kemp, asking `who is mrs hudson?` got a confidently wrong answer — Watson denied any such person had ever belonged to the household, and Holmes then fabricated an unrelated, contradicting identity for the visitor ("Mrs Kemp's sister, a laundress from Stepney").

## Root cause

`who is mrs hudson?` routes through the intent parser's `QUESTION_PREFIXES` match into the `query` intent type, resolved by `resolveQuery()` in `engine/resolvers/meta.ts`. That resolver's `WORLD QUERY` prompt note only told the model to draw on (1) location atmosphere/description and (2) generic Victorian-gentleman knowledge — it had no instruction to stay consistent with anything already established earlier in the same session (an NPC met, a caller just announced, a household fixture). With no such grounding, the model improvised and contradicted the scene it had itself just narrated.

This is a gap in the engine/AI contract's "verified state only" discipline for the one resolver whose scope is deliberately open-ended (arbitrary player questions) — it never had a "don't contradict what already happened" safety rail the way TALK/topic misses and absent-NPC blocks do.

## Fix

Added an explicit anti-contradiction clause to the `WORLD QUERY` prompt in `resolveQuery()`: answer consistently with anyone/anything already established this session (an NPC met, a caller just announced, an event already narrated, or a household fixture such as Mrs Hudson) — never deny knowledge of them or invent a conflicting identity or account.

This is a prompt-text-only change; no state/logic changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` — passes
- [x] `npm run qa:engine` — 444 passed, 0 failed (2 pre-existing unrelated warnings)
- [x] `npm run qa:validate` — passes
- [x] `npm run qa:hints`, `npm run qa:diary-leads`, `npm run qa:lambda-imports` — all pass
- [ ] `npm run qa:narration` / live model check of the `who is mrs hudson?` case — not run; `GEMINI_API_KEY` is not available in this cloud session (per repo's CLAUDE.md, expected — reporting the skip rather than treating it as a blocker)

The single `orchestrator` role becomes two, the design document is rewritten for the new
model, and an adversarial review of the whole thing is folded in. Ten commits: six from the
work itself, four from the review.

## What changes

**A dispatcher and a lead, instead of one role at every scope.** A **dispatcher** is the top
of a tree and the only thing `sb start` creates. It holds no task and no context: it relays
what it was given to a child, adds nothing of its own about how the work should be
approached, and asks rather than guessing when the intent is unclear. Everything it is given
goes to a child, including a one-line question, so that the follow-up reaches the agent that
has the context. A **lead** owns one task end to end at any depth — it holds everything about
it, plans, splits, assigns disjoint files, synthesises and cleans up. That prompt is the old
orchestrator prompt, carried across essentially unchanged.

They were one role because the only difference looked like scope, and scope is told to an
agent at spawn. The split exists because "hold everything about your task" and "hold nothing"
do not fit in one prompt without a conditional, and a conditional gets read selectively.

**`orchestrator` still works, and resolves all the way to `lead`.** It is a config alias, so
a stale `--role orchestrator` gets a lead — not the fallback role, which cannot delegate at
all. The Role that comes back carries the new name, so the prompt, the board and the stored
row agree. Aliases are read from a repo's own settings as well as the shipped ones.

**Work that belongs in another repo stops the dispatcher.** It asks Andrew and starts nothing.
This is a stopping rule rather than a capability: there is no cross-repo spawn, and the one
real incident was an agent that, finding no way to root a child in another repo, forked a
worktree of *this* one and edited the other project through a path with nothing refusing it.

**`sb start` finds the running tops by the `is_top` stamp, not by the role name.** This was a
live defect the review caught: the lookup matched roots whose role equalled the configured top
role, and the rename made every existing row invisible — so the next bare `sb start` would
have opened a third top without the line telling Andrew how to get back to the one blocked and
waiting on him. Verified against a copy of the real store: empty before, both tops after.

**`DESIGN-TRUTH.md` is rewritten for the model** and corrected where it was not true of the
code, including what the dispatcher's home actually is and the fact that the dispatcher *role*
is not gated at all — a lead can ask for it, and only the prompt says not to.

## What is deliberately not in it

- **No tool-layer enforcement of what a dispatcher may do.** No gate, no blocked verbs. A
  dispatcher legitimately writes a handoff file, and a rule that cannot tell that from doing
  the work would either block the job or wave the work through. The prompt is the mechanism,
  which is why so much of this change is prompt text and why it is written to survive being
  read alongside rules that tell every other agent to do the work.
- **Real cross-repo dispatch is not built.** The store is per repo, so a child elsewhere would
  have no parentage, no messaging, no status, no board row and no cleanup reaching it — a
  multi-store fleet, not a flag. Whether it is ever built is open.
- **The herdr grouping limitation is accepted as it stands.** herdr can adopt a dispatcher as
  a repo's group parent if it is the first pane open in that repo's folder, which nests that
  repo's agents under it. Nothing breaks; the view muddles. The only real fix is in herdr and
  Andrew has chosen not to take it, so the document records it as a decided limitation rather
  than pending work.
- **`sb init` is still not refused to agents.** Only `sb start` is. The prompt says setting up
  another repo is Andrew's to do, and that sentence is a rule rather than a wall; whether to
  add the gate is unanswered.
- **Whether every level gets its own worktree is still open with Andrew.** Today only a
  dispatcher's children fork one and a lead's children share the lead's. The document was
  written to match the code, and several entries change if the answer is the other one.

## The review

Four rounds of adversarial review, each with a fresh reviewer and a different lens: the prompt
as a mechanism, the moment it lands on a running fleet, whether the trusted document is true
of the code, and the code read cold. Every round changed the artifact. What it produced, in
short: the flat "a dispatcher does none of the work" rule and the tie-break that makes it beat
the surrounding prompts, a verb for the moment a child finishes, the cleanup prohibition, the
stamp-based top lookup, the corrected document sentences, and the repo-layer fix for aliases.

Also here: `README` and the house-rules preset updated for the new names, and all twenty-four
line-range citations into `DESIGN-TRUTH.md` repaired, with a test that fails when one stops
pointing at an entry.

Suite green at **1206**, up from 1197.

body: Second follow-up to #40. My #45 fixed the template path but left the check rejecting **every legitimate single-platform image**. ## Problem `imagetools inspect --format '{{json .Image}}'` marshals an OCI image config, whose top-level key is **lowercase `config`** (capitalised `Env` nested inside). Confirmed against the real config blob for `ghcr.io/wyre-technology/autotask-mcp@sha256:b92a86a8…`: ``` top-level keys: architecture, config, created, history, os, rootfs has("Config")=false has("config")=true .config.Env = ["PATH=…","NODE_VERSION=26.7.0","NODE_ENV=production", …] ``` So `has("Config")` was false for every single-platform build, sending it down the platform-map branch, iterating the wrong values, and hard-failing. `docker image inspect` — a **different** command — *does* return capitalised `Config`. That is the trap. The check now accepts either. This blocked `autotask-mcp` **v2.32.5**'s deploy. I pulled the rejected digest from GHCR by hand: `application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json`, image config, 12 layers — a genuine image. A false positive, not a real catch. ## Why the previous revision passed review and still broke I tested #45 against fixtures I hand-wrote, which encoded the same wrong casing assumption I was trying to verify. That is the actual root cause of the repeat failure, and it is worth naming. This revision is verified against the **real config blob pulled from GHCR**, using the filter **extracted from the committed YAML** rather than a hand-copy: | input | result | |---|---| | real single-platform config (from GHCR) | PASS | | real multi-platform map (real configs, platform-keyed) | PASS | | real config with `Env` stripped | **REJECT** | | `null` `.Image` | **REJECT** | | legacy capital-`Config` shape | PASS | #40's original intent — refusing to hand an attestation-manifest digest to `deploy` — is preserved in both reject cases. ## Also On rejection the step now prints the `.Image` payload it actually saw, inside a collapsed log group. Without it, diagnosing a false positive means pulling the manifest out of the registry by hand — which is precisely what this one cost. `actionlint` clean (the single `SC2129` is pre-existing in the `release` job). --- Need help on this PR? author: mc-nv
body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs
  `pre-commit run --files` against PR-modified paths only, never `--all-files`.

## Caveats

Editing the config alone scans nothing. Each contributor must run once per clone:

```
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
```

Without the second, the `pre-push` stage stays dormant.

author: twilwa
adolkun
body:
Closes #65.

## Lots

Derived by replaying the trade ledger, never stored (ADR 0002). Each buy is a lot at its own date and price; a sell consumes them oldest-first. A Snapshot Holding — a provider position with no trades behind it — has no lots, which is reported as `snapshot`, not as one lot of unknown date.

Holding period is always computed: to the sell date when closed, to today while open. One year *or more* is long, so the anniversary itself counts. A 29 February lot turns long on 1 March, because a common year has no anniversary for it. A short-term lot shows how many days it still has to run.

## The gain, and the two conventions behind it

Splitting a Realised Gain needs *which* units left and *what* they cost. This takes the first from FIFO and leaves the second on the weighted average the app already books, so one sell keeps one Realised Gain — the tax split can't say 240 while the position says 250. `build_lots` consumes the ledger's own per-sell gains rather than re-deriving them, and asserts the two replays agree on sell order. Recorded as ADR 0003.

`realised_long + realised_short` always equals the ledger's Realised Gain, tested both on the Decimals and after rounding to cents — rounding each half on its own loses a cent whenever an odd number of them splits evenly (9.01 read as 4.50 + 4.50), which is exactly where the user would have seen it.

## Tax character

`GET /api/assets/{id}/tax-lots` reports `tax_character: false` and no lots for a wallet that is not Taxable — including a holding in no wallet at all. The gain there is never Reportable, so a long-versus-short answer would be noise dressed as advice. The derivation itself never sees a tax treatment, so the Wash Sale rule can still replay an IRA's ledger when it arrives. ADR 0002 now records that this is what "hidden" meant.

## UI

Expanding a position lists each wallet leg with its lots — acquisition date, quantity, unit price, cost, character, and days remaining for a short-term lot — plus that leg's long/short split of both the open position and what it has realised. The split is per wallet deliberately: tax character attaches to a wallet, so a consolidated cross-wallet split would blend a taxable leg with a Roth one into a figure no tax return could use.

## Tests

`backend/tests/test_tax_lots.py` — 28 tests, mostly pure: one year exactly, one day either side, both leap-year boundaries, open versus closed, FIFO matching, partial sales, a sale spanning two lots, re-bought positions, the cent-level invariant, and the tax-character gate for every treatment. Plus three API-level tests. Full suite: 2670 backend passed, 91 frontend passed; `tsc` and `eslint` clean.

## Known limits

A holding whose provider quantity predates its first manual trade reports lots for the traded slice only; the ledger becomes authoritative for it the moment a trade lands (ADR 0002), which is what restores agreement. Specific-identification is not offered — the lots derived here are what such a choice would pick from.

body:
The **complete sample-format refactor** (plan: `AI-docs/Squid/in-progress/2026-07-29-sample-format-refactor-plan.md`) plus the start of the rotation feature it was built for. Each commit independently revertible. The well→stage formula that existed in **six independent copies** is now computed in exactly one module, and the monolithic calibration cache is split into geometry (catalog + sparse user overrides) and measured placement (deltas).

## The series

1. **Atomic cache writes, never fatal at import** — an interrupted write used to brick startup (`import control._def` raised on a truncated cache).
2. **Dead/stale state deleted** — zero-caller duplicate parser, write-only viewer field, dead ini keys in 8 templates, the 1536 selector's drifted hardcoded geometry.
3. **Dialog cancel restores the previous format** — two interlocking bugs; plus `select_format_silently()` kills the spurious index-0 emission that momentarily reconfigured the app for the wrong plate.
4. **One filename convention for custom plate images** (spaces preserved; legacy underscore accepted).
5. **Golden oracle** — exact-`==` pins on every producer site, offset-parameterized, with the sites' *disagreements* documented as tests.
6. **`PlateTransform` + `plate_transform_for`** — pure module; identity path `==`-identical to legacy arithmetic; `well_index_at` inverse; `nominal()` for display assets.
7. **Four identity sites swapped** through it (oracle unchanged).
8. **MCP server behavior fix** *(the one intentional change)* — `_parse_wells` now applies `WELLPLATE_OFFSET` like every other site and stops inventing `a1=0`/`spacing=9`; unknown formats raise. Oracle expectation flipped in the same diff.
9. **Plate-PNG renderer draws from `nominal()`** — offset provably cannot leak (byte-identical PNGs under offset 0 vs 25 mm).
10. **`WellplateSettings` object replaces the 10-arg signal** — slots can no longer silently truncate the payload.
11. **Compute-time resolution in `ScanCoordinates`** — a calibration edit or offset change now applies to planning without a signal re-emit; the oracle's snapshot-vs-live disagreement test flips to agreement.
12. **Per-axis spacing/size + `well_shape` as derived data** — the 10-column CSV stays frozen; scalars broadcast; shape's name-based mapping becomes one code-side default.
13. **Geometry/placement split** — `objective_and_sample_formats/sample_formats_user.yaml` (sparse overrides + custom formats, incl. anisotropic carriers; tracked `.example`) and `cache/plate_placement.yaml` (a1 **deltas** + raw measured points; optional per-format `rotation_deg`), with a **one-time idempotent migration** of the legacy cache. Composed coordinates equal the legacy cache bit-for-bit — asserted, not argued.

## Rotation (phase 2, started)

14. **Closed-form placement fit** (`control/core/plate_fit.py`) — similarity fit, rigid-only application, angle rounded to 0.01° *before* a1 derivation, σ̂ from the similarity residual (k=4), predicted RMS/p95 including the discarded-scale bias term, per-axis pitch QC (**both** axes), and the gate set: spread G > 1.5, predicted error > half a well radius (catches one-pitch mis-clicks), signed-area mirror check on the *measured points* (the fitted similarity's det = s² can never fire), pitch > 5% warns, |rotation| > 1° warns-with-confirmation. 25 tests incl. skimage cross-check over randomized poses and Monte Carlo σ̂ unbiasedness across true scales.
15. **Holder rotation record** (`machine_configs/plate_holder.yaml`) — one angle per machine, minimal schema (the answer + the raw measured points; derived numbers recomputed, never stored), provenance **required** for a nonzero angle so a hand-typed or copied-example value cannot validate; tracked `.example` ships with rotation unset. `resolve_rotation_deg()`: override-with-inherit in one branch, zero arithmetic between stored angles — measured placement override > holder record > 0.0; pitch-0 formats (glass slide) always resolve to 0. 8 tests covering the full inherit chain.

16. **Navigation viewer maps stage↔pixel through the plate frame** — the background image is a *nominal* drawing, so forward (FOV boxes) applies R(−θ) about A1 and inverse (double-click) applies R(+θ); planned FOVs land on the wells they will image and clicks navigate to where wells actually sit. Unrotated path kept bit-for-bit legacy (asserted); rotation resolved at call time, once per batch redraw. 5 tests incl. pixel→mm→pixel round trip.
17. **Out-of-travel FOVs dropped loudly** — every region producer counts travel drops into `ScanCoordinates.out_of_travel` (queryable by the upcoming wizard) and warns with exact counts, instead of quietly imaging fewer FOVs than selected. Lifecycle-correct (re-add/remove/clear purge). 8 tests.
18. **Provenance stamps on saved coordinate CSVs** — one JSON comment line records format, effective A1, rotation + source, and save time; "Load Coordinates" warns (but still loads) when the placement has since changed, naming exactly what moved. Legacy unstamped files load as before. 8 tests.

19. **`HolderAlignmentSession`** — the wizard's entire state machine, pure Python: computed reference rings pinned to the design table (96 → A1/A12/H1/H12, 1536 → A1/A47/AE1/AE47 because AF48 is out of travel), method-by-well-shape (rim×3/circumcenter vs one same-corner touch), the constant-offset cancellation theorem asserted to 1e-9, hold-out verification that refuses fit wells, and a save that writes the minimal holder record and *nothing else* — the fitted translation dies there by design. 19 tests.
20. **Holder-rotation mode in the calibration dialog** — third mode radio, a thin view over the session: live fit panel with gates inline, reject-gates disable Save, warn-gates require *typing the angle*, stale per-format overrides offered for clearing at save, hold-out + drive-to-test verification. 8 tests driving the dialog as an operator would.

Point capture keeps **old-widget parity** (owner decision): the button is labeled "Set Point" and captures the stage position exactly like the existing modes' Set Point.

## Cleanup (post-review, 4-agent /simplify pass)

21. **Applied cleanup findings across the rotation series** — the big one: `control/models/yaml_store.py`, one shared guarded-load + atomic-save for the sidecar YAMLs with a stat-signature parse cache (re-parses only when the file changes; callers get deep copies). This removed 10–20 YAML parses/sec the viewer's per-tick rotation resolution was doing on the GUI thread, and the ~1,500 parses that stalled holder-mode entry on a 1536 plate. Also: `rotate_deg()` in `plate_transform` is now the *only* implementation of the rotation leg (viewer, wizard, and transform all call it; θ=0 legacy paths untouched, identity test still exact `==`); `plate_transform_for` no longer reads the placements file twice; the fit's quality query covers only *reachable* wells (`worst_well` doubles as the Drive-to-Test target, which must never command an out-of-limit move); the viewer tracks catalog identity separately from display identity (no more sample-name string matching); out-of-travel bookkeeping is lifecycle-correct; five copy-pasted test fixtures became two shared conftest fixtures.
22. **User-formats YAML adopts `yaml_store`** — the third and last hand-rolled copy of the load/save pattern retires; the import-time load gains the parse cache for free.
23. **One circle solver in the calibration dialog** — `calculate_circle` delegates to the holder mode's `circumcenter`; the retired `np.linalg.solve` version silently returned a wildly-off circle for near-collinear points, where the shared solver rejects them with the dialog's existing collinear-points message.

Deferred to its own PR (noted in the design doc): the ScanCoordinates travel-filter chokepoint refactor — one `_finalize_region` owning filtering/counting/S-pattern/registration for all five planners, which also gives manual regions per-region drop attribution. The backlash concern is closed by

author: dbolser
body:
Implements IMPROVEMENTS.md §1.6: `check_untyped_defs` is now on globally, with a mechanically generated per-module baseline that can only shrink.

## Today's numbers

Reproduced with the exact toolchain CI uses (`mypy==1.16.1` from the pre-commit pin, with numpy): enabling `check_untyped_defs` on current `main` surfaces **2,166 errors in 185 files** (IMPROVEMENTS.md measured 2,172 in 186 at the time of writing; the tree has moved since). The worst offenders are unchanged: `Bio/Align/bigbed.py` (148), `Bio/Seq.py` (120), `Bio/Blast/_parser.py` (118), `Bio/Restriction/Restriction.py` (89), `Bio/GenBank/Scanner.py` (55).

## Scoreboard

**179 modules baselined** (185 failing on the original tree, minus 5 fixed here and `Bio.Pathway` fixed in #97). The number in `.mypy.ini` only goes down.

## The ratchet rule

Stated in the `.mypy.ini` header: baseline entries may only be **removed** (after fixing the module so it passes with `check_untyped_defs` on), never added. New modules are born checked.

## Why per-module `check_untyped_defs = False`, not `ignore_errors = True`

IMPROVEMENTS.md proposed `ignore_errors = True` per module, but that is a much blunter ratchet: it silences *everything* in the module, including the errors mypy already catches today without `check_untyped_defs` — so a baselined module could quietly regress on checks that used to protect it. Per-module `check_untyped_defs = False` preserves the status quo *exactly*: every check that ran yesterday still runs on every module, and clean/new modules additionally get their function bodies checked. Verified: with the baseline in place, the pinned mypy run on the full tree is green.

The sections were generated by script from mypy's own error output (error file list → module names), not hand-typed.

## Proof the ratchet catches regressions

Added this deliberately broken untyped function to `Bio/File.py` (a clean, non-baselined module), ran the pinned mypy, then reverted it:

```python
def _ratchet_demo():
    handle = open("x")
    return handle.made_up_attribute
```

New config catches it:

```
Bio/File.py:637:12: error: "TextIOWrapper[_WrappedBuffer]" has no attribute
"made_up_attribute"  [attr-defined]
        return handle.made_up_attribute
               ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 304 source files)
```

The same injected error under the old behaviour (`--no-check-untyped-defs`) passes clean: `Success: no issues found in 304 source files`. That is exactly the class of latent `AttributeError` §1.6 is about.

## Five trivial fixes (second commit)

Five modules each had exactly **one** error, all `[var-annotated]` — an empty container literal mypy cannot infer. Annotating the literal is a runtime no-op, so these come off the baseline instead of onto it:

| Module | Annotation | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `Bio/SeqIO/FastaIO.py` | `lines: list[str] = []` | only ever holds `line.rstrip()` strings, joined with `"".join` |
| `Bio/AlignIO/MauveIO.py` | `seqs: dict[str, str] = {}` | keys are regex-group id strings, values built by `+=` of line strings |
| `Bio/ExPASy/ScanProsite.py` | `match: dict[str, str \| int] = {}` | values are `int(self.content)` or `self.content` (str), keyed by element name |
| `Bio/Pathway/Rep/Graph.py` | `self._adjacency_list: dict = {}` | keys are caller-supplied node objects of no constrained type; `sorted()` over the keys rules out `object`, so bare `dict` |
| `Bio/Graphics/DisplayRepresentation.py` | `self._label_info: dict = {}` | keys are caller-supplied segment names, values unconstrained labels |

Everything non-obvious stays baselined. `Bio.Pathway` was deliberately left for the separate bug fix in #97 rather than papered over with an annotation. body:
## Problema

Nada validava o código antes do merge. Um pull request podia quebrar o build e isso só aparecia quando o Render falhava no deploy, que é o lugar mais caro e mais tarde possível para descobrir.

Já aconteceu: o deploy quebrou com `Cannot find module '/opt/render/project/src/dist/main'` porque o `prisma/seed.ts` passou a entrar no build e mudou a estrutura da pasta `dist`. Um passo de build rodando no pull request teria mostrado a falha antes de qualquer coisa chegar em produção.

## O que este PR faz

Adiciona um workflow do GitHub Actions que roda em todo pull request para a `main` e em todo push nela, executando lint e build.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**
- Instala dependências com `npm ci`, que respeita o lockfile e garante que a validação use exatamente as mesmas versões do ambiente local.
- Roda `prisma generate` antes de lint e build, porque o Prisma Client é gerado e não versionado. Numa máquina limpa ele não existe, e sem esse passo tudo quebraria por um motivo que não é o código.
- Usa uma `DATABASE_URL` fictícia. O `prisma generate` apenas lê o schema e não abre conexão, mas o schema referencia a variável.

**`.nvmrc`**
- Fixa a versão do Node. O arquivo é lido tanto pelo GitHub Actions quanto pelo Render, então um único lugar passa a controlar a versão nos dois ambientes. Sem isso, o CI poderia validar numa versão diferente da que roda em produção.

**`lint:ci` no `package.json`**
- O script `lint` existente usa `--fix`, o que é correto no desenvolvimento e problemático no CI. O runner é descartável, então a correção seria descartada, e uma violação corrigível automaticamente deixaria o CI verde enquanto o código versionado continuaria com o problema. O novo script apenas reporta.

**Correção de lint**
- `bootstrap()` no `main.ts` estava sem tratamento da Promise retornada. Passa a usar `void`, deixando explícito que o retorno é ignorado de propósito.

body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs
  `pre-commit run --files` against PR-modified paths only, never `--all-files`.

## Caveats

Editing the config alone scans nothing. Each contributor must run once per clone:

```
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
```

Without the second, the `pre-push` stage stays dormant.

## Description

Docs-only prerequisite for issue #1520's Google Drive integration: registers the `drive` commit scope and records the design in ADR-0069, applying ADR-0063 (Gmail OAuth2 credential storage) and ADR-0066 (Gmail named-account store) to a second Google API instead of re-litigating each decision from scratch. Nothing else in #1520's breakdown (#1522–#1526) should start before this lands, since those issues implement what this ADR decides rather than redesigning it.

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- Added a `drive` scope to `.omni-dev/scopes.yaml`, mirroring the existing `gmail` scope's shape (`src/drive/**`, `src/cli/drive.rs`, `src/cli/drive/**`)

- Added `docs/adrs/adr-0069.md`, recording: `DriveSettings`/`DriveAccountSettings` as a field-for-field mirror of Gmail's settings block; a single `drive.readonly` OAuth2 scope with no `DriveScope` enum; no `drive account import-legacy` command and no `Legacy`-named resolution variant (`ResolvedAccount::{Named(String), Unconfigured}`), since Drive has nothing to migrate from; why the OAuth/client/account-resolution code stays duplicated from Gmail's rather than extracted (Drive is Gmail's second such consumer, one short of this repo's stated third-consumer extraction threshold); `--account` scoped to `DriveCommand`'s subtree, not root `Cli`; and the `https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3` API base host

body:
Tracks #238 — close only after published-artifact qualification.

## What changed

- Adds repository profile schema v3 under `@vespeneventures/governance/repository` with caller-owned `rootEntries`.
- Adds pure `validateRepositoryRootEvaluationInput` and `evaluateRepositoryRoot` APIs. Unknown direct children, missing required entries, and observed prohibited entries fail closed.
- Requires every declared direct child to carry an explicit `canonical`, `extension`, `exception`, `compatibility-alias`, or `legacy-artifact` classification and a separate `required`, `allowed`, or `prohibited` disposition.
- Keeps repository-root vocabulary in the existing repository subpath. Account-container discovery and composition remain caller-owned, so no broad governance workspace package or subpath is introduced.
- Updates conventions machine guidance from one workspace authority to discovery and composition across multiple account-owned workspace planes.
- Leaves provisioning implementation unchanged.

## Public API

New functions:

- `validateRepositoryRootEvaluationInput(value)`
- `evaluateRepositoryRoot(value)`

New constants and types:

- `PREVIOUS_REPOSITORY_PROFILE_VERSION`
- `RepositoryProfileV3`
- `RepositoryRootEntry`
- `RepositoryRootEntryClassification`
- `RepositoryRootEntryDisposition`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluationInput`
- `RepositoryRootEntryEvaluation`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluation`
- `RepositoryRootEvaluationStatus`
- `RepositoryRootFinding`
- `RepositoryRootFindingRule`

`REPOSITORY_PROFILE_VERSION` advances to `3`. Closed v1 and v2 profiles remain explicitly supported.

## Consumer migration

1. Upgrade direct consumers to `@vespeneventures/governance@~0.10.0`.
2. Existing v1 and v2 profiles remain valid without edits.
3. To prove an exact root, adopt schema v3 and declare every admitted direct child in `rootEntries`.
4. Discover direct children outside Foundry and pass only normalized names as `observedEntries`.
5. Treat `invalid` and `nonconforming` reports as fail-closed; the caller retains ownership of inventory, observations, paths, retention, precedence, and any mutation.

The deprecated `@vespeneventures/repository@0.4.0` compatibility package forwards the new API. Other governance compatibility packages receive patch releases only to keep their 0.x dependency ranges linked.

## Proposed package versions

- `@vespeneventures/governance@0.10.0`
- `@vespeneventures/conventions@0.5.0`
- `@vespeneventures/repository@0.4.0`
- `@vespeneventures/catalog@0.2.7`

- Conventions tests: 112 passed

## Boundary

No unresolved structural boundary remains for #238. Filesystem discovery, machine manifests, retention decisions, alias removal, and mutation remain consumer-owned. Provisioning v2 remains separate follow-up work.

body:
### Problem
- `bun test --isolate` (and every `--parallel` worker) kills the subprocesses a file left running when it swaps globals between files, but a subprocess spawned at module scope (top level of the file, outside any test or hook) is only killed for the first file of the run. The same spawn in the second and later files outlives the swap and leaks out of the run.
- The killer only registers spawns while `auto_killer.enabled` is set. `--isolate` sets it once at startup (`src/runtime/cli/test_command.rs:2316`; `--parallel` workers do the same in `src/runtime/cli/test/parallel/runner.rs:637`), which is why the first file's module scope is tracked. `Execution::on_group_completed` (`src/runtime/test_runner/Execution.rs:571`) then calls `disable()` after every group of tests, and nothing turns tracking back on until the next group starts, so it is off while the next file's module scope runs. `swap_global_for_test_isolation` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:5057`) kills and clears the tracked set, but those spawns were never in it.
- The comment next to the per-file cleanup in `test_command.rs` ("under --isolate ... we need tracking to remain enabled and populated until then") describes the intended behavior; the per-group `disable()` has defeated it since `--isolate` was added in #29354.

### Fix
- `Execution::on_group_completed` leaves the killer enabled when `vm.test_isolation_enabled` is set. Under `--isolate` tracking is then on for the whole run and the swap's kill + clear covers every spawn the file made, at module scope or inside a test. Without `--isolate` nothing changes: tracking is still per group and the set is still cleared per file.
- Correct because it is the documented contract of `--isolate` (docs/test/parallel.mdx: between files Bun closes "subprocesses the file left open") and it is already how the first file of every run behaves; the change makes the later files match it. The swap is the only place that kills the set between files, so keeping the set populated until then has no other consumer.
- Side effect, stated explicitly: a test timeout under `--isolate` kills everything tracked (`Execution::handle_timeout`), so in files 2+ it now also kills that file's module-scope spawns, as it already did in file 1. #38774 makes the timeout kill per group; once both land a timeout no longer kills module-scope spawns in any file and the swap still kills everything. The two diffs touch adjacent functions and do not conflict.
- Module-scope `spawnSync` calls under `--isolate` now wait on the event loop in every file instead of only the first (the blocking fast path in `js_bun_spawn_bindings.rs:1049` is gated on the killer being off); that is the path every `spawnSync` inside a test already takes.
- Considered and not done here: registering subprocesses with the `ActiveHandle` sweep that runs before the swap (`src/runtime/jsc_hooks.rs`), which would let the killer go back to being timeout-only. The swap has used the killer for subprocesses since #29354 and #38774 is reworking the killer's internals, so this PR keeps the one-line policy change and leaves that reshape as a follow-up.
- Test: `test/cli/test/isolation.test.ts`, "module-scope subprocesses are killed for every isolated file, not just the first", run once for serial `--isolate` and once for a single `--parallel` worker running all three files. Each fixture file spawns a sleeper at module scope and logs its pid; its test asserts the sleepers of the files that ran before it are dead, so the third file to run observes the second file's leak. Both variants fail on the unfixed build (one surviving pid, the second file's) and pass with the fix; the existing in-test spawn case and `test-timeout-behavior.test.ts` still pass.

### Background
- `ProcessAutoKiller` (`src/jsc/ProcessAutoKiller.rs`) is a per-VM set of live `Bun.spawn` processes. `Bun.spawn` adds a process to it only while `enabled` is true, exits remove it, and `kill()` SIGTERMs and empties it. `bun test` uses it in two places: a test timeout kills whatever is in the set, and the `--isolate` swap kills the set to clean up after a file.
- An execution group is the unit `bun:test` runs at a time (a test with its hooks, or a batch of concurrent tests). Without `--isolate`, tracking is turned on and off around each group so a timeout only kills processes spawned while tests were running, and the set is cleared at the end of each file.
- The isolation swap (`swap_global_for_test_isolation`) runs after every file under `--isolate`, and after every file inside a `--parallel` worker (workers always isolate). A file's module scope is evaluated before any of its groups start, which is the window in which tracking was off.

<details>
<summary>Earlier revision</summary>

The first push also switched the two startup sites from `auto_killer.enabled = true` to `auto_killer.enable()` so that `ever_enabled` was set before the first group. The only effect was pruning a first-file module-scope process that exits before any test runs slightly earlier (the swap releases it anyway), so those hunks were dropped after self-review and the diff is now the `on_group_completed` change plus the test.
</details>

author: dillind
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a notification row filed under one date heading while labelling itself with
another — a row under **THIS WEEK** reading "Yesterday".

The heading comes from `dayBucket`, which counts whole calendar days in the
Household's timezone. The row's own timestamp came from `formatRelativeTime`,
which divides elapsed hours by 24 on the device clock. Those two agree most of
the time and disagree at a boundary.

`formatAlertTime` now shares `dayBucket`'s basis, through a `calendarDaysAgo`
helper extracted from it.

## Extra Info / Things to note

**Stacked on #53** (`refactor/CRU-046-plain-alert-sentence`), not on `main`. Both
touch `alert-row.tsx`, and branching off `main` would have produced a pointless
conflict in the same JSX block. Merge #53 first.

**Anything under a day stays a duration** — "30m ago", "5h ago". An hour is an
hour wherever the reader is standing, which is the rule `dates.ts` already
states for `formatRelativeTime`. Only the day-and-over range moves to calendar
days.

**`AlertRow` now takes a `timezone` prop.** It needs the Household's zone to
count days, and the screen already had it.

**`post-card.tsx` still uses `formatRelativeTime` and is deliberately untouched.**
It renders a timestamp with no date heading above it, so there is nothing for it
to contradict. Changing it would be churn.

Two of the new tests are the boundary cases that produced this: 26 hours back is
two calendar days back in Brisbane, and the same instant is "Yesterday" in
Brisbane but "20h ago" in New York.

No migration, no schema change, no new dependency.

## How to Test

1. Open the bell on Home → `home/notifications`.
2. Confirm every row under **YESTERDAY** reads "Yesterday", and every row under
   **THIS WEEK** reads "2d ago" / "3d ago" — never a row under one heading
   labelled with another.
3. Confirm rows from earlier today still read as durations: "Just now",
   "30m ago", "5h ago".
4. Confirm rows older than a week read as a date ("1 Aug"), with the year added
   for a different year.
5. The interesting case, if you can reach it: an alert written late in the
   evening, read the next morning. It should say "Yesterday" and sit under
   **YESTERDAY**, not "13h ago" under **YESTERDAY**.

Verified on the iOS simulator against the live inbox, across the day boundary
that produced the original mismatch.

author: mc-nv
body:
## Description

Enables the NVIDIA `secret-scan-trufflehog` pre-commit hook, pinned to `v0.3.0`,
as the first entry under `repos:` so scanning runs before any formatter rewrites
the working tree.

This adopts the centrally maintained hook published by `NVIDIA/security-workflows`
rather than a hand-rolled TruffleHog invocation, so the scanner version and its
per-platform checksums are bumped in one reviewed place instead of 27.

`v0.3.0` is pinned deliberately. It installs the scanner inside pre-commit's own
Python environment — removing the shell installer, so Windows works without Git
Bash — and it adds `--exclude-detectors=lob`. That exclusion matters here: a Lob
API key is `test_` followed by 35 characters, so the detector matches ordinary
pytest function names such as `test_gpu_conf_compute_attestation_report`, and
Lob's verifier reports them as *verified* — the one result class this hook fails
on.

Behaviour: scans only the files pre-commit supplies (staged files at commit time,
the push range at push time), reports verified secrets only, and fails closed on
a finding.

Deliberately **out of scope**:

- No `ci: skip:` block. That is prescribed for the hosted pre-commit.ci sandbox,
  which has no network access. No Triton repo uses pre-commit.ci — CI runs
  pre-commit from `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` — so it would be dead config.
- No `default_install_hook_types` change. Activation is a developer action;
  changing that key would alter install behaviour for *every* hook in the repo,
  not just this one. Tracked separately.

## Changes

- Add `NVIDIA/security-workflows` `secret-scan-trufflehog` @ `v0.3.0` as the
  first entry under `repos:`.

## Affected Files

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`

## Test plan

- `pre-commit validate-config` — passes.
- `pre-commit run secret-scan-trufflehog --all-files` — passes, with **zero**
  pre-existing verified secrets, so CI does not break on merge.
- TruffleHog **3.95.9** confirmed installed into pre-commit's Python environment
  and executed, so the hook is functional rather than a silent no-op.
- Blast radius is bounded: `.github/workflows/pre-commit.yml` runs
  `pre-commit run --files` against PR-modified paths only, never `--all-files`.

## Caveats

Editing the config alone scans nothing. Each contributor must run once per clone:

```
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
```

Without the second, the `pre-push` stage stays dormant.

## Problema

A marca d'água "REFERÊNCIA" não aparecia na imagem enviada, mesmo com o checkbox marcado.

## Causa

`ctx.globalAlpha = 0.28` atenuava **em dobro** a opacidade: multiplicava o alpha já baixo do contorno (`0.35 × 0.28 ≈ 0.1`) e do preenchimento, deixando a marca praticamente invisível.

## Correção

- Opacidade embutida direto nas cores (`rgba(255,255,255,0.55)` no preenchimento e `rgba(0,0,0,0.45)` no contorno), sem `globalAlpha`.
- Fonte um pouco maior e espaçamento menor entre as repetições.

Renderizado em Chromium headless (Playwright): a marca altera **~21% dos pixels** de uma imagem clara — claramente visível.

author: willb77
body:
## The bug

`Prism Data → PRISM Report (PDF)` navigated the **current** tab, so Home was replaced by the PDF.

The code already tried to do the right thing — open a tab synchronously inside the click gesture, then redirect it once the presigned URL resolves — and the comment even explains why that ordering matters. The **features argument defeated it**:

```js
window.open("", "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")   // → null
```

Passing `noopener` (or `noreferrer`, which implies it) makes `window.open` return **null** by spec. So `win` was always `null` and execution fell through to `window.location.href = url`.

**Verified in Chrome 150, inside a genuine user gesture** (a synthetic click is not enough — the popup blocker nulls both):

| call | returns |
|---|---|
| `window.open("", "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")` | **NULL — no handle** |
| `window.open("", "_blank")` | **HANDLE** |

## The fix

Open with no features so the handle survives, then sever the opener by assignment — the same protection the flag existed for:

```js
const win = window.open("", "_blank")
if (win) win.opener = null
```

The blocked-popup fallback no longer navigates the current tab (that *is* the bug). It shows a toast with an **"Open report"** action; clicking that is itself a user gesture, so opening with the URL up front is not blocked.

**Deliberately not touched:** the other `window.open` call sites (`ChatWindowChatTab`, Honor, Job Fit) pass the URL *directly*, so a null return costs them nothing — the tab still opens. Only this one needed a handle back.

## Why the tests didn't catch it

They mocked `window.open` to **return a fake window** — which is exactly what a real browser refuses to do here. A mock cannot reproduce a null return.

Now 6 tests (was 4). They pin the **call shape** — `("", "_blank")` with features free of `noopener`/`noreferrer` — and assert `opener` is severed. A new test covers the blocked-popup path: location unchanged, and the toast offers a way through.

**Both halves verified to gate:** restoring the features fails the 2 call-shape tests; restoring the navigating fallback fails the new one (0 toast calls).

<!-- Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing (see ../CONTRIBUTING.md) -->
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The e2e test `[It] Workload cluster creation when Creating a highly available cluster with Azure CNI v1 [REQUIRED] can create 3 control-plane nodes and 2 Linux worker nodes [Azure CNI v1]` fails intermittently with a 409 Conflict error:

```
Operation cannot be fulfilled on daemonsets.apps "azure-cni": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again
```

Root cause: `InstallCNIManifest` in `test/e2e/cni.go` calls `workloadCluster.CreateOrUpdate(ctx, cniYaml)` twice during a test run. The first call (during `EnsureCloudProviderAzure`) creates the `azure-cni` DaemonSet. Between the two calls (~81 seconds), kube-controller-manager on the workload cluster mutates the DaemonSet, advancing its `resourceVersion`. The second call uses the stale `resourceVersion` from the static manifest bytes, and the API server rejects the Update with HTTP 409. Because `CreateOrUpdate` does not retry on conflict, the error propagates immediately as a terminal test failure.

The fix wraps the `CreateOrUpdate` call inside `InstallCNIManifest` with `retry.RetryOnConflict(retry.DefaultBackoff, ...)`. This retries only on `apierrors.IsConflict` (HTTP 409); on each retry, `CreateOrUpdate` performs a fresh Get to obtain the current `resourceVersion` before re-issuing the Update, directly resolving the stale-resourceVersion race. All other errors propagate immediately and no other behavior is changed.

Changes are confined to the single call site inside `InstallCNIManifest` in `test/e2e/cni.go`.

 	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
+	apierrors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors"
+	utilerrors "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors"
+	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/wait"
 	"sigs.k8s.io/cluster-api/test/framework/clusterctl"
 )
 
@@ -48,7 +52,66 @@ func EnsureCNI(ctx context.Context, input clusterctl.ApplyCustomClusterTemplateA
 	}
 }
 
-// InstallCNIManifest installs the CNI manifest provided by the user
+// cniInstallBackoff is the backoff used when retrying CNI manifest installation on conflict.
+var cniInstallBackoff = wait.Backoff{
+	Duration: 500 * time.Millisecond,
+	Factor:   2,
+	Jitter:   0.1,
+	Steps:    6,
+}
+
+// isConflictError reports whether err is retryable due to a resource-version conflict.
+//
+// Semantics:
+//   - nil is not a conflict.
+//   - A direct apierrors.IsConflict error is retryable.
+//   - A utilerrors.Aggregate is retryable only when it is non-empty and every
+//     contained error satisfies apierrors.IsConflict.
+//   - A mixed aggregate (some conflict, some not) is not retryable.
+func isConflictError(err error) bool {
+	if err == nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	if agg, ok := err.(utilerrors.Aggregate); ok {
+		errs := agg.Errors()
+		if len(errs) == 0 {
+			return false
+		}
+		for _, e := range errs {
+			if !apierrors.IsConflict(e) {
+				return false
+			}
+		}
+		return true
+	}
+	return apierrors.IsConflict(err)
+}
+
+// retryCreateOrUpdate runs fn with bounded exponential backoff, retrying only
+// on conflict errors. lastErr is set to the most recent error returned by fn.
+// It returns the terminal error from the backoff loop (nil on success,
+// the non-conflict error if fn returned one, or wait.ErrWaitTimeout if all
+// attempts were exhausted due to conflicts).
+func retryCreateOrUpdate(ctx context.Context, fn func() error, lastErr *error) error {
+	backoff := cniInstallBackoff
+	return wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext(ctx, backoff, func(_ context.Context) (bool, error) {
+		*lastErr = fn()
+		if *lastErr == nil {
+			return true, nil
+		}
+		if isConflictError(*lastErr) {
+			// Retryable: the caller will perform a fresh Get on the next attempt.
+			return false, nil
+		}
+		// Non-conflict errors are terminal.
+		return false, *lastErr
+	})
+}
+
+// InstallCNIManifest installs the CNI manifest provided by the user.
+// It retries on HTTP 409 Conflict (stale resourceVersion) using bounded
+// exponential backoff so that a second call after a controller has mutated
+// the DaemonSet does not fail the test.
 func InstallCNIManifest(ctx context.Context, input clusterctl.ApplyCustomClusterTemplateAndWaitInput) {
 	By("Installing a CNI plugin to the workload cluster")
 	workloadCluster := input.ClusterProxy.GetWorkloadCluster(ctx, input.Namespace, input.ClusterName)
@@ -56,7 +119,19 @@ func InstallCNIManifest(ctx context.Context, input clusterctl.ApplyCustomCluster
 	cniYaml, err := os.ReadFile(input.CNIManifestPath)
 	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
 
-	Expect(workloadCluster.CreateOrUpdate(ctx, cniYaml)).To(Succeed())
+	var lastErr error
+	retryErr := retryCreateOrUpdate(ctx, func() error {
+		return workloadCluster.CreateOrUpdate(ctx, cniYaml)
+	}, &lastErr)
+	if retryErr != nil {
+		// ExponentialBackoffWithContext returns wait.ErrWaitTimeout when steps are
+		// exhausted without the condition returning true; surface the last conflict
+		// error instead for a clear failure message.
+		if lastErr != nil {
+			Expect(lastErr).To(Succeed())
+		}
+		Expect(retryErr).To(Succeed())
+	}
 }

author: jacobecox
body:
## Summary

Live-tested the stack in AWS (us-east-1) and found the current `main` **cannot deploy or serve traffic**. This PR fixes the three blockers found in testing, upgrades all outdated dependencies, rewrites the README, and cleans up the repo. The fixed stack was verified end-to-end against real infrastructure (Lambda → NLB targets healthy, proxy target AVAILABLE, PrivateLink service name exported) and then destroyed.

## What was blocking

1. **PostgreSQL 15.12 no longer exists in RDS** — AWS retired that minor version, so `terraform apply` fails outright with `Cannot find version 15.12 for postgres`. The `rds_engine_version` variable also wasn't wired through (the module hardcoded the version, so overriding it did nothing).
2. **The RDS Proxy had no database registered behind it** — AWS creates the proxy's default target group empty; the config never registered the DB instance (`db_instance_identifier` was passed into the module but unused). Clients could reach the proxy through the NLB, but the proxy had nowhere to send connections.
3. **The RDS instance was unreachable by the proxy** — no security group was passed to the DB (the community RDS module does not auto-create one, despite a comment claiming it does), so the instance landed in the VPC default SG, which blocks the proxy's traffic.

## What was updated

**Fixes**
- Register the DB instance as the proxy target (`aws_db_proxy_default_target_group` + `aws_db_proxy_target`) — verified target health reaches `AVAILABLE`
- Dedicated `rds-instance-sg` allowing 5432 from the VPC CIDR
- `rds_engine_version` wired through, default bumped to a currently-offered minor (15.18), parameter-group family derived from it

**Upgrades**
- AWS provider `~> 5.0` → `~> 6.0` (5.x is security-fixes-only upstream); Terraform floor `>= 1.11.1`
- terraform-aws-modules/rds `~> 6.0` → `~> 7.0`, migrating to write-only `password_wo` — the DB password is no longer stored in Terraform state
- Lambda runtime `python3.12` → `python3.14`; vendored dnspython 2.6.1 → 2.8.0
- RDS storage `gp2` → `gp3`

**README rewrite**
- Architecture diagram embedded; full documentation of every input/output and both deployment modes
- Removed the incorrect IAM-authentication claim (the proxy uses Secrets Manager auth; clients connect with username/password and **TLS is required**)
- Added the existing-mode prerequisite that the DB's security group must allow the proxy, retired-minor-version troubleshooting, and teardown instructions

**Repo hygiene**
- Untracked ~100 committed Python 3.8 `.pyc` files; `.gitignore` now covers `__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`, and `.claude/`

## Verified non-issue

The out-of-VPC Lambda using the 169.254.169.253 resolver **works** — that resolver is reachable from Lambda's managed environment and the proxy endpoint resolves via public DNS. Both proxy IPs were registered and healthy in the NLB target group during testing. No change made there.

author: arkadianet
body: In-depth audit of the Argus alpha (Rust core, FFI, Flutter shell, platform storage, and the live send path). Full write-up is in `docs/alpha-audit.md`. ## Verdict This is a Phase 0/1 scaffold with correct EIP-3 **address derivation**. It is **not a spendable wallet**. Do not put real funds on this build. Address vectors pass. The security model in `docs/security-design.md` does not match the code. ## P0 (must fix before anyone funds this) 1. **Seed wrap is circular.** AES key is `Argon2(seed[..32])`. Unlock passes `keyMaterial: []`. Restore after process death cannot work. 2. **Signing uses the BIP-32 master key**, not `m/44'/429'/0'/0/i` children. Displayed P2PK boxes cannot be signed. `ergo-lib::Wallet::from_mnemonic` at the pinned SHA does the same. 3. **Quick-create never shows the mnemonic.** Combined with (1), a killed process loses the wallet and the user never saw the phrase. 4. **Empty-wallet UI shows the public appkit test address** via `test_derive_display()`. Receive/QR/copy advertise it. 5. **Send never broadcasts.** `submit_transaction` is not on the FFI. The UI says “Transaction submitted”. 6. **Release APK has no `INTERNET` permission** (debug/profile only) and is signed with the debug keystore. 7. **Every send sweeps all UTXOs** and builds change with empty registers — NFTs are destroyed. `box_selector` exists and is unused. 8. **Two independent UTXO fetches** (build vs reduce) can disagree; reduce zips and drops the tail. ## P1 highlights - Mnemonics are Dart `String`s (the “no secret in Dart heap” claim is false). - Production send appends an undisclosed **0.011 ERG Citadel fee**; unit tests disable it. - Change address is trusted from Dart `sender_address`. - Discovery is not BIP-44 (UTXO-only gap, `next_unused` ≈ 980, always reports scanned 999). - iOS `SecureStorageHandler.register(with: self)` is the wrong type; FRB generated files are gitignored so a clean checkout cannot build. ## Recommended order Do not add DeFi until create → backup → restore → EIP-3 sign → submit works on a fixture. 1. Kill the circular KDF; platform wrap only (or a real user secret). 2. Load EIP-3 child keys into `Wallet`; add a fixture sign test. 3. Mnemonic backup UI; validate BIP-39; remove `test_derive_display` from the app. 4. One UTXO fetch → select → reduce → sign → submit, with fee/change preview. Citadel fee off or disclosed. 5. Preserve registers; don’t sweep NFTs. 6. Discovery via tx history. 7. Commit or generate FRB in CI; add `INTERNET` to the main manifest. This PR is documentation only. No code changes.
