author: jbylund
body:
`IN (subquery)` forms that the optimizer can't unnest were reaching the Python executor, which
compiled `x IN (SELECT ...)` to `IN(x)` — silently dropping the subquery. Others were rewritten by
`decorrelate()` into a LEFT-JOIN anti-join, which doesn't preserve the three-valued NULL semantics of
`NOT IN`. Either way the query returned a confident wrong answer.

This makes those forms raise `ExecuteError` instead, and closes the guard holes that let them
through. With `t.a = {1, 2, NULL}` and `u.b` as noted:

| Query | On `main` | Correct answer |
|---|---|---|
| `a NOT IN (SELECT b FROM u)`, `u.b = {2, 3}` | `[(1,), (2,)]` | `[(1,)]` |
| same, `u.b = {2, NULL}` | `[(1,), (2,)]` | `[]` — NULL poisons every row |
| `a NOT IN (SELECT b FROM u WHERE b = t.a)` (correlated), `u.b = {2}` | `[]` | `[(1,)]` |
| `NOT (a IN (SELECT b FROM u))` | `[(1,), (NULL,)]` | `[]` |
| `SELECT 1 WHERE 1 IN (SELECT 1)` (no outer FROM) | `[]` | `[(1,)]` |

Raising is a stopgap until the optimizer learns a NULL-safe rewrite — the goal here is to stop
returning wrong rows silently. The guard is now one `_is_negated` helper shared by `unnest()` and
`decorrelate()`; it looks through parentheses and counts negations, so `NOT (x IN ...)` and
correlated `NOT IN` can no longer slip into the unsafe rewrite, while `NOT NOT (x IN ...)` still
takes the plain-`IN` path. Plain `IN`, and everything the optimizer fully unnests, are unchanged.

Disclosure: implemented with Claude.

author: joshbrooks
body:
Rakaia compares what a replay would write against what your tables already hold,
to check that replaying the log reproduces your data. Any column holding a date
or a time always failed that comparison — not sometimes, always. When an event is
recorded, timestamps get rounded down to the nearest millisecond, but the
database keeps microseconds, so the two never matched. Dates were worse still:
the recorded form is text and the column hands back a date, which can't be equal
whatever the value.

The visible cost is a verification report that always shows differences, which
teaches you to stop reading it. The expensive cost is quieter: the same
comparison decides whether a replay can skip rewriting a row it hasn't changed.
So every replay rewrote every row with a timestamp — bumping "last modified"
fields, re-firing whatever listens for saves, and re-replicating it all, for
values nobody touched.

Both sides are now rounded down to milliseconds before comparing, which is the
only way to make them meet — reading the recorded value back isn't enough on its
own. The trade-off is that a change smaller than a millisecond now counts as no
change; that's deliberate, since a difference that small can't be recorded in the
log to begin with. Stored values keep their full precision. Closes #83.

## What & why

Frontend-completion program groundwork. Three audit reports scoped the work; this PR builds the **reusable UX foundation** the rest of the program (ELV workspace, per-module 360s, etc.) will stand on, so we don't repeat the "102 bespoke tables" pattern.

**Scope guardrail: UI/UX only.** No API contract, controller, service, schema/migration, business-logic, financial-calc, or auth-rule changes. New pages/primitives read/act over existing endpoints and existing BFF proxies.

## Contents

**Audit (`docs/reports/`)**
- Frontend surface audit (102 controllers × 173 pages) + gap register + per-page UX scorecard (measured, static-signal).

**P0-A — UX foundation**
- `aura-data-table` → operational register: URL-persisted state, pagination, faceted filters, column visibility, row deep-linking, and **responsive rows→cards** (`useIsMobile`). Pure engine extracted to `table-query.ts` (+20 unit tests).
- `DataState` composed loading/empty/error wrapper; `RelatedRecords` + `ActivityTimeline` connectivity primitives; `use-media-query` hook.
- `lib/data-error.ts`: extracted the client-safe error taxonomy out of `lib/api.ts` (which imports `next/headers`) so client components can use `DataState`; `api.ts` re-exports it (no import churn).

**PR-04 — shared record shell**
- Promoted `crm/record-shell` → `components/ui/record.tsx` (usable by every module, not just CRM). `crm/record-shell.tsx` is now a thin re-export, so the 5 CRM 360 consumers are untouched. `RecordShell` gained optional `related`/`activity` props.

**PR-05 — project context (URL-derived, no divergence)**
- `lib/project-scope.ts` pure `readProjectScope`/`buildScopeUrl`/`toAIContext` (+15 unit tests) + `lib/project-context.tsx` provider that **re-derives from the URL each render** (setters navigate, never `setState`) with a dev divergence guard. Wired into the project layout; discipline selector in the shell. `ai-dock` sends structured `page.projectContext` read from the **same URL** the engineer is on — nested in the existing `page` object, so **no API-contract change**. Context is UX/AI-only, **not** authorization (RLS remains enforcement).

## Verification

- Typecheck 0, lint 0 (new files), **48/48** web unit tests, production build passes.
- **Live prod-browser** gates: PR-01 (search/sort/filter+URL, filter→page-1 reset, deep-link/refresh restore, mobile cards, empty/loading — and caught+fixed a real `next/headers` client-boundary bug the build missed); PR-05 (2 real projects: init, deep-link restore, divergence guard `URL id === server head id`, scope isolation A→B, structured AI context, AI-dock transport captured on the wire).

author: jbylund
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #18.

`NOT IN (subquery)` is spelled in a form that keeps its three-valued NULL semantics and that the optimizer can already execute:

```sql
x NOT IN (SELECT b FROM u)
=>
NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT b FROM u) _u_0
            WHERE _u_0.b = x OR _u_0.b IS NULL OR x IS NULL)
```

The OR arms carry the NULL logic: a NULL in the subquery poisons every row, and a NULL `x` survives only when the subquery is empty (`x IS NULL` makes the EXISTS true exactly when the subquery is non-empty — the case a naive `IS NOT NULL` escape gets wrong). The derived-table wrap counts the subquery's result rows, so a grouping, aggregate or `LIMIT` inside keeps its meaning.

The rewrite only fires conjunctively (WHERE / join-ON through AND); correlated or multi-column `NOT IN` is still declined and raises in the executor.

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite green (`python -m unittest`)
- [x] New `test_not_in_subquery` executor cases: poisoned subquery, empty subquery, single/double/triple negation, literal and NULL left operands, computed and aggregated inner projections
- [x] New DuckDB-checked `optimizer.sql` entries; plans also differentially verified against DuckDB on poisoned / empty / null-free data
- [x] TPC-H Q16 fixture regenerated: one LEFT JOIN, no extra CTEs
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean

Disclosure: implemented with Claude.

Pin the cargo ecosystem to `versioning-strategy: increase`. Dependabot made `increase-if-necessary` the default for every Cargo crate on 2026-06-10 (dependabot/dependabot-core#14306, closing dependabot/dependabot-core#4009), after which bumps that already satisfied the existing requirement updated `Cargo.lock` alone and left the `Cargo.toml` requirements behind.

The upstream default is motivated by manifest churn dragging the MSRV up. MSRV is verified by a separate CI job here, so keeping the requirements in step with the resolved versions stays safe.

author: zakolenko
body:
Closes #212.

`getSearchParams` returned one module-level empty `URLSearchParams` object for every URL without a query string. Because that object is mutable, one caller could contaminate later queryless requests in the same process.

This makes every call return a fresh, caller-owned instance. The regression test repeats the same queryless URL, mutates the first result, and verifies that the second result has a different identity and no inherited value.

author: benceruleanlu
body:
## Summary

Adds the DES-550 post-first-output discovery card and continues the generated image into three dedicated continuation workflows.

## Changes

- Shows the card after every first-run tour ending, and adds Animate, 4× Upscale, Nano Banana restyle, and Browse all templates actions.
- Seeds the captured output through each template's declared `io.inputs` metadata and fails closed if catalog/workflow metadata is incomplete or drifts.
- Filters the three actions against the served catalog, so an install on an older template package hides an action instead of failing it on click.
- Falls back to the template browser when nothing is seedable — an install serving none of the three, or a run that produced no image. Suppressing the card there would take the way forward from the users who most need it (#14144).
- Correlates output to the newly accepted first-run job across every media key, including WebSocket output arriving before HTTP job metadata, and outliving the tour so walking to the end during a long generation does not discard the result.
- Prefers a saved result over a preview on both the direct and the buffered path, but seeds a preview's `temp` file when nothing saved one — a `PreviewImage` sink is the whole result and the backend still serves it.
- Holds the card open while a continuation loads, so dismissing it cannot leave a graph swap or an error toast behind.
- Waits for the served catalog before rendering, so the card cannot paint the fallback and then rewrite itself into the continuations under the user. Capped at 3s, because a stalled fetch must not withhold the card from the user it is for (#14144).
- Preserves delayed display, dialog deferral, close/Escape behavior, no-auto-run, and loading/error feedback.

## Template dependency

Workflow templates: [Comfy-Org/workflow_templates#1184](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/pull/1184) (merged).

Static mappings:

- `video_minimax_h3_i2v_continuation`
- `utility_seedvr2_7b_int8_upscale_image` (existing template; 4× multiplier)
- `api_google_nano_banana2_image_edit_continuation`

The paid action continues to rely on the existing execution-time auth and billing guard. Installs pin `comfyui_workflow_templates` independently of the frontend, so the catalog filter above is what keeps an older package from producing dead buttons.

Linear: [FE-1355](https://linear.app/comfyorg/issue/FE-1355/e-22-fe-post-nux-discovery-everything-you-can-do-free-paid)

## Telemetry

`tour_completed` is dropped from `nudge_shown` and `explore_templates_clicked`. `nudge_suggestion_clicked` is added, carrying the chosen action and whether its template opened.

All three nudge events now carry `suggestion_count` — this is a schema change for anyone querying them. Zero means the card fell back to the template browser, which is the only signal distinguishing template-package skew from a nudge that never appeared. The count reported is always the one rendered: the card and the event share a single catalog gate, so neither can describe a state the other never showed. Each tour reports its own impression — a second first-run tour is a second nudge, not a repeat of the first.

## Testing

- Focused unit/component tests across four suites, including catalog skew, a catalog that lands late and one that stalls, per-tour impression reporting, missing `io` metadata, the temp/saved output preference on both the direct and the buffered path, video output, late output after the tour ends, and the missing-filename path.
- `pnpm test:unit`, clean-install `vue-tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, type-aware Oxlint, formatting, and `knip --cache`.

## Screenshots (if applicable)

[Figma reference](https://www.figma.com/design/SSo9GcILgQhAV3uoa4r1xJ/Onboarding?node-id=2602-18740)

author: papadanico
body:
## What happened

#202 gave the homepage hero CTAs `w-full sm:w-auto` — full width on a phone, intrinsic width "once they sit in a row" — and shipped **without a test**, because the rule looked like it only had one interesting viewport.

It had two. At `lg` the hero splits into two columns and the left one narrows to ~450px, while the buttons at their intrinsic widths need `266 + 188 + 12 = 466px`. `sm:flex-wrap` did exactly what it was asked and wrapped them — back into a stack, 266px above 188px, ragged, at the single most common desktop width.

| viewport | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 390 | 358 / 358 (stacked) | unchanged |
| 768 | 266 / 188 (**one row**) | unchanged |
| 1440 | 266 / 188 (stacked, ragged) | **456 / 456** |

The rule was never about narrow screens. A button alone on its line should fill the line, and `lg` is the other place that is true.

## The test

`e2e/hero-cta.spec.ts` asserts the **rule**, not the breakpoint: at 390, 768 and 1440, two CTAs that land on separate lines must match in width, and two that share a line must share a baseline. Deciding "stacked" by geometry rather than by breakpoint keeps the test honest if the copy in either button changes length and moves where the wrap happens.

**Mutation-verified**: reverting `lg:w-full` makes the desktop case fail with `stacked CTAs differ by 78px at 1440px`. The phone and tablet cases stay green, which is the point — the old fix was correct as far as it went.

## How it was found

A first-screenful ink-coverage sweep across both platforms. JiPange desktop measures 19–26% ink against 38–48% on mobile; Mwangaza measures 26–41% desktop against 78–85% mobile. That pointed at the hero, and the screenshot showed the wrap. The broader desktop density question is real and larger than this PR — flagging it rather than folding it in here.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- `e2e/hero-cta.spec.ts` 3/3 pass; fails 1/3 without the fix

author: jackweiw
body:
## RFC 0003 — Controllability & feedback-adjustment contract for automated iteration

Proposes the control-path prerequisite for Phase 2 auto-iteration, which is currently missing:

- **Named knob space** — the synthesis knobs the agent may steer (`working_set_mb`, `access_pattern`, `archetype`, `compute_ratio`, `memory_ratio`, …), drawn from the codegen templates.
- **Adjustment schema** — a structured delta (`{stage, knob, from, to, rationale, expected_metric, expected_direction}`) the agent emits and codegen honors, replacing free-text instruction rewriting.
- **Agent `revise_instruction` step** — refills the slot removed as dead code in #32; reads comparator diffs + a sensitivity table to emit knob deltas.
- **Steerability spike as a mandatory gate** — `examples/steerability_spike.py` proves the key knobs actually move Topdown/bandwidth in a monotonic, expected direction. The auto-iteration loop is **not** wired until this gate passes.

### Why now
RFCs 0001 (thread-pool codegen) and 0002 (context compaction) both presuppose a control contract exists. This RFC defines it, so it lands first.

### What's in this PR
- `docs/rfc/0003-controllability-and-feedback-adjustment.md` (status: In Review)
- `examples/steerability_spike.py` — disposable ARM measurement harness (OAT sweep, 6 knobs × 3 points, writes `sensitivity.json` + `sensitivity.md` with controllable/weak/dead verdicts)
- `docs/rfc/README.md` index entry

### Non-goals (explicitly out of scope, gated on the spike)
The loop driver wiring `revise_instruction` into `run_full_pipeline`, `revise_instruction` implementation, and context compaction (RFC 0002) — these land in follow-up PRs **after** the spike passes on ARM and the sensitivity table is in hand.

### Quality gates
Spike script passes `ruff check` + `ruff format` + `mypy --strict` (examples/ is outside CI scope, but pre-commit runs on it locally). No `src/` or `tests/` changes — existing suite unaffected.

### Next step
Run `examples/steerability_spike.py --devkit-cmd <devkit> --out-dir ./spike_out` on the ARM target. The resulting `sensitivity.json` decides whether the follow-up is `revise_instruction` (gate passes) or codegen knob-fix tickets (dead knobs surface here).

author: elares
body:
The last six. The ratchet is now **0**, and #122 criterion 1's *"validates clean with zero untyped schemas"* is **met** rather than approached.

## Five were arrays of objects

Each element shape was confirmed from the **producer or the parser**, not from the field name:

| field | evidence |
|---|---|
| `primitives[]` (×2) | documented as force / restrict / reject / default **objects** |
| `failures[]` | "each an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer and a reason" |
| `signals` | assembled as `Vec<serde_json::Value>` in `repository.rs:11795` |
| `transform` | `parse_transform` errors with *"a JSON array of well-formed transform steps"* |

Guessing from names would have got `signals` **wrong** — it reads like a map and is an array.

## The sixth is why this was per-field work

`client_secret` is a genuine **union**: a bare string, or `{ "file": ... }`, or `{ "env": ... }`. It now carries a custom schema emitting `type: ["string", "object"]`.

Calling it `type: object` would have cleared the count while telling every generated client that a plain string is invalid. That is a **worse contract than saying nothing**: an untyped field makes a generator emit `any` and the caller stays correct; a wrongly typed one makes it emit a type that *rejects valid input*.

## The ceiling stays at zero rather than being deleted

Reaching zero is not the same as staying there. The next `serde_json::Value` added without a `value_type` lands as a failure, not as a number somebody bumps.

## Verification

`value_type` and `schema_with` are schema hints, not serde, so runtime is untouched — **136 ironauth-admin tests green**, read from the run's own exit code. clippy clean. `openapi-check` and `openapi-lint` both clean, each verified by its own exit code post-commit (the pre-commit run reports drift by design, since the regenerated artifact was not yet committed).

## Criterion status on #122

- [x] **1.** typed OpenAPI spec, zero untyped schemas — the spec was already published and versioned; this closes the quality half
- [ ] 2. third-party SDK passes a conformance suite
- [ ] 3. cookie / session / CSRF / error-code formats documented with a stability policy
- [ ] 4. generated Go and Python SDKs build in CI
- [ ] 5. auto-generated changelog from a spec diff
- [x] **6.** CI fails when the API changes without a regenerated spec — `openapi-check.sh`, now joined by `openapi-lint.sh` for quality

author: akadlec
body:
PR 11 of the #1166 epic. Track F (#1167), companion half — deliberately **before** the backend gate: gating the client first means Free riders lose the page while the endpoint stays open (invisible). The reverse order shows two broken cards on an otherwise-working page.

## The gate

`useFeature("advanced_analytics")`, failing **closed on `isSuccess`** and never on `isLoading` — a query that has not started yet (auth store unhydrated) reports neither loading nor error while being entirely unresolved, and reading that as entitled would open the page for the whole hydration window.

**Both** data effects are skipped while locked or unresolved. They are separate `useEffect`s — the ride paging (`fetchAllRides`, which walks the entire history 100 rows at a time) and an independent `fetchRideBreakdown` — and the second hits exactly the endpoint PR 12 gates. Gating only the first would have meant a **403 on every visit** by a Free rider.

Non-entitled riders keep `StatsPageHeader` and get a locked teaser, so the route never shows an unexplained gap — and never the generic "No rides recorded yet", which would blame the rider for a tier boundary.

## `LockedFeatureCard` had a silent hole

It hardcoded `capability={{ feature: "advanced_ride_stats" }}`. That is a **Pro-and-up** flag, so `upgradeTierForFeature` resolved no target for a Pro rider and the card rendered no CTA at all — the upsell this workstream exists to create, missing precisely for the tier most likely to buy. The capability is now a prop (defaulting to today's value, so existing call sites are untouched) and this page passes the Premium flag.

## D-2: this restricts real riders on merge

`advanced_analytics` is **not** among the nine keys seeded dark, so a genuinely Free rider (no `launch_tier` gift, no override) loses this page the moment the gate merges. #1104's go-live checklist stays at **nine** overrides. Recorded in `docs/feature-flags.md` §6.2 alongside the scope decision: the whole route is gated client-side because its inputs are the rider's own ride rows; only the per-segment aggregate is server-enforced, and `GET /rides/stats` stays open at every tier because it serves the Ride History KPI cards.

## Test evidence

Companion **2434 tests / 213 files** passing, typecheck and lint clean.

Eleven new tests — entitled renders, non-entitled locked, unresolved locked, live upgrade unlocks without a reload, neither request issued while locked **or** unresolved, and a Pro rider gets a real Premium CTA. Three mutation-checked: failing open on unresolved, gating only the ride paging, and restoring the hardcoded capability each fail tests.

The new `LockedFeatureCard` suite also pins the negative — a Pro rider under the DEFAULT capability still gets no CTA — so a later refactor cannot quietly reintroduce the hardcoded flag.

## Risk

Client-only. No contract, schema or migration impact. PR 12 adds the server-side gate on `stats/breakdown`.

author: raphaelgneiss
body:
Closes the `in` divergence recorded in `UPCOMING.md`, and narrows that note to what is genuinely still open.

## The bug

`in` was not the same operator on the two sides of one field vocabulary. `internal/policy` honoured a member that trimmed to nothing; `internal/macaroon.splitSet` has always dropped it.

The reachable spelling is a **trailing comma**, not the doubled one. The note recorded this as "a policy nobody has written", and that was the part worth rechecking: `"us,eu,"` is an ordinary typo and it put `""` into the approved set. Against allow-list posture, where a rule declares something ROUTINE and the default is approval-gated:

```
set="us,eu,"  region=""   -> approved-region  consequential=false
set="us,eu,"  region="cn" -> default          consequential=true
```

An action carrying an empty attribute was classified routine and skipped the approval gate that a genuinely unapproved region correctly triggers. A space-only member does the same.

## Consistent with a rule the schema already stated

`Condition.validate` refuses `in` with an empty value outright, so an empty member list is already meaningless. Honouring an empty member *inside* a list was the same concept accepted piecemeal, which is the shape #71 cleaned up for infinities (`1e400` refused while `Inf` was taken).

Nothing on the authority side moves: policy adopts what macaroon already did.

## Compatibility was checked, not assumed

Evaluation semantics reach the independent verifier, which re-derives decisions from the policy carried inside a signed export, so a change here can in principle make a recorded entry stop verifying.

Every `in` value in the repository was checked, including the one inside `testdata/audit_export_v2.golden.json` that a verifier re-derives. None contains an empty member. The change is observationally a no-op on every policy and every export that exists.

## The OPA backend needed the same fix, and that is the interesting part

Its `in` was written to mirror the classifier, and it mirrored it faithfully **while the classifier was wrong**. Both backends agreed, so the conformance suite stayed green throughout.

The infinity divergence in #71 was caught because Rego's `to_number` independently refused what the classifier accepted. There was no such accident here. A differential catches a divergence, and a bug reproduced on purpose is not one.

That limit is now recorded in `UPCOMING.md` beside the suite it qualifies, because the corollary matters for any future backend: translating the reference implementation's behaviour is precisely how to build a second implementation that cannot find anything.

## Watched failing, independently

- Removing the classifier's guard drops **5** conformance cases while the OPA module stays green.
- Removing the Rego guard drops **3** in the OPA module.

The first attempt at the second mutation reported zero failures because the edit had not applied. Worth stating, since it is the reason the mutation was verified rather than trusted.

The conformance cases carry a control asserting the members either side of a discarded one still match, so they cannot pass by `in` ceasing to match at all.

## What stays open

`UPCOMING.md` is updated rather than cleared:

- `==`, `!=` and `in` are still spelled twice. They agree now, but two copies that agree is the condition that produced both defects so far. Hoisting them wants a design decision, since `internal/scalar` is named and documented for ordering and membership does not belong under that name without rescoping.
- Whether a trailing comma should be **refused** rather than tolerated. That is the stricter reading and the riskier change: `Validate` is shared with `export.Parse`, so tightening it would make an old export carrying such a policy fail to parse wholesale rather than degrade one entry.

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - Board access is the operator control plane: board API keys authenticate a human operator to `/api` and are treated as full-control context
> - `board_api_keys` has no notion of scope, so every key minted for a user inherits that user's full company membership set with unrestricted read/write
> - That means a key handed to a CLI, a script, or a dashboard integration that only needs to read is indistinguishable from an admin credential, and there is no data model to express anything narrower
> - This pull request adds the storage and contract layer for scoped board keys: a `scope` column on `board_api_keys` (`read_only` | `all_access`), a backfill that pins every existing key to `all_access`, and the scope surfaced through the validator, service, and board actor
> - The benefit is that read-only key issuance and enforcement can be built on a stable, already-migrated column instead of shipping schema and enforcement in one risky step

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

No public GitHub issue exists for this, so the underlying bug is described inline following `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`.

**What happened?**

Every row in `board_api_keys` is unscoped. `actorMiddleware` resolves a board key to `resolveBoardAccess(userId)` and installs the creating operator's full membership list on `req.actor`, so any board key carries that operator's full read/write authority across all of their companies. There is no way to mint a key limited to reads, which is what CLI logins, status scripts, and third-party dashboards actually need, and nothing in the key row records the intended level of access.

**Expected behavior**

A board key should carry an explicit scope, and a `read_only` key should not be able to perform mutating operations. Keys that already exist must keep working exactly as they do today.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `POST /api/access/board-api-keys` with `{ "name": "readonly-dashboard" }`.
2. Send the returned token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to any mutating board endpoint (for example creating a project).
3. The write succeeds, and neither the stored key row nor `req.actor` records that the key was only ever meant to read.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduces on `fold/tea-patches-v2026.722.0` at `de08d94` (this PR's merge base).

**Deployment mode**

Not mode-specific: this is a core board-auth gap, reproducible on the embedded PGlite dev database and on Postgres, in the board (operator) access context. Not adapter-specific.

This PR is the schema and contract half of the fix. Enforcing `read_only` on mutating routes is a deliberate follow-up so the column can land and backfill on its own.

## What Changed

- `packages/db/src/schema/board_api_keys.ts`: new `scope` column, typed as `BoardApiKeyScope`, `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'all_access'`.
- `packages/db/src/migrations/0218_board_api_key_scope.sql`: idempotent migration that adds the column, backfills defensively, and adds a value check constraint.

```sql
ALTER TABLE "board_api_keys" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "scope" text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'all_access';--> statement-breakpoint
UPDATE "board_api_keys" SET "scope" = 'all_access' WHERE "scope" IS NULL;--> statement-breakpoint
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'board_api_keys_scope_check' AND conrelid = 'board_api_keys'::regclass) THEN
    ALTER TABLE "board_api_keys" ADD CONSTRAINT "board_api_keys_scope_check" CHECK ("scope" IN ('read_only', 'all_access'));
  END IF;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
```

- `packages/db/src/migrations/meta/_journal.json`: registers `0218` so the column is applied on startup.
- `packages/shared/src/constants.ts` + `index.ts`: `BOARD_API_KEY_SCOPES` and the `BoardApiKeyScope` type, so the column's `$type<>` and the migration's check constraint share one source of allowed values.
- `packages/db/src/board-api-key-scope-schema.test.ts`: asserts the column shape (`text`, `NOT NULL`, default `all_access`), that `0218` is journaled, that the migration backfills existing rows and constrains the allowed values, and that the constraint stays in sync with `BOARD_API_KEY_SCOPES`.

This PR is deliberately storage-and-type only. Threading `scope` through `createBoardApiKeySchema`, `server/src/services/board-auth.ts`, `server/src/routes/access.ts`, and the board actor on `req.actor`, plus enforcing `read_only` on mutating routes, is the follow-up that builds on this already-migrated column.

## Verification

- `pnpm -r typecheck`
- `pnpm test:run` — `packages/db/src/board-api-key-scope-schema.test.ts` covers the column shape, journal registration, and migration backfill/constraint; `packages/db/src/client.test.ts` applies every migration including `0218` against embedded Postgres.
- Manual: `rm -rf data/pglite && pnpm dev`, then inspect `board_api_keys`: the column exists and every row, including keys created before the migration, reads `all_access`.
- Re-running the migration is a no-op (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` plus a guarded `ADD CONSTRAINT`).

## Risks

- Migration safety: additive column with a non-volatile default and a check constraint. On Postgres 11+ this does not rewrite the table. The backfill `UPDATE` touches only `board_api_keys` and does not bump `updated_at`, so it stays within the repo's migration backfill gate.
- Behavior is unchanged by design: every existing and newly created key defaults to `all_access`. `read_only` is storable but not yet enforced, so callers must not assume a `read_only` key is actually restricted until the enforcement follow-up lands. That is the main sharp edge in this PR.
- Rollback drops a column, which is safe while no server code reads it yet, but must be sequenced ahead of the enforcement follow-up.
- The check constraint means adding a future scope value requires a migration, not just a constants change.

> For core feature work, check [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) first and discuss it in `#dev` before opening the PR. Feature PRs that overlap with planned core work may need to be redirected — check the roadmap first. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Model Used

Claude (Anthropic) via [code]smith, `claude-sonnet-4-5` with extended thinking, 200K context, agentic tool use and code execution in a sandboxed workspace. The change was authored and reviewed with that tooling; the branch was reduced to a schema-only change after an earlier stale-workspace commit reverted unrelated upstream work, then rebased onto the current `fold/tea-patches-v2026.722.0` head so the merge base is fresh.

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have checked ROADMAP.md and confirmed this PR does not duplicate planned core work
- [x] I have searched GitHub for duplicate or related PRs and linked them above — searched the PR list for `board_api_keys scope` and `board api key read_only`; no duplicates or related open PRs.
- [x] I have either (a) linked existing issues with `Fixes: #` / `Closes #` / `Refs #` OR (b) described the issue in-PR following the relevant issue template
- [x] I have not referenced internal/instance-local Paperclip issues or links (only public GitHub `#NNN` / `github.com/paperclipai/paperclip` URLs)
- [ ] My branch name describes the change (e.g. `docs/...`, `fix/...`) and contains no internal Paperclip ticket id or instance-derived details — the branch name predates this PR and carries an internal ticket id; renaming it now would close this PR, so it is left as-is.
- [ ] I have run tests locally and they pass — the workspace has no installed dependencies, so `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm test:run` were not run locally; CI is the source of truth for this head.
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable

body:
## What Implements T5 from the native iOS plan: a cache-first `DepthRepository` decorator backed by SwiftData, the `app_config` update-gate data path, and the two new repository reads T6 needs (`teams()`, `appConfig()`). - `CachedSnapshotStore` — a `@ModelActor` over SwiftData: per-team `TeamSnapshot` JSON payload rows (capped at 32, oldest evicted first), a typed 32-row team-list cache (for local search without decoding blobs), and a singleton `app_config` cache row. Every row carries a `schemaVersion`; a mismatch (or a payload that fails to decode against this build's Domain structs) is treated as a cache miss and the row is discarded — "safe schema discard." - `CachingDepthRepository` — actor decorator over `DepthRepository`: `teams()`/`teamSnapshot()` are cache-first (return the cached value immediately, refresh in the background, deduplicated per-key so concurrent calls don't double-fetch, and a failed background refresh never clears the existing cached row). `appConfig()` is network-first with cache fallback — a stale cached minimum-build value would defeat the point of the gate. - Extended `DepthRepository`/`SupabaseDepthRepository` with `teams()` (flat 32-team projection, no nested joins — T6's team selector) and `appConfig()` (new `app_config` table). `teamSnapshot()` itself is untouched. - `Player` gains `name`/`photoUrl` (dropped by the T4 mapper on purpose, pending a real consumer) and `TeamSnapshot` gains `Codable` so the cache can persist it as one JSON payload. - New migration `20260814120000_add_app_config.sql`: public-read `app_config` singleton, RLS + explicit grants (a raw CLI migration doesn't auto-grant table privileges the way the hosted dashboard does — same pattern as `20260701171029_grant_default_table_privileges.sql`). `lib/database.types.ts` regenerated. ## Spec drift None — this is new, additive surface on top of the shipped T4 seam, not a change to it. ## Why Cache-first rendering, background refresh, and an update gate are locked decisions in the design spec (`../obsidian/Projects/depth/specs/2026-08-14-native-ios-app-design.md`, decisions #7-9) that T6's UI depends on directly. ## Tests - `xcodebuild -scheme Depth test` (DepthTests only, App/Features untouched by this PR — placeholder `ContentView` still in place): 34/34 pass, including 9 new `CachingDepthRepositoryTests` (cache hit/miss, dedup, retained-last-good-on-failed-refresh, schema-version discard, app_config network-first/cache-fallback/no-cache-throws) and 3 new local-Supabase RLS tests (`anonymousCanReadTeamList`, `anonymousCanReadAppConfig`, `anonymousWriteToAppConfigIsDenied`). - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run format:check` clean. - `supabase db reset --local` + `npm run db:types` — migration applies cleanly, types regenerate with only the expected `app_config` addition. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

Adds the native iOS cache-first repository layer, SwiftData persistence, team-list and update-gate reads, supporting domain mappings, and a public-read app_config migration. - Introduces cache-first team reads with deduplicated background refreshes and network-first app configuration fallback. - Adds version-aware SwiftData models and repository cache metadata accessors. - Extends Supabase projections, generated database types, RLS coverage, and cache behavior tests.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with non-blocking cache-evolution gaps around store recovery, app-config versioning, and snapshot metadata validation. The new repository and database paths are coherent, but the disposable cache can become unrecoverable at container initialization and two cache APIs do not consistently apply the stated safe-schema-discard contract. **Files Needing Attention:** ios/Depth/Support/DepthEnvironment.swift, ios/Depth/Data/CachedSnapshotModels.swift, ios/Depth/Data/CachedSnapshotStore.swift

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | ios/Depth/Data/CachedSnapshotModels.swift | Adds SwiftData cache entities, but CachedAppConfig omits the schema version promised for every persisted row. | | ios/Depth/Data/CachedSnapshotStore.swift | Implements isolated cache persistence and eviction; snapshot age metadata bypasses snapshot compatibility validation. | | ios/Depth/Data/CachingDepthRepository.swift | Implements cache-first reads, per-key refresh deduplication, and network-first app-config fallback. | | ios/Depth/Data/SupabaseDepthRepository.swift | Adds explicit lightweight team-list and singleton app-config projections with typed error mapping. | | ios/Depth/Support/DepthEnvironment.swift | Wires the persistent cache decorator but treats all disposable cache-container initialization failures as fatal. | | supabase/migrations/20260814120000_add_app_config.sql | Adds a constrained singleton app_config table with explicit read grants, RLS, and service-role write privileges. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as iOS Feature participant CacheRepo as CachingDepthRepository participant Store as CachedSnapshotStore participant API as SupabaseDepthRepository UI->>CacheRepo: teamSnapshot(teamId) CacheRepo->>Store: teamSnapshot(teamId) alt valid cache hit Store-->>CacheRepo: cached snapshot CacheRepo-->>UI: cached snapshot CacheRepo->>API: background refresh API-->>CacheRepo: fresh snapshot CacheRepo->>Store: save fresh snapshot else cache miss Store-->>CacheRepo: nil CacheRepo->>API: fetch snapshot API-->>CacheRepo: snapshot CacheRepo->>Store: persist snapshot CacheRepo-->>UI: snapshot end UI->>CacheRepo: appConfig() CacheRepo->>API: network-first fetch alt network succeeds API-->>CacheRepo: current config CacheRepo->>Store: cache config else network fails CacheRepo->>Store: cached config fallback end ```
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["feat(ios): SwiftData cache layer, update..."](https://github.com/cwharris77/depth/commit/48de5748b1aef9259ef93d4d169bcd60e962615a) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=53562335) > Greptile also left **3 inline comments** on this PR.

author: cjohnhanson
body:
Two findings from the second cold review.

1. **A dependency pinned at a second revision was silently discarded.** The closure keyed a git member on the URL alone, so the first pin answered for both and a document that exists only at the other pin read as a broken link. Members are now keyed by URL and resolved revision. The bare clone cache stays keyed by URL, so one fetch still serves both.
2. **`addr_is_loopback` and `origin_is_local`.** All three servers need the same two answers before they accept a request: does this bind address reach only this machine, and does this browser origin belong to it. The consumers wire them into their HTTP layer next.

142 unit tests, clippy clean.

author: picatz
body:
## The finding

The `comms-review` skill already said the GitHub API budget was bounded and to be careful with it. It never said the budget is **readable**, and that omission cost a session most of a working queue.

```console
$ curl -sS https://api.github.com/rate_limit
```

One call, counts against nothing. Run during an exhaustion that had merges on hold:

| pool | used | limit | remaining |
|---|---|---|---|
| core (REST) | 13 | 15,000/hr | 14,987 |
| graphql | **10,039** | 5,000/hr | **0** |

The session had stopped merging because "the API is exhausted" with 14,987 REST calls untouched — a 500× misestimate of what was left, from guessing at a bounded resource instead of looking at it. That is the same failure `CLAUDE.md` writes about everywhere else: ask which resource is actually scarce, then bound *that* one.

## What follows from measuring

**The pools are not comparable in kind.** REST is metered in calls. GraphQL is metered in *points* by query complexity, so a thread listing with nested connections costs many points per call — which is how a few dozen reads went 2× over a 5,000-point budget while REST barely moved.

**Almost nothing in the review loop needs GraphQL.** Verified against the live API during the same session:

| operation | endpoint | pool |
|---|---|---|
| read review comments | `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/comments` | REST |
| react to a finding | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/comments/{id}/reactions` | REST |
| reply on a thread | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/comments/{id}/replies` | REST |
| resolve a thread | `resolveReviewThread` mutation | **GraphQL** |
| read `isResolved` | `reviewThreads` connection | **GraphQL** |

So the scarce pool gets spent on resolve mutations at roughly a point each — hundreds per hour, far more than any review wave needs — and the loop stops being blocked by the pool it was barely using.

## One honest limit, recorded rather than smoothed over

Direct `curl` through the proxy does real work without moving the `core` counter `rate_limit` reports (five calls left `core.used` at 13). The two are not the same meter. The skill says to treat `remaining` as a floor on what is left, not a gauge to plan against, rather than asserting a tidier model than the evidence supports.

## Scope

Documentation only — `.claude/skills/comms-review/SKILL.md`. No code, no schema, no CI change.

## Verification

`go run ./tools/gate` — PASS (1 leg run, 8 skipped; no Go packages affected).

author: saidai-bhuvanesh
body:
_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of @saidai-bhuvanesh._

## What
Fixes #376 — `PUT /api/user/avatar` returned HTTP 500 for malformed (non-JSON) request bodies.

## Root cause
`app/api/user/avatar/route.ts` destructured `avatarId` directly from `await req.json()` inside the outer `try` block. A request with invalid JSON syntax threw during parsing and fell through to the generic `catch`, which returns `500` with the raw error message. Invalid request syntax should produce a predictable `400`, not a `500`.

## Fix
Wrap `req.json()` in its own `try/catch` that returns `{ error: 'Invalid JSON payload' }` with status `400`, then validate `avatarId` against the parsed body. This mirrors the exact pattern already used in `app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` and `app/api/user/score/route.ts`.

## Verification
- `isAvatarId` already accepts `unknown` (`value is AvatarId` type guard), so destructuring as `{ avatarId?: unknown }` is type-safe.
- The change is consistent with sibling auth/score routes that already handle malformed JSON with a 400.
- No new dependencies; node_modules not installed in this environment (would run husky lifecycle hooks), so CI/lint will run on the PR.

author: 0pcom
body:
## What

Two machine-output post-processors on the skywire CLI, plus a fix so the existing `--json` and `--help --json` work on the **top-level `skywire` binary** — not only under `skywire cli …`.

- **`--jq <filter>`** — run the JSON value through **gojq** (already vendored) before printing. Implies `--json`.
  ```
  skywire cli visor info --jq '.ar_registration.entries[].type'
  skywire --help --json --jq '.subcommands[].name'
  ```
- **`--shape`** — print the output type's **skeleton** (every field at its zero value, `omitempty` forced visible) instead of live data, so a command's schema is discoverable without a populated response.
- **Top-level parity** — `skywire tree --json`, `skywire --json`, `skywire --help --json` (the full machine-readable command tree) all previously failed with `unknown flag: --json`. Now they work.

## Why / how

The output flags, the jq/shape logic, and the `--help --json` hook lived only on the `cmd/skywire-cli/commands` root, so the combined `skywire` binary (`cmd/skywire/commands`) — a *separate* root that mounts the cli subtree as `cli` — never had them on its own top-level commands.

Moved the reusable pieces into the canonical **`pkg/cliout`** package:
- `RegisterOutputFlags(cmd)` — adds `--json`/`--jq`/`--shape` persistent flags.
- `SetJSONHelp(cmd)` — installs the `--help --json` machine-description hook (`clihelp.Of`).
- `ApplyJQ` / `Skeleton` — the jq filter and reflection skeleton, now honored by `cliout.Print` (25 callers) **and** delegated to by the legacy `cliutil.PrintOutput` (67 callers), so both behave identically.

Both roots (`cmd/skywire` and `cmd/skywire-cli`) call the shared setup.

## Notes

- `--json` stays a **bool** (unchanged) — no invocation breaks; `--jq` is a separate string flag that implies JSON.
- `--shape` reflects over the output type: struct field order preserved, custom `json.Marshaler` types (`cipher.PubKey`, `time.Time`, `uuid`) render as their zero marshaled form, recursion cycle-guarded. CLI is native-only (never TinyGo), so reflect is fine.
- Validated live: `skywire tree --json`, `skywire --help --json`, `--shape`, `--jq`, and plain `--json` all work; `cliout` tests + gofmt green.

author: zaneham
body:
Hiya,

Third one of these, after #15002 and #15005. The power backend doesn't recognise any `Cextcall` idioms either, so `sqrt` goes out to C where amd64 and arm64 emit an instruction. This makes it emit `fsqrt`.

No feature gating needed. `asmcomp/power/NOTES.md` gives the supported platform as 64-bit little-endian POWER, ELF ABI v2, and `fsqrt` is in the base Power ISA for everything that covers.

The byte swaps don't come across, same as on riscv, so this is sqrt only.

Tested on a real ppc64le machine, cfarm120, where it builds `world.opt` and the test programs give the right answers for both zeros, infinities, NaN, negative input, max, min normal, a denormal and a thousand exact squares. Only little-endian is tested because the port dropped big-endian, so cfarm121 doesn't apply.

Kind regards,
Zane

author: massimoseq3
body:
Clicking a swipe opened its permalink in a new tab, which made the swipe file a bookmarks folder — you filed the ad to tear it down later, and "later" meant leaving the app.

A swipe now opens **the same detail view Outliers does**, Analyze Ad and Remix Transcript included.

## How

`SwipeDetail` adapts the saved row back into a `DiscoverResult` and renders the **one** `ResultDetailModal` rather than a second copy that would drift within a release. The modal gains three optional props — `onSave` omitted drops the Save button (a filed row has nothing left to save), and `onMediaError` + `mediaOverlay` are how the Bank reports an expired link. Outliers passes none of them, so its behaviour is unchanged by construction.

This is a deliberate cross-app import (Bank → Outliers), taken against the self-contained-apps rule because the alternative is duplicating a 340-line modal. Reasoning is recorded in the finder CLAUDE.md.

## The video

The one thing a swipe doesn't keep. `mediaUrl` is a signed CDN link with hours (TikTok) or days (Meta) on it, so:

- A dead link is **dropped** rather than re-rendered — a failed `<video>` keeps its transport controls and reads as something you could press.
- The member gets **Restore video — 1 credit**. `refreshResultMedia` re-resolves through `/v2/tiktok/video` or `/v1/facebook/adLibrary/ad` and writes the new link back to the row, so a second visit inside its lifetime is free.
- Analyze greys until then — the same credits-on-a-button-you-pressed contract the transcript already has. `downloadWithRefresh` covers only the case where a link looks alive and 403s at fetch time.

Two rules worth keeping: a refresh re-resolves **media only, never the stats** (the snapshotted numbers are what make this a swipe file rather than a bookmark), and a transcript bought here is written back to the row, so it's paid for once rather than once a visit.

## Vendor notes

TikTok's detail endpoint is sent **both** `video_id` and `url` — its doc page and its own search snippet disagree on which it takes, the same self-contradicting-docs hazard that once made every TikTok search return nothing. Meta's returns an identical `snapshot` to the search endpoint, so `pickCreativeUrl` is reused unchanged.

## Verification

Both platforms open correctly (Meta gets no stats grid, no Transcript block, no Remix). Dead-link and never-had-a-link states both render; the no-API-key path toasts rather than failing silently; Escape closes; the card's star/copy/delete stack still doesn't trigger the modal. `tsc` clean, no new lint problems.

Tested by hand-injecting swipe rows — the Settings demo seeder has no `swipes` coverage at all, which is filed separately.

body:
## 变更摘要

修复 #1348：runtime-roots / config / retry 三层 allowed-roots 判据仍以"非 strict `Path.resolve()` 遇 symlink 环会抛"（CPython 3.13+ 已不成立，GH-113838）为前提——3.13+ 上环路 root 被静默收作 approved containment base（phantom root，同 #1332/#1344/#1345 fail-open 族），且 PR #1346 之后同一次运行的 slurm preflight 与 runtime-root preflight 证据面对同一环根给出相反裁决；≤3.12 上站点 1 裸 `raise` 逃逸 RuntimeError、站点 3 rejection lane 两端死码。

三站点统一 #1346 范式（`os.path.realpath(strict=True)` + `except OSError` + errno 分流，两种 `Path.resolve()` 形态禁用）：

- **站点 1** `_scheduler_allowed_roots`（scheduler_runtime_roots.py）：改配对函数 `_scheduler_allowed_roots_and_blockers`，旧名保留为 `[0]` 读取面；ENOENT → 非 strict realpath 保留 admitted 语义；其余 errno：db-free 走 #831 词法容忍臂，数据库态剔根 + `SCHEDULER_ROOT_ALLOWED_ROOTS_<REASON>` 结构化 blocker（掩码纪律沿用 evidence_safe_paths）；`:457` 裸 raise 删除。两条 preflight 臂解包、unsafe blocker 先于 policy MISSING。facade（FORWARDER_NAMES/赋值/EXPORTS）+ `SCHEDULER_COMPATIBILITY_INVENTORY.md` 登记。
- **站点 2** `_db_free_allowed_roots`（scheduler_config.py）：同配对形态。fixture 评审 round-2 纠正了"db-free 专用"的错误前提——数据库态 `repair_missing_forcing` 运行同样走 `db_free_runtime_preflight` 的真实 containment 判定，该 lane 环根现剔除 + `db_free_allowed_root_unsafe` blocker；db-free 词法臂逐字保留（#831）。
- **站点 3** retry.py db-free selector allowed-roots lane：`db_free_allowed_root_unresolvable` rejection 死码复活（≤3.12 被 RuntimeError 穿过、3.13+ 永不触发 → 现两端真实可达）。
- **D6** `require_runtime_roots=False`（db-backed 默认态）显式裁定：not_required payload 共享裁决产物，环根剔出展示列表、无 blocker（该 payload 无 blocker 通道且不做 containment 判定）、永不抛；blocker 责任面留在独立运行的 slurm storage preflight。#1346 留下的 **B8 tripwire 按其自身 docstring 契约翻转**为结构化断言（移除 `skipif(>=3.13)`）。
- **主锚点**：双证据面一致性回归测试——同 config 同环根，一个进程内实调 `_slurm_preflight` 与两条 runtime-root preflight 臂，断言两个 `allowed_roots` 证据面同为丢根 + 各自 blocker。

行为变更披露：EACCES/EPERM（不可 traverse 祖先）根从"全版本静默放行"收紧为数据库态剔根 + `..._NOT_WRITABLE` / selector rejection——判据是 "not ENOENT"，收紧作用于生产解释器 3.11/3.12。

OpenSpec change: `runtime-allowed-roots-errno-split`（expanded/high；两轮 fixture 评审的修复已并入 fixture 本体）。

## 偏离记录

1. 站点 1/2 单元 seam 判决表用冻结 `_AllowedRootsConfigStub`（3 属性 + `db_free_required` property）而非真实 `ProductionSchedulerConfig`——#1347/PR #1349 后配置构造期就把 `<missing>/../<loop>` 折叠成裸环、把词法形折叠成规范形，两行在 3.13+ 经真实 config 不可达。磁盘故障形状全真实、不 mock 任何解析原语；stub 漂移风险由真实 config 的 preflight 臂/双平面/repair lane 锚点端到端兜底。
2. EACCES/EPERM 无专属测试（design 明示授权：容器 root 用户绕过 chmod，不可移植构造），由 ENOTDIR 行代表 "not ENOENT" 判据 + proposal 具名披露。
3. 双平面主锚点实调 `_slurm_preflight`（非仅 `_preflight_allowed_roots`），比较两个真实证据字段——fixture 允许两者取一，取了更强的。
4. fixture 评审 round-2 的 P1（站点 2 "db-free 专用"错误前提）在 fixture 层修复后实现，见变更摘要站点 2。
5. Round-1 评审修复（e6f1fc91）：EC-1——preflight payload 曾二次裁决 allowed roots（fs race 下证据面可自相矛盾），改为 `_scheduler_root_preflight_payload` 新增 keyword-only `allowed_roots` 参数、两臂线程化裁决 #1 产物，payload 与 blocker 出自同一次裁决（计数测试钉住）；FT-2——站点 2/3 ENOENT 测试原用已规范路径（词法直通突变全绿存活），换判别形 `<missing>/../<realdir>` + canonical≠lexical 守卫断言；FT-1/EC-2 为 fixture 措辞修正（`<missing>/../<loop>` 行限定 seam 输入面、"storage preflight 承担 blocker" 限定 slurm-enabled）；HY-2（每根一 blocker 不去重）经裁决按 #1346 族形状保留，全族统一去重记入 known-limits。

## 测试证据

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_production_scheduler.py` → **1253 passed, 0 skipped**（基线 1224 passed + 1 skipped；+27 新测试、tripwire 翻转后不再 skip）
- `-k "preflight or allowed_root"` → **160 passed**（基线 131 passed + 1 skipped，issue 撰写时 122 条口径含收集差异）
- 兄弟套件：retry/retry_cancel/backfill/timing/orchestrator 5 文件 172 passed
- `uv run ruff check .` → clean；`openspec validate runtime-allowed-roots-errno-split --strict` → valid
- 红证：只 stash 四个源文件后 `-k` 集 **28 failed / 132 passed**——27 条新测试 + 翻转后的 tripwire 全红、零既有回归；`git stash list` 空（两次核验）。红证强度注记：两条 ENOENT 行修前红仅因配对符号不存在（ENOENT 行为设计上前后一致）；站点 3 死码以行为断言证明（环根被纳入 → `assert roots == ()` 红）。
- Round-1 修复后复验（e6f1fc91）：全文件 **1255 passed**（+2 计数测试）；红证——站点 2/3 ENOENT 臂改词法直通突变 → **3 failed**；payload 线程化回退（恢复二次裁决）→ 计数测试 **2 failed**。

## Evidence Floor 覆盖声明

Issue #1348 验收标准 7 条全覆盖：AC1 站点 1 范式 + 全文件零 allowed-roots 用途 resolve ✓ / AC2 双证据面一致性主锚点（显式 `require_runtime_roots=True`）✓ / AC3 数据库态结构化 blocker（SCHEDULER_ROOT_ 家族）替代裸 raise，not_required 态由 D6 裁定 + tripwire 翻转覆盖 ✓ / AC4 站点 2 同范式、#831 两路径既有行为保持 ✓ / AC5 站点 3 rejection 真实触发（红证）✓ / AC6 版本不敏感（真实故障形状 + errno 断言）+ `<missing>/../<loop>` 组合 ✓ / AC7 `_optional_config_path` 零触碰 ✓

## 已知限制与后续路由

- 运维提示：本 PR 使 EACCES/EPERM 祖先根在生产解释器（3.11/3.12）上从静默放行收紧为剔根 + blocker；上线前建议对生产 `NHMS_SCHEDULER_ALLOWED_ROOTS` 各条目做一次 strict-resolve 体检，避免既有配置踩中收紧面。
- `SCHEDULER_ROOT_ALLOWED_ROOTS_UNAVAILABLE` 臂（else errno 兜底）无专属测试；可移植构造方式为 ENAMETOOLONG，未纳入本 PR 范围。
- 每根重复 blocker 不去重为 #1346 族既有形状（HY-2 裁决 DISCARD）；如需去重应全族统一落地，暂记为 cosmetic note，不立 issue。
- 家族后续已立项：#1400（path-level twin 全量清查）、#1401（`_local_runtime_root_safety`）、#1402（`_local_artifact_allowed_roots` 第 5 站点）。

author: sdubois777
body:
## What this adds

`game/Data/MinionTypes.csv`, a new generated table holding one stat block per
minion type, and the sheet, generator, row struct and DataTable asset behind it.
Two rows: the Imp and the Mote.

Issue #209 reversed the rule that minions have no stats of their own, and
`docs/Cataclysm_GDD_v2.md` line 1588 now reads "Every minion type has its own
stats. A minion is not a percentage of its summoner." No such table existed.
Partly answers #336.

## Why a table rather than numbers on each skill

- **Two skills produce the same creature.** Summon Imp and Open the Rift both
  make a lesser imp, so numbers held in each skill's `ShapeParams` column would
  exist twice and drift apart.
- **One skill produces two creatures.** Iron Fortress deploys ballistae and spike
  traps, which a flat list of key-and-value pairs cannot express at all.

A skill decides how many, how often and how long. The type decides what the thing
is.

## Two rows, not five

The vertical slice is Demonic, so only two minion types are designed:

| Minion type | Produced by | Weapon |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Imp | Summon Imp (Special), Open the Rift (Ultimate) | Staff |
| Mote | Cinder Swarm (Special) | Wand |

The bolt turret, ballista and spike trap are War skills on Crossbow and Spear and
are deliberately absent.

## The numbers

| | Imp | Mote |
| :-- | --: | --: |
| Base health, per level | 200, 90 | 100, 45 |
| Base damage, per level | 10, 10.0 | 5, 4.5 |
| Attack interval | 1.0s | 0.8s |
| Move speed | 4.4 m/s | 5.5 m/s |
| Threat | 100% | 40% |
| Reach, notice radius | 200cm, 1500cm | 350cm, 1000cm |
| Target mode | Nearest | Nearest |
| Scaling attribute | spirit | spirit |
| Most active at once | 3 | 4 |

Three decisions from the project owner on 2026-08-15 drove them:

1. A mote is a **weaker body in larger numbers**.
2. The two produce **different total output**. Left to me, and set so four motes
   deal about three quarters of what three imps deal. The swarm is paid back by
   the burst each mote leaves when it expires.
3. **Three permanent imps out-damage the summoner's own basic attack.** This
   reverses the floor #336 proposed, which was the opposite.

Damage was set from the top down: a Staff character's basic attack deals 2,652 a
second at difficulty tier 8, so three imps were sized at 1.15x that. Summon Imp
holds 3 imps for 20 seconds against a 5 second cooldown, so three are permanent
in normal play.

## The mid-game bulge, recorded rather than hidden

Three imps are worth **1.14x** the basic attack at difficulty tier 8 and about
**2.0x** at tiers 2 and 3.

That cannot be removed while the storage shape stays as it is. A minion's damage
rises with the summoner's **level alone**; the summoner's own damage rises with
level *and* affix tier *and* gear upgrade level. The player's output climbs about
twelve times from level 12 to level 100 where a linear-in-level minion climbs at
most eight, so a straight line cannot track it.

It is also not purely an artefact: a minion falling behind a geared summoner is
the shape the design asks for, and closing that gap is what minion affixes (#337)
and points in Spirit are for. An uninvested summoner is therefore not the balance
case. `docs/DECISIONS.md` states this, and
`test_a_minion_falls_behind_a_geared_summoner_rather_than_keeping_pace` records
it as a property rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

## Also in here

**The missing `Keyword.Summon` tag on Open the Rift.** Summon Imp and Cinder
Swarm both carry it; Open the Rift did not, so anything searching for summon
skills by that keyword missed it. One line in the design workbook, one line in
`game/Data/WeaponSkills.csv`. The gameplay tag count is unchanged at 175 because
the tag already existed.

## The plumbing

A new generated table touches more than its own file. All of it is in here:

| File | What changed |
| :-- | :-- |
| `docs/All_Things_Cataclysm.xlsx` | New "Minion Types" sheet, plus the tag on Open the Rift |
| `tools/generate_datatables.py` | A `minion_types` reader and a `TABLES` entry |
| `tools/generate_datatable_assets.py` | An entry so the DataTable asset gets built |
| `game/Source/Cataclysm/Data/CataclysmDataRows.h` | The `FCataclysmMinionTypeRow` row struct |
| `game/Source/Cataclysm/Tests/CataclysmDataTableTests.cpp` | A `CHECK_TABLE` line pinning the row count at 2 |
| `game/Content/Data/DT_MinionTypes.uasset` | The imported DataTable asset |
| `docs/README.md`, `game/README.md` | Sheet and table counts, 17 to 18 |

The generator refuses a row whose family and scaling attribute disagree with
#335, an unknown target mode, an attack interval of zero and a minion with no
health.

## What is deliberately not here

`docs/Cataclysm_GDD_v2.md` says the attribute rows granting increased minion
damage per point land with #336. They are not in this change. Adding them means
adding `minion_damage` to the character sheet in
`sim/cataclysm_sim/character.py`, which touches the stat groups, the default stat
line and the gameplay tags, and is a larger change than a stat block table. **#336
stays open for it.**

## Evidence

```
python -m pytest                                2369 passed, 1 skipped   (2353 baseline)
python -m ruff check .                          All checks passed!
python tools/generate_datatables.py --check     All 18 DataTable CSVs are up to date.
python tools/generate_gameplay_tags.py --check  CataclysmTags.ini is up to date (175 tags)
python tools/unreal_build.py tests --prefix Cataclysm.Data
                                                7 tests performed, 7 succeeded, 0 failed
```

The C++ tests were run by hand with the Unreal editor closed, since continuous
integration compiles no C++.

Four guards proved with `tools/prove_guard.py`, no run disturbed:

| Break | Test that caught it |
| :-- | :-- |
| The imp is weakened until three lose to the basic attack | `test_three_imps_out_damage_the_summoners_own_basic_attack_at_every_tier` |
| The mote is raised until a swarm beats the imp squad | `test_a_full_swarm_of_motes_deals_less_than_a_full_squad_of_imps` |
| A creature is set to scale from agility | `test_a_creature_scales_from_spirit` |
| The imp is made tough enough to ignore | `test_a_minion_is_fragile_enough_to_be_worth_killing` |

author: izakfilmalter
body:
Mission control's design system lived inside `apps/web`, so the desktop shell and the upcoming chat app had no way to reuse the primitives, Tailwind theme, or layout components without copying them.

This moves the shadcn primitives, the Tailwind theme, and their supporting helpers into `packages/ui`.

## Layout

I scaffolded a real `create-better-t-stack` monorepo first rather than guessing at its conventions. Its `packages/ui` is source-only (no build step), exports subpath patterns, owns `globals.css`, and ships its own `components.json` so shadcn installs land in the package. The app keeps `src/components/` for app-specific pieces. This mirrors that:

```
packages/ui/
  package.json        exports ./globals.css, ./lib/*, ./components/*, ./hooks/*, ./postcss.config
  components.json     aliases ui/utils/hooks -> @laborer/ui/*
  postcss.config.mjs  for non-Vite consumers
  src/components/     58 primitives + reui/kanban.tsx
  src/hooks/          use-mobile.ts
  src/lib/            utils.ts (cn), haptics.ts
  src/styles/         globals.css  (was apps/web/src/index.css)
```

`apps/web/src/index.css` is now a single `@import "@laborer/ui/globals.css";`, matching the BTS default.

## Judgment calls worth reviewing

**Only the primitives move.** The 40 root-level components (`workspace-card`, `terminal-list`, `kanban/`) import `@/atoms/laborer-client`, `@/panels/panel-context`, and `@laborer/shared/rpc`. Hoisting them would drag Laborer's RPC and atom layers into a package the chat app is meant to consume — and a chat app would never want `workspace-card`. BTS draws the same line by default. The shared surface is the primitives, the theme, and the layout components (`sidebar`, `resizable`, `tab-bar`).

**`panel-type-picker` moved back into the app.** It was sitting in `ui/`, but it imports `PaneType` from `@laborer/shared/types` and hardcodes Terminal/Agent/Server options. That is domain, not a primitive, and it was the one thing preventing the package from typechecking standalone.

**`lib/utils.ts` had to be split.** `cn` belongs in the package, but `extractErrorMessage`/`extractErrorCode` read `@/atoms/renderer-connection`, so they stay in the app as `@/lib/errors`.

## Verification

- `packages/ui` typechecks standalone under `types: []`, so no app types leak in
- 1227 web tests pass; repo-wide `typecheck` and `format` are clean
- Production build succeeds

Tailwind's content detection is rooted at `globals.css` and would otherwise only see `packages/ui`, so the stylesheet declares consuming apps explicitly. I checked this against real output rather than assuming: `text-[10px]`, used only in app components, survives into the emitted CSS, and removing the glob shrinks the bundle by 4K. So it covers files Vite's module graph misses and will matter for a PostCSS-based consumer.

Note: `@laborer/server`'s `daemon-rpc` test fails on this branch, but I confirmed via `git stash` that it fails identically on a clean tree. Pre-existing and unrelated.

Desktop is main-process only today (it loads web over a URL), so it gains nothing yet. The payoff is the chat app, which can now depend on `@laborer/ui` and inherit the theme.

## What changed

- add the public `@dsh-1024store/cli` wrapper around the official DeepSeek Harness CLI while preserving all passthrough arguments
- record privacy-preserving installation events, timestamps, per-client state, hourly rollups, unique clients, and retryable local telemetry
- add install rankings and package-level activity to the DSH 1024Store UI
- add the strictly validated `POST /api/v1/install-events` API and read APIs on the existing `CATALOG_DB`
- add additive D1 migration `0003_installation_events.sql`
- integrate the latest dynamic D1 catalog and repair URL-canonical repository identities

## Why

DSH 1024Store needs verifiable install counts that do not depend on GitHub stars. The wrapper delegates to the official CLI without a shell and never uploads command arguments, output, paths, usernames, environment variables, or raw errors.

## Data safety

The migration only creates new tables, indexes, and triggers. It does not alter, update, or delete existing catalog or star-history data. Client UUIDs are HMACed before storage.

body:
**Closes** #1138 · **Files** #1199 · **Seal:** cannot move.

### The two-valued exit forced a lie

Three probes print a word that is neither pass nor fail — `BIRTH_INPUTS_NONE`, `NO_FIRING`, `NO_LIBERATIONS`. Zero says the contract **held**, which it did not — it was never tested. One says it **broke**, which it did not either.

The tree had already settled this one directory over: `DreamReader` has five codes because #1011 needed *"nobody by that name"* told apart from *"you typed the flag wrong"*, and #1112 refused a zero-tick day because **a day that never happened must not exit 0**. A probe whose scenario never arose *is* that day.

```
Probes.leave(verdict, held, exercised)   0 held · 1 broken · 2 never arose
```

### The bench reads the third as `UNEXERCISED`

Counted, printed, in the summary line. Not a pass — a row that reaches no miracle must not stand in for one that does — and not a failure, because nothing broke. #970's `INSTRUMENTS_UNPROVEN` argument in the other axis.

### Two of three

`BirthInputs` prints its word from **two** places, one of them `no_file` — a missing input, arguably a refusal and arguably a different code again. Guessing at that inside a unit about not guessing would be the wrong shape. Filed as #1199.

### Evidence

```
ClauseAftermath 500 42    → VERDICT NO_FIRING, exit 2      (the third code, reached)
ClauseAftermath 40000 42  → VERDICT AFTERMATH_ACCOUNTED, exit 0
SameTick 6000 42 / 6000 7 → VERDICT SAME_TICK_ABSORB, exit 0

bench.sh --no-build → probes=55 judged=48 pass=48 fail=0 unexercised=0
                      secs=123 budget=300 WITHIN · BENCH_GREEN
```

`unexercised=0` today — the field exists so that a row which *stops* being exercised is a number rather than a silence.

author: brownbobasushi
body:
## Summary
- Wires the S3 mechanism locked in `AGENTPAY — SPR-001-DEMO-STORE-X402-MERCHANT-SPEC`: the "Weekly Grocery Bundle" ($28.00, already in the catalog since PR 1) passes AgentPay's own 5-30 SGD Mint Gate range check, so a decline can only happen if the sandbox wallet is under-funded at settlement — a StraitsX-side (rail) failure, not an AgentPay refusal. This matches SIG-018's block-attribution principle: AgentPay blocks what the user never confirmed; StraitsX blocks what the user never allowed.
- New `src/lib/store/classify_execution.ts`: a pure classifier that reads an `execute_purchase` result and sorts it into `settled` / `block_receipt` (AgentPay's own refusal — always carries a Block Receipt id) / `rail_failed` (StraitsX declined settlement — no receipt exists at all).
- **Caught a real bug writing the unit test for that classifier**: the receipt-id regex from PR 3 didn't match the success path's `"receipt: rcpt_..."` (colon) against `"Block Receipt rcpt_..."` (no colon) — fixed. Settled orders were silently misclassifying before this.
- `src/lib/store/orders.ts`: `StoreOrder` gains a `rail_failed` status + `detail` field.
- The order-status route now persists `rail_failed` terminally on first occurrence. This matters because a rail failure after payment was sent consumes the confirmation's nonce — without persisting, a second poll would re-call `execute_purchase` and get back an unrelated "nonce already used" Block Receipt instead of the real S3 failure.
- `OrderStatus.tsx`: distinct amber "blocked by the payment rail" panel vs. the red "blocked by AgentPay" panel, so the attribution is visible on screen, not just in the data model.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit-verified `classifyExecutionResult` against every real message shape `execute_purchase.ts` produces (settled, Tuple-mismatch Block Receipt, nonce-replay Block Receipt, rail failure before/after payment sent) — all 5 pass
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Dev-verified: checkout + order-polling live for the $28 grocery bundle (clears AgentPay's range check as intended)
- [x] Both new UI branches (Block Receipt / rail failure) screenshotted via a temporary debug-only mock path in the component — removed before commit, never shipped

author: gchaix
body:
## Summary

Mobile client for Lagoon (Android-first, iOS from the same codebase) targeting SBS with a context switcher for any number of Lagoon clusters, mirroring `lagoon-cli`'s context model.

- **Stack**: Expo SDK 57 (managed + dev client), expo-router (typed routes), strict TypeScript, Apollo Client 4 + graphql-codegen against a vendored Lagoon schema
- **Contexts**: add a cluster with name + GraphQL URL (Keycloak/UI URLs derived, editable); per-context Apollo client with isolated cache; quick switcher in every header
- **Auth**: Keycloak OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE via system browser (`lagoon` realm, `lagoon-ui` client by default, per-context override), refresh tokens in secure storage, single-flight refresh, 401 → forced refresh → one retry; pasted-token fallback with admin guidance when a cluster pins redirect URIs
- **Monitor**: projects with search, prod/dev environment cards, deployments & tasks with status/duration, Info tab (routes, services, key facts); live status via graphql-ws with automatic 10s polling fallback; ANSI-aware log viewer (chunked parsing, tail-follow, 10k-line windowing) for multi-MB build logs
- **Operate**: deploy latest + cancel deployment behind confirmation sheets; registered advanced tasks with generated argument forms; raw commands behind an Advanced disclosure
- **CI**: codegen drift check, eslint, tsc, jest (40 tests) on every push; manual EAS build workflow; Claude auto-review workflow on PRs

The base branch is the M0 scaffold; each subsequent commit is one milestone.

## Test plan

- [x] CI: lint, typecheck, jest, codegen drift — green
- [x] Device: build dev client (`npm run android` or EAS `development` profile — not Expo Go, OAuth needs the custom scheme)
- [x] Add SBS as a context; verify browser PKCE login (or token-paste fallback if SBS Keycloak pins `lagoon-ui` redirect URIs — the login screen shows the admin fix)
- [x] Browse projects → environment → watch a running deployment's status/log refresh
- [x] Trigger + cancel a deployment on a dev environment; run a registered task

author: dustindoan
body:
## Problem

`qobuz-fetch.py` called `album/get` for **every purchased album on every poll cycle**, before any watermark check — the work list is built before tracks are filtered. So per-cycle API cost was **O(albums ever purchased)**, not O(new purchases), against a loop that runs every 15 minutes forever.

| Library | Requests/cycle | Requests/day |
|---|---|---|
| 1 album (today) | 2 | ~192 |
| 50 albums | 51 | ~4,900 |
| 200 albums | 201 | ~19,300 |

Invisible today. It matters because this is the account holding the purchases — the one account that can't afford to get flagged, since losing it means losing re-download access to music that was actually paid for. Ramping unnecessary traffic against it as the library grows is the wrong direction.

## Fix

The watermark is now two-level. Albums whose every track has landed are recorded in `complete_albums` (`{album_id: tracks_count}`) and never re-expanded. Steady state is **one `getUserPurchases` call per cycle at any library size**.

Three decisions worth reviewing:

- **The stored count comes from `getUserPurchases`, not `album/get`.** Same-source comparison. If the two endpoints counted tracks even slightly differently, every album would look "changed" every cycle and silently re-expand forever — undoing the fix while still being correct, i.e. the failure mode nobody notices. It also buys re-issue detection for free: an album reporting a different count gets re-expanded and picks up new tracks. `tracks_count` already rides along in the response, so the check costs nothing.
- **Promotion trusts only the durable track watermark.** A track skipped merely because it's still in staging isn't proof it was fetched, so that album stays unpromoted and expands again next cycle. Worst case is one wasted call, never a missed track.
- **`album_is_complete` sentinels on `False`, not `None`** — `None` is a legitimate stored value (API omitted `tracks_count`), and so is `0`.

## Migration

None needed. The box's state file has 14 track IDs and no `complete_albums`; on the first run the album expands once more, all 14 tracks are already in the watermark, and it gets recorded. Cycle two onward skips it permanently.

## Testing

19 logic checks pass, run against a replica of the box's actual on-disk state: legacy-file migration, promotion surviving restart, count-change re-expansion, absent `tracks_count`, `tracks_count == 0` vs unrecorded, manual runs (no `QOBUZ_STATE`) staying a no-op, corrupt-file fallback, and fresh-dir creation.

Logic-level only — this doesn't touch Qobuz. **First real proof is the deploy:** the second poll after redeploy should print `(1 complete album(s) not re-expanded)`.

## Deploy notes

- `git pull` on coralstack-apps, then `docker compose up -d --build qobuz-poll`
- The rebuild re-reads `QOBUZ_TOKEN` from `.env` at container start. That token is now 30 days old and unrefreshed — it was still authenticating cleanly across 409 poll cycles as of today, but the restart is the natural moment to confirm it survives.
- Unrelated: the poll loop has still never live-fired on a genuinely new purchase. Every cycle so far has only confirmed "already present."

author: shunmeicho
body:
## Immediate unblock

Three stdlib advisories were published after #113 landed, all fixed in `go1.25.13`:

| Advisory | Package | Reached from |
|---|---|---|
| GO-2026-6089 | `net/http` | `daemon.Server.ListenAndServe` |
| GO-2026-6090 | `crypto/tls` | `ListenAndServe`, `shim.LocalBinaryHash`, `hosts.FormatRedeployReminder`, `plugin.PostNotification` |
| GO-2026-6218 | `net/url` | `plugin.PostNotification` |

Verified with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.25.13`: build, vet, `go test ./... -race -count=1`, and govulncheck all pass — `No vulnerabilities found`.

## The recurrence is the point

CI went red again **two days** after #113, with no source change. That is exactly what #113's closing note flagged:

> Pinning a full patch version in `go.mod` while scanning with `govulncheck@latest` means CI will go red again on the next stdlib advisory, with no code change involved.

`go.mod` currently pins a full patch version, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the toolchain from it with `go-version-file: go.mod`. So a rolling advisory database is being evaluated against a frozen toolchain. Every new stdlib advisory is an unavoidable red build, and the only remedy is another one-line bump like this one. That is not a sustainable steady state — it also means a genuinely important advisory looks identical to routine noise.

## Options for the steady state

**A — keep as-is.** Accept that `go.mod` pins the exact toolchain and treat these bumps as routine maintenance. Most reproducible; guarantees recurring red builds between advisory and bump.

**B — make `go.mod` a floor instead of a pin.** Write the directive as a minor version (`go 1.25`) so `setup-go` resolves the newest patch. This matches how the directive is conventionally used — "requires Go 1.25+", not "requires exactly 1.25.13". Worth confirming `setup-go`'s resolution behaviour for a patchless directive before relying on it.

**C — separate build floor from scan target.** Keep `go.mod` pinned for builds, and give the Govulncheck step its own `setup-go` with `go-version: 'stable'`. Unambiguous, and it draws the right line: the pin says what the project is guaranteed to build with, the scan says whether current Go has a problem this code reaches.

The tradeoff between B and C is what a red Govulncheck should *mean*. Under B and C it means "current Go has a vulnerability this code reaches" — actionable. Under A it means "the pinned floor has a known vulnerability" — also true, but it fires on a schedule set by the Go security team rather than by anything in this repo.

This PR does not implement any of them; it only unblocks. Happy to follow up with whichever you pick.
