author: joshhulett
body:
# ConvLSTM Refactor: Classification Loss, Shared Metrics, and Standalone Evaluation

## Summary
This PR merges the ConvLSTM refactor branch into `main`. It is representative of the finalisation of the ConvLSTM refactor and the effort of three team members. The branch moves the bushfire ConvLSTM model from a regression training/evaluation setup to a proper binary classification setup, adding functionality such as new evaluation, metrics, and local inference modeuls, and fixes several correctness issues found along the way.

At a high level:
- The model now trains with a masked classification loss (Tversky, with Focal added as an alternative) instead of MSE.
- A shared `evaluation/metrics.py` module is the single source of truth for classification metrics (PR-AUC, F2, Brier, ROC-AUC, skill ratio vs. climatology), used identically by both the training script and a new standalone evaluation script.
- Implemented a new standalone `evaluation/convlstm_evaluation.py` script that is responsible for performing evaluation on any portion of the training set, used to test model performance without requiring another trial run.
- The training script's evaluation step now reports these classification metrics and derives `fire_threshold` from the validation split instead of using a hardcoded placeholder.
- Several data-handling and training-loop bugs were fixed: scaler fit on train-only data (no val leakage), best-model checkpoint stored as a deep copy, invalid GeoJSON coordinates dropped instead of defaulting to `(0.0, 0.0)`, and epoch loss weighted by actual batch size.
- A local inference script was added for testing, along with trained model and scaler checkpoints from a ~10 epoch test run, allowing for 

Individually reviewed PRs on this branch:
- #200 - Shared classification metrics module
- #199 - Masked Tversky loss
- #201 - Standalone evaluation script + Masked Focal loss
- #210 - Training script data/checkpoint/GeoJSON/loss-averaging fixes
- #206 - Training script integration with metrics module, with classification metrics, validation-derived threshold

Planner task:
https://planner.cloud.microsoft/webui/v1/plan/H6UJiW7Qd0-pqy0lPXGgZ8gADBxI/view/board/task/w05L3RMWxEaVToiOt-FRxcgAKsAM?tid=d02378ec-1688-46d5-8540-1c28b5f470f6

## Type
- [ ] dataset
- [x] feat
- [x] fix
- [ ] config/infra
- [x] refactor
- [ ] docs
- [ ] test
- [ ] chore

## Contributors
- @JoshHulett 
- @AlinaBlox 
- @ArchCompy 

## Changes

### Shared metrics module (`src/evaluation/metrics.py`)
- `flatten_valid()` - masks and flattens gridded predictions to 1D so training and evaluation mask identically
- `compute_metrics()` - metrics computed on pooled predictions across a whole split (not per-batch and averaged)
- `find_best_threshold()` - selects a decision threshold from the validation precision-recall curve only
- `climatology_baseline()` - no-skill reference values computed from labels alone
- `format_metrics()` - renders a metrics dict as a readable log block
- Headline metric is PR-AUC (threshold-independent, usable to compare loss functions); F2 used by default over F1 to weight recall; accuracy deliberately excluded; Brier score and ROC-AUC included with ROC-AUC flagged as inflated under class imbalance; skill ratio reported against climatology baseline
- Dependencies limited to numpy/scikit-learn - no torch import, so it's importable from either script

### Masked Tversky loss
- Added `MaskedTverskyLoss`: converts logits to probabilities via `torch.sigmoid()`, computes TP/FP/FN, configured with `alpha=0.3`, `beta=0.7` to weight false negatives above false positives
- Reuses the existing `[H, W]` spatial mask (ocean/NSW excluded), broadcast across batch/horizon/output dims
- Replaces `MaskedMSELoss` as the active training criterion; training/validation loop and logging updated accordingly

### Masked Focal loss (alternative)
- Added `MaskedFocalLoss` (`nn.Module`): binary focal loss from raw logits, masked to valid land cells
- `gamma` (default 2.0) down-weights easy examples; `alpha` (default 0.85) applies a fixed positive-class weight
- Additive only - Tversky remains the default/active loss unless explicitly swapped in

### Standalone evaluation script (`src/evaluation/evaluate_convlstm.py`)
- Loads a checkpoint + scaler/metadata bundle, reconstructs the time-ordered test split using the same pipeline as training, runs inference, reports classification metrics
- Uses `flatten_valid()` / `compute_metrics()` / `format_metrics()` from the shared module so a checkpoint scores identically whether evaluated during or after training
- Operating threshold defaults to the value stored in the scaler bundle at training time
- Writes `metrics.json` to `--output-dir` (default `src/evaluation/eval_results`)

### Training script: classification metrics + threshold (`training/train_convlstm.py`)
- Replaced the old regression-metrics block (MAE/RMSE/R², no longer meaningful against a single fire-probability output channel) with:
  - validation-only threshold selection via `find_best_threshold()` / `flatten_valid()`
  - test-set evaluation via `compute_metrics()` / `format_metrics()`
- `fire_threshold` saved to the scaler bundle now reflects the validation-selected value; `FIRE_THRESHOLD` retained as an explicit fallback
- Removed unused `mean_absolute_error`, `mean_squared_error`, `r2_score` imports; updated `main()` docstring to match actual `STEP` prints

### Training script: data handling and checkpoint fixes
- **Scaler leakage**: split train/val before fitting `StandardScaler`; scaler fit on training data only, then applied separately to train/val/test
- **Best-model checkpoint**: best model state now stored via `copy.deepcopy(model.state_dict())` so it's independent of later training updates
- **GeoJSON handling**: failed coordinate parsing now produces `NaN` (was `(0.0, 0.0)`, which silently created a valid-looking but artificial grid location); invalid-coordinate rows are counted, reported, and dropped before the spatial grid is built, with the full weather time axis preserved beforehand
- **Batch loss averaging**: training/validation loss now weighted by actual samples per batch rather than averaged per-batch unweighted, so a smaller final batch doesn't count equally to a full batch; `drop_last=True` avoided so no samples are discarded

### Local inference / test artifacts
- Added a local inference script for manual testing, calls the `api/model_loader.py` and the `api/inference/bushfire_forecaster.py` scripts to return and save a full one-timestep inference as a `.geojson` file
- Produced trained model and scaler checkpoints produced from a minimal ~10 epoch training run, intended for use while testing end-to-end operation and backend integration

## Reasons
- **ConvLSTM finalisation**: finishes the transition from a regression weather model to a binary bushfire classification objective, bringing all components (loss, training, evaluation, inference).
- **Loss/metric mismatch**: MSE and MAE/RMSE/R² were leftover regression code that no longer matches the refactored binary fire-probability classification output.
- **Metric drift**: computing metrics separately in training and evaluation code risks silent divergence (masking, thresholds, per-batch vs. pooled averaging); a shared module removes that risk and lets a checkpoint score identically wherever it's evaluated.
- **Comparable loss functions**: validation loss can't be used to compare Tversky against Focal since their scales are unrelated; PR-AUC is loss-agnostic and gives a fair comparison basis.
- **Class imbalance**: positive rate is ~0.1%, so accuracy is uninformative (predicting no fire everywhere scores >99.9%) and raw PR-AUC needs a baseline to interpret; Tversky/Focal, F2, and the climatology skill ratio all address this directly.
- **Threshold correctness**: `fire_threshold` was a hardcoded `0.5` placeholder, which at this imbalance

## Summary
This is the v1.9.0 branch train: read-back/diagnostics/panic/supply-chain (DB-034…DB-040) followed by Privileged Display capability safety and experimental HDR (DB-041…DB-046).

**Read-back, diagnostics, panic, supply-chain (DB-034…DB-040)**
- Privileged Display now re-reads all seven toggles from the device on open (Tasker's `_ShowPrivilegedScene` behavior), fixing a stale-screen bug where flipping Night Light from the system tile left the UI asserting the opposite (DB-034). The circadian flag and in-flight temperature key stay app-owned since they have no stable device counterpart.
- Rejected `ControlReceiver` broadcasts now explain themselves at debug level 8, with the check moved ahead of the sink construction it was gating (DB-035), and `LOAD_PROFILE`'s caller-chosen overlay name is now bounded to 40 chars with control/bidi characters stripped.
- Fixed a ~2-in-3 flaky `DraftSettingsViewModelTest` that polled the DataStore instead of the view model's own derived `dirty` state (DB-036).
- Panic (S.O.S.) is now shared across both gesture collectors, the notification Reset, and the control intent via `panicAndStop`, restoring vibrate-after-restore ordering so a sibling DISABLE can't cancel mid-recovery and leave the user buzzed but not restored; added re-entry guarding against a double-tapped Reset (DB-037).
- All 39 GitHub Actions call sites are now pinned to commit SHA (Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies), with Dependabot covering the refresh path and top-level `contents: write` scoped down to job level (DB-038).
- The read-back merge guard from DB-034 fired only once because writing device values into the draft broke its own "draft matches profile" precondition, freezing tracking after the first entry; fixed by comparing against the draft's own last-produced state instead of conflating "user has uncommitted edits" with "draft differs from profile" (DB-039). A follow-up review found three more holes — background collector writes read as user edits, the effect not re-running on Discard, and the pre-seed draft standing the gate open — fixed by scoping equality to owned fields, making read-and-write one atomic `update`, and refusing before the seed (DB-040).

**Privileged Display capability safety + experimental HDR (DB-041…DB-046)**
- A real black-screen incident on an OEM whose framework reports Night Display unavailable led to fail-closed capability gating on `config_nightDisplayAvailable` and `config_dozeAlwaysOnDisplayAvailable` at the controller boundary, so unsupported writes become harmless no-ops across profile swaps, circadian ticks, direct Apply and panic, and the corresponding UI hides (DB-041). Force-SDR was dropped in this pass: AOSP's `DisplayManagerService` doesn't observe the Global rows a direct Settings write would touch.
- Capability-gated reads defaulting to `false` were silently erasing hidden Night Light/AOD profile values through unrelated device read-back; snapshot booleans are now nullable capability sentinels so unavailable fields survive, and authorization-before-capability ordering was restored so every setter rejects below ELEVATED before an unsupported no-op (DB-042).
- Corrected an overclaim from DB-041: AOD's availability is the conjunction of the Night Light flag AND a non-empty `config_dozeComponent`, matching AOSP ambient-display gating (deliberately ignoring its debug-property escape hatch); missing/unreadable resources fail closed, with lookup tests pinning exact resource names and the AOD truth table (DB-043).
- Per owner decision, Android-14+ `user_disabled_hdr_formats` is retained as **Disable HDR (experimental)** rather than removed — it's a stored-preference control, not the DisplayManager Force-SDR service API, so apply/clear may require reboot and an HDR/display-mode transition may briefly blank the screen. This is disclosed as expectation risk distinct from the Night Light catastrophic-failure class (DB-044).
- HDR read-back was normalizing any nonblank enforced format list to a single Boolean, which let direct Apply broaden a partial/malformed external preference to the full disabled set while saving an unrelated field. Only canonical-off and canonical-all-disabled now map to Boolean; everything else maps to null and is preserved rather than overwritten, with the UI showing a custom-preference preservation notice in that state (DB-045).
- Fixed the CI-only failure this introduced: the HDR round-trip fixture assumed absent Global rows meant OFF, but production now classifies absent/malformed rows as unrepresentable null — the test previously passed only via cross-test state leakage in shared Robolectric Settings. It now explicitly seeds `are_user_disabled_hdr_formats_allowed=1` plus a blank format list before asserting OFF; production semantics are unchanged (DB-046).

## Release impact
v1.9.0 / versionCode 21. Semver minor bump: new user-visible feature (Disable HDR experimental control, capability-gated Night Light/AOD availability) plus behavioral bug fixes (read-back staleness, panic ordering, HDR preference preservation) — no breaking changes.
Changelog: `fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/changelogs/21.txt`

## Verification
- `./gradlew :platform:compileDebugUnitTestKotlin --no-daemon`
- `scripts/ladder.sh --guards-only`
- Targeted Robolectric execution was attempted locally, but the `android-all-instrumented` dependency download failed with network unreachable in this environment; CI is the authoritative rerun for the full suite.
- Truth-table/lookup tests pin the AOD capability conjunction (DB-043) and the HDR canonical-state classification (DB-045/DB-046).
- On-device display behavior (Night Light, AOD, HDR reboot/blank caveats, panic vibration/recovery ordering) remains owner-verified only — no emulator/KVM available in this environment. See Owner queue in `docs/STATE.md` for the specific device passes still outstanding (§11.39a, §13.44a, §5.14a, DB-041…DB-045).

## Repo hygiene
None — this train is entirely app-behavior fixes and safety hardening; the only non-app-behavior item (Actions SHA pinning + Dependabot refresh path, DB-038) is called out above since it's a supply-chain rather than app-behavior change but ships in this same train.

## Owner action
Squash-merge to `main`, then tag `v1.9.0` from the squash commit and publish the release from `fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/changelogs/21.txt`. Before merging, strip any stray skip-ci token from this body if one was introduced by an intermediate edit (D-115). After release, the outstanding device-verification items in the Owner queue (`docs/STATE.md`) remain open: Privileged Display read-back, control-drop reasons, panic vibration (§11.39a/§13.44a/§5.14a), and Night Light/AOD/HDR capability-gate behavior including HDR reboot/brief-blank caveats.

author: arsalanam
body:
Closes #30.

The chart expansion (v0.4.0) added columns to pre-existing tables without an Alembic revision. Stamped databases disable the registry's auto-ADD fallback — by design — so those columns went silently missing until an INSERT failed on a real dev PostgreSQL.

**The fix is a reconciliation revision, not a fixed column list**: migration `0003` runs an inspector-guarded, add-only `ALTER TABLE` pass against the registry-merged metadata (env.py bootstraps the registry, so module extension columns are included). That makes it idempotent and correct from *any* stamped drift state — a database that already has the columns gets a no-op. The loop is one shared implementation (`reconcile_missing_columns`) used by both `ensure_columns` (pre-Alembic databases) and the migration (stamped ones).

CONTRIBUTING now states the boundary once: pre-Alembic databases auto-heal; stamped databases run `just db-upgrade`; every schema change from now on ships its own autogenerated revision.

**Verification**: end-to-end test via the alembic command API (create schema → drop chart-expansion columns → stamp `0002` → `upgrade head` → columns restored → second reconcile is a no-op), plus a live PostgreSQL run against `hdh_test` exercising the full `0002→0003` chain. 161 tests + qa + qa-postgres green.

1. **Section labels** — `.camp-filter-label` confirmed a legitimate filter-bar idiom, left as-is. `.csp-field-label` → `.section-label-sub`, redundant CSS rule deleted.

author: aouggad-web
body:
## Contexte

Investigation d'une branche pod auto-créée par Emergent (`conflict_150826_0917`, « Save to GitHub » avec divergence détectée). Cette branche partait d'un point très ancien (avant la PR #391) et réintroduisait plusieurs régressions déjà corrigées (routes `/login`, `/merci`, `/tarifs` en 404, `ModuleNotFoundError` catch-all trop large sur billing, suppression de l'étape GeoIP dans `sync_emergent.sh`) — **non repris**.

Un seul changement de cette branche était une correction réelle et absente de `main` : le cookie CSRF posé en `SameSite=Strict` ne revient pas sur nos propres requêtes `fetch` quand l'app est chargée dans l'iframe d'aperçu Emergent (document top-level = `app.emergent.sh`, origine différente de la nôtre).

## Changement

- `backend/middlewares/csrf_protection.py` : cookie `csrf_token` posé en `SameSite=None` (HTTPS) / `SameSite=Lax` (HTTP local) au lieu de `Strict`.
- `frontend/src/services/csrf.js` : même ajustement côté client pour le cookie miroir lisible en JS.

La protection double-soumission CSRF ne dépend pas du blocage cross-site de `SameSite` (elle repose sur le fait que seul du JS same-origin lit/écrit le cookie et l'en-tête), donc ce changement n'affaiblit pas la protection. `SameSite=None` exige `Secure`, d'où le fallback `Lax` en HTTP.

## Effet attendu

L'authentification (register/login) fonctionne correctement quand l'app est visualisée dans l'iframe d'aperçu Emergent, sans régression de la protection CSRF.

body:
## What changed

- Added the canonical `data/JANUS-AXLE-COIN-TWO-SIDED-LAUREL-A1-v2.5.json` record for the two-sided print-in-place fidget.
- Added `data/JANUS-COIN-ORIGINAL-TWO-SIDED-v1.0.json` for the original JANUS threshold/return coin.
- Added a topology-preserved registry copy of the supplied JANUS coin under `artifacts/3d_printing/janus_coin_family/`.
- Added front/back geometry QA images and validation receipts.
- Added a family README documenting hashes, provenance, claim ceiling, printing state, and distribution status.

## Why

This gives the JANUS physical-object line a provenance-aware, machine-readable home in the meta-registry. It preserves the original coin as the semantic core and records the v2.5 mechanism repair, A1 support profile, geometry counts, clearances, and remaining physical-print gate.

## Mechanical root cause recorded

The prior ornament mask protected only each ring's nominal axis and could modify the neighbouring side of an axle/socket interface, reducing a measured clearance to about 0.12 mm. v2.5 protects every axle diameter touched by each ring and restores the source clearances: approximately 0.200 / 0.200 / 0.309 mm.

## Distribution gate

The printable v2.5 fidget binary is not committed in this PR because its mechanism source embeds MakerWorld `Standard Digital File License` metadata for designer Kike. The validation receipt and QA renders are included, and the exact validated binary SHA-256 is recorded. This is a license/provenance gate, not a geometry failure.

The supplied JANUS coin is included as a topology-preserved registry artifact. To pass the connector's binary transport boundary, only vertex decimal serialization was normalized to `1e-6 mm`; topology and the triangle block are unchanged. Both source and registry-container SHA-256 values are recorded.

## Validation

- `jq empty` passed for all four JSON records/receipts.
- Repacked JANUS coin: ZIP CRC test passed.
- Source coin: 2,032,128 vertices and 3,193,616 triangles.
- Registry coin SHA-256: `4d01cb3be463c1c597a8cdd73b16ba0fbb23d85967b1188fa7f773c95efe0a9d`.

author: tsouza
body:
## Summary

Issue #2104: phase B of the two-phase structural fetch stamps `TraceIDRestriction` onto a `StructuralJoin` so every physical spans scan reads only the top-N traces phase A ranked. The canonical closure's anchor folds it (`structuralAnchorWhere`); the union recursive (`&>>`/`&<<`) **inverse** closure's anchor (`buildStructuralInverseClosure`) built its own window-only WHERE by hand and never folded it, so that anchor's seed scan read every windowed trace on the R side instead of granule-pruning to the top-N literals via `idx_trace_id` — exactly the read amplification phase B exists to avoid.

This is a **read-amplification bug, not a correctness one**: the inverse closure only ever projects `_depth > 0` rows, which come from the step arm alone, and the step arm already restricts them (`structuralStepWhere`) — `TestSearch_UnionTwoPhase_Parity_ChDB` legitimately passed before this fix and still passes after it.

## Fix

Extracts `structuralAnchorNodeBounds` (trace-id restriction + window) as the bound both anchors share:
- The canonical anchor keeps going through `structuralAnchorWhere`, which now composes the canonical-only candidate prefilter with `structuralAnchorNodeBounds` (same emitted SQL — byte-identical, just refactored).
- The inverse anchor (`buildStructuralInverseClosure`) now calls `structuralAnchorNodeBounds` directly instead of the window-only `structuralAnchorWindowFrags`, so it picks up the trace-id restriction fold for the first time.

## Verification

- New tests in `internal/chsql/structural_join_anchor_mutation_test.go`, mirroring the existing canonical-anchor mutation-kill tests:
  - `TestEmitStructuralRecursive_InverseAnchorCarriesTraceIDRestriction` — a union recursive (`&>>`) plan with `TraceIDRestriction` set renders the restriction into the inverse closure's `_seed WHERE`.
  - `TestEmitStructuralRecursive_InverseAnchorUnrestrictedHasNoSeedWhere` — the complement: no restriction set means no seed WHERE, so the assertion above can't be satisfied by an emitter that always splices one in.
- `go test -race ./internal/chsql/...` — all pass.
- `go test -tags chdb ./internal/chsql/... ./internal/api/tempo/...` — all pass, including `TestSearch_UnionTwoPhase_Parity_ChDB` (the phase-B correctness parity test) unchanged.
- `go test -tags chdb ./test/spec/traceql/... -run TestRoundTripChDB` — all 100+ TraceQL spec fixtures pass unchanged; none of them set `TraceIDRestriction` (it's an API-layer phase-B stamp, not something the spec-level lowering exercises), so this is a zero-diff refactor for every existing golden — no `just update-golden` regeneration needed.
- `node .github/scripts/forbid-sql-raw.mjs` — clean.
- `gofumpt -extra` / `goimports -local` — clean.

Closes #2104

author: makenowjust
body:
Closes #1.

The README showed the code that renders a diagram but never the result.
The example becomes a top-down decision with labeled Yes and No branches (Commit → CI passes? → Merge / Fix), the shape pozeiden's layout draws cleanly, and its rendered SVG is committed as `examples/flowchart.svg` and displayed below the code block, the same arrangement as dewasm-merman.

`rake example_svg` rewrites the file, and the test suite fails when the committed SVG no longer matches a regenerated one; the render is deterministic (two renders agree byte for byte), so the test compares bytes.
pozeiden's SVG uses plain `<text>` labels and a white background rectangle with fixed dimensions, so it displays correctly as an image with no `foreignObject` or sizing concerns.

## Verification

- Regenerated the module with dewasm at the pinned revision; `rake test` passes: 24 runs, 66 assertions, 0 failures.
- Rasterized candidate layouts and picked by inspection: the left-right variants place the branch labels on elbow segments and a back edge leaves a large empty area, while the top-down branch is symmetric with the Yes and No labels beside their lines.

author: stunwill
body:
## What changed

MathQuest 0.26.0 delivers the roadmap's Number and Algebra intervention, interactive learning, platform reliability, and reporting correction work.

- Adds focused 5, 10, and 15-minute interventions for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, fact families, and unknown-value equations
- Uses check, teach, practice, and retrieval phases with operation-specific strategy cards and model recommendations
- Adds vertically aligned fraction comparisons, number-line jumps, place-value models, arrays, and explicit Why?, Show another way, and Start over controls
- Moves worksheet visuals, read-aloud, scratchpad, confidence checks, and related state into React-owned components
- Preserves per-question answer drafts and gives every visual a stable question identity to prevent stale carry-over
- Reconciles worksheet evidence and separates independent from supported accuracy
- Excludes parent test activity from learner reporting and Home Assistant evidence
- Updates all add-on version references, release notes, and documentation to 0.26.0

## Why

Sienna needs targeted Number and Algebra support that teaches efficient strategies instead of relying on finger counting. The same release also strengthens worksheet state ownership and evidence reporting so supported completion is not confused with independent understanding.

## Validation

- Backend: 113 tests passed
- Frontend: 28 tests passed across 9 files
- TypeScript: passed
- Production Vite build: passed
- Python compile validation: passed
- Version consistency: 0.26.0 across all 7 required locations
- Git diff whitespace validation: passed

## Manual review focus

1. Start 5, 10, and 15-minute interventions and confirm the recommended focus and phases.
2. Check subtraction, written calculation, fact-family, and unknown-value equation support.
3. Open Maths tools and test Why?, Show another way, Start over, fraction stacking, number lines, place value, and arrays.
4. Type an answer, navigate away, exit, and resume. Confirm the draft and correct visual return.
5. Confirm grid highlights contain no answer labels and visuals never carry over between questions.
6. Compare live worksheet counts with completion, calendar, parent, and Home Assistant reporting.
7. Complete a parent test and confirm it does not affect Sienna's learning evidence.

## Known limitations

No release after 0.26.0 is sufficiently defined in the roadmap. Development should stop at this review gate until this PR is merged and the next product scope is agreed.

author: yasser1164-ux
body:
## Summary

**1. Zoom-dependent markers (Google Maps behaviour).** Pins scale with zoom via `zoom-low` / `zoom-mid` / `zoom-high` classes on the map container: below city zoom they're small brand-gradient dots, at mid zoom small emoji pins, and from street zoom the full 44px poster pins — with a smooth transition. Sizing uses a centred CSS `transform: scale()`, so marker anchor points stay exactly right and no icon rebuilding is needed on zoom.

**2. Real density heat layer (Snapchat style).** The per-event glow circles are gone. Instead, [Leaflet.heat](https://github.com/Leaflet/Leaflet.heat) (pinned 0.2.0 via CDN) renders a kernel-density heatmap of **all visible items**, weighted by each item's `heat` value, in a warm brand gradient (deep purple → coral → amber). Venues close together merge into one warm hub that fades outward — the Khobar corniche reads as a single glowing hotspot. The layer refreshes on every filter change (type / date / category).

**3. Clustering with count badges is unchanged**, as requested.

## Testing

Headless mobile emulation against the 30-item live-data snapshot: zoom classes and computed pin transforms switch at the intended levels (0.32 → 0.68 → 1.0); the heat canvas renders and updates when filters change; and the full 30-item popup audit (card open + direct pin tap, popup survives with tappable CTA) still passes with zero console errors. Screenshots at all three zoom levels reviewed.

author: mateuszpuchalski
body:
## Kontekst

Ślad audytowy zbiera 29+ typów zdarzeń z pełnymi indeksami od pierwszego dnia, ale nic go nie agregowało — `audyt.ts` z założenia tylko czyta, a `raporty.ts` liczył cztery wskaźniki. Nowa zakładka podglądu biura odpowiada na cztery pytania właściciela:

- **kto ile robi i kiedy jest szczyt** — wykresy operacji per dzień i per godzinę,
- **czy magazyn nadąża** — dostawy zamknięte, mediana czasu, pozycje na dostawę, problemy,
- **czego ludzie szukają i nie znajdują** — top zapytań + lista „bez wyniku",
- **który kolektor się sypie** — upadki, baterie, odrzucone operacje per urządzenie.

Do tego **eksport CSV** jednym plikiem (sekcje, BOM, separator `;` dla Excela PL).

## Odwrócona decyzja — świadomie i z dokumentacją

**Raport wydajności per osoba wchodzi na ekran.** Od 0.27.0 istniał na serwerze, ale strona celowo go nie odpytywała i pilnował tego test. Właściciel — uprzedzony, że to monitoring pracowniczy (Kodeks pracy art. 22²: zapis w regulaminie/obwieszczeniu + uprzedzenie załogi 2 tygodnie przed użyciem kadrowym) — zdecydował inaczej.

Test strażnika został **przepisany na odwrotny**: pilnuje teraz, żeby sekcja imienna nigdy nie stała bez podstawy prawnej nad tabelą i bez zdania, że zgłoszone problemy nie są miarą błędu. Trzy reguły raportu nietknięte: zgłoszenie wyjątku to nie wpadka, kolumny błędów nie ma, tempo z próbki <20 pozycji pokazuje się jako „MAŁO DANYCH" zamiast liczby.

## Decyzje techniczne

- **Bramka jak w audycie** (`biuro`, `admin`) — nie jak w `/api/metrics`, bo odpowiedź niesie dane imienne. Eksport CSV zostawia ślad `analiza_eksport` — kto pobiera zestawienia o ludziach, sam trafia do logu.
- **Dni bucketowane po zegarze magazynu w JS**, nie po dobie UTC w SQL — zdarzenie z 23:30 UTC należy do następnego dnia polskiego (lekcja 0.31.1). Test to wymusza.
- **Wspólne reguły `PRACA`/`bezDubli`/`OKNO`** z `raporty.ts` — rozłożenie linii emituje dwa zdarzenia i liczy się jako jedna pozycja.
- **`search` zapisuje teraz `wynikow` i `przyblizone`** — bez tego lista braków nie miała z czego się policzyć. Zdarzenia historyczne (samo `q`) nie wchodzą do „bez wyniku"; potraktowane jako zero zamieniłyby całą historię w fałszywe braki.
- **Wykresy to inline SVG** składane w JS — strona ma zero zależności i zero builda; dwa jednoseryjne słupkowe nie uzasadniają biblioteki. Świadomie poza `/api/health` (memoizowana gorąca ścieżka).

## Pliki

| plik | co |
|---|---|
| `server/src/services/raporty.ts` | `analiza(days)` + `mediana()` |
| `server/src/routes/analiza.ts` (nowy) | `GET /api/analiza`, `GET /api/analiza/csv`, `csvAnalizy` |
| `server/src/routes/products.ts` | zdarzenie `search` niesie liczbę wyników |
| `server/src/web/biuro.html` | zakładka ANALIZA, wykresy SVG, aktualizacja komentarza o decyzji |
| `server/src/routes/biuro.test.ts` | odwrócony test strażnika + `/api/analiza` na liście tras za bramką |
| `services/analiza.test.ts`, `routes/analiza.test.ts` (nowe) | 17 testów |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `docs/architektura.md` | 0.48.0 + odnotowane odwrócenie decyzji |

## Weryfikacja

- `npm -w server test` — **600 zdanych** (583 + 17 nowych)
- `npm -w server run build`, `docs_check.py`, `styl_check.py` — czysto
- `node --check` na wyciętym inline JS strony (strona nie ma builda, więc literówka wyszłaby dopiero w przeglądarce)
- **Prawdziwy render w Chromium** na danych demo: serwer + konto biura + zdarzenia w kilku dniach/godzinach, zrzut całej zakładki, zero błędów konsoli. Godziny na wykresie zgodne z przesunięciem strefy — zdarzenia siane w UTC wylądowały we właściwych słupkach lokalnych.

## Wdrożenie

**[wymaga działania]** Restart `wertis-api` po `git pull` — bez nowego APK (panel to strona serwowana przez serwer). **Zanim raport per osoba zostanie użyty kadrowo**: zapis w regulaminie pracy albo obwieszczeniu i uprzedzenie załogi co najmniej 2 tygodnie wcześniej. Panel pokazuje podstawę prawną nad tabelą i w CSV — ale sam obowiązek jest po stronie pracodawcy.

author: pravbeseda
body:
Closes **GHSA-jj27-h5hq-8x99** — high severity, XSS in Angular i18n via event-handler attributes, first patched in **21.2.19**. Two open Dependabot alerts point at it, on `@angular/core` and `@angular/compiler`.

## Why one manual PR instead of merging four

Dependabot filed the fix as four separate pull requests — #277 `core`, #280 `common`, #283 `compiler`, #290 `platform-server` — because **security updates bypass the grouping** in `dependabot.yml`. Merging them one at a time produces this:

| package | after merging the four | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | 21.2.15 | |
| `common`, `compiler`, `platform-server` | 21.2.19 | |
| `animations`, `forms`, `router`, `platform-browser`, `platform-browser-dynamic`, `compiler-cli` | **21.2.6** | untouched — Dependabot filed nothing for them |

That mixed set is exactly what the `angular` group in `dependabot.yml` exists to prevent, and three intermediate states of it would exist while the four PRs land one by one.

## What changed

All twenty packages move together, along their three release lines:

| set | packages | to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| framework | `core`, `common`, `compiler`, `compiler-cli`, `animations`, `forms`, `router`, `platform-browser`, `platform-browser-dynamic`, `platform-server`, `language-service` | **21.2.19** |
| toolchain | `@angular/cli`, `@angular-devkit/*`, `@schematics/angular`, `@angular/ssr` | **21.2.21** |
| Material | `@angular/cdk`, `cdk-experimental`, `material` | **21.2.14** |

The numbers differ because Angular's lockstep requirement is a shared **minor** across the framework set, not an identical patch across every line — the CLI and devkit release more often, and Material versions on its own line. This is the same reason `dependabot.yml` groups these packages rather than pinning them equal.

Everything here is a patch inside 21.2.x, so no schematics are involved and `nx migrate` is not needed: a version edit and an install are the whole change.

## Checked

`@codemirror/state` still resolves to a single copy with no nested duplicates — a duplicated copy breaks the production build while leaving the unit tests green, so it is worth confirming after any dependency change here.

## Gates

`lint` (6 projects), `test --configuration=ci` (5 projects), `lint:coverage`, `test:scripts` (8), `lint:playwright`, `format:check`, `lint:styles`, `lint:types`, `lint:workflows`, `knip`, `build`, `test:playwright` — all green.

## Not in this PR

- **Nx 22 → 23** — a separate major, and separable: `@nx/angular@23.1.1` peers on the Angular toolchain as `>= 20.0.0 < 23.0.0`. Its own PR next.
- **Angular 21 → 22** — #296, blocked on the Node version its toolchain requires (`^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`).

Supersedes #277, #280, #283, #290.

author: nabaho
body:
## 결론 먼저 — 자료가 사라지는 새 구멍은 없었습니다

동기화되는 배열 **51개**를 훑었습니다. `dbSet` 이 이미 **열한 겹**으로 막고 있습니다 — 읽어 보니 실제 사고를 겪으며 하나씩 쌓아 올린 것이더군요.

초기 동기화 전 쓰기 보류 · 0건 차단 · 급감 차단 · **서버 대비 옛자료 차단** · 확인 실패 시 보류 · **트랜잭션 병합** · 묶음표 병합 · 되돌림 방지 · meta 되돌리기 · 비번 보호 · 중복 id 제거.

그래서 질문은 하나로 좁혀졌습니다 — **그 병합을 못 타는 게 무엇인가.** 조건이 「모든 항목에 `id`」라서입니다.

| | |
|---|---|
| **33개** | id 있음 → 병합됨. 손댈 것 없음 |
| **1개** | `leave_ledger` — 업무 자료인데 id 없음 → **고침** |
| **14개** | id 없지만 까닭이 있음 → 예외로 못박음 |

⚠ **정정**: 첫 훑기에서 `payroll_irregular`·`ieum_lectures`·`dc_contributions` 를 위험으로 잘못 짚었습니다. 셋 다 id 가 있어 안전합니다.

---

## 고친 것 — 연차대장

행이 `{이름, 연도, …}` 라 id 가 없어 병합을 못 탔습니다. 게다가 화면이 이랬습니다:

```js
var s = useState(dbGet('leave_ledger', []));              // 열 때 한 번 찍어 두고
function persist(next){ … dbSet('leave_ledger', next); }  // 그걸 통째로 되씀
```

**열어 둔 사이 남이 넣은 행이 사라지는 길**입니다.

### 다섯 가지

**① 행에 열쇠를 붙였습니다** — `ll-이름|연도`

⚠ 같은 사람·같은 해 행이 **둘일 수 있습니다**(옛 자료·이관 중복). 같은 id 를 주면 `dbSet` 의 중복제거가 **한 줄을 지웁니다.** 그래서 나온 순서대로 `#2`·`#3` 을 붙이고, **겹친 건수를 화면에 알립니다.** 한 줄도 버리지 않습니다.

> 「같은 사람·같은 해 행이 몇 건인지」는 제가 셀 수 없습니다(대표님 자료를 못 봅니다). 그래서 **세는 대신 겹쳐도 안전하게** 만들었습니다.

**② 저장 직전에 최신을 다시 읽어** 내가 고친 행만 얹습니다

**③ 서버가 바뀌면 화면을 다시 읽습니다** — 단, **치고 있는 중에는 안 바꿉니다.** 치던 숫자가 눈앞에서 사라지면 더 나쁩니다

**④ 이름·연도가 아니라 id 로 그 줄만** 고칩니다. 전에는 겹친 행이 **같이** 바뀌었습니다

**⑤ 빈 대장은 저장하지 않습니다** — 2026-07 실데이터 사고 경로입니다(코드 주석에 남아 있습니다)

---

## id 없이 두는 14개

| 열쇠 | 까닭 |
|---|---|
| `locked_*_months` 6개 | `['2026-06', …]` — **달 이름만** 든 배열. 붙일 자리가 없음 |
| 설정표 4개 | 대표 혼자 고치고 통째로 바꾸는 것이 정상 |
| 기록·결과 4개 | 다시 만들면 됨 |

**여기 없는 새 배열이 id 없이 들어오면 검사가 걸립니다.**

---

## 남긴 것

- `tests/erp-overwrite-guard.test.js` — 열한 겹이 그대로 있는지 + 예외 목록
- `tests/erp-leave-ledger-merge.test.js` — 연차대장 (겹친 행·빈 대장·편집 중 보호)
- `docs/자료-덮어쓰기-방어.md` — 저장 코드를 건드리기 전에 읽을 것

## 검사

26개 새로, 전체 **2766개 통과**.

## 머지 뒤 확인 (연차대장)

1. 대장이 **전과 똑같이 보이는지** (건수·숫자)
2. 칸을 고쳐서 **저장이 되는지**
3. 「같은 사람·같은 해 행이 n건 겹쳐 있습니다」가 뜨면 → **알려 주세요.** 지우지 않고 그대로 뒀습니다
4. 두 기기에서 동시에 다른 사람 칸을 고쳐 보면 **둘 다 남는지**

author: swati510
body:
`answer.py` was 2,805 lines and had stopped being one thing. It sequenced retrieval, graded the result, built six different reply shapes, decided whether a cached row could be served, and held every feature flag the tool has. This moves each of those jobs into a module that owns it, and leaves the orchestrator behind.

It is deliberately sequenced after #1580. A structural pass and a behaviour fix must not share a diff, because a move-diff is exactly where a behaviour change hides: everything looks like relocation, so nothing gets read closely. The fixes landed first so this one could be held to a much stricter standard.

## The lever

The previous pass split `get_answer` into stages *inside* the file, and the line count went up rather than down — every extracted function costs a `def`, a signature, a docstring and a call site. Splitting in place cannot shrink a file. The reduction only comes from moving code out.

So the question was which siblings should own what, and the answer mostly already existed. `confidence.py` was grading hedges and values but not running the cascade that reads them. `data_shape.py` was mining a shape but not shaping it into a reply. `config.py` held the knobs but not the flags that switch them. Three of the four new modules are concerns that were already named in comments in the old file and simply had nowhere to live.

`answer.py` is now 793 lines: `get_answer`, the retrieval pipeline, and nothing else.

| module | owns |
|---|---|
| `payload.py` (new) | every reply shape but the synthesis-less ones — the serve-time size cuts, the ranked shortlist that travels with every post-retrieval return, answer-by-union, the legacy abstain, the value fast path, and the graded reply with the note whichever gate fired writes |
| `degraded.py` (new) | the synthesis-less reply and the next action it names |
| `cache.py` (new) | when a stored row may be served, and how one is written |
| `evidence.py` (new) | mined rationale comments, the de-duplication that keeps one comment from reaching the payload twice, and the resolvability check every advertised `symbol_id` passes |
| `bodies.py` (new) | selecting and inlining live symbol bodies, plus line-grounded quotes |
| `confidence.py` | gained the gate cascade and the two dominance signals it reads |
| `config.py` | gained every `REPOWISE_ANSWER_*` flag |
| `data_shape.py` | gained the payload builders for a mined shape |

The import graph is a directed acyclic graph, checked rather than assumed, and the module-level invariant guard that catches the excerpt cap disagreeing with the prompt formatter stays in `answer.py` — it is still the only module that sees both halves.

## What stayed, and why

`_run_retrieval_pipeline` looks like it belongs in `retrieval.py` and does not move. The unit suite patches `_hybrid_retrieve`, `_hydrate_hits` and `_anchor_symbol_hits` on this module; moving the pipeline out would quietly detach every one of those patches, leaving the suite green while it exercised the real retriever against a live index. A refactor that makes tests pass for a different reason than they used to is worse than the file being long. The same reasoning keeps `_attach_page_excerpts`, `_get_exclude_spec`, `_resolve_provider_for_answer` and `synthesize` called from here.

A handful of helpers are re-exported from `answer.py` with a comment saying why: they moved, but existing callers import them from their old home and an import path is not worth churning in a diff whose whole claim is that nothing changed.

## Comments

Roughly a third of the old file was comment, and a good part of that was evidence rather than reasoning — corpus names, measurement dates, sample sizes, byte and millisecond figures from a local dogfood harness. None of it belonged in shipped source, and it is stripped. The rule applied was to keep the reason and drop the evidence: a comment saying a cap exists because the bodies *are* the answer stays; the measurement that established it goes.

Every comment naming a trap, an invariant, or an alternative that was tried and rejected is kept. Those are the ones that stop the next person re-deriving a decision from scratch.

## Behaviour

No payload changes. Not a key, not a value, not an ordering.

This is pure movement plus comment edits: no logic, no conditions, no thresholds, no evaluation order, no defaults. `_ANSWER_SCHEMA_VERSION` is untouched, which is the point — nothing about the response moved, so charging every install a re-synthesis wave would buy nothing.

## Verification

The unit suite is the primary oracle and it covers this file heavily: full `tests/unit/server` passes, with no test edited. That constraint was load-bearing rather than decorative — if a test had needed changing, the refactor would have changed behaviour and the change would have needed explaining instead of fixing.

Beside it, a payload-level check built for exactly this kind of diff. It captures byte-comparable full responses on both sides of the refactor with the LLM removed as a variable, running three deterministic arms — no provider, a fixed synthesised string, and a synthesis failure — against a real indexed corpus with the answer cache disabled, so the whole post-synthesis cascade is exercised without prose variance moving underneath it. Captured before the change and after, the responses are identical.

An adversarial review of the diff ran alongside, comparing every moved definition at AST level with comments and docstrings stripped. It found one real loss: the only statement anywhere in the tree of why an inlined body deliberately carries no `verified` key, which had been cut as if it were evidence when it was a contract. Restored.

body:
Draft — do not merge. Implements **Slice 2** per **Issue #23**, stacked on `feat/autonomous-acquisition-v1` (`d3450a2`). Discovery only: it discovers, deduplicates, qualifies and feeds businesses into the reviewed Slice-1 pipeline, stopping at `DEMO_READY`. **Zero outreach; zero provider provisioning; zero production change; zero Smart Answer change.**

## Implemented
- **Schema** (`20260815140000_autonomous_discovery.sql`, manifest → 37): `discovery_missions` (bounded state, cursor, counts, cost + ceiling, retry, operator `import_seed`), `discovery_candidates` (provenance + layered `dedup_key` with `UNIQUE (mission_id, dedup_key)` for concurrency-safe claiming), `discovery_mission_events`. Service-role only.
- **Deterministic engine**: bounded, resumable, idempotent `advanceMission` (one page/call; no long-lived worker — Cloudflare/Nitro friendly). Explicit target / hard max-candidate / per-page / retry+backoff / metered-cost-ceiling bounds; state fully in the DB.
- **Provider adapter contract** + deterministic fixture/**import** provider (the lawful V1 source — operator supplies real businesses they may process). **Live discovery is an external dependency** (no lawful API/credential wired; no scraping).
- **Layered dedup**: canonical domain → provider id → phone → name+locality (both required, so same-name/different-locality independents never merge). Exact/format duplicates collapse on the unique key; the hard no-duplicate-prospect guarantee is the Slice-1 `prospects.canonical_domain` unique constraint.
- **Explainable pre-qualification** (reuses the hardened Slice-1 SSRF gate incl. 6to4/Teredo): reasons `insufficient_identity`, `not_target_vertical`, `outside_geography`, `no_website`, `unsafe_url`, `existing_prospect`.
- **Operator API + UI** `/acquisition/discovery`: create / start / pause / resume / cancel / advance, progress, disposition counts, explainable per-candidate outcomes. No public interface.

## Tested (all executed locally on this branch)
- **591/591** tests pass (**45** new discovery tests): mission lifecycle/auth, paging + transient-failure/retry, target/max/cost caps, vertical/geo filters, all dedup layers + same-name/different-locality prevention, qualification reasons, retry/resume idempotency, two-worker concurrency (no duplicate prospects), accepted → Slice-1 `DEMO_READY`, machine-checked no-outreach/no-provider + no-lifecycle-beyond-`demo_ready`.
- `tsc` clean · changed-file prettier + eslint clean · `verify:migrations` (37) · `verify:assets` · production Cloudflare build · `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` **exit 0** · `git diff --check` clean.

## Externally verified
- None. Reliability is a **synthetic** 101-candidate mission (no live business, no network): 91 demos built, 0 duplicate prospects, 0 duplicate demos, **0 outreach**; 1 phone-duplicate + 7 rejections (all reason codes) + 2 collapsed exact dups. See `docs/AUTONOMOUS_DISCOVERY_RELIABILITY.md`.

## Deferred
- Live discovery providers; continuous/scale discovery; all outreach (Slice 3).

## Safety
No email/SMS/voice, no outreach records, no Twilio/Vapi/Stripe provisioning or charge, no production deploy, no Smart Answer change. Changed-file surface is entirely the discovery slice + migration/manifest/CI/docs — no Slice-1/Smart Answer/other app code touched.

author: marcoaccardi
body:
Two migration slices from the fund plan (#249 ordering), one commit per issue so the PR reverts piecewise: #215's cycle shape first, #225's candidacy fields second. Both migrations are applied to **staging** (`eralyiwkfrpqsawivegz`) and `database.types.ts` is regenerated per slice. Production is untouched (#80 books both). Money stays off throughout — no Aura surface is touched (contributions and fund activity yield zero points, unchanged and still pgTAP-asserted).

Closes #215
Closes #225

## Slice (i) — cycle shape (`20260815075408_fund_cycle_shape.sql`)

- `year` + `fund_editions_year_active` → global one-active-cycle unique index `fund_editions_one_active` (`(phase <> 'closed') where phase <> 'closed'`); two non-closed cycles are a `23505`.
- Phase CHECK → `candidacy | screening | voting | announcement | realization | closed`; default `candidacy`.
- `voting_starts_at` / `voting_ends_at` (nullable, ordering CHECK) — data now, **#217 enforces the window**.
- `min_funding_cents` / `min_voters` / `min_candidacies` — **NOT NULL, no default** (FUND-SPEC §5 forcing function). pgTAP pins both halves: `col_not_null` + `col_hasnt_default`, and a `23502` per missing column.
- `split_pct` / `cost_fee_statement` / `equity_declared` — nullable shape only; **#232 owns the frozen-at-open semantics** and will tighten them.
- `getActiveEdition` resolves by the one-active invariant (no `year` sort); `fundPhaseSchema`, `PhaseList`, `annual.tsx`'s voting gate and the `fund.phase.*` i18n pairs (IT+EN, old four deleted, five new) follow in the same commit.

**Backfill values chosen for known rows** (staging's seeded 2027 world row; production carries no rows): phase map `community→voting` (behaviour-preserving — `community` was the votable phase and the seeded world sits there with votes), `reputation`/`ethics`→`screening`, `event`→`announcement`; minimums `min_funding_cents = 100000` (€1.000 against the €50.000 goal), `min_voters = 5` (the seed casts 6 → decisive), `min_candidacies = 3` (D7's working assumption; the seed holds exactly 3). These are chosen values for a fake world, not defaults — the columns stay default-less.

## Slice (ii) — candidacy fields (`20260815080109_candidacy_fields.sql`)

- `budget_cents bigint not null check (> 0)`; `min_viable_cents` beside it (`> 0` and `<= budget_cents`) — **ballot information, not the shortfall gate** (FUND-42 owns the gate; the column comment says so).
- `skills_needed text[]` ≤ 10, vocabulary membership against `@athanor/core` `SKILLS` enforced at the api boundary (`submitCandidacy` refuses an unknown key before any insert) — the `profiles.skills` (#149) pattern: the DB bounds shape, the app bounds vocabulary.
- `category` CHECK derived from the `project_category` enum **as-is** (`enum_range`, so the two can never drift): `startup | artistic | business | scientific | volunteer`.
- Nullable `dream_id` FK → `public.dreams`; both write policies gain `dream_id is null or athanor.owns_dream(dream_id)` via `ALTER POLICY` (names unchanged, `policies_are` lists intact; the DEFINER helper keeps an own-dream link valid across later soft-deletes). pgTAP: foreign dream denied on **insert and update**, own dream accepted.
- Zod: insert schema carries the new fields (skills/category/dream_id defaulted — #226 owns their wizard steps), rejects `budget_cents <= 0`, a non-integer budget, and a minimum above the budget.

**Backfill values chosen for known rows**: `marta_ceramica` €8.000 / €5.000 min, `ele_yoga` €12.000 / €6.000, `rocco_film` €15.000 / €9.000; categories `craft→artistic`, `wellbeing→volunteer` (§4's mapping, D-24); any tester-submitted staging row (the wizard could not declare a budget before this column existed) is placeholdered at €1.000/€1.000, and any other out-of-vocabulary category is nulled rather than failing the ALTER.

`supabase/staging-seed/seed-staging.sql` §12 now writes the cycle shape (no `year`, phase `voting`, the three minimums, a published voting window) and the candidacy budgets/categories/skills. The hourly world-refresh replays from the installed seed, so **the installer must be re-run** after this merges or the next refresh inserts rows the new constraints reject.

## Issue drift found by issue-check (both issues verified before work)

- #225 cites `candidacyUpdateSchema` / `updateCandidacy` (`candidacy.ts:52-80`) — both were deleted the day after the issue was filed (#272, commit `a5d5042`). Only `candidacyInsertSchema` / `submitCandidacy` exist; the payload work landed there. Resubmission (their future consumer) stays with #226.
- #215's Done-when grep (`\.year` in `packages/api/src/fund.ts`) was vacuously green before any change — the code read `year` as a string argument. The stricter check (`grep -n "year" packages/api/src/fund.ts`) now also returns nothing.

- **`fund.phase.*` i18n rewrite + `PhaseList`/`annual.tsx`** — the issue's Where list named no UI consumer; the schema enum change forces all three (typecheck).
- **pgTAP fixture sweep** — 0041/0042/0044/0045/0046/0078 all inserted `fund_editions` with `year`/old phases; every fixture now supplies the three minimums.

- Staging voting stays walkable (seed phase `voting`, `cast_vote` gates `voting`); the window columns are published but unenforced until #217.

author: punxsyprominence
body:
Answers open decision 4 in the evidence-baseline handoff — *who may write platform rows beyond an operator running the importer* — which the owner decided as **operator-only**. This makes that enforceable rather than a convention. Branched from `origin/main` at `4289a6fe676b2c430c2de471796709cbd0dc5df0`.

## Handoff

| Item | Classification | Evidence | Change | Tests | Blocker/Next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Operator-only" was a convention, not a check | OWNER_DECISION → VERIFIED_GAP | Owner decided operator-only; nothing failed if a write path were widened | New convention gate, both directions + route sweep | 23/23 | None |
| Principals cannot exist in `__platform__` | EXISTING | `platformLibraryScope.pg.test.ts` proves the three CHECK guards against real Postgres | None — not duplicated | n/a | n/a |

## What this guards that the database cannot

The database already covers half: no account, membership or athlete may reference the reserved organization, so no principal can exist there and no principal-derived write can land there.

The half a CHECK cannot reach is the **application deliberately aiming at it**. The read paths were widened on purpose; the write paths were deliberately left alone. That asymmetry is invisible in review — the two are one helper call apart — and a widened write would put one gym's uploads into the corpus every other tenant reads.

**Pinned in both directions**, the way the response validator's cases are:

- **Must not widen (8):** `createShadowLibrarySource` / `Document` / `Chunk`, `listShadowLibrarySources`, `reviewShadowLibrarySource`, `listShadowLibraryReviewQueue`, `upsertShadowCapabilityMap`, and `listApprovedGlobalEvidenceForResearchBridge` — the last for a different reason than the rest: it is an *export*, and including the baseline would ship the platform corpus out as though it were one gym's evidence.
- **Must keep widening:** `searchShadowLibrary`, `persistEvidenceBundle`, `hasRetrievableLibraryEvidence`, the rabbit-hole citation join's literal, and the conversation history join's `ei.library_organization_id`.

A one-directional test would pass just as happily against a build where retrieval had quietly stopped returning the baseline at all.

**Plus a route sweep:** no file under `app/api` may name the reserved organization, by constant or by literal. Every route derives `organization_id` from the authenticated principal, so a route naming it at all would be reaching past that. The only legitimate writer is the importer, which is a script.

## A mistake of mine, recorded

My first extractor required `export`, and `persistEvidenceBundle` is module-private — so it reported the single most important write path as un-widened when it is in fact widened, correctly, three lines from the insert (`library_organization_id` set from `c.organization_id`, lookup scoped by `any($11::text[])`).

I read the source before believing my own tool, so nothing was filed as a defect. The extractor now admits both forms, terminates on a line that is **only** a closing brace — these signatures end `}): Promise<T> {`, which also starts at column zero, so the naive "first line beginning with `}`" ends the body at the parameter type — and a vacuity test fails if any named function stops being found or returns a stub.

## Falsification

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Widen a write path (`createShadowLibraryChunk`) | 1 of 23 fails |
| Un-widen a read path (`persistEvidenceBundle`) | 1 fails |
| Add a route naming the reserved organization | 1 fails |

Each fails exactly one test — precise rather than a shotgun — and all revert clean to 23/23.

## Results

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `jest --runTestsByPath src/server/pilot/platformLibraryWriteScope.convention.test.ts` | **23/23** |
| `npm --workspace web run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm --workspace web run lint` | **0 errors**, 11 pre-existing warnings |
| `npm --workspace web test` | **394 suites, 5322 tests** |

## Scope

One new file. **No `package.json` change** — jest's `testMatch` already collects `*.test.ts`, so this needs no wiring and does not touch the migration chain, which also means no collision with #360.

No source file is modified: this only observes. No database was touched and no workflow dispatched.

Admins and submitters get notified on the Community inbox, website suggestions can hand off to staff site-create, and only the active tab is paginated. ## Notifications - Admins get an in-app bell on new problems, suggestions, and website requests (admin role only; marketing is not notified) - Guest problem reports also write an activity log - Submitters get a bell (when logged in) and email when status **leaves pending** - Notes-only or later status changes do not send again - Blank report emails fall back to the submitter’s account address - Review emails use the public app host (`publicRoute` / `app_public_url`) - Leaving-pending status updates are compare-and-swap (already-reviewed → 422, no second mail) - Types: `community_feedback_reviewed`, `website_suggestion_reviewed` (`system_updates` preference) ## Website suggestion → create listing - **Create listing** prefills staff site-create (`site_name`, `site_url`, ISO country/language, `suggestion_id`) - Saving that listing marks the suggestion **accepted** only when the new listing domain matches - Integer `suggestion_id` is kept; arrays/booleans do not coerce to `1` - A stale or missing `suggestion_id` does not fail site-create - Rejected/reviewed suggestions for the same domain are accepted when the listing is saved; already-accepted rows are not mailed again - Accept in the inbox does **not** auto-create a site - If the domain already occupies a catalog row: **Already in catalog** → edit that listing ## Performance - Only the active Community tab is paginated; the other three tabs get an empty paginator ## Tests `CommunityInboxTest`, `CommunityFeedbackTest`, and `AdminAssignSiteForPublisherTest` cover notify-once, listing handoff, domain-match accept, rejected recovery, stale/array suggestion ids, occupying-domain link, catalog/email-center previews, and active-tab pagination.

author: ll-nick
body:
The `trigger` type got one more member: `AFTER_PREVIOUS` automatically starts an animations after the previous animation finished playing. This also allows auto-playing animations after entering a slide if the first animation cue uses that trigger.

Under the hood, a few things changes to make this trigger simple and robust to work. Instead of using the wall-clock to trigger animations, the animation engine now uses the same progress-driven approach the transitions already have: Each step is a continuous movement across a progress from 0 to 1. Reversing that is trivial and so is snapping to the end. `WITH_PREVIOUS` and `AFTER_PREVIOUS` are part of a single progress chain, with their start offset from the `progress=0` by the offset and duration of their predecessors.

author: allplays-paulbot[bot]
body:
Closes #4673

## What changed
- Retain and reuse the latest normalized admin-user search result.
- Share one in-flight promise across concurrent same-term renders.
- Apply official-status filters locally against retained candidates and official links.
- Invalidate candidate and official-link state after successful official mutations.
- Preserve existing candidate and enrichment query ceilings.

## Root Cause
The debounce helper treated every render as a new search generation. Official-status changes therefore canceled or repeated remote candidate discovery even when the normalized query was unchanged.

## Prevention / Learning
Separate remote candidate acquisition from local rendering filters. Key retained async work by normalized inputs and provide explicit invalidation for mutations that can change candidates or enrichment state.

## Regression Tests
- Same normalized terms share in-flight and completed results.
- Different terms trigger one new search while stale responses remain suppressed.
- Explicit invalidation forces the next same-term reload.
- All, Officials, and Non-officials filters produce expected rows with one remote search.
- Cache-delivery and query-ceiling checks remain green.

## Recurrence Risk
Low. Focused tests cover reuse, invalidation, filtering, stale suppression, and unchanged query ceilings.

author: d3xt3r1ty
body:
Bridge 1.5.5 based on the 1.5.4 runtime log.

The log proves the D2 manual-snapshot command is still using channel 1 (`Captured requested snapshot for D2 using channel 1`). This is because existing Home Assistant saved `cameras:` options predate the later `snapshot_channel` field; updating config.yaml defaults does not retrofit fields into that saved list. Runtime camera definitions now apply D2=2 / D3=1 defaults when those fields are absent, while preserving explicit user values.

For day/night, D2 was being disabled by capability probing because 1.5.3/1.5.4 tried to GET the native UI's `Private/Exposure` write endpoint. 1.5.5 now reads current state from ordinary `Image/Advanced/Exposure`, uses ImageCapabilities to establish support, and reserves `Image/Advanced/Private/Exposure/` for the D2 PUT observed in the packet capture.

- runtime D2 snapshot/image-control defaults for existing saved HA options
- D3 runtime defaults remain channel 1
- generic Exposure GET for D2 day/night state/readback
- native Private/Exposure PUT retained for D2 writes
- day/night support may be established from ImageCapabilities
- bump to 1.5.5

author: istefox
body:
Closes #60.

`_bookmarks/_assets/` only ever grew. Three call sites trashed a bookmark note and none of them touched its cover: `deleteBookmark` and `deleteBrokenSelected` in `bookmark-view.ts`, and `applyDedup` in `organize-dedup.ts`. Deduplication was the worst of the three, because `readDedupNote` awards a cover 100 points of richness score, so the loser of any group where both notes had one was orphaned every single time.

## The change

New `src/cover-gc.ts` owns `trashBookmarks(app, settings, notes)`. All three call sites go through it; nothing calls `fileManager.trashFile` on a bookmark note directly any more. A cover is reclaimed as a consequence of deleting the bookmark that owned it, never as a separate sweep the user has to remember to run.

Three rules gate every asset deletion:

1. **Only inside the assets folder.** `setCoverFromVault` lets a user point a bookmark at any image they already own. That image outlives the bookmark unconditionally; the plugin only reclaims what the plugin downloaded.
2. **Only when nothing else references it.** References are counted across the vault with the notes being trashed excluded. Two bookmarks sharing one picked image is a real case, and so is a user embedding the image in an unrelated note.
3. **`fileManager.trashFile`, never `vault.delete`.** Removal honours the "Deleted files" preference and stays recoverable, the same rule the note deletions already followed.

Reference counting reads the `image` frontmatter directly and unions `resolvedLinks` on top. It does not rely on `resolvedLinks` alone: frontmatter links depend on Obsidian's `frontmatterLinks` support, and a cover must not be deleted because a cache did not list it.

Covers are read before anything is trashed and counted after, excluding the just-trashed paths. That is correct whether or not the metadata cache has caught up; a plain scan-after-delete is not.

Failures never cascade. A note that fails to trash keeps its cover, because the reference scan finds the surviving note. A cover that fails to trash is logged and skipped, leaving the already-successful note deletion alone.

`applyDedup` now merges every victim first and trashes the survivors as one batch, so two victims sharing a cover release it. The existing invariant holds: a victim whose merge failed is still never trashed.

No new setting. The cleanup touches only files this plugin downloaded, into its own folder, only when nothing references them, and recoverably. A toggle would be a setting whose "off" position means the folder grows forever. Rationale and the rejected alternatives are in `docs/architecture/ADR-005-cover-garbage-collection.md`; ADR-003's "orphan cleanup is not implemented" bullet now points at it.

## Verification

`npm run build` and `npm run lint` green, on top of the merged bookmark bar.

A throwaway 29-assertion harness over `cover-gc.ts` with a stub `App` covers: wikilink resolution including the hand-edited nested-array shape, a remote cover and an empty cover yielding nothing, a non-image target refused, the happy path, an image outside the assets folder surviving, a sibling `_assets-old/` folder not matching, a custom root folder moving the assets folder with it, a second bookmark protecting a shared cover, both sharers deleted releasing it once, a body embed elsewhere protecting it, the note's own embed not protecting its own cover, a failed note deletion keeping its cover, a partial batch, an empty batch, and a cover that cannot be trashed leaving the note deletion reported as successful.

Not verified: the manual checks in Obsidian. Save a cover and delete the card; point two bookmarks at one picked image and delete them one at a time; point a bookmark at an image elsewhere in the vault and delete it; run Deduplicate on a group where both notes have local covers.

## Migration

None. Assets orphaned by earlier versions stay where they are; nothing scans for them retroactively.

# Description

This PR expands the documentation for building apps with the UI5 view builder, focusing on two critical areas:

1. **Chain formatting rules** — Adds comprehensive guidance on how to format method chains for readability and maintainability:

   - Use variables to return to nodes instead of unwinding with multiple `end()`s

   - Explains why it matters (ABAP editor strips trailing blanks on save)

Also updates the ABAP check skill description to mention trailing whitespace as a known gap in CI checks.

body:
## Summary

Navya told leads in mid-August 2026 that BPT counselling "hasn't started yet" and promised rounds in May/June — months already gone. No prompt ever stated today's date: WhatsApp Navya and the website chat injected none at all, and the voice agent used `toISOString()` (UTC), so after 18:30 IST it reported yesterday. Compounding it, `loadCounsellingUpdates` returned `""` when `counselling_sources` had no fresh row, which dropped the *"never state a round date not listed here"* guardrail along with the data — it now returns an explicit "you have NO verified dates" block and logs the query error, so the agents deflect instead of inventing even while the scraper is down.

## Changes

- **`buildTemporalContext` / `buildTemporalLine`** in `web-chat-server/knowledge.ts`, mirrored in `voice-agent/knowledge.ts` (the two services build from their own Dockerfile context) and re-exported through `_shared/nimt-admissions-context.ts` for the edge functions. Wired into WhatsApp Navya, website Navya, the voice agent and the staff copilot. Session rolls over in **April**, not January.
- Reworded the static `Application window: January–July` line, which read as "closed" in August.
- `counselling-watch`: IST for its own `Today is`, and it now accepts the vault `CRON_SECRET` as well as the service-role bearer.
- Migration repoints the cron at the `x-cron-secret` header that other working crons use.

## Testing

`web-chat-server/temporal.test.ts` — 3 passing tests covering the April session rollover, the guardrail text, and the `19:30Z` case that proves the UTC bug is gone. `deno check` clean on all touched files. The three edge functions are already deployed to prod and the previously-missing `counselling_updates_watch` migration has been applied (its ledger version reconciled to the committed filename).

## Known gap

The `counselling-watch` cron still cannot authenticate — **both** `_app_config.service_role_key` and `vault.CRON_SECRET` mismatch the edge env (each verified 401). The function accepts either credential, but neither stored value is correct, so no live counselling dates flow yet. Fixing it means rotating a secret shared with other crons (whatsapp-buffer-worker, marketing dispatcher), which needs a human decision. Until then Navya deflects on round dates rather than inventing them — the correct failure mode.

## Related Issues

None.

## Summary

This PR refactors the `popover_display` method in `z2ui5_cl_smp_app_052` to follow the chain-building conventions documented in AGENTS.md, and adds linting rules to enforce these patterns across the codebase.

## Key Changes

- **Refactored popover chain structure**: Split the deeply nested method chain into separate statements using intermediate variables (`DATA(popover)`), improving readability and making the XML tree structure explicit through indentation. Each subtree now starts on its own line with consistent indentation that reflects the hierarchy.

- **Improved chain formatting**: 
  - Removed long runs of `end()` calls that obscured the tree structure
  - Aligned attributes and elements to show their relationship clearly
  - Ensured each statement's indentation monotonically reflects nesting depth

- **Added `chain-indentation` linting rule**: Enabled in `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` as a warning to catch chains that break their own rhythm (siblings at different indentation levels, calls misaligned with their elements).

- **Added `whitespace_end` linting rule**: Enabled in `abaplint.jsonc` to catch trailing whitespace that the ABAP editor strips on save, preventing spurious diffs in future commits.

- **Updated AGENTS.md**: Documented the three rules that keep chain layouts truthful:
  1. Indent states depth — one level per container with consistent step size
  2. Never unwind with `end()` runs to start siblings — use variables instead
  3. Controls may share lines with their attributes or opening containers, but not whole subtrees

## Implementation Details

The refactored `popover_display` now demonstrates the documented pattern: intermediate variables (`popover`) are assigned once, then reused in separate statements for each major subtree (SimpleForm content, footer toolbar). This makes the XML hierarchy immediately visible from indentation alone, matching the corpus conventions described in AGENTS.md section 10.

author: zethasaintlab
body:
Menutup kaki ketiga gate F5: merchant dapat menghubungkan tablet kasirnya sendiri, tanpa bantuan.

Dua endpoint yang brief-nya asumsikan ada ternyata **tidak ada** — keduanya dibangun di sini.

---

## ⛔ `GET /devices` tidak pernah ada

`POST /devices`, `/devices/{id}/credentials`, `/devices/{id}/sync-token`, dan `/devices/{id}/revoke` semuanya lengkap sejak F2/F3. Tidak ada satu pun cara **membaca** daftarnya. Layar manajemen perangkat yang tidak dapat menampilkan perangkat yang sudah ada bukan layar manajemen.

| Keputusan | Alasan |
|---|---|
| `token_hash` **tidak pernah** dikirim | Ia SHA-256 dari secret perangkat. Layar hanya perlu tahu **apakah** kredensial sudah diterbitkan (`adaKredensial`), bukan nilainya |
| Perangkat **dicabut tetap ikut**, dengan `revokedAt` | `order.device_id` menunjuknya. Menyembunyikannya membuat merchant membuat ulang dengan kode yang sama — dan `ux_device_outlet_code` hanya menolak yang aktif, jadi itu **berhasil** dan menghasilkan dua perangkat berkode sama |
| Urutan dijamin SQL | `ORDER BY (revoked_at IS NOT NULL), code` — bukan di JS |

`GET /outlets` ditambahkan karena layar harus **memilih** outlet; tanpa daftar ia hanya dapat meminta UUID sebagai teks — masalah yang sama dengan field "ID Tenant" di layar masuk.

---

## ⛔ "PIN sementara" tidak dapat membawa pemasangan ini

Perangkat kasir butuh **enam** nilai (`packages/sync-client/src/perangkat.ts`): `deviceId`, `deviceCode`, `tenantId`, `outletId`, `baseUrl`, `tokenSecret`. Yang terakhir sendiri 43 karakter base64url dari CSPRNG — memendekkannya berarti memperlemah kredensialnya.

Yang ditampilkan: keenamnya satu per satu (bentuk yang layar K-15 kasir terima **hari ini**) **plus** satu baris kode pemasangan yang membungkus semuanya, untuk saat K-15 diberi kotak tempel. K-15 sendiri sudah menyebut bentuk yang dituju: *"kasir memindai/menempelkannya sekali"*.

Kodenya berawalan **`LUMI1.`** supaya pembaca yang lebih baru dapat **menolak** kode lama alih-alih menerimanya separuh — perangkat yang tersambung setengah gagal berhari-hari kemudian, di outlet. base64url tanpa padding: tanpa `=`, `+`, `/`, spasi, atau baris baru, karena ia disalin dari layar lalu ditempel di tablet.

⛔ **Kode itu bukan enkripsi, dan ada test yang menyematkan kenyataan itu.** Siapa pun yang memegangnya memegang secret perangkat. Ia dibungkus supaya menjadi *satu* hal yang disalin, bukan supaya aman disebar.

---

## ⛔ Cacat yang hanya browser dapat tunjukkan

Versi pertama memakai `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? window.location.origin` sebagai alamat server di kode pemasangan. Dijalankan, ia menghasilkan **`http://localhost:1422`** — origin **back-office**, bukan API (3000).

Perangkat yang dipasang dengan kode itu menembak Vite dev server, dan gejalanya muncul **di outlet** sebagai sinkronisasi yang tidak pernah jalan. Typecheck bersih, lint bersih, layar terlihat benar.

Penyebabnya **dua sumber kebenaran** untuk satu alamat: `sesi.tsx` memakai `?? 'http://localhost:3000'`, layar ini `?? window.location.origin`. `baseUrl` sekarang diekspos `useSesi()`. Diverifikasi dengan membongkar kode pemasangan di browser: `http://localhost:3000`.

---

## Keputusan lain

- Blok kredensial menyatakan ia hanya dapat dibaca **sekali**, dan **ditutup** begitu perangkatnya dicabut — menampilkan kode pemasangan untuk perangkat yang baru dicabut adalah instruksi yang dijamin gagal.
- Pesan server dipakai apa adanya: *"Kode K1 sudah dipakai device … di outlet ini"* menyebut perangkatnya.
- Status membawa **teks**, tidak pernah warna saja (aturan DS #5).
- `1px solid` dihapus — `lint:ds` menolak nilai piksel mentah (aturan #6), meski `components.css` sendiri memakainya di mana-mana.

---

## Diverifikasi di browser terhadap server sungguhan

```
tambah K1 → terbitkan kredensial → kode LUMI1.… membongkar jadi enam field
yang benar → cabut → blok kredensial tertutup, perangkat tetap terlihat
bertanda "Dicabut"
```

## Verifikasi

```
backoffice 62 · identity 69 · tenancy 47 · catalog 161 · ordering 134
payment 127 · isolation 199 · domain 212 · kasir 272 · sync-client 95
server 26 · schema 14 · runtime 3 · ds-adherence 10      — 0 fail
typecheck bersih · lint:ds bersih · build 228,0 kB / 71,4 kB gzip
```

---

## Koreksi terhadap laporan saya sebelumnya

Saya menyebut `POST /users` termasuk endpoint tanpa penjaga peran. **Itu salah** — ia punya `assertBolehKelola`, yang saya lewatkan karena grep saya mencari `assertBoleh(` dengan kurung. Lubang RBAC yang sebenarnya lebih sempit: `POST /items` dan seluruh permukaan katalog, `/catalog/import`, `POST /devices`, `/credentials`, `/revoke`, dan `/tax-rates`. Itu pekerjaan branch berikutnya (`sec-rbac-sweep`).

author: yasuflatland-lf
body:
Release v1.0.0 — the first stable release of gashuu.

Version bump for both workspace crates (`gashuu`, `gashuu-core`) 0.18.0 → 1.0.0 plus the
lockfile sync. **No application behavior changed since v0.18.0** — this release promotes the
0.18 line to 1.0 and carries the dependency, CI, and documentation work merged since.

## What 1.0.0 means

The reader is feature-complete for the scope it set out to cover: folders and CBZ/ZIP/CBR/RAR
archives, two-page manga spreads, per-book view settings, a cover-flow library with
continue-reading, and in-app updates — all shipped, gate-green, and exercised by 975 tests.
1.0.0 is the point where that surface stops moving under users: settings and library files on
disk have a stable, versioned schema, and the keyboard map and view semantics are no longer
expected to change between releases.

Distribution is unchanged: macOS (universal `.app`), Windows (x64 portable), and Linux
(`.deb` + AppImage), with in-app self-update on the platforms that support it.

## Highlights

- **Sources** — a folder of PNG/JPG/JPEG/AVIF images, or a `.cbz`/`.zip`/`.cbr`/`.rar`
  archive, detected by extension or magic bytes. Archive extraction is in-memory; unsafe,
  oversized, or corrupt entries are skipped and counted, and a badly damaged archive still
  opens with the pages that survived.
- **Library** — a cover-flow carousel with real cover art, per-book progress bars, numeric-aware
  title order, live search, selection mode with bulk delete, and a continue-reading bookmark
  that re-focuses the book you last read.
- **Spreads & direction** — single / double / auto spreads that follow window resizes,
  right-to-left (manga) or left-to-right binding, standalone or paired cover.
- **Per-book view settings** — direction, spread, cover layout, and fit mode are remembered
  per book with a fallback to your global defaults, and can be reset back to them.
- **Zoom, pan, and fast turns** — cursor-anchored wheel zoom, drag pan, Whole/Width/Actual fit,
  an LRU decoded-page cache with background prefetch, a thumbnail strip, and an RTL-aware
  page scrubber.
- **Bilingual UI** — English / 日本語, switched instantly from the Settings dialog.
- **Safe decoding** — oversized images and decompression bombs are rejected before allocation
  (16384×16384 px / 512 MiB / ~128 Mpx limits) with a status-bar error instead of an OOM crash.

## Since v0.18.0

### Security

- `lru` and `webbrowser` bumped to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0253 and RUSTSEC-2026-0257.
- `i18n-embed-fl` bumped to 0.10.1, which drops the transitive `proc-macro-error2` dependency —
  the RUSTSEC-2026-0173 ignore has been removed from `deny.toml` rather than carried forward.

### Build / CI

- Renovate automerges non-major updates (minor, patch, pin, digest) and lockfile maintenance
  once every status check is green; major bumps still wait for a human.
- Toolchain pins refreshed: `cargo-nextest` 0.9.143, `cargo-binstall` 1.21.1, and the
  `Swatinem/rust-cache` action digest across the CI and release workflows.
- Lockfile maintenance advanced transitive crates so upstream advisories drop out on their own.

### Docs

- `docs/toolchain.md` documents the Renovate automerge policy and its `deny.toml` consequence:
  an automerged lockfile refresh can make an advisory ignore stale, and cargo-deny's
  `--deny advisory-not-detected` is what catches it.
- The documented Rust pin now matches `mise.toml`: `README.md`, `docs/toolchain.md`, and ADR-0002
  all said 1.96.0 while the toolchain has moved to 1.97.1.

## Verification

Local gates green: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `nextest` 975/975 passed,
`check-tokens.sh`, `check-docs.sh`.

**Self-update + relaunch: NOT verified hands-on for this release.** The per-release checklist in
`docs/toolchain.md` (a real Windows host, and a real Linux host where available) has not been run
for v0.18.0 or for this release, so the self-replace, relaunch, and session-persistence path is
covered only by the automated gates — neither the gates nor `release.yml` can accept a GUI update
prompt or inspect the relaunched process. No code on that path changed since v0.18.0. This note
will be updated once the checklist has been run.

author: chemistreal
body:
> *"다크모드는 안해도돼. 다크모드하지마. 다양한 기능을 넣으라고했어. 디자인도 화려한것을 100배 더 화려하게 해주고. 그걸 다시 더 개선해서 화려하게 만들어줘"*

## 다크 모드는 흔적 없이 걷어냈습니다

토큰 두 벌 · 단추 · 자바스크립트 · 검사 · CI 단계 · 저장 칸 장부까지. **남은 것 0.**

## 화려한 것이 장식이 아니라 차례가 되게

숫자 칸 셋이 흰 상자로 나란히 서 있었습니다. 다 맞는 숫자인데 **아무것도 먼저 보이지 않았습니다** — 눈이 셋을 차례로 읽고 스스로 견줘야 했습니다.

- **놋쇠 실선**과 겹친 그라데이션 — 이 저장소가 모든 머리띠에 쓰는 표식을 이었습니다
- **큰 숫자 셋** + 왼쪽 색띠. 급한 칸이 0 이 아니면 색띠가 **3.2초에 한 번 아주 천천히 숨 쉽니다**(빠르면 성가십니다)
- **통과율 고리** — 비율은 막대보다 고리가 한눈에 읽힙니다
- 그 아래 **몫 막대**(색 + 빗금)와 범례
- 맨 밑 **한 문장** — 「미응시 4명 · 재시 4명 남았습니다」. **색이 안 보이는 분께는 이 줄이 본체입니다**

**숫자가 0에서 차오릅니다.** 예쁘자고가 아니라 「방금 시트에서 받아 왔다」 는 뜻이라 **값이 달라졌을 때만** 돕니다. 30초마다 도는 새로고침에서 매번 꿈틀거리면 정작 자료가 바뀐 순간을 못 알아봅니다. 움직임 줄이기를 켠 기기에서는 한 번에 최종값을 적습니다.

> 여기 뜨는 것은 `renderFig` 가 쓰던 것과 **같은 배열**입니다. 세는 자리는 그대로 하나이고 그리는 자리만 위로 옮겼습니다 — 도넛·막대가 위아래로 두 번 있던 것을 한자리에 모았습니다.

## 반별 현황도 올렸습니다

- **몫 막대**를 반마다 — 「8명 중 3」 이 큰지 작은지 눈으로 나누지 않아도 됩니다
- **정렬 바꾸기**: 급한 순 · 이름 순 · 인원 순

## 만들다 제가 낸 거짓말

머리판 밑에 **「위 숫자를 누르면 그 사람들 이름으로 바로 갑니다」** 라고 적어 놓고, 그 숫자는 **눌리지 않는 상자**였습니다.

화면에 적은 말은 참이어야 합니다 — 갈 데가 있는 칸은 단추로, 없는 칸은 상자로 세우고, **눌러서 실제로 가는지 자로 박았습니다**(70px, 손가락 기준 넉넉).

## 자들이 잡아 준 것

옛 선택자(`.card`)를 보던 자 넷을 새 자리(`.hn`)로 옮겼습니다 — `hub.js` · `hub-touch` · `hub-a11y`. 지키려던 것(「급한 것이 앞에 온다」 · 「한 뜻에 한 이름인가」)은 그대로 두고 **보는 자리만** 바꿨습니다.

`hub-a11y` 의 WebGL 칸은 3D 가 없어졌으니 「없으면 조용히 안 그린다」 가 아니라 **애초에 그릴 것이 없다** 로 고쳤습니다.

그리고 앞에서 이름 순으로 바꿔 놓고 뒤에서 급한 순을 기대한 **제 검사 순서 문제**도 자가 잡았습니다.
