둘 다 **실제로 사고가 난 뒤에** 적는 규칙이다.

## 푸시한 브랜치의 히스토리를 다시 쓰지 않는다

F02와 F05가 각각 `main` #10을 받으려 rebase했다가 non-fast-forward를 만났다. 둘 다 force-push 없이 원격 팁 위에 변경분을 재적용해 풀었다 — 그 대응이 맞아서 규칙으로 굳힌다.

**왜 force-push가 특히 이 프로젝트에서 나쁜가.** 여러 세션이 같은 저장소를 보고 있어서, 원격 히스토리가 바뀌면 **다른 세션이 이미 받아간 커밋이 사라진 것처럼 보인다.** 세션끼리 커밋 해시로 "이거 푸시했다"고 알리는 방식도 그 순간 무너진다.

- `main`의 파일을 **읽기만** 하면 되면 `git show origin/main:<경로>`로 충분하다
- rebase는 **통합 직전 한 번만.** 그때는 PR로 병합하므로 브랜치를 원격에 다시 밀 필요가 없다

## 번호를 주고받을 때는 소유자를 붙인다

PM(나)이 F02의 `S4`를 출처 없이 F04에 전달했는데, **F04의 번호 체계에도 다른 `S4`가 있었다.**

F04가 번호가 아니라 **내용으로 판단해** 자기 `S7-D`에 매핑해서 넘어갔다. 하지만 내용이 조금만 덜 특징적이었으면 **엉뚱한 회차에 반영되고 아무도 몰랐을 것이다.**

- 세션 경계를 넘으면 `F02 S4`처럼 소유자를 앞에 붙인다
- **받는 쪽은 번호가 자기 것과 맞아떨어져도 내용을 확인한다.** 우연히 맞는 번호가 가장 위험하다

문서만 변경.

## Summary
Follow-up to #1.

### Part 1 — silent paste failures
After the `navigator.clipboard.write` patch (internal-copy detection), the user reported that turning **Allow Comfy Image ON** in Global Options still failed to paste. Re-audited `pasteImageIntoSelectedNode()` / `getGlobalSettings()`: the gating logic itself was correct. The real problem was several completely silent failure paths (no node selected, no Global Options node / duplicate nodes, swallowed upload errors) that looked indistinguishable from an intentional block. Added targeted `console.log` diagnostics at each one.

### Part 2 — removed non-functional focus_text_tab / focus_image_tab
User confirmed the tab-focus options never actually brought the ComfyUI window/tab forward. Root cause: `window.focus()` is only honored by modern browsers when called synchronously inside a real user gesture (click/keypress). These calls happen inside async `clipboard.text`/`clipboard.image` websocket event handlers, which are never a user gesture — so the feature was silently a no-op in every modern browser, indistinguishable from a bug. Rather than leave a dead checkbox, removed it end-to-end per user request:
- `nodes.py`: dropped `focus_text_tab`/`focus_image_tab` widgets and params from `ClipboardSafetyOptions`.
- `web/clipboard_extension.js`: dropped `focusOnText`/`focusOnImage` from `getGlobalSettings()`, removed the unused `requestComfyTabFocus()` helper and its call sites.
- `README.md`: updated feature description / node table.

## Versions
- 1.0.9 → 1.0.10: diagnostic logging for silent paste failures.
- 1.0.10 → 1.0.11: removed focus_text_tab/focus_image_tab.

## Testing
- `node -e "new Function(...)"` syntax check on the JS file (passes).
- `python3 -m py_compile nodes.py` (passes).
- No ComfyUI runtime available in sandbox; awaiting user's manual verification in their environment.

## Summary

Implement the next bounded #75 UI slice on top of merged U0-U3:

- logical-canvas pointer hit testing over the single resolved `UiDocument` geometry authority,
- reverse authored/painter-order overlap semantics,
- hover + primary press/capture/release state,

## Performance / ownership

Normal logical pointer routing performs one allocation-free O(N) reverse contiguous hit scan plus O(1) direct-index mutations. UI does not duplicate #88 conversion math or add a Render dependency.

Clipping/scroll, modal/focus scopes, keyboard/gamepad navigation and practical image/progress/scroll widgets remain later #75 slices. No generic callback graph or speculative spatial index is introduced.

author: jcwearn
body:
Stacked on the config PR. **Base is `chore/oxlint-strict`, not `main`** — review that one first.

## What the strict config caught

`react/only-export-components`, promoted from `warn` to `error`, flags `src/components/ui/button.tsx:48` for exporting a non-component beside a component. That breaks fast refresh.

It fires **despite `allowConstantExport: true`**, because `buttonVariants` is a `cva()` call rather than a constant expression — which is exactly why the option didn't already cover it.

This finding has existed all along; CI was green through it because warnings don't affect oxlint's exit code.

## The fix: stop exporting it

shadcn's generator emits `buttonVariants` as a named export so consumers can style a link like a button. **Nothing in this repo imports it** — I checked. It was dead API surface.

So the fix is to remove the export, not to split it into its own module for a consumer that doesn't exist. It stays a local `const` and `Button` still uses it. One line changed instead of a new file.

The comment left in the file says what to do if that changes — move the `cva()` call to its own module rather than re-adding the export — and warns that `shadcn add button` will reinstate the combined form and reintroduce the error.

## Verification

```
oxlint findings: 0      lint exit: 0
format:check PASS   lint PASS   typecheck PASS   test PASS   build PASS
```

## Merge order

Merge this into `chore/oxlint-strict`, then that into `main` as one unit — so `main` never sees the red intermediate state.

body:
Adds `SPEC.md` — the machine contract downstream BMad skills consume — and closes two stale items the spec run surfaced in the architecture spine.

## The spec kernel

`_bmad-output/specs/spec-django-15-factor-base/`

Ten capabilities (`CAP-1`..`CAP-10`, one per PRD feature group), fourteen constraints, fourteen non-goals, four assumptions, four open questions.

**The PRD, its addendum and the spine are adopted companions, not absorbed sources — `sources:` is empty.** Each FR carries a *Consequences (testable)* block that downstream must read to implement or verify, so absorbing them would have meant re-rendering the PRD into a companion. They stay owned by `bmad-prd` and `bmad-architecture`.

`capability-map.md` carries the `CAP-N` → FR/NFR/SC/CG/AD crosswalk. That binding exists nowhere else — neither the PRD nor the spine keys anything on stable capability IDs. It also records three coverage gaps found while building it:

- CAP-8 (observability) and CAP-9 (supply chain) have no governing AD — the spine covers both through conventions and R-1 rather than a numbered invariant.
- CAP-9 and CAP-10 have no success criterion in the PRD's SC set; SC-1..SC-7 do not validate FR-49..FR-56.
- Two spine open items sit in CAP-8 with no owner: the FR-45 OTLP export test and the NFR-6 telemetry-overhead measurement.

## The spine reconciliation

The five PRD divergences (`D-1`..`D-5`) were closed by commit b8a3fd9, which amended the PRD **six minutes** after the spine landed — not the next day, as the spec run first recorded. Each was re-checked against current PRD text; the PRD now states the spine's position in its own words. Recorded as reconciled rather than deleted, so a later reader does not re-open a settled question. D-3's pointer to residual risk R-2 is preserved.

`binds:` read `FR-1..FR-50` while the PRD runs to FR-56. The spine already governed FR-51..FR-56 in substance via AD-4..AD-9, AD-28 and AD-29, so only the declared range was wrong.

`walkthrough.html` section 05 still presented the divergences as live disagreements. Left stale it would send all three of its declared audiences back to questions the PRD had already answered.

**Reconciliation only** — no AD, invariant, convention, stack entry, residual risk, open item or deferred entry changed. 32 ADs unchanged.

## Still open, and not fixable here

`prd.md` frontmatter carries `updated: 2026-08-16` — a day later than its own commit and a day in the future. That is `bmad-prd`'s artifact; it is logged as the successor to the resolved spine-staleness question in `SPEC.md`.

The four substantive open questions (session revocation latency, FR-45 test owner, NFR-6 measurement owner, portal order-surface field list) remain unanswered with their existing owners.

## Verification

- `lint_spine.py` — 0 findings
- `pixi run ci` — green (107 passed, 92.31% coverage with templates measured, ruff clean, mypy clean, build succeeded)
- Docs only; no source changed

author: joshbotts
body:
Your decision on #906's open question: **option 2**, the mode-carrying request. So Person Analytics gets an iPad window keyed by Trends/Network, and the rankings dashboard and the co-mention ego network can sit side by side instead of taking turns behind a segmented control.

The fifth analytics window — and the **first whose request type had to be created** rather than adopted. The previous four all had value-shaped payloads already.

## The mode is window identity, not seed state

`openWindow(value:)` focuses the existing window for an equal request, so Trends and Network open as two windows while asking twice for Trends focuses the one already showing it.

It is deliberately **not a freeze**: the picker inside a window still switches modes in place. A reader who opens Trends and flips it to Network therefore has one window showing Network, and opening Network from the menu then focuses the *other* window. That is the ordinary consequence of keying a scene by a value the surface can also change, and it beats the alternative — disabling the picker in windows — which would make the two hosts behave differently for no gain.

## The Browse menu becomes a submenu where windows are available

Without this, the mode-carrying request would be **theoretical**: the menu could only ever open Trends, and a reader wanting the network beside it would have no way to ask for a second window. Where the surface is still a sheet, the single item is right — a sheet has no side-by-side to offer, and its own picker already switches modes.

## A test leak, found by running the whole suite rather than the new test

Scenario 10 left its map window open. iPadOS restored it, so the next scenario alphabetically (`testTabBarNotObstructingLastBrowserRow`) launched **inside the restored map**, found no Browse tab, and failed — while passing in isolation, which is the signature of leaked state rather than a defect in either test.

It now closes the window before returning, and STATUS.md records the general rule: **any future test that opens a window owes the same courtesy.** Sheets never needed it; scenes do. This is the second face of the restoration behaviour #904 flagged, and worth having hit now rather than in CI later.

## Not covered by your decision

**Cross-Reference Analytics stays a sheet.** It has no mode enum, so option 2 has nothing to key on there — only option 1 (an empty marker, one window) would apply, and you scoped the decision to Person Analytics.

## Verification

- **3,545 unit tests pass**; both schemes clean-build with **no source warnings**.
- **The whole `UIObstructionTests` suite passes on a freshly erased device (7/7)** — which is what caught the leak; running only the new scenario would have missed it.
- The mode-as-identity property is **mutation-tested**: collapsing equality to `true` (the empty-marker shape you rejected) fails `"Trends and Network are two windows"` by name.

## Owner's to verify

- [ ] **iPad, Stage Manager**: the Person Analytics submenu opens each half in its own window, and both are on screen at once.
- [ ] **iPad**: opening the same half twice focuses one window rather than stacking duplicates.
- [ ] **iPad without multi-window / iPhone**: one menu item, and the sheet still presents.
- [ ] **macOS**: unchanged — the new scene is iOS-only.

author: abankar1
body:
Fixes #2919.

Four reporting CLIs swallowed a mistyped flag and reported a result computed from inputs nobody asked for, at exit 0.

## The sharpest case

`rejection-latency.mjs` had **both** defects `lib/cli-flags.mjs` exists to end, on a script whose output is a blacklist suggestion — so its silent failure mode is a false negative the user then acts on.

Fixture: one company 217 days past the 30-day courtesy threshold.

```
$ node rejection-latency.mjs --tracker sb/applications.md --file sb/ai.md --today 2026-08-15 --summary
  SandboxCo               2026-01-10      217    courtesy   30d
  Suggested data/blacklist.md rows (copy manually — nothing is written for you):
```

One transposed letter:

```
$ node rejection-latency.mjs --traker sb/applications.md --file sb/ai.md --today 2026-08-15 --summary
  No post-interview silence exceeded the configured thresholds.
$ echo $?
0
```

Same exit code, opposite conclusion — `--tracker` fell back to `DEFAULT_TRACKER_PATH` and the tool answered from a file the caller never named. That is `doctor.mjs`'s `--targe` (#2874) with a worse payload.

The `=` form failed identically: `argValue` was `args.indexOf(flag)`-based, which returns -1 for `--tracker=path` and silently discards the value — defect #2401/#2402, in a script that never got the fix.

## Scope

| script | `--flag=value` | mistyped flag | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rejection-latency.mjs` | ❌ own `indexOf` helper | ❌ ignored, exit 0 | `flagValue` + `hasFlag` + `validateFlags` |
| `weekly-digest.mjs` | ✅ own local copy | ❌ ignored, exit 0 | `validateFlags` + a `USAGE` block (it had neither) |
| `process-quality.mjs` | ✅ imports the helper | ❌ ignored, exit 0 | `validateFlags` |
| `detect-reposts.mjs` | ✅ imports the helper | ❌ ignored, exit 0 | `validateFlags` replacing a bare `--help` check |

Every value flag involved either redirects the script to a different data file or moves the threshold that decides what gets reported, so a dropped value changes the answer rather than producing an obvious error.

## Two things worth reviewing

**`hasFlag` is paired with `flagValue` on purpose.** `flagValue` returns `undefined` for *both* an absent flag and one supplied without a value, so testing it alone would have turned a trailing `--tracker` from a usage error into a silent fall back to the default path — trading one silent default for another. `lib/cli-flags.mjs` documents pairing them for exactly this case. There is a test pinning it at exit 2.

**Two calls sit inside the main-module guard, not at top level.** `rejection-latency.mjs` imports `parseActiveInterviews` from `process-quality.mjs`, and `company-history.mjs` imports `detectReposts`/`parseScanHistory` from `detect-reposts.mjs`. A top-level `validateFlags` there would judge the **importer's** argv and reject its perfectly valid flags. There is a test covering that too.

I kept `rejection-latency`'s local "value must not itself look like another flag" check rather than dropping it for the shared helper — it is stricter, and it is what stops `--today --summary` from setting the evaluation date to `'--summary'`.

## Commits

1. `rejection-latency.mjs` — both defects.
2. `process-quality.mjs` + `detect-reposts.mjs` — flag-name validation, inside the guard.
3. `weekly-digest.mjs` — validation plus the missing usage block.
4. `tests/cli-flag-validation.test.mjs` — the regression suite.

## Verification

The test suite was checked for discrimination rather than assumed: **with all four source fixes reverted, 12 of the 17 tests fail**, and the 5 survivors are exactly the assertions that pin behaviour which must *not* change (space-separated form, trailing-flag usage error, `--today --summary`, the importer check, and detect-reposts' pre-existing `--help`).

Self-tests all still pass: rejection-latency 34/34, process-quality 21/21, detect-reposts 8/8, weekly-digest 52/52. `node test-all.mjs --quick`: 3936 pass / 0 fail (the 2 warnings are pre-existing and environmental — no user data, no Playwright browser). The new fixtures are tmpdir-only; nothing reads or writes the real `data/`.

## Deliberately out of scope

`upskill.mjs`, `salary-gap.mjs`, `tracker-sync-check.mjs` and `stats.mjs` also exit 0 on a bogus flag, but carry boolean flags only — a dropped `--summary` prints JSON instead of a table, which is visible immediately. Worth sweeping, not the same severity.

`weekly-digest.mjs` also carries its own local `flagValue` duplicating the shared one (its docstring notes `company-history.mjs` carries "this same note and the same fix"). It is exported, so folding it into `lib/cli-flags.mjs` touches importers — a refactor better done on its own than mixed into this fix.

## Summary

Closes #88 — scaffolds the Angular application for the Go/Angular reimplementation at `go-angular/web`:

- Standalone single-component app (Angular 22, signals, no routing, no SSR).
- Health view that calls the Go backend `GET /api/health` on init and renders the returned status (with graceful error handling via a `signal<string | null>`).
- `HealthService` in `src/app/services/health.service.ts` with a typed `HealthResponse { status: string }`.
- Dev-time proxy (`proxy.conf.json` → `http://localhost:8080`) wired into `angular.json` under `serve.options.proxyConfig`, so `/api/*` is same-origin in dev (no CORS).

`go-angular/web` uses **npm**, not the root pnpm workspace. The root is a single-package Next.js workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` has no `packages` glob), so it doesn't conflict; npm keeps the Angular app's `package.json`/lockfile self-contained as a separate parallel build. Documented in `go-angular/web/README.md`.

  README.md, .gitignore, .editorconfig, .prettierrc

author: obrien-k
body:
ADR-0034 asserted in three places that #367 stays open and keeps the eslint 10 question visible in the PR list:

- **Cross-links header** — "(stays open)"
- **§Decision 1** — "#367 stays open, pointing here."
- **§Consequences** — "#367 will keep appearing in the PR list; that is intended."

#367 was closed unmerged the day after the ADR landed, and no tracking issue replaced it. All three statements are now false, in a document whose entire job is to be the record.

## Corrected, not softened — because the consequence actually changed

Renovate treats a closed PR as an instruction not to re-offer that version. So eslint 10 will not resurface on its own: no PR, no issue, no dashboard entry. Revisiting it means someone deciding to come looking, and this ADR is the only thing they'll find.

§Consequences now says that plainly, including that it's a deliberate choice to keep the PR queue quiet rather than an oversight, and what that choice costs. §Decision 1's heading changes from "eslint 10 stays open" to "deferred, not abandoned", since "open" now reads as a claim about the PR rather than the question.

The technical content is unchanged — the `eslint-plugin-import` peer ceiling, the three options in §Alternatives, and the suppression evidence all stand as written.

Docs only. `prettier --check` clean.

author: vaibhavsharmavvs
body:
The last two items in Goal 3, and they are one piece of work: a diff needs something to diff against.

Every plan is snapshotted whenever the agent loads it, so a plan edited in a text editor is versioned exactly like one changed through the dashboard. Identical content is never recorded twice -- every rebind and every folder change reloads, so without that the history would fill with copies of whatever the plan currently says. Twenty versions are kept per automation.

Not SQLite, which is what PLAN.md called for. What has to be stored is a few dozen copies of a few kilobytes of JSON, keyed by name and ordered by time, which is what a directory is. SQLite would add a native dependency and a schema to migrate in exchange for querying nobody needs, and the data would stop being readable with the tools the rest of this project is already inspectable with. The version is the file: restoring is a copy, inspecting is opening it.

The diff exists because the concept shows only the new plan, and a new plan on its own is not reviewable. The question worth answering is not "is this reasonable?" but "what did it change?", and those have very different answers when a model has quietly dropped a step. The headline is +n -n, which tells a reviewer whether the plan was fixed or rewritten before they read a line of it. Added and removed lines carry a marker as well as a colour, because this is the screen where missing a removed line matters most.

It appears in both directions this can happen -- a repaired plan pasted back, and an old version restored -- since those are the same review with the arguments swapped.

That closed a hole in the repair loop. Pasting a repaired plan was refused for colliding with the automation it repaired, so the loop had no last step: you had the fix and nowhere to put it. The collision is now the interesting case, and the diff is what makes accepting it a review rather than a leap.

Restoring revokes approval, deliberately. It changes what is about to become live, and the gate exists so a person reads what is about to become live -- including when that is something they wrote last week.

One fix that came out of this rather than into it. The crash-reporting added with the repair exporter caught the InvalidOperationException that killed the agent during the hotkey-capture work and that I could not reproduce at the time: HotkeyCaptureWindow closes itself when it loses the keyboard, and saving a chord deactivates it on the way out, so it called Close on a window already closing -- which WPF refuses. It threw every single time a chord was saved; the dispatcher guard was catching it, which is why the agent survived and nothing looked wrong. Now guarded properly.

author: oblomov-dev
body:
# Description

Thirty workflow files ran about twenty-one jobs on every pull request, and most of that was runner startup rather than work.

The nine static gates were the clearest case. Each is a Node script that reads the sources and decides one rule, and together they run in **under a second** — measured, not estimated:

| gate | script | its own job in CI |
|---|---|---|
| `check:abapgit` | 333 ms | 14 s |
| `check:api` + `check:guide` | 128 ms | 15 s |
| `check:dynamic` | 109 ms | 12 s |
| `check:atc` | 109 ms | 20 s |
| `check:naming` | 54 ms | 20 s |
| `check:icons` | 67 ms | 16 s |
| `check:formatter` | 49 ms | – |
| **total** | **~0.9 s** | **~2 min + 9 checks** |

As nine separate workflows they cost nine runner starts, nine checkouts and nine toolchain setups to do that one second of work. They are one job now, one step per rule.

The steps are `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, which is what makes this an improvement rather than a trade: a pull request that trips three gates reports all three in one log, instead of surfacing the next one only after the previous has been fixed and pushed. The paths filters are gone with them — they saved nothing at this runtime, and a check that does not run cannot be a *required* check in the branch protection.

Each gate runs as the npm script a developer runs locally, so a failure names the command that reproduces it. **No rule changed**, and no reasoning was lost: every gate's justification already lived in the script it runs (and the chain layout's in `abap2ui5lint.jsonc`), which is where a rule and its "why" belong together.

Three more consolidations of the same shape:

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| **`abaplint.yaml`** | `ABAP_STANDARD` + `ABAP_CLOUD` + `test_rename` | One job. They shared their whole expensive half — `npm ci` plus `npm run deps` — and differed only in which config they handed to abaplint; the install was paid three times for three runs of seconds. `ABAP_702` stays separate: different ref, different trigger |
| **`mirror.yaml`** | a reusable workflow + one caller per mirror | A matrix. A caller was a schedule and three strings; the `workflow_call` indirection is gone, so a third mirror is a line rather than a file |
| **`.github/actions/setup`** | checkout-plus-setup-node-plus-install in every workflow | A composite action, used by 17 jobs. It had drifted while it was copied — half the callers pinned the actions, half tracked a tag — so this also puts the Node version and the pinned sha in one place |

**30 workflow files → 18, ~21 jobs per pull request → 10.**

`trigger_local` is the one job that cannot use the composite action: both its checkouts go into subdirectories, so there is no repository at the workspace root for a local action to be loaded from. It keeps `setup-node` directly, with a comment saying why.

## This PR will be red, and the failure is the point

`check_gates` fails on `check:abap2ui5`, and **it fails on `main` today** — this branch changes no ABAP at all:

```
src/01/04/z2ui5_cl_ui5_app_start.clas.abap
  751:7  warning  this chain is not in the house layout — 1 line(s) differ  chain-house-layout
```

That is the exact defect #2598 set out to repair ("main has been failing `npm run check:abap2ui5` ever since"). Its merged diff touches only `SKILL.md`, `building-apps.md`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` — **the ABAP fix it describes never landed**, and `check_chain_format` never reported it because its paths filter only fires on a PR that touches `src/**/*.abap`.

The cause is reproducible, and it is not a stray edit — the two autofixers disagree about that line:

```
$ npx abap2ui5lint --fix     →      )->end( ).      (4 spaces)
$ npm run auto_abaplint      →        )->end( ).    (6 spaces, back again)
```

`auto_abaplint_fix_pr` runs `npm run app2abap` (which ends in `auto_abaplint`) and commits to every PR branch, so it lands *after* any chain fix in the same PR and reverts it. That is why #2598's fix disappeared, and it is why I did **not** put the one-line fix in this PR: the bot would revert it here too. It needs a decision about which tool owns that column — most likely an abaplint `indentation` exclusion for chain-closing lines — which is a separate change.

Removing the paths filters is what makes this visible on every PR instead of only on one that happens to touch an `.abap` file.

## How to test

The gate scripts, run exactly as the new job runs them (after `npm ci`):

```bash
for t in check:frozen check:abapgit check:atc check:naming check:dynamic \
         check:abap2ui5 check:api check:guide check:icons check:formatter; do
  npm run --silent "$t"; echo "$t -> $?"
done
```

Nine pass; `check:abap2ui5` fails for the pre-existing reason above (verify with `git stash` — it fails on a clean `main` too).

Structural checks over the workflow tree:

```bash
# every workflow and the composite action parse
python3 -c "import yaml,glob; [yaml.safe_load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('.github/workflows/*.yaml')+['.github/actions/setup/action.yml']]"

# every ./.github/actions/* use is preceded by a checkout into the workspace root
```

That second check caught a real bug while writing this: `trigger_local` had been converted to the composite action, where it could never have resolved it.

## Checklist

- [ ] `npm run verify` — **not run in full** (it downports, transpiles and runs the unit suite; this branch changes no ABAP, JS or ABAP tooling config). What was run: the ten gate scripts above, plus YAML parsing and the local-action/checkout ordering check over all 18 workflows
- [x] Unit tests added/updated where it makes sense — n/a, no source under `src/` or `node/` changed
- [x] No manual edits under `src/00/01/`, `src/00/02/`, `src/01/03/` or `build/`
- [x] Public API in `src/02/` only changed additively — no API change at all
- [ ] Changes were made via abapGit: **no**

## One thing to do by hand

The check names change. Any of these listed as a **required check** in the branch protection has to be re-pointed at `check_gates` / `abaplint` in the repository settings — that is not something a diff can carry.

Also left alone: `actions/cache@v6` in `test_browser.yaml` is the last unpinned action. I did not have its sha and did not want to guess one.

author: jperla
body:
Adds TrustedRouter as a provider. It's an OpenAI-compatible router — one key reaches models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek and others, with per-request routing and failover.

Wired the same way as `openrouter` / `requesty`: added to `BuiltinProvider` and `PROVIDERS_OPENAI`, a client in `llm_openai.py` at `https://api.trustedrouter.com/v1`, plus `PROVIDER_API_KEYS`, `PROVIDER_DEFAULT_MODELS`, `PROVIDER_DOCS`, and a `MODELS` entry (required by the `set(PROVIDERS) == set(MODELS.keys())` assert in `data.py`).

**On the double prefix.** Model ids are namespaced and TrustedRouter rejects a bare id, so `MODELS["trustedrouter"]` keys are the full path after `trustedrouter/`. `trustedrouter/trustedrouter/auto` resolves to provider `trustedrouter` + model `trustedrouter/auto` — which is what the API expects. I verified this through `get_model()` rather than assuming:

```
trustedrouter/trustedrouter/auto      -> provider=trustedrouter model=trustedrouter/auto      ctx 200000
trustedrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 -> provider=trustedrouter model=anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 ctx 1000000
```

The `trustedrouter/*` keys are routing policies rather than single models: each picks an upstream per request and fails over, and `zdr` restricts routing to providers that retain no data. Their listed prices are the blended rate the router bills for the policy, so they're averages rather than one model's — noted in a comment above the block since it's otherwise misleading.

Verified: `pytest -k "model or provider"` → 560 passed, 60 skipped, 0 failed. (First run showed 21 errors, all `fixture 'mocker' not found` — my venv was missing `pytest-mock`, unrelated to this change; clean after installing it.)

body:
## What changed

- Continues Phase 5 after the merged Sindel-scheme / DAG slice.
- Extends the MK3 invasion after `Shao Kahn breaches Earthrealm` into the sourced soul-claim and extermination campaign.
- Adds `Mortal Kombat 3 — Liu Kang Biography` for the narrow claim that Liu Kang becomes the prime target of Kahn's extermination squads.
- Adds `Mortal Kombat 4 — Game Story` as later Original-continuity confirmation that Shao Kahn was defeated by the Earth warriors.
- Adds canon Facts for Kahn claiming Earthrealm's human souls, Liu Kang being the prime extermination target, and Earth warriors defeating Shao Kahn.
- Updates CHANGELOG, AGENTS, ROADMAP, and dedicated manual verification.

## AGENTS review correction

The initial implementation connected `Shao Kahn breaches Earthrealm → Shao Kahn claims Earthrealm's human souls` as a causal edge. Review found that MK3 establishes those beats in invasion sequence/context, but does not directly support that narrower causal assertion.

That edge was removed. The chronology rail still shows breach before soul-taking, while the causal graph no longer promotes adjacency into causality.

The stronger supported continuation remains:

`Shao Kahn claims Earthrealm's human souls → Shao Kahn sends extermination squads after the survivors`

because MK3 explicitly distinguishes the protected chosen warriors whose souls cannot be taken and then describes Kahn sending warriors to eliminate the survivors.

## Evidence discipline

MK3 preserves the important qualification that the chosen Earth warriors' souls are protected, so the data does not flatten the story into a literal claim that every human soul was taken.

MK3 Liu Kang biography identifies Liu Kang as the prime target of the extermination squads.

MK4 later treats `Shao Kahn's defeat at the hands of the earth warriors` as established history. This PR therefore models the broad canonical outcome, but does **not** promote the narrower arcade-ending claim that Liu Kang personally defeated Shao Kahn. Liu Kang is intentionally not inserted as a participant in the defeat Event from ending-only evidence.

## Chronology / causality

`Earth warriors defeat Shao Kahn` is placed after the invasion campaign in story order, but remains causally disconnected. MK4 confirms the outcome; it does not identify the extermination-squad Event as its immediate cause.

The chronology rail from PR #12 therefore carries two intentional gaps safely:

- breach → soul claim: chronological sequence, no direct edge;
- extermination campaign → Shao Kahn defeat: historical sequence, no direct edge.

## Manual review

See `docs/PHASE5_MK3_INVASION_OUTCOME_MANUAL_VERIFICATION.md`.

Highest-value checks:

1. breach and soul-taking are chronologically ordered without a manufactured direct causal edge;
2. soul-taking → extermination squads remains the supported causal continuation;
3. Liu Kang is the prime squad target via biography evidence;
4. MK4 supplies later confirmation of Shao Kahn's defeat by Earth warriors;
5. no canon claim says Liu Kang personally defeated Kahn in this slice;
6. chronology places the broad defeat after the invasion while causality preserves the unsupported transition as a gap.

## Review / CI

- manual quick pass completed;
- standard AGENTS review completed;
- review finding fixed;
- CHANGELOG reviewed and updated;
- AGENTS and ROADMAP updated to current Phase 5 scope;
- final `pnpm check` CI succeeds on review-corrected head.

## Schema

No schema change is required.

author: desmotech
body:
Fixes the failed prod run of the join → install → shop funnel (`saarku+pa@gmail.com`, `1.0.5+39`). API half: **desmotech/FitKit#252**.

## What broke

The server did everything right — prod logs show the intent created, served, and consumed. The redirect was lost entirely on the client, to a **gate mismatch** in `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`:

| Condition | Waits on |
|---|---|
| `shouldShowShop` | `plans` + `paymentConfig` |
| `tabsReady` | those **plus** `enrollments` + `orgPrograms` |

`usePendingIntent` was gated on `shouldShowShop` alone. In the window where the first two queries have landed and the other two haven't, the layout is still rendering its loader — `<NativeTabs>` isn't mounted and there's no `shop` route — so `router.replace('/(tabs)/shop?plan=…')` had nothing to land on. Then `handledRef` latched and it never retried.

The logs confirm where the member ended up: after sign-in the app fetched `sessions`, `assignments/my-week`, `personal-records/me`, `goals/me`, `members/me/stats`, `badge`, `forms/mine` — all **home tab** queries. No onboarding calls, so AuthGate wasn't overriding anything.

My own comment in that file had the bug written into it:

> *"Waits for the shop gate so it never routes at a tab that isn't there; `tabsReady` below governs when the shell itself renders."*

Those were assumed to be the same condition. They aren't.

**Combined effect:** intent consumed server-side, navigation dropped, member on home, intent gone for good — the exact silent dead-end this feature exists to prevent.

## The fixes

1. **`navigatorReady` gate.** The hook now needs both `shopAvailable` *and* the navigator being mounted. Returning without latching means the effect re-runs once the shell comes up, so the resume still happens — just a beat later.
2. **Don't burn the one-shot early.** `handledRef` and `consume` only fire once there is somewhere to land.
3. **`fetchWithAuth` tolerates empty bodies.** Every successful response was fed to `res.json()`, so a `204` threw and reported failure for work the server had completed (FITKIT-MOBILE-4). `204`/`205` and zero-length bodies now resolve as no content. This is general — it affected any 204 endpoint, not just this one.

## Testing

510 tests green (+6), typecheck and lint clean.

- `pending-intent.test.tsx` — new case renders with `navigatorReady={false}`, asserts **no navigation and no consume**, then rerenders ready and asserts both fire. That's the prod failure as a test.
- The existing happy path deliberately still answers `204`, since field builds talk to whichever API version is deployed.
- `use-api-empty-body.test.tsx` — 204, empty 200, normal JSON, and error responses.

## Shipping

Ships as an **OTA to 1.0.5** — pure JS, same `runtimeVersion`, so existing TestFlight installs get it without a store round-trip. Merge **#252 first**.

Not verified: no device retest. The full round-trip is worth walking once this is out, since that's what caught it.

author: gregovate
body:
## Fix

The scheduled runner was healthy and returned HTTP 200, but Python's normal `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` access record is written to native `stderr`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 converted that redirected record into a PowerShell error, and the launcher's global `ErrorActionPreference = Stop` terminated the long-running process.

This change:

- temporarily uses `Continue` only while the native Python server is running
- continues writing both stdout and stderr to the service log
- restores the launcher's strict error preference afterward
- keeps the Python process exit code as the authoritative success/failure result
- extends the PowerShell launcher regression contract

## Evidence

The recorded failure itself was a successful request:

`GET /health HTTP/1.1 200`

## Impact

No token rotation, server pairing, API deployment, parser run, ingest, SQLite change, PostgreSQL write, or reconciliation is required.

## Validation

- 22 parser/runner tests passed
- launcher remains ASCII-only for Windows PowerShell 5.1
- `git diff --check` passed

author: test1card
body:
fix: default_cool ACCENT becomes STATUS_INFO, by owner decision

The owner looked at the filled status pills and said the info colour and the
accent colour cannot be told apart by eye. He is right, and the measurement is
an outlier rather than a marginal call: CIEDE2000 between STATUS_INFO #6490c4
and ACCENT #7c8cff is 8.6, where the next-closest pair anywhere in this palette
is 24.1. Below about 10, most viewers cannot separate two colours at a glance.

He then chose the direction: make them one colour rather than separating them.
Two state colours that are nearly the same read as an inconsistency; the same
colour on purpose does not. ACCENT is now exactly #6490c4.

The 300/500/600 rungs move with it. They are the hover and pressed states, so
leaving them indigo would change hue the moment an operator touched a control.
They are re-derived from the new base with the same saturation and value offsets
the old scale used, not picked by hand.

ACCENT is per-pack, and STATUS_INFO is not. That is why the accent is the side
that moves: the status colours carry safety meaning. The other eleven packs are
untouched and each keeps its own distinct accent; only default_cool had this
collision.

test_default_cool_accent_preserved_as_indigo pinned #7c8cff, and its own message
names the sanctioned path for an intentional change: update this test and ADR
002. This change takes that path rather than removing the guard. The test is not
relaxed. It still pins one exact value, and it now also asserts the property the
decision creates (ACCENT equals STATUS_INFO) and, explicitly, the regression it
has always existed to catch (ACCENT must never equal STATUS_OK). The superseded
indigo is named in the message so the history stays legible.

default_cool is a pre-ADR pack and sits outside _ADR_001_PACKS, whose rule that
ACCENT stay at least 30 degrees from every status hue would otherwise forbid
this. The six ADR packs keep that separation untouched.

NOT changed, and the distinction matters: theme.py:110 and
tests/gui/test_theme_tokens.py:98 also contain #7c8cff, but they are the
PLOT_LINE_PALETTE and share the hex by coincidence. A blind replacement of that
value would have silently changed a chart line colour.

Controls: tests/gui/test_theme_loader.py, tests/gui/test_theme_tokens.py and
tests/design_system, 65 passed.

Documentation still carries the old value in eleven files. That propagation is
tracked separately so this change stays reviewable as one decision.

author: jankneumann
body:
## Summary

Implements OpenSpec change **`add-local-model-provider-tier`**: a sixth first-class dispatch provider, `local`, backed by a GX10-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with the two durable rules from the proposal encoded as enforced config rather than prose:

- **MoE-first hardware matching (D4)** — `local` roster entries in `archetypes.yaml` use an extended form (`model`, `total_params_b`, `active_params_b`, `reviewed`) validated at coordinator startup against a `local_host_class` block (GB10: 12B active-parameter ceiling; dense ≥30B rejected even though they fit in 128 GB). Initial roster: `standard` = gpt-oss-120b (117B/5.1B active), `economy` = qwen3-coder-30b-a3b (30.5B/3.3B active).
- **Archetype trust boundary (D3)** — resolution under `local` is an allowlist (`runner`, `analyst`, `documenter`, `validator`); `architect`/`reviewer`/`gatekeeper`/`implementer` are refused with a structured 403 (declared as an OpenAPI delta in this change's contracts) audited with `success=False`. The dispatch adapter independently enforces the same allowlist as defense-in-depth.
- **Adapter (D2/D5)** — `_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` gains `local` with a stdlib OpenAI-compatible runner: 3s health probe (30s TTL, connection-error invalidation, single-flight), wall-clock deadlines on probe and dispatch, per-process concurrency cap (default 4, clamped at 64), http(s)-only base URLs, 10 MB response budget. The roadmap policy engine will not switch to `local` while the probe reports unavailable.

**Inert by default (rollback path):** with `LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL` unset the provider degrades to the existing structured fallback, and a snapshot test proves resolution for all existing providers is byte-identical — so rollback is unsetting the env var, or reverting this change's commits; no persisted state, no migration.

## Review

Independent review (same-vendor fallback — no non-claude vendor CLIs in this container; degradation reported) returned request-changes with 20 findings: 1 critical, 5 major, 10 minor, 4 info. 19 fixed in a second round, including the critical (the smoke path previously dispatched a refused archetype to the endpoint; it now uses INIT/`runner` and treats refusal as a hard failure). One deferred as a follow-up: F-15, the coordination bridge collapses the 403 refusal into its generic non-200 warning. Full findings table with dispositions: `openspec/changes/add-local-model-provider-tier/change-context.md`.

## Test evidence

- agent-coordinator: 2208 passed, `mypy --strict` clean (75 files), ruff clean
- skills: 2368 passed (suite) + 239 adapter/policy/contract package tests, ruff clean
- `openspec validate add-local-model-provider-tier --strict`: valid; work-packages schema/DAG/lock/parallel-zone validation: valid
- Live-service smoke: **skipped** (no Docker daemon in this cloud container; soft gate)
- Pre-existing, not introduced here: 7 failures in `skills/tests/autopilot/test_phase_{dispatch,archetype}_e2e.py` (reproduce on a clean baseline); 33 collection errors when running `skills/tests` as a single root (duplicate module basenames, present on main)

## Known follow-ups (out of scope, recorded)

- F-15: bridge-side surfacing of trust-boundary 403s (vs generic transport warning)
- `skills/pyproject.toml` `testpaths` omits `autopilot/scripts/tests` and `tests/autopilot-roadmap` (pre-existing CI coverage gap)
- `token_budget_check.py` duplicates the provider roster without `local`
- Serving-stack deployment on the GX10 is operator config (llama.cpp `llama-server` / vLLM / Ollama); see `docs/proposals/magnitude-local-model-harness.md` for the evaluation and re-evaluation triggers

Planning artifacts (proposal, design D1–D7, spec deltas, contracts, work-packages) and the magnitude evaluation doc are included on this branch.

author: kirschblutex
body:
HUMAN:
I led this feature from trust-boundary analysis through implementation and final verification. I designed and implemented the authenticated repository-validation endpoint in the existing git router, kept stored provider credentials exclusively on the server, added optional ref verification, restricted outbound requests to supported provider hosts, disabled redirects and environment-proxy inheritance, and bounded and sanitized every result returned to the caller. I personally developed and reviewed the 48-test coverage for public repositories, named and missing credentials, optional refs, provider failures, transport failures, invalid input, and sensitive-data redaction, then ran the scoped pre-commit verification. I confirmed that callers can supply credential names only and that credential values and provider response bodies never appear in API responses or logs. I retain responsibility for the security decisions, implementation, validation, and final submission.

---
AGENT:
AI assistance was limited to targeted secondary review and help organizing the verification evidence. I personally reviewed the resulting feedback and test evidence, made the implementation and security decisions, and verified the final endpoint behavior before submission.

## Why
I traced the automation preflight flow and confirmed that it needs a trusted server-side check for repository and ref access. Agent Canvas cannot safely resolve stored provider credentials itself, and it cannot reliably distinguish private-repository access denial from provider or transport failures without delegating the check to the server that owns the git-provider credential APIs.
I therefore placed this bounded validation endpoint in the existing git router, where repository access and stored credentials already have an authoritative owner.
Related to OpenHands/OpenHands#16565.

## Summary
I implemented the repository-access validation flow to:
- add authenticated `POST /api/git/validate-repository` to the existing git router
- accept an allowlisted repository URL, an optional ref, and an optional credential name without accepting raw credential values
- resolve named GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket credentials only on the server and optionally verify the requested ref
- authenticate Bitbucket correctly for both bare tokens and `username:token` credentials, and move secret-store lock access off the event loop
- restrict outbound requests to supported provider hosts and disable redirects and environment-proxy inheritance
- normalize provider, transport, credential, ref, and input failures into bounded, actionable results
- prevent provider response bodies, credential values, and other sensitive details from reaching API responses or logs

## Issue Number
Related to #3035 (the existing Agent Server git-provider credential APIs) and OpenHands/OpenHands#16565 (the automation preflight tracker).

## How to Test
I ran and reviewed the complete git-router test file:

```text
uv run pytest tests/agent_server/test_git_router.py -q
48 passed
```

I then ran the scoped pre-commit checks against the implementation and test files:

```text
uv run pre-commit run --files openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/git_router.py tests/agent_server/test_git_router.py
all scoped hooks passed
```

### Authenticated endpoint reproduction
I exercised `POST /api/git/validate-repository` through the authenticated FastAPI test client with an allowlisted repository URL, optional ref, and credential name.
- An accessible repository or ref returns `{ "ok": true }`.
- A missing named credential returns an actionable failure that can be mapped to the relevant field.
- Provider and transport failures return bounded, sanitized availability errors.
- Invalid input and unsupported provider hosts are rejected without making an unsafe outbound request.
The 48-test coverage includes public repositories, optional refs, named credentials, both supported Bitbucket credential forms, missing credentials, provider failures, transport failures, invalid input, event-loop-safe secret lookup, and sensitive-response redaction. I also verified that no credential values are accepted from or returned to the caller, and that neither secret values nor provider response bodies appear in responses or logs.

## Video/Screenshots
The companion Agent Canvas PR contains deterministic mock UI screenshots for both failed and passed preflight states: [reproduction steps and visual QA evidence](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/pull/16614#issuecomment-5302632897).

## Design Doc
Not included. I kept this as a bounded endpoint within the existing git-router owner and reused the established authentication and provider-credential boundaries.

## Type
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes
- I led the work from trust-boundary and failure-model analysis through endpoint implementation, security hardening, test coverage, scoped verification, and final evidence review.
- AI assistance was supplementary; I retained ownership of the code, security decisions, validation, and final submission.
- This endpoint is consumed by the Automation service's local deployment path.
- Older deployments remain compatible because Agent Canvas treats only `404` and `501` validation endpoints as advisory unsupported states.
- The five coordinated PRs should be reviewed and rolled out together so the shared preflight contract and its security boundaries remain consistent.

Companion changes:
- Agent Canvas: https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/pull/16614
- Automation: https://github.com/OpenHands/automation/pull/341
- Sandbox Server: https://github.com/OpenHands/sandbox-server/pull/6
- Extensions: https://github.com/OpenHands/extensions/pull/476

author: a-h-911
body:
## DEF-075 — `POST /api/members/me` is documented idempotent, and was not

Two concurrent first-logins for one subject both reached the INSERT. Measured on the `AC-011` e2e leg
(#278), from the api container log:

```
Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbUpdateException
 ---> SqlException: Cannot insert duplicate key row in object
      'membership.committee_members' with unique index 'IX_committee_members_KeycloakUserId'
```

It can only ever happen on a subject's **first** provisioning — every later call takes the sync path,
where nothing is inserted. That is why it survived this long: in e2e, a run's first login was driven
by `ac043-reorder`, which uses `loginAs` + `captureBearer` and never calls `meMember`, so exactly one
provisioning call was ever in flight. #278 is the first spec to call `roleSession` at the start of a
run, which adds a second concurrent with the SPA's own.

**The harness was not the defect.** `apiHelpers` calls this endpoint deliberately, as a guard against
racing the SPA's async provision — a legitimate use of a contract the endpoint advertises and did not
keep. The SPA has a `useRef` guard, but two tabs opened together on a user's very first login race the
same way, which is the worst possible moment for it.

## The fix, and why it is this small

I originally recorded on the row that this would need a retry *above* `TransactionBehavior`, on the
assumption the ambient transaction was doomed. **That assumption was wrong and is corrected here.**
Two facts make a local recovery correct, and both sit next to the code:

- **SQL Server does not fail the second insert immediately.** It blocks on the winner's exclusive key
  lock and raises the duplicate only once that transaction has **committed** — so the winning row is
  already visible when we are refused, and the loser's re-read is guaranteed to find it.
- **A unique violation aborts the statement, not the transaction** (`XACT_ABORT` is off), so the
  ambient transaction is intact and `TransactionBehavior` commits it normally. Nothing partial was
  written either, which matters because MARS disables EF's savepoints.

So the loser detaches its own pending insert, re-reads, and returns the winner's row. A
`DbUpdateException` with **no** winning row behind it is rethrown unchanged — the recovery is scoped
to the one situation it understands.

## Proof

Four tests, each aimed at one guard. Every mutant compiled and killed exactly its own:

| Mutation | Tests killed |
|---|---|
| Recovery removed (the pre-fix behaviour) | **3** |
| Detach removed — the loser re-submits its own insert | 1 |
| Non-race failure absorbed instead of rethrown | 1 |
| Loser still reports `created` (emits `MemberProvisioned`) | 1 |

⚠ **The race is simulated, not run, and that is deliberate.** The InMemory provider does not enforce
unique indexes, so a genuinely concurrent test here would pass whether or not the fix existed — the
exact shape of `DEF-066`, where four green suites sat over a write that could never work on SQL
Server. These tests reproduce *the state the loser finds itself in* and assert the recovery. The other
half — that SQL Server really blocks then raises, and leaves the transaction usable — is proven where
it can only be proven: on a real database, by #278's e2e leg, which is what produced this defect.

Backend **1699 green** (counts reconcile: 1005 baseline + 4), `dotnet format` clean.

## Test plan

- [ ] Backend + e2e green here
- [ ] Rebase #278 on this; its `ac011-guest-scope` `beforeAll` should then get past provisioning

author: joehalliwell
body:
Closes #29.

Two mechanisms, plus the bug that made both unreliable.

**Search hides notes the repository no longer holds.** A note deleted since the
last index run is skipped rather than quoted back. Filtering happens while
walking the ranking, not after truncating it, so hidden hits don't eat into
`--limit`. `--include-deleted` reaches them while they are still in the index.

A note that has merely been *edited* keeps matching on its old chunks until the
next index run. It is still there to open, so a slightly stale quote costs the
reader less than the note dropping out of search in the meantime — the
predicate is a bare existence check.

**Indexing prunes.** The index only ever grew: chunks are keyed on the commit
that last modified their note, so editing a note added a second version
alongside the first, and deleting one left it behind forever. Indexing already
computes the live set to decide what is new — pruning is that same set read the
other way round, so an edited note's old chunks go once its new ones are there
to replace them. On by default, `--no-prune` to opt out.

**`_build_path_commit_map` was cached on `repo_dir` alone**, though its
docstring claimed `(repo_dir, head_ref)`. After any commit the map went on
reporting the superseded commit for every file that commit touched, so
incremental indexing never noticed an edited note at all. Fixed first, in its
own commit.

Store-level tests now use a bare `SQLiteSearchIndex` with no existence
predicate: they work with synthetic paths that were never on disk, so the
filtering belongs to the tests that go through `test_repo.index`.

Full suite green; mypy clean.

author: comfybear71
body:
Completes the shelf added in #33 so the sheets can actually be stored and fetched.

```
POST /api/crash/character-plates/upload    multipart: file, styleId, name, note?
GET  /api/crash/character-plates?styleId=  every plate held for a show
GET  /api/crash/character-plates/file?styleId=&file=   stream one
```

The character **name is required on upload** rather than inferred from the filename. Plates are looked up by name later, and one filed under the wrong name is worse than one never uploaded. The stored filename is a slug of that name (`plate_dazza.png`), so re-uploading a character's sheet replaces it rather than stacking duplicates — matching the unique index from #33.

`findCharacterPlate` matches the way `mobilePlates.resolveCastKeyByName` matches cast — exact name first, then containment either way — so a script speaker and a plate name that differ slightly still resolve to each other.

Cloud-only by design: a plate is a show-level asset shared across episodes, and local disk on Vercel is per-invocation `/tmp`, so writing there would silently lose it. The error says so explicitly rather than appearing to succeed.

fix: point the assistant at gemma4:12b, the only model installed

The owner removed gemma4:e4b and gemma4:e2b from the lab PC and installed
gemma4:12b. `ollama list` returns gemma4:12b alone, so every default naming e4b
referred to a model that cannot load, and the assistant would have failed at
first call.

Changed: config/agent.yaml (default_model, intent_model, format_model),
AssistantConfig.default_model, OllamaClient.default_model, and IntroConfig's
model plus its agent.yaml fallback.

Every figure in the new comments was measured against the running ollama rather
than carried over from the e4b notes. gemma4:12b at num_ctx=32768 sits 100% on
GPU at 8.4 GB, cold load 9.3 s, warm load 0.32 s, about 56 tok/s. That is
smaller in vRAM and faster than the ~11 GB and ~39 tok/s recorded for the e4b it
replaces, so the existing timeouts hold and none were widened. The e4b and 26b
lines are retained as the comparison that justifies the move. The note directing
a Mac to downgrade to e2b now says that e2b is absent here and its presence on
the Mac is unverified, rather than naming a fallback that may not exist.

The report annotation no longer hardcodes the model. It said
"Гемма (gemma4:e4b)" as a literal, which would attribute a delivered report to
whatever model the literal named regardless of what ran. The model is now passed
in beside the intro text so the two cannot disagree, and when it is unknown the
sentence omits the model entirely instead of guessing: naming the wrong source

defect before the call is reinstated rather than after.

body:
So far, the `qlever` commands took the script name and the engine name from `sys.argv[0]` (computed once in `qlever/__init__.py` and read as globals), and everywhere else the name `qlever` was simply spelled out in the help strings and in the messages that tell the user which command to run next.

Now the top-level parser provides three defaults, which the commands read from `args` like any other option: `engine_short_name` (used for the container names), `engine_display_name` (the name shown to the user), and `main_command_name` (what the user types before a command). All three are `qlever`/`QLever` for now and are set in one place in `config.py`. Nothing depends any more on how the script was invoked. In particular, the hook that imported engine-specific Qleverfile arguments from a module named after the script is removed. The output is unchanged, except that a few command descriptions no longer say `qlever index` or `qlever start`.

Also a number of small cleanups, such as replacing the deprecated `log.warn` by `log.warning`, moving `dict_to_yaml` to `util.py`, and applying the automatic fixes from `ruff 0.16`.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

This started as a perf change (dispatch `subtest`'s block through the
compiled path instead of the AST carrier) but investigation surfaced three
distinct bugs, two of which are fixed here and are independent of subtest
specifically:

1. **Fixed** — A tail-position `Stmt::Call` with named/slip arguments (in
   the common no-phasers closure-body compile path) blindly flattened any
   Slip-shaped argument value, silently dropping an `Empty`-valued operand
   (`roast/S03-operators/andthen.t`). Routed through the existing
   `compile_tail_stmt_call_value` helper instead, which both tracks
   named/slip argument positions explicitly at compile time and keeps the
   call's result on the stack.

2. **Fixed** — `coerce_hash_var_value`'s object-hash (`.WHICH`-keyed) re-key
   step rebuilt a fresh `HashData` without carrying over `value_type`/
   `key_type`/`declared_type`/`default` from the source hash, so an
   object-hash declared with an inline `is default(...)` initializer lost
   that metadata when later bound through a `for`-loop's positional
   sub-signature destructuring (`roast/S02-names/is_default.t` test 113).

3. **Reverted** — The original perf change itself (`subtest` dispatching
   through `vm_call_on_value`) broke Cro::HTTP's async byte-level
   middleware (`http-middleware.rakutest`'s before-parse/after-serialize
   transforms silently became no-ops), caught by CI's bundled-library gate.
   Confirmed via a clean A/B that this reproduces on the PR's own base
   commit, independent of fixes 1/2. `subtest_call_block` is reverted to
   always use `call_sub_value` (the pre-PR behavior). Findings and a
   suggested path back to re-attempting the perf win are recorded in
   `todo/deep/subtest-compiled-dispatch-breaks-class-registry-restore.md`
   (which also documents a second, pre-existing, dispatch-independent bug
   found along the way: `restore_subtest_decls` erases a class's registry
   entry even when its type object escaped the subtest via a captured
   variable).

Also files `todo/deep/blind-slip-flattening-in-fixed-arity-calls.md` (the
underlying architectural gap fix 1 only narrowly avoids) and
`todo/tickets/native-array-storage-write-through-lost-in-release.md` (an
unrelated, pre-existing, release-build-only failure found during the
regression sweep, confirmed to reproduce on `main`).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build` / `cargo build --release`, `cargo clippy -- -D
      warnings`, `cargo fmt`
- [x] Full local `prove t/` (3181 files) — clean
- [x] `roast/S03-operators/andthen.t`, `roast/S02-names/is_default.t` —
      pass on debug and release
- [x] `roast/S02-names/*`, `roast/S03-operators/*`, `roast/S06*`,
      `roast/S12-construction/*`, `roast/S17-supply/syntax.t` whitelisted
      files (91 files) — pass on release
- [x] `Cro::HTTP`'s `t/http-middleware.rakutest` (the file that regressed) —
      all 24 top-level tests pass again on release after the revert
- [x] New regression test: `t/for-destructure-object-hash-default.t`

The `View all` chevron was **iOS blue** — `#0A84FF`, the previous design's accent — sitting two sections under an Ember heading.

Underneath it was worse than a colour: **seven hand-rolled section headers and two using `SectionHeader`.** I built the new components for Featured and Upcoming and left Nearby, Interested, Nightlife, the checked-in strip and the city-top rail on the old styles. Two of the seven were a centred heading flanked by divider rules — a treatment in **no frame at all**.

All seven are now `SectionHeader`. Not recoloured — **deleted**, along with `sectionTitle`, `viewAllText`, `viewAllRow`, `sectionFancyRow`, `sectionDividerLine`. Recolouring would have left seven places for the next person to copy from; there's now one.

**Fills changed together with their text.** White on `#FF906D` fails contrast — `EMBER.onGradient` is the dark the palette defines for this, and three text styles were still white because they were legible on blue.

`__tests__/pulsePalette.test.ts` greps the files that draw this screen for `APP_COLORS.accent` and hardcoded blues, and asserts no hand-rolled header styles survive.

A grep is crude and it's the only thing that catches this. A typecheck can't see it, a unit test can't see it, and **a render test couldn't either** — both colours are valid, both render, and the only symptom is that the screen looks like two designs.

`APP_COLORS` stays: screens not yet restyled use it deliberately, so the guard is scoped to The Pulse's own files.

author: blockfluit
body:
Clicking a card that leads to the player — Continue Watching, a History row, an episode row, or the Play/Resume button on `/v/:slug` — landed on `/watch/:slug` **paused on its poster**. The viewer had already said what they wanted to watch and still had to press play again. The route was built for exactly this ("a link that starts playing can be shared as one"); nothing ever called `play()`.

Every arrival now plays: card click, Play button, refresh, or a pasted link.

### Where the call goes, and why not `autoplay`

`play()` goes in `onLoadedMetadata`, **after** the resume seek. The `<video>` and its `<source>` are server-rendered, so the `autoplay` attribute would open at 0:00 while Vue was still hydrating and only then be seeked to the resume point — a second of the wrong scene, out loud, on every resume.

Not gated on `prefers-reduced-motion`: that setting is for decoration nobody asked for, which is why `HeroBackdrop` honours it and this does not.

### When the browser refuses

A browser that has not yet decided to trust the origin rejects an unmuted play it saw no click for. That rejection is left alone — the poster and the controls are already on screen, so it costs one press, where muting and playing anyway would start a film silently.

### Two things in the browser suite assumed a player that never moves

- Playwright does not pass `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`, and a fresh headless profile has no engagement score, so the player is refused there and only there. Without the switch the new test fails against working code.
- **`/watch/:slug` never reaches `networkidle`** now — a playing video keeps issuing range requests — so `visit()` waits until the test times out. That is a hang with no failing assertion to point at it, and it is what the hard-load test did on the first run. `visitPlayer()` waits for `readyState >= 1` instead.

Tests about *where a seek lands* call `freeze()`, which pauses **and** re-pauses on `play`: the autoplay attempt is a promise that can settle after a bare `pause()`.

### Verified in a real browser

Against a throwaway database and a generated 40s clip with a real audio track (the policy only blocks media with audio):

- new: player starts on arrival (asserts `paused === false` **and** that the position advances) — pass
- new: player starts on a hard load of its URL — pass
- adapted: `pressing Resume opens where it was left…`, `skip intro seeks past the intro` — pass
- unchanged: all 6 `on the player page` tests, the admin player-page test, the player legibility audit — pass
- `viewer.spec.ts` overall: 19 passed / 4 failed / 8 skipped. The 4 failures are all `main a[href^="/c/"]` in a fixture with no collections, and **fail identically on unmodified `origin/main`** in the same environment.
- `apps/web` vitest: 246 passed. `nuxt typecheck`: clean.

author: collectrix
body:
## Summary

Clears the four nodes `NODE-REGISTRATION-GAP-1` (#1261) had to hold back, registers them, and **empties the `PAGE_BLOCKED_WAIVER`** so the gate that row promoted to blocking now covers every shard with nothing suppressed. **605 → 609 nodes, 609/609 shards assembled.**

#1261 correctly refused to register four nodes whose blockers sat outside its fence, and named every one instead of dropping them silently. But it staged no follow-up, so four names sat waivered inside a blocking gate with nothing on the board to remove them. A named waiver with no owning row is how a temporary exception becomes permanent.

All four blockers were re-confirmed still live before any work started.

## The four blockers, each cleared for real

| Node | Blocker | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `art-615` | no `chaingraph/<id>.html` (catalog-parity "url page missing on disk", never baselineable) | node page authored |
| `art-619` | same | node page authored |
| `art-595` | FV-COVERAGE-GATE-1: floor digest no longer matched the live kernel | floor re-executed green, digest re-stamped from kernel bytes |
| `art-620` | FV-COVERAGE-GATE-1: no `__proptests__` floor file at all | class-B floor authored |

**Node pages** clone art-618's verified chrome and inline each kernel's `compute()` verbatim. Verified by recomputation, not by reading: each page's inline `compute()` was extracted and executed in a sandboxed `node:vm` with no fs/net/process, over every fixture vector, and compared against both the kernel's own `compute()` and the recorded fixture payload — 12/12 for art-615, 8/8 for art-619, byte-identical on all three surfaces.

**art-595** was diagnosed before being touched. The gate's own comment warns a digest mismatch cannot tell "the kernel moved" from "the digest was never correct". Recomputing `sourceDigest()` over every git revision of the kernel showed the recorded value is the real digest of `adb17b0a` (#1194), the revision the floor was authored against; `ART595-ART590-UTF8-FIX-1` then moved the kernel. Cause (a), honest drift — not the `art-598` fabrication class. Floor re-executed green against the current kernel *first* (oracle 4/4, 220 trials, 0 violations), then re-stamped with the gate's own printed command.

**art-620's floor** is 7/7 fixture oracle + 2243 property checks, 0 violations. The row pointed at "art-621's standard", but no `art-621` exists anywhere in the tree, so it is built to art-619's standard instead. P2 is the load-bearing property and is deliberately **not** self-consistent: the kernel hand-rolls SHA-256 (the guest has no host crypto), so a floor reusing that same `_sha256` to build its trees would be checker and checked sharing one implementation — the exact shape SO #34 names. `node:crypto` is an independent SHA-256 **and** a Node built-in, so P2 differentials the hand-rolled implementation and the chain-walk at once, adding no dependency. It passes over 200 randomly built trees. P3 forces the Maxwell broken-MST attack (eprint 2022/043 §4.1) the kernel exists to defend against.

## Registration

One node at a time, each only after its own blocker was cleared — never as a batch. Per node: append to `order.nodes` → add to `hub-categories.json` → re-assemble → drop that node's waiver entry → gate green.

The gate was then **verified by mutation**, not by reading it: art-620 was removed from `order.nodes`, re-assembled, the gate confirmed RED naming that exact shard, then restored and confirmed GREEN. An empty waiver list is not an inert gate.

## ⚠ §18 ratchet — needs Tim's eyes

Registering four unproven nodes mechanically raises the deferred `gpu:false` count **5 → 9**. They were not newly deferred here; they were deferred *and invisible*, which is a node hiding its own deferred status. All four are `gpu:false` with `compute_proof_ready:"deferred"` in their own shards:

- `art-595` `build_ap2_cartmandate_hashchain` — no receipt
- `art-615` `classify_mla_charge_inclusion` — awaiting GPU queue
- `art-619` `recompute_ccd2_aprc_annex3` — kernel uses `Math.pow` with a real-valued exponent, a named `GPU-CYCLE-PREFLIGHT-1` slow pre-screen flag; cycles must be measured before booking
- `art-620` `verify_summa_mst_inclusion` — no receipt

The provenance discriminator confirms all four are **new** nodes, not proof regressions — the legal category for a raise. The raise was made by a targeted, asserted edit naming exactly those four, which refuses to run unless the starting state is `deferred=5` and none of the four were already known. **`--update-baseline` was not used and remains forbidden**: it rewrites `deferred_nodes` wholesale, which is exactly how a regression gets absorbed invisibly (S18-BASELINE-GUARD-1).

No re-prove is staged or proposed, per Tim's 2026-08-15 ruling that we are not reproving nodes at this time. **Standing debt: these four plus `art-616`/`art-618` from #1261 — six nodes owing proofs, ceiling at 9, path back down deferred until proving resumes as a program.**

## Two findings, reported not fixed (SO #25, both out of fence)

1. **art-620 `compute()` throws** `"Cannot convert object to primitive value"` on a null-prototype object in `root.hash`, `root.sum` or `proof.leaf.balance` — three unguarded `String()` coercions in `_stripHexPrefix()` and `finalize()`. **Not reachable** from the declared input path: `JSON.parse` always returns `Object.prototype`-backed objects (asserted in the floor's P1b, not assumed). P1 is scoped to the JSON-representable domain and P1b prints the out-of-domain result on every run, so it is neither red on an unreachable input nor silently dropped.
2. **`gen-kernel-identity.mjs --write`** (monolith mode) crashes on its own post-edit safety re-parse. Reproduced identically against `origin/main`'s data, so not caused by this branch. Preflight only invokes `--check`, green in both modes.

## Churn deliberately reverted

Two regenerations were reverted as out-of-fence no-ops, each verified to leave its own gate green: `gen-kernel-identity.mjs --write --shard` reformatted 181 unrelated shards (identical content, collapsed onto one line), and `gen-euc-register.mjs` rewrote `generated_at` on 606 pre-existing entries (its `--check` is content-based). This matters beyond tidiness — SO #35 measured that regenerating shared derived artifacts pushes open sibling PRs into conflict, destroying their merge ref and silently removing their CI (SO #34c).

## Test plan

- [x] `node scripts/preflight.mjs` **PASSED**, all hard CI gates green (1036s)
- [x] `check-shard-assembly.mjs` green at 609/609 with the waiver list empty, and proven RED-then-GREEN by mutation
- [x] page ↔ kernel ↔ fixture `output_payload` parity, 20/20 vectors, sandboxed re-execution
- [x] art-620 floor 7/7 oracle + 2243 checks, art-595 floor 4/4 + 220 trials
- [x] `FV-FLOOR-DIGEST-GATE-1 --verify-authoring` clean on both touched floors
- [x] SO #26 screenshots: both pages captured over CDP, initial and exercised, **0 console errors**; art-619 reproduces its fixture (10.0% APRC, 26 iterations) in-browser
- [x] art-615 verdict styling swept across all 36 states: 30 informational, 6 conditional, 0 red

### Visual review caught a real defect

art-615 first rendered "Included in the MAPR" in the **red failure style**. This node classifies a charge; it never passes or fails one, and both `true` and `false` are ordinary correct answers. A DOM assertion would have passed it — the handler ran, the panel showed, the payload was right. Only the colour was lying. Fixed to a neutral informational style, amber reserved for the cells the closed set genuinely cannot resolve, red removed from the page entirely.

author: ignacebleukx
body:
As discussed in #1082 there is an inconsistency in the value computation for expressions with partial functions, as the previous argval approach did not catch all cases.

To fix it I had to make quite in-depth changes to the value function: basically, to be correct, each Boolean expression should wrap its `argval` computation in a try/catch and propagate `IncompleteFunctionErrors` to False as its return value.
But that's cumbersome, so it's implemented in the `Expression` superclass instead.
This superclass function now calls `compute_value()` on the subclass (which is the old `.value()`) and does the try/catch there.

## Hva

Legger til en **skill** for oppslag av EESSI ISG-landkoder mot ISO 3166-1, pluss et notat
om når en MCP ville vært verdt det.

## Endringer

- **`skills/eessi-country-lookup/`**
  - `SKILL.md` — instruksjoner + UK↔GB / EL↔GR-avvikene
  - `query/lookup.rq` — parameterisert SPARQL (ISG, ISO alpha-2/alpha-3, label, URI)
  - `scripts/lookup.sh` — `curl`-basert oppslag: `--isg`, `--iso`, `--all`, `--format json`
- **`MCP-TODO.md`** — hvorfor en skill holder, og når en MCP lønner seg
- **`README.md`** — bygg/kjør + dokumentasjon av skillen

## Hvorfor skill og ikke MCP

Endepunktet er åpent HTTP SPARQL — et oppslag er én forespørsel + parsing, uten state
eller hemmeligheter. En MCP gir først mening ved gjenbruk på tvers av klienter, caching
eller en typet kontrakt. Detaljene ligger i `MCP-TODO.md`.

## Verifisert mot live-endepunktet

| Kommando | Resultat |
|----------|----------|
| `--isg UK` | UK → GB / GBR / United Kingdom |
| `--iso GR` / `--isg EL` | EL → GR / GRC / Greece |
| `--all` | 32 land |

Landkoder valideres (`^[A-Z]{2,3}$`) før innsetting i SPARQL for å hindre injeksjon.

author: git-init-priyanshu
body:
Adds document version history and file export, and closes an authorization hole found along the way.

## Version history

Every document keeps up to 50 snapshots, browsable and restorable from a History tab in the editor's right rail.

Snapshots ride along with the existing autosave rather than adding a second write path, but a snapshot per keystroke would be useless and expensive, so `app/writer/[id]/versions/policy.ts` gates them: at most one per 60 seconds, and never for content identical to the previous snapshot. That policy is shared by the server action and the guest `localStorage` path specifically so the two cannot drift apart.

Guests get the same feature against `localStorage`, and deleting a guest document now clears its versions with it.

## Export

Markdown and plain-text export from the editor header. `exportMarkdown.ts` walks the stored Tiptap JSON directly — headings, lists, blockquotes, code blocks, and inline marks — so export does not depend on the editor being mounted or on the DOM.

## Authorization fix

`GetDocDetails` created a `UserOnDocument` row as a side effect of opening a document. Anyone with a document id became a collaborator on it simply by visiting the URL, which is the whole access-control model for this app.

It is now read-only. Membership is written by document creation and by an explicit share, and a caller who is not already a member gets the same answer as for a document that does not exist — no distinction between "forbidden" and "not found" for someone probing ids.

## About the commit history

Three commits here add WebSocket room authentication and a fourth (`e38c056`) reverts them. The server side worked — signed tokens, 401 rejection, two peers syncing text and cursor awareness through it — but the browser integration never did, and the debugging ran long because `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBSOCKET_URL` pointed at a deployed Render instance rather than the local server everything was being verified against. The net diff of this branch contains none of that code.

The history is left intact rather than squashed because #64 is stacked on this branch.

## Verified

- Migration applied: `DocumentVersion` table with a `(documentId, createdAt)` index
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next lint` clean, production build passes

author: ldktc
body:
## Summary

A previous fix (#10) stabilized the release signing key so future builds share a certificate, but anyone with a build already installed from *before* that change (or any build signed with a different key) still hits Android's install failure with no explanation from inside the app — the in-app installer fired an `ACTION_VIEW` intent at the system package installer and reported success immediately, regardless of what actually happened.

- Switch the native install path (`MainActivity.kt`) from a fire-and-forget `ACTION_VIEW` intent to the `PackageInstaller` session API, so the app observes the real, final install result via a `BroadcastReceiver`.
- Distinguish `STATUS_FAILURE_CONFLICT` (signed differently than the app already on the device) from other failures, and forward the outcome back to Dart over the existing `quetzalib/apk_installer` method channel.
- `ApkInstaller.install` (`lib/services/apk_installer.dart`) now returns an `InstallResult` instead of a bare `Future<void>`; `UpdateService.install` (`lib/services/update_service.dart`) turns a `conflict` outcome into a clear, actionable exception ("uninstall QuetzaLib first...") that surfaces in the existing Settings → App update error `SnackBar`.
- Drop the `FileProvider` provider declaration, `file_paths.xml`, and the `ACTION_VIEW`/package-archive `<queries>` entry, since reading the APK bytes directly into the `PackageInstaller` session no longer needs a `content://` URI handoff. Also drop the now-unused explicit `androidx.core:core-ktx` dependency.
- Update the README's "App updates" section to describe the new install flow and the signature-conflict message.

## Test plan

- [ ] No Flutter SDK available in this environment to run `flutter analyze`/`flutter test`/`flutter build apk` — please run these before merging.
- [ ] Manually verify on a device: install an old build (different signing key), then use Settings → App update to install a new build from this branch, and confirm the app shows the new "uninstall QuetzaLib first" message instead of a silent/opaque failure.
- [ ] Manually verify the happy path still works: install this build fresh, then update again to a newer same-key build, confirming the update installs normally.
