author: thethinkmachine
body:
Turns the example picker into a command palette over three things: the examples, the exact algorithms, and a model. One prompt, one machine, no conversation — the canvas is the memory.

## The property that matters

Seven stages run between the prompt and the diagram:

```
assemble → request → parse → compile → lint → verify → apply
              ↑                                   │
              └────────── repair, ≤2 rounds ──────┘
```

**Every stage before `apply` produces a candidate object and touches nothing else.** A rejected key, an unparseable answer, a DFA that turned out nondeterministic — all of them leave the canvas exactly as it was. `tests/statemate.test.js` pins it by comparing `exportWorkspaceState()` either side of a failure.

## Verification

The model must predict what its machine does on ≥3 words, and those predictions are executed through the app's own simulator **before anything is drawn**. `computeBatchResults()` is DOM-free by construction, so the sandbox is: stash the workspace, import the candidate without emitting, decide, restore in a `finally`. Failures go back to the model once, carrying the words that failed and what the machine actually did.

This is what separates "usually right" from "checked". The result card shows `5/5 checks` for a reason.

## The spec is not the save format

No ids, no coordinates, `start`/`accept` as booleans on the state. Field names differ (`on` not `symbol`, `move` not `dir`) so a model that regurgitates a save file fails loudly at the gate instead of half-working.

The compiler diffs it against the live machine **by state name**, so a state that survives an edit keeps its id, its position, its anchored notes and its hand-tuned edge curve. Verified in the browser: asking for a trap state on a two-state DFA left `even` at `(0,0)` and `odd` at `(179,0)` and placed `trap` at the centroid of its neighbours. Nothing else moved.

## Derived from the app's own registries

Legal fields from `MachineTypes`, notation from `App.config.sym`, concept text from `MachineGuides`, and the worked example in the prompt generated by running a bundled example file through `machineToSpec()` — so the few-shot cannot drift from the schema, and a machine added to `state.js` is buildable with no prompt edit. All 27 machine types are covered.

## Keys

Settings deliberately do **not** live in `App.config`: `exportWorkspaceState()` deep-copies the whole config into every workspace tab and `getBackupPayload()` writes it to IndexedDB, so a key there would be a key on disk. StateMate keeps its own store under its own localStorage key, and a test asserts the key reaches none of the four serializers — including `getEditorSettingsData()`, the settings profile users hand to each other.

BYOK, no server, nothing logged. In Electron the request goes through the main process, which sidesteps every provider's CORS policy.

## Drive-by fix

`loadExampleFile` ended in `snapshot()` — recording the example that had just been loaded, so the first <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> restored the example rather than the work it replaced. `performClear()` also empties `App.history`, so the stack is now carried across it by hand; without that, loading an example was an edit that could not be undone *and* discarded every undo point behind it.

## Notes

- The whole feature adds **exactly one name** to `bridge.js` (`loadExample` out, `openStateMate` in). Everything else wires listeners at creation, the way `reference.js` does.
- An exact algorithm outranks the model in the palette — typing "minimize" surfaces the real DFA Minimize construction above the ask row.
- `tests/dom-stub.js` gained `append`/`prepend`, real DOM methods `showExampleCard` already used.
- Version bumped to 2.1.0; `package.json` had drifted behind the `v2.0.1` tag, so the About dialog was reporting the wrong version.

**711 tests passing** (80 new). Production build clean. Every path above was also driven in a real browser, not only under the stub.

body:
## What changed

- Replace the DocuSeal report's legacy placeholder manifest with the synthesis-derived WGO manifest.
- Record structured business concerns and conclusions, evidence boundaries, source provenance, reviewer versions, and report relationships.
- Add the latest API-equivalent cost summary under `execution.costEstimate`.
- Preserve the Unreconciled result honestly with `totalUsd: null` and the included-evidence subtotal as `reconciledSubtotalUsd: 151.49`.
- Normalize all 34 displayed monetary values in `controls/cost-estimate.md` to dollars and cents (`$X.XX`). Exact fractional values remain in the frozen calculation JSON.

## Why

The existing manifest was an ingestion-era placeholder with unresolved labels and no machine-readable business conclusions, reviewer provenance, or cost state. Replacing it with the completed audit contract lets WGO and future processors understand why the audit ran, what it concluded, and the latest cost status without treating an incomplete subtotal as a final total.

## Impact

The DocuSeal report becomes compatible with the manifest contract introduced by [wgo-audit/code#10](https://github.com/wgo-audit/code/pull/10). No audit findings or exact calculation evidence change; this PR updates report metadata and monetary display formatting only.

## Merge order and current check

Merge [reports#1](https://github.com/wgo-audit/reports/pull/1) before this PR. Its removal of the obsolete ingestion scripts and `Reindex` workflow prevents the legacy indexer from rewriting the new manifest into its old `label` model. The current `Reindex / verify` failure is that known dependency: its log shows only generated `README.md` and `audits/index.json` label changes. Do not commit those obsolete derived changes here.

The manifest contract itself is introduced by [wgo-audit/code#10](https://github.com/wgo-audit/code/pull/10), which should also merge before this report is published.

## Validation

- `manifest.json` parses as valid JSON.
- Current manifest validator: 0 errors and 0 warnings for the manifest.
- All 34 displayed monetary values use `$X.XX`; no fractional-cent display remains.
- Published files match the generated DocuSeal audit copies byte-for-byte.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Existing limitation

The complete historical audit predates parts of the current WGO structural contract and still reports 89 unrelated legacy-format errors. This PR does not modify or claim to resolve those audit artifacts.

author: ionfwsrijan
body:
## Problem

`src/api/plaid-webhook.ts` prepends every reconciliation event to a module-level `reconciliationLogs` array with no upper bound. On every webhook invocation the array grows by one entry and is never trimmed, so a long-running server leaks memory and can eventually OOM. (issue #1545)

## Fix

- Added a `MAX_RECONCILIATION_LOGS` constant (500) bounding the in-memory buffer.
- After each `reconciliationLogs.unshift(...)`, the array length is trimmed to `MAX_RECONCILIATION_LOGS` so only the most-recent entries are retained, preventing unbounded growth.

## Files changed

- src/api/plaid-webhook.ts — capped the reconciliation log buffer.

## Testing

Static review only; dependencies are not installed so no build/lint was run. Verified the trim runs after each append and limits the array to `MAX_RECONCILIATION_LOGS` entries.

Closes #1545

## Summary

A persisted `/loop` is owned by a durable session ID, while its captured route remains stable across `/new`. The gateway watcher previously rebuilt only the route, which could permit a due wakeup from the previous conversation to enter its replacement.

This change:

- verifies that the route still resolves to the loop's recorded session before claiming a wakeup;
- attaches existing strict-session metadata to every accepted wakeup, so a reset that races after verification is rejected before a new turn begins;
- clears the outgoing loop at `/new`, and clears a claimed wakeup if the strict gate rejects it; and
- preserves the explicit compression migration path.

author: mirek
body:
## Summary

- `@prelude/emitter` `emit()` iterated the live listener `Set`; JS Sets visit entries added during iteration, so a listener registered from inside a handler ran in the *same* emit. Concretely, the common pattern of a `once` handler that re-registers itself (`const h = () => { …; e.once('x', h) }`) re-fired unboundedly within a single `emit('x')` whenever another `'x'` listener kept the Set alive (1000 calls in the repro, i.e. an infinite loop without a guard).
- Iterate a snapshot (`Array.from`), matching Node's `EventEmitter` semantics: listeners added during an emit run from the next emit. Tests cover the self-re-registering `once` and add-during-emit ordering.

## Validation

Package tests, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` green locally; CI on Node 22/24 gates the merge.

## Summary

Principal-engineer audit of the Android/Kotlin Kotha translator.

### Changes
- Request microphone permission only when entering active translation.
- Remove unused CAMERA and foreground-service permissions.
- Stop using destructive Room migration fallback, which could erase conversation history.
- Add an explicit `TranslationResult` model to prepare the translation layer for real error handling instead of implicit demo fallbacks.

### Audit findings still requiring architectural work
- `RelayTransport` is currently a simulation/loopback implementation, not a real multi-device transport.
- Gemini API credentials are embedded into the Android client through `BuildConfig`; production should put the provider credential behind a trusted backend/token broker.
- Translation/audio fallback currently fabricates sample phrases and synthetic tones. That must be replaced with an explicit unavailable/error state in production.
- Gemini response parsing should use typed Moshi DTOs rather than regex over JSON.
- Audio capture and playback need stronger lifecycle ownership and instrumentation tests.
- Add a Gradle wrapper and CI build/test workflow before treating the repository as release-ready.

This PR deliberately fixes the low-risk correctness/security issues without pretending the simulated transport is production networking.

author: bhall2001
body:
## The problem

Devcontainers commonly bind-mount the host's commands directory read-only:

```jsonc
"source=${localEnv:HOME}/.claude/commands,target=/home/node/.claude/commands,type=bind,readonly"
```

That is the **correct** setup — SET is installed once on the host and every container inherits it, with no way for a container to corrupt the install. But under `set -euo pipefail` the installer's `mkdir -p "$COMMANDS_DIR"` aborted with a bare `Permission denied` and no explanation, which reads like a broken installer rather than a working design.

## The fix

Probe writability up front and explain what's actually going on.

**In a container:**
```
[SET] Cannot write to /home/node/.claude/commands

[SET] This looks like a container, where ~/.claude/commands is typically
[SET] bind-mounted read-only from the host. That is intentional — SET is
[SET] installed once on the HOST and every container inherits it.

[SET]   Fix: run this installer on the host, then restart the container.
[SET]   Do NOT try to install SET inside the container.

[SET] Currently mounted SET version: 1.3.2
```

**On a host** (a real permissions problem), the same check points at ownership instead.

Reporting the mounted version matters: it tells the user what the container actually has, which is the question they're really asking when an update appears not to take.

Container detection uses `/.dockerenv`, `REMOTE_CONTAINERS`, and `CODESPACES`.

## Verified

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| Normal writable install | unchanged — installs successfully |
| Read-only, no container markers | ownership/permissions advice |
| Read-only, `REMOTE_CONTAINERS=true` | container model + host instructions + mounted version |

## Also

`update.md` documents the same constraint — an in-container agent running `/set-update` is exactly who hits this, and it should relay the host instruction rather than trying to work around the mount.

## Scope

Rebased onto `main` after #20 merged; version **1.3.3**. Installer + one doc note, no command-logic changes.

author: holland-built
body:
Closes #65

## What changed

`createSubnet` records a failed `nextavailablesubnet` lookup as `"(unavailable)"`, and the comment above it states the rule: a failed preview is DETECTABLE **but it must still never abort the dry run**. `createSubnets` broke that one level up — the placeholder is non-empty, so it passed the reverse-zone guard, reached `CidrToReverseZone`, and killed the whole preview with `invalid CIDR address: (unavailable)/24`. One transient 500 destroyed the safe mode operators are told to run first.

The guard is now the **`address_preview` marker**, which `createSubnet` sets in exactly the two states where it has no usable address:

| preview outcome | `address` | `address_preview` | reverse zone |
|---|---|---|---|
| succeeded | a real IP | absent | planned, as before |
| block genuinely full | `""` | `none-available` | skipped, and now says so |
| lookup failed | `"(unavailable)"` | `unavailable` + `reason` | skipped, naming the upstream reason |
| lookup succeeded, upstream returned a non-address | garbage | absent | **still aborts** |

`createDHCPRange` one branch up has always emitted-and-continued on the same unusable address — the reverse-zone step was the outlier.

The `none-available` row is a second, smaller fix: that case skipped in total silence, so a preview under-reported what a real run would create and said nothing about it.

## Why the guard is the marker and not a parse of the address

My first approach was `net.ParseIP(addr) == nil`. Codex rejected it on two counts before any code was written, both correct:

- It would soften a **successful** lookup that returned a non-address — an upstream contract violation that should still fail loudly.
- It would break `TestSiteProvisionDryRunFailureNeverRollsBack` (`site_rollback_test.go:437`), which deliberately injects `previewAddrs = ["10.10.1.0", "not-an-ip"]` as its failure mechanism. That test is untouched by this PR and still green.

Codex also flagged that the message threw away `subnet["reason"]` — the operator-safe upstream sentence — and reported only the bare `unavailable` marker. The message now prefers `reason`.

## Watching the guards fail

| Break | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| marker branch disabled (old guard restored) | `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_FailedPreviewDoesNotAbortTheRun` | RED — `createSubnets() error = invalid CIDR address: (unavailable)/24, want nil` |
| same break | `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_FullBlockSaysWhyTheZoneWasSkipped` | RED — `a silently skipped reverse zone; steps=[[DRY-RUN] Creating subnet /24 ...]` |
| message drops `reason`, reports the bare marker | `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_FailedPreviewDoesNotAbortTheRun` | RED — `step = "  Cannot preview the reverse zone for test-net: unavailable", want the upstream reason` |
| tree restored | all four | GREEN |

## Tests added

All four drive `createSubnets` — the level where the promise was broken. `site_test.go` already pins `createSubnet` s three preview states one level down, and that is precisely why this was invisible: the guarantee was only ever asserted below the layer violating it.

- `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_FailedPreviewDoesNotAbortTheRun` — no error, the skip is announced with the upstream reason, nothing fabricated into `reverse_zones`, and the subnet preview is still recorded so the run really did carry on
- `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_FullBlockSaysWhyTheZoneWasSkipped` — names `none-available`, so a full block and a broken lookup do not read the same
- `TestCreateSubnets_DryRun_GoodPreviewStillPlansTheReverseZone` — happy path unmoved, `created: false` preserved
- `TestCreateSubnets_UnmarkedGarbageAddressStillAborts` — the deliberate non-softening

## What I ran

```
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/provision/ ./internal/server/   # ok
go test -race ./...                                              # all packages ok
```

author: hjosugi
body:
Closes #1398

#1191 admitted the expression body and held this one. The gate's comment fixed
the obligation on whoever landed it — *"a slice that later admits the block body
must move this assertion and leave the lifted-lambda wording untouched"* — and
that is what this does.

## Four things had to learn about a block body

Each is the same shape: something keyed on `=>` or on a brace, where a lambda
is keyed on its `(`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `lambda_parameters_end` | spans by braces when the body is a block, so every reader of that span — scope building, the lift walk, the capture check — covers the block without learning about it |
| `emit_lifted_argument_lambdas` | lowers a block through `lower_body`, the walk that lowers a named function body, so `return` is an ordinary return. A second statement lowerer for lambdas is how the two would drift |
| `parent_block_open` | could not see a lambda scope at all: it walks `{` tokens, and a lambda is keyed on `(`. A block body was parented to the enclosing function, so the parameters of the lambda were not in scope inside its own body |
| `lambda_captures` | a binding declared inside the body is not a capture. Comparing scope ids alone called every block local one and refused with `E2S96`, which is about reading an *enclosing* binding |

The use-scope resolution needed the same correction from the other side: a use
inside a block-bodied lambda resolved in the parameter scope, which is the
*parent* of the block holding the binding, so a local read three lines below its
own declaration reported `E2S35 outside its lexical scope`.

## The widening that only a real program caught

Accepting `(params) { ... }` made **every** parenthesised group followed by a
brace a lambda. `if (a == b) { ... }` spanned as one, its condition became a
parameter list, and the bindings read there were redeclared —
`bootstrap/stage1/compiler.kofun` reported `E2S47 duplicate binding` on a `let`
it declares once.

Every fixture here passed, because every one of them used the new construct. The
misparse needed an *old* construct with the same token shape;
`selfhost-profile` found it. The fix is the token the grammar already names:
`trailing_block_lambda = "fn", "(", parameters, ")", block`.

Requiring it of `previous` then broke the callers that pass `-1` — half of them
hold a `(` they already know is a lambda and have no previous token to give — so
the question is asked of the source instead. That walk is backwards over
whitespace only, and a `#` earlier on the same line answers no: it refuses a
valid lambda rather than accepting an invalid span, chosen rather than inherited.

## The boundary moved, it did not disappear

A block-bodied lambda outside the trailing position is now refused **by name**.
Before this it was refused by accident — `E2S35 unknown lexical binding` about
the parameter of the lambda itself, a symbol the author did not write.

Three fixtures elsewhere held that accident and each moves to what it now tests:

- `spec/grammar.ebnf` derives `trailing_block_lambda`, and
  `unsupported_block_lambda` in `issues_35_47` asserted the old misparse while
  asking, in its own comment, to be updated together with the grammar. Both done.
- `tests/conformance/int-bits/block_trailing_lambda.kofun` reaches the check it
  always deserved: `E2S169: \`and\` takes no trailing lambda`. It keeps its IR and
  token checkpoints like every other refusal in that loop, so it joins the loop —
  and a new `block_lambda_position` fixture takes over the atomicity case, which
  needs a refusal that really is parser-owned.
- the registry's `e2s158_trailing_lambda` companion becomes the position shape,
  because that is the boundary `E2S158` still has.

## Verification

`task verify` green on eedb3edb with a clean working tree. The Kofun twin
carries every change and round-trips identically; `SHA256SUMS`, the manifest
seed digest, and the release evidence pack were regenerated by their owning
commands after the last edit. `stage2-events` counts 416 repository error
companions, recomputed by running the gate.

author: mrandreyisachenko
body:
oneinch_lo_executions_macro.sql picks a trusted token's leg value first when computing amount_usd, to avoid trusting a manipulated or illiquid price on the other leg. That's correct most of the time, but a maker can set a degenerate making_amount (as low as 1 wei on-chain - checked the raw decoded calldata and the contract's own output_0 return value, this is not a decode error) while genuinely trading real value on the taker side. Since the trusted leg always won regardless of its own amount, amount_usd landed near zero for these fills even though the trade had real value.

Measured against production data: 169 LOP fills in the 30 days before 2026-08-16, across ethereum, bnb, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon and gnosis, show this pattern - always a wrapped-native maker leg with a dust amount. About $656/month understated.

Fix: the trusted leg only loses if its own transferred amount, normalized by decimals, is below 1e-9 of a token - nine orders of magnitude above the observed 1-wei bug pattern and far below any plausible real trade. A trusted leg with a normal amount but a smaller dollar value than an untrusted leg (for example an illiquid token with an inflated price) is untouched, exactly as before.

First version of this fix compared dollar values between legs instead of the trusted leg's own amount, and that turned out to be wrong: a regression sweep of real trades found a DATA/USDC pair where DATA (illiquid, ~$243k) overstates value and USDC's smaller ~$173 is the correct one - exactly the case trusted-preference exists to protect. A dollar-ratio check can't tell "trusted leg has a dust amount" apart from "untrusted leg has an inflated price," so it would have broken that case. Checking the trusted leg's own amount instead of a ratio fixes that.

Validation, all against real production data:
- Reproduced the exact fix logic against the known bad transaction (17 fills in one batch, each independently decoded with its own order_hash and call_trace_address - not a trace-collision issue): 6 of 17 corrected to real values, 11 unchanged only because those particular tokens have no price data at all (a separate, unrelated gap).
- Confirmed the DATA/USDC case above is untouched.
- Broad regression sweep: pulled every "normal-looking" trade (amount_usd > $1) in the 30-day window with a skewed leg ratio, expanded to 123 individual fills across 8 chains, diffed old vs new for each. 37 changed, all matching the dust-amount signature (old value 1e-15 to 1e-19, corrected to $0.005-$179). 86 unchanged, including every legitimate divergence case like DATA/USDC. No false positives found.

author: v22kumar
body:
## What happened

Twenty-one players, round two. Games died on a **two-to-three second** blink of the network and never came back — boards read "Reconnecting…" until people killed the app. The quarter-finals, semi-final and final were played on lichess instead.

## Why

The length of the outage was never the problem. Only **one** of the two ways a socket dies led back to a retry:

```dart
void _onError(Object error) {
  _cancelPingTimer();
  _controller?.add({'type': 'connection_error', ...});   // and stops
}

void _onDone() {
  ...
  _scheduleReconnect();                                   // only path that retries
}
```

The sequence that killed each game:

| t | event |
|---|---|
| 0.0s | network blinks, socket dies → `onDone` → retry queued for t=1 |
| 1.0s | retry runs; network **still down** → failure arrives on `onError` |
| 1.0s | `onError` announces it and **schedules nothing** |
| 3.0s | network is back. Nobody is trying. |

A three-second blackout was therefore *worse* than a thirty-second one — it guaranteed the single retry landed while the radio was still down. Every phone that blinked died permanently, which is exactly why it hit so many at once.

The bloc's comment — *"the reconnect always replays a full 'state' snapshot"* — was true whenever a reconnect happened. It just never happened on the error path.

## The fix

- **`onError` schedules a retry**, like `onDone`. Every road out of a live socket leads back to one.
- **A `connect()` that throws immediately is caught** — "no route to host" while the radio is down is the ordinary case here, and thrown from inside a delayed callback it landed in nobody's hands and ended the retries.
- **One drop, one reconnection**: `onError` and `onDone` both fire for the same death, so scheduling is guarded, and the previous subscription is cancelled before a new socket opens — otherwise two sockets race to apply the same moves.
- **Jitter on the delay** (100–500 ms on top of the backoff): twenty-one phones losing the same access point and reconnecting on the same tick are each other's outage.

## Not in this PR

The 60-second **disconnect forfeit** and the missing organiser **match reset** are real and separate — a game killed by an outage still can't be replayed in-app. Worth doing before the Play Store release, but they are not what happened on Saturday.

## Checks

Five tests, one per road, including the exact tournament sequence (error-during-retry). **Validated by CI, not locally** — this container was rebuilt without the Flutter SDK, so the pinned 3.44.8 in `ci-tests.yml` is the gate.

Gladys 4.86 lets a manifest name the shelves of the store catalog it is browsed under, 1 to 3 keys of a fixed vocabulary. Air quality is one shelf and not three: `["environment"]`, the field being about where the store lists the integration, not about what the core renders — that is the `category` of a feature, a different word for a different thing.

Declaring the field at all requires a `gladys_version` floor at 4.86.0. Ours already is, for the `no2-sensor`/`o3-sensor`/`so2-sensor` feature categories, so nothing moves there; `test/manifest.test.js` now checks the coupling, the 1-3 bound and the vocabulary, since the store drops an unknown key with a warning rather than refusing it — a typo would be invisible otherwise.

The SDK goes to ^0.12.0, an additive release: nothing in the code has to adapt. It does start exporting NO2_SENSOR, O3_SENSOR and SO2_SENSOR, which `airQualityStation.js` spells out as strings; that stays as it is, the flat list the core validates against being the contract. The two README/CLAUDE.md notes saying the SDK had no such constant are updated so they stop claiming something false.

author: cwdcwd
body:
Closes genebaer-pyg.4. Stacked — **merge #9 → #10 → #11 → this.**

The mechanism behind the epic's reframe: a `RunConfig` names a scoring **contract**, and the registry decides which connected workers satisfy it. Nothing in a run ever names a machine — which is exactly why a worker thread and a browser tab are interchangeable rather than two architectures.

## Version is part of the match

Jobs now carry `evaluatorVersion`, and matching is on `evaluatorId@version`. A v1 worker is **never** handed a v2 job.

This isn't fussiness: scores from two model versions are not comparable, so serving one run from both would distort its fitness landscape mid-flight **with no error anywhere**. The canary makes the point — matching on id alone reds **30 tests**.

## HTTP worker transport

`register` / `deregister` / `claim` / `score` / `heartbeat` / `fail` / list. Deliberately transport-agnostic in shape; nothing in it knows what kind of worker it's talking to, which is what lets the browser reuse it over WS in pyg.8.

Two choices worth flagging, both tested:

- **`score` is not gated on the lease still being valid.** If the job is still unscored, a late answer is perfectly good work and discarding it wastes an inference. Correctness lives in the queue's refusal to *overwrite*, not in rejecting late arrivals.
- **An unknown `workerId` gets 404**, not a silent idle — so a reaped worker learns to re-register instead of polling forever for work it will never be offered.

Reaped and deregistered workers have their leases released, so their jobs return to the queue rather than stranding.

author: michalvalco
body:
Adds `docs/citation_audit.md`: a footnote-by-footnote verification of all 36 footnotes in the peer-review manuscript "Appropriating Badiou's Appropriating Saint Paul: On Constructing a Migrant Asian Christian Identity" (*Theology Today*, MS TT-26-0019).

## What the document contains

- **Method and limitations** — states up front which sources were reachable and which were not, so the confidence of each row is bounded honestly.
- **Reference table** — every bibliographic item as `Footnote # | As cited | Verified form | Status (OK / Corrected / Not found / Unverifiable)`.
- **Quotation checks** — the direct Badiou quotation, the two terms placed in quotation marks and attributed to him, and a claim attributed by name to Thomas Nail.
- **Editor's summary** — four patterns, a table of items that need author input, and a recommendation.

## Findings

- 33 distinct bibliographic items across 36 footnotes. **Nothing appears fabricated** — every cited work exists.
- **9 corrections**, including a wrong author given name, a wrong publisher and place, a wrong publication year, an inverted East Asian name, and a wrong place of publication for a 1998 imprint.
- **3 items unverifiable** from indexed sources (a Chinese-language seminary journal, two chapter page ranges).
- **4 quotation-level problems**, the most serious being an evaluative claim attributed by name to a living scholar that the available evidence appears to contradict.
- Errors cluster in the Asian-studies references the manuscript's original contribution rests on, and in the Badiou short-form citations — a distribution the summary flags for the editor.

## Notes

Direct access to the Crossref API, WorldCat and several publisher sites was blocked at the network layer in this environment; verification proceeded through search-surfaced records of those sources instead, cross-checked across independent sources where possible. The document says this in its own limitations section rather than presenting the results as more settled than they are.

No code changes — documentation only.

body:
Implements **Sprite rendering and collision detection**.

Acceptance criteria:
- Opening index.html via file:// renders an 11-column by 5-row grid (55 total) of identically colored/sized rectangles positioned in the classic invader formation, drawn with fillRect.
- The formation moves sideways as a single unit each step; when any invader reaches the left or right canvas edge, the whole formation drops down by a fixed step and reverses horizontal direction on the next step.
- invaders.js exposes update/draw entry points and collision.js exposes a collide entry point; game.js only imports and calls them (wiring diff only) without reimplementing canvas setup, the game loop, player input, or the bullet entity.
- collision.js implements one generic reusable AABB overlap function used for both pairings: player bullet vs each invader, and any invader-owned bullet vs the player ship (no duplicated per-pairing collision logic).
- When a player bullet's bounding box overlaps an invader's bounding box: the bullet is removed, the invader is replaced by a short fixed-duration explosion visual before being removed, and the score value increases by a fixed, consistent amount.
- When a bullet flagged as invader-owned overlaps the player ship's bounding box, the existing lives-decrement hook (owned by the player-ship card) is invoked exactly once per overlap; this card implements no lives/game-over logic of its own. Since no invader ever fires within this card's scope, this path is verified manually (e.g. a temporary console/debug invocation documented in the README), not through normal play.
- Within the game loop, collision resolution for a frame completes before that frame's draw/render calls run (collide-then-draw ordering), confirmed by code review of game.js, invaders.js, and collision.js.
- All 55 invaders share identical visual appearance (same color and size); no per-row or per-invader visual variation is implemented.
- invaders.js contains no invader bullet-spawning or shooting-AI logic (explicitly deferred to 'Level 2: they shoot back').
- The game still opens and runs correctly via a direct file:// double-click of index.html with no console errors, no build step, no bundler, and no new external dependency introduced by invaders.js or collision.js.

author: binflip
body:
Closes #13.

`to_path` rendered its segments into a string and then rewrote that string with
a chain of `replace` calls. Three defects fell out of the chain.

## The one that matters

**Absolute prefixes survived.** `C:\evil.exe` rendered as `C:/evil.exe`, and on
Windows `Path::join` discards the base when the argument is absolute:

```rust
Path::new("out").join("C:/evil.exe")   // -> C:/evil.exe
```

That is reachable through the crate's own extraction example — `dump.rs` renders
with `to_path()` at line 335 and joins at line 347 — so a hostile installer
could write outside the directory the user chose, in a crate whose threat model
is that every input byte is adversarial.

Drive specifiers, UNC prefixes and leading separators are now removed. The test
for it checks the rendered string rather than `Path::is_relative`, because a
Windows drive path looks relative to a Unix `Path` and the assertion would pass
for free on CI.

## The other two

- `.replace("..", "_")` matched substrings, so `file..txt` became `file_txt`.
  Traversal is now handled per component: only a component that *is* `..`
  becomes `_`.
- `.replace("//", "/")` collapses non-overlapping matches only, so `a///b` came
  out as `a//b`. Components are assembled with single separators now, so it
  cannot recur.

Language strings were also dropped outright, which let two files whose names
differ only by the reference collide on one path; they render as `_lang_<id>`.

## `to_install_path`

The same writer gained a second style, which is the point of doing this before
the destination-path work: `to_install_path()` reproduces the path the installer
would write to — references verbatim, backslash separators, a leading
`$INSTDIR\` removed, empty becoming `file` — matching 7-Zip's `GetReducedName`
exactly, including that the prefix strip is case-insensitive and requires the
trailing backslash (a bare `$INSTDIR` is left alone; I checked the reference
rather than guessing).

So `dest_path()?.to_install_path()` will give byte-identical output to 7-Zip's
listing, while `dest_path()?.to_path()` gives the safe relative form. That was
the open question from the API discussion, now settled in the code.

`Display` picks up 7-Zip's wording for the two unresolvable cases: `$(LSTR_n)`
and `$_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_SHELL_[primary,fallback]`.

## Cost

Rendering is one pass into a pre-sized buffer instead of five intermediate
strings, and shell folders write into the caller's buffer rather than
allocating a `String` per reference. `shell_folder_name` stays as a thin
wrapper for external callers.

## Behaviour changes worth noting in review

- `Display` output changed for language strings and unmappable shell folders
  (both previously used a non-7-Zip spelling).
- `to_path()` output changed for language strings, unmappable shell folders,
  absolute paths, `..`, `.` and repeated separators — every case a fix.

`cargo test` (252), `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` and
`cargo doc` with `-D warnings` are clean.

author: jbailes
body:
The ref was derived from a module's position in required + optional. That welded
"is this module essential" to "which event kinds does it own": promoting one
module from optional to required renumbered every module after it. Measured on
the current inventory, adding a required module shifts ten of them and moves
economizer's event kinds from 11009 to 11265 -- every grant naming them, every
AIMEE_*_EVENT_* constant in C, every deployed config -- for a change that is
nothing at runtime.

And it IS nothing at runtime. The formula lives in exactly one enforcing place,
validate_module_process_contracts.py; everywhere else it appears it is a comment
explaining why a constant has its value. The bus never derives anything from a
ref: bus_runtime.c matches a grant by equality and event kinds are plain uint32s
checked against a grant's serve list. No routing, no authorization and no
start-up ordering reads an ordinal.

So the ref is now DECLARED, in principal_refs alongside required and optional.
Every current value is preserved exactly as the positional scheme produced it,
which is what makes this a no-op: verified module by module that each declared
ref and every carved event kind still equals what process-contracts.json already
ships.

Refs are RETIRED, NEVER RECYCLED. retired_principal_refs records numbers that
have been used and must never be issued again, so a grant or a capture still
naming a departed module can never come to mean a different one. The validator
refuses a ref that appears there.

Component ORDER in process-contracts.json is no longer meaningful either, so the
check that it exactly follow inventory order becomes a coverage check. Order used
to matter only because position was identity.

Proved rather than asserted: promoting a module to required now leaves every ref
untouched, and is refused by the required-process policy allow-list instead --
which is the right reason to refuse it, a policy decision rather than a
renumbering event. test_principal_ref_identity pins that, plus rejection of
duplicate and retired refs, and is wired into module-inventory CI.

Schema goes to 2; the five inventory readers that assert its envelope are updated
together. No module is added or reclassified here.

author: oferchen
body:
## Problem

`crates/engine/src/local_copy/context_impl/state.rs` had grown to 1549 lines holding four unrelated concerns, and `CopyContext::new` was a 212-line constructor with 130 lines of inline derivation in its body. Anything touching one concern had to be read against all four.

## Change

Pure movement - no behaviour change, no signature change, no new abstraction. `state.rs` keeps the context's own state and drops to 554 lines; each concern moves to its own submodule alongside the ones the crate already splits this way (`local_copy/executor/file/`, `local_copy/dir_merge/parse/`):

| Module | Lines | Concern |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_setup.rs` | 170 | `--write-batch` buffer, NDX codec, flist writer, token encoder, adaptive level |
| `link_dest.rs` | 278 | `--link-dest` / `--copy-dest` / `--compare-dest` alternate-basis resolution |
| `backup.rs` | 508 | `--backup` / `--backup-dir` staging and the forced removal that makes room |
| `deferred_updates.rs` | 140 | `--delay-updates` scheduling and the deferred-deletion plan |

`CopyContext::new`'s body becomes five named calls, so the constructor reads as what it assembles rather than how each piece is derived:

```rust
let batch_delta_buf = build_batch_delta_buffer(&options);
let batch_ndx_codec = build_batch_ndx_codec(&options);
let batch_flist_writer = build_batch_flist_writer(&options);
let batch_token_encoder = build_batch_token_encoder(&options);
let adaptive_level = build_adaptive_level_controller(&options);
```

## Note on the rebase

This branch predates #7356 (`--safe-links` before the backup fast path), which landed in the same file. #7356's `backup_refused_by_safe_links` predicate and both of its call sites are carried forward verbatim into `backup.rs`, where the backup concern now lives - they are not re-derived. The 36 `safe_links` tests, including #7356's own `safe_links_blocks_backup_of_unsafe_destination_symlink`, pass on this branch.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p engine --all-features`: 4974 passed, 24 skipped - the same set as master.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.
- Net line count +61, which is the module headers and the five extracted constructor helpers; nothing else was added.

body:
## Summary

This targets the remaining Romanian EPG gaps without adding fuzzy matching or changing the existing EPGShare priority.

It adds a small audited local override layer for provider channel identities that the pinned `iptv-org/epg` `programetv.ro` channel list is missing or cannot represent unambiguously.

### New Romanian EPG targets

| Playlist channel | Programetv site ID | Probe programmes |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `Antena3CNN.ro` | `antena-3-cnn` | 45 |
| `TVSE.ro@SD` (Exploris) | `exploris-tv` | 93 |
| `TeleMoldovaPlus.ro@SD` | `telemoldova-plus` | 36 |
| `Telestar1.ro@SD` | `telestar-1` | 48 |

`epg_prepare` now optionally loads audited rows from:

`data/epg_site_overrides/<provider>/*.channels.xml`

author: atomlink-ye
body:
`TeamWakeReconciler` iterated `members.filter(m => m.role === 'member')`, so a direct mailbox message addressed to the Team Lead was persisted and then never materialised. It stayed queued forever. This is the "member→lead messages are never materialised" gap from the collaboration cross-check.

The change is one line plus a comment: iterate every live participant instead of members only. The existing guards are untouched — an `active` participant is still skipped (busy delivery stays a durable queue rather than a second concurrent turn), `stopped`/`failed` are still skipped, and the planner still restricts work-attempt wake messages to their assignee. Only the direct-message path gains the Lead as a possible recipient.

## Why this is opened for CI feedback, not for merge tonight

PR #68 reworks this area more thoroughly (`CollaborationActivationReconciler` + provider-neutral `ParticipantActivation`) and reportedly covers the same gap with an auditable claim chain. That work is not mine and is still draft.

This PR exists because the gap currently has **no runtime evidence either way**: #68 is draft, and `real-runtime` skips drafts by design (its summary says so explicitly — "This is a skip, not a pass"). So nothing has yet exercised a member→lead message end to end against a real provider.

Running this branch through `real-runtime` produces that evidence against the architecture that is on `master` today. **Whoever picks this up should decide between this and #68 rather than merging both** — if #68 lands first, close this.

## What a green here does and does not show

It shows the four real-provider flows still pass with the Lead included in reconciliation — i.e. no regression from widening the loop. It does **not** by itself prove a member→lead message was delivered and consumed; the existing smokes do not exercise that path. That assertion is still missing and is recorded as such in the round's C-stage evidence ledger.

author: jfallows
body:
## Description

Adds `JsonModelExtFactorySpi`/`JsonModelExt`/`JsonModelExtContext`/`JsonModelExtHandler`, the JSON-model analog of `AvroModelExtFactorySpi` — lets a provider install its own additional pipeline stage(s) into `model: json`'s decode pipeline via `ServiceLoader`, discovered per schema/config through the existing generic `ModelInfo.extensions()` mechanism (`$defs/models/model/allOf` in the aggregated JSON schema). No behavior changes for configs that install no extension.

Building and exercising this against a real consumer (a decode-time field-disclosure extension) surfaced four latent bugs, all invisible until a live decode pipeline with an installed, value-substituting extension was exercised for the first time:

- **`model-json`'s own schema patch** wrongly closed `options.value` to provider extensions (`additionalProperties: false`) — model-avro's own schema patch has no such restriction; this one was inconsistent with it.
- **`JsonModelDecoderPipeline`** conflated destination-buffer-sizing padding (`decodePadding()`, extension-inclusive) with the catalog's own source-side framing-byte skip count (extension-exclusive) — a new `prefix()` method separates the two, matching how `AvroModelDecoderPipeline` already keeps them apart.
- **`common-json`'s `JsonStream.into(JsonGeneratorEx)`** had no structured-delivery opt-out, unlike its `into(JsonSink)` sibling — a value-substituting stage needs one, since byte-preserving delivery splices bytes a substitute doesn't have. New `into(JsonGeneratorEx, Map<String, ?>)` overload mirrors `JsonEx.createSink`'s existing config-bag convention.
- **`TestBindingFactory`** (the `type: test` binding backing every k3po `*IT.java` test engine-wide) never handled `ModelStatus.OVERFLOW` from a model's own pipeline — a value whose transformed size exceeds the fixed model buffer spun forever against an already-full destination window with no exception. It also hardcoded every call's source-side flags to "complete message," so a value split across multiple `DATA` frames presented each continuation frame to the model as a spurious fresh restart, and destination-fill state reset on every call instead of persisting across frames. This is the same class of bug independently surfaced and fixed by PR #2383 for the encode direction.

`JsonTransformable` also picks up the same self-bounded generic type parameter PR #2383 gave `AvroTransformable`, so `JsonModelHandlerImpl.extend()` no longer needs to cast the result of an installed extension's `transform()` back to `JsonStream`.

### Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw clean verify -pl runtime/model-json,runtime/common-json` — unit tests, `JsonModelIT` (10 tests), checkstyle, license — all pass
- [x] `./mvnw clean verify -pl runtime/engine` — 208 tests including `HalfDuplexIT`/`SimplexIT`/`DuplexIT` (the k3po ITs exercising `TestBindingFactory`'s DATA-frame semantics), all pass
- [x] `./mvnw clean verify -pl runtime/model-avro,runtime/model-protobuf,runtime/binding-kafka` — broader regression sweep (395+ tests) against the `TestBindingFactory` fix, all pass
- [x] Confirmed the `TestBindingFactory` fix resolves a real, previously-latent regression in two existing `JsonModelIT` fragmented-schema-rejection tests before landing the final version

Fixes # (none — surfaced while building `JsonModelExtFactorySpi` for issue #1682, not tied to a specific bug report)

## What

**CLAUDE.md** gains a "State discipline" section (explicit Owner order, spec-9 precedent for same-day execution):

- Verify state live before every mutation — PR open/merged state checked immediately *before* any push; file content fetched from the target branch before modifying. A check after the push is an incident report, not a check.
- Session start ritual for repo work: list open PRs and branches first.
- Merged branches deleted promptly; a commit stranded on a merged branch is re-landed on a fresh branch, never left as the only copy.

**Spec 10** (still PROPOSED) gains rule 2 — *literal wording wins*: when the Owner specifies an output element literally (label, menu, structure), the literal spec beats interpretation; diverge → ask. Targets the front-diamond template, awaits the Owner's decision. Counterargument on record: scoped to concrete, enumerable wording only, so it can't suppress design judgment on open requests like "beautify."

## Process note

This is the second stranded-commit re-land today: the first version of this change was pushed to `generic-labels-cleanup` after #30 had merged — the exact failure the rule describes, made while writing the rule. The check-then-push order is now stated explicitly in the rule text. Stale branches `hub-nav-and-experience-map` and `generic-labels-cleanup` can both be deleted; their stray commits are fully re-landed here and in #32.

author: danielchalmers
body:
## Summary

Fixes the flake in `options.spec.ts › exports current settings from global settings` (3 of 8 isolated runs failed on `main`), flagged during the dependency PR #116.

**Root cause.** The test seeded an expired snooze (`until: 1_234_567_890` — epoch ms in 2009). The seed's own `storage.onChanged` woke the background's clear-expired-snooze pass (`src/background/snooze.ts`), which rewrote the entire stored object through `updateData`: snooze cleared, groups normalized to carry `enabled: true`, `rulesVersion` bumped. That rewrite raced both the test's raw `readStorage()` snapshot and the export (which serializes the normalized `loadData()` view) — the test only passed when the rewrite happened to land before the snapshot.

**Fix.** Seeds are now fixed points of `normalizeStoredData`, so nothing ever needs rewriting mid-test:

- `defaultGroup` in `test/e2e/helpers.ts` carries `enabled: true`, mirroring the app's `createDefaultGroup()`. This also hardens `keeps existing settings when global settings import fails`, which deep-compares a raw snapshot the same way.
- The export test's `work-hours` group gains `enabled: true`, and its snooze moves to the far future — the same fixture shape the sibling import test already uses.

**Coverage kept.** The behavior the old fixture tripped over by accident is now pinned on purpose: a new `lifecycle.spec.ts` test seeds an expired snooze plus an unnormalized group and polls storage until the background persists the settled form — snooze cleared, `enabled` materialized, `rulesVersion` bumped.

## Test plan

- [x] Export test: **20/20** isolated runs (was 3/8 failing on `main`)
- [x] New expired-snooze test: 8/8 isolated runs
- [x] Full e2e suite: 44/44
- [x] `npm run check:fast` — format, lint, both typechecks, 174 unit tests

body:
## Description

This change replaces scattered string-based facility type checks (`type == 'rural'`, `type == 'urban'`) with a typed `FacilityType` enum, used consistently across models, services, and views. Firestore still stores the value as a lowercase string only at the persistence boundary via `FacilityType.fromFirestore()` / `.toFirestore()`, so no data migration is needed.

This picks up the work from #273 and #414, both of which were closed after review feedback went unaddressed. Specifically, this PR resolves:

- **From #273**: the test suite is now fully migrated — `optimization_service_test.dart`, its `optimization_service_regression_test.dart`, and `route_optimization_map_test.dart` all use `FacilityType` values. The `createFacility` helper in `optimization_service_test.dart` now takes a `FacilityType` parameter instead of a `String`, and the placeholder `"hospital"`/`"clinic"` values (which were never part of the enum) have been replaced with valid enum values rather than a direct string swap.
- **From #414**: `facility_profile_page.dart:182` called `.toUpperCase()` directly on `_facility!.type`, which no longer compiles now that `type` is an enum. Fixed by converting to the Firestore string form first (`type.toFirestore().toUpperCase()`).

While migrating, I also found a compile-break neither prior PR had touched: `admin_overview.dart` called `.toLowerCase()` on `facility.type` for search filtering and passed it directly where a `String` was expected for display. Both are fixed here as well.

Fixes #241

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] Chore / code cleanup / dependency update

## Verification & Checklist

- [x] `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .` (Code formatting)
- [x] `flutter analyze` (Static analysis check - zero warnings)
- [x] `flutter test` (Unit/widget tests — 205/205 passing)

Please also confirm:

- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

## Screenshots / Visual Proof

Not applicable. This change does not affect the UI's appearance or behavior — only the internal representation of facility type.

## Files touched

- `lib/models/facility.dart` — new `FacilityType` enum with Firestore string mapping
- `lib/services/simulation_service.dart`
- `lib/services/firebase_service.dart`
- `lib/services/optimization_service.dart`
- `lib/views/admin/route_optimization_map.dart`
- `lib/views/facility/facility_profile_page.dart`
- `lib/views/admin/admin_overview.dart`
- 9 test files updated to use `FacilityType` values consistently

## Summary

`DELETE FROM events` on content-event dedupe apply would CASCADE-delete a `command_audits` row. The quarantine archive copies event columns only, so `--restore` could not bring the audit back.

A prompt/transcript that carries an audit stays in the identification scan (same clustering rule as retention-held / attested rows) and is never archived or deleted. Apply has a last-line guard if a plan is stale.

- `DedupeContentEvents` apply with an audit on the later transcript of a pair: event + audit remain; ordinary prompt duplicates still move
- Three rows 9s apart, middle has an audit: middle + audit stay; the outer duplicate archives
- Planner unit: audit-held-only cluster yields no group; middle audit-held row keeps the cluster

`go test ./infrastructure/sqlite/` and `go tool golangci-lint run` exit 0.

Closes #1862
Leaves parent #1906 open

author: marsninja
body:
## What this is

Phase 4, the emitter's finish line for epic #8201 lane 2: the jsx port per the PyJsxProcessor audit, genai refusal parity pinned by test, the standing canary manifest in the internals doc, and the remaining-family flagged sweep. After this PR the emitter has zero refusals except genai (deliberately refused in both lanes) and a complete flag-lane validation map.

## jsx (differentially verified)

All seven audited methods ported mechanically: elements lower to jaclib `jsx(tag, attrs, children)` calls (dynamic tag recipes, `Constant(None)` fragments, element-name recipes; empty/spread-merged/plain attribute dicts; comment and whitespace-text child filtering via `get_normalized_text`); element names choose component `Name` vs tag-string `Constant` on leading case; string attribute values and text children pass through `html.unescape` at compile time (documented in the sealed-lane caveats list beside `textwrap.dedent`); slots lower to `Constant(None)`, comments to nothing. The fixture compiles a server-pinned module (placement pins via a temp-dir `jac.toml`) so the PyJsxProcessor lane is genuinely exercised, covering nested elements, comprehension children, string/expression/boolean attributes, spread attributes, fragments, and entity unescaping, with exact dump and recursive code-object equality against pyast_gen.

## genai parity

The parser never produces `genai_call`, and pyast_gen's refusal was latent (it constructed the ice and dropped it, failing later on empty py_ast). One-word fix makes pyast raise deliberately; the differential suite builds the construct synthetically and pins both lanes' refusals: pyast's "temporarily disabled" ice and the emitter's `NotImplementedError` naming the construct and location. Zero blast radius (dead branch).

## Canary manifest

`docs/internals/codegen-ir.md` section 11.2 now carries the named-file list validated under `JAC_CODEGEN=jcir` (19 suites across compiler, runtimelib, langserve, and language families, plus the full from-clean-cache dev-toolchain build on the jcir lane), with the run recipe and the one known exclusion (`test_micro_suite`, whose per-node `jac_link` assertion is the tooling contract the jcir tail omits by design). The cutover CI job can lift it verbatim.

## Phase 4 sweep results (all under JAC_CODEGEN=jcir, one named file at a time)

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| tests/compiler/test_client_codegen.jac | 14/14 |
| tests/compiler/test_codespace_inference.jac | 54/54 |
| tests/compiler/test_placement_evidence.jac | 5/5 |
| tests/compiler/test_interop_manifest.jac | 4/4 |
| tests/compiler/test_front_end_native_idioms.jac | 22/22 |
| tests/langserve/test_server.jac | 32/32 |
| tests/runtimelib/test_serve.jac | 12/12 |
| tests/runtimelib/test_serve_bridged_endpoints.jac | 1/1 |
| tests/runtimelib/test_client_bundle.jac | 12/12 |

Zero failures in the remaining families. Flag-off validation from a clean cache stays green: differential harness 27/27, round-trip suite 8/8.

## Harness hardening

Differential compiles now pass `no_ir_cache=True`; a cache-warm-dependent checker flake on the distinct-types fixture (passed cold, failed warm on the same source) surfaced during this phase and is neutralized for the harness. The underlying cache-state sensitivity in distinct-type checking is noted for the checker owners; it is not a codegen issue.

No wire format changes; format version stays 1.

author: mazzuccoda
body:
…ra por material

Tres correcciones sobre lo entregado en el commit anterior, reportadas por el usuario probando el PR contra datos reales:

- app/comparar: la "cascada" ahora es un bridge real (total A -> paso a paso por etapa, en el orden logistico que ya usa el waterfall de /costo -> total B), no un tornado ordenado por magnitud. Antes se leia como un grafico de barras cualquiera; ahora conecta los dos totales igual que la cascada de costo de nivel 2 y que los graficos de cascada del Excel que se tomo como referencia al principio del proyecto.
- app/comparar: cuando ninguna de las dos corridas tiene KPIs de barrido importados (kpis_por_corrida.csv) la tabla de comparacion quedaba vacia aunque ambas corridas estuvieran auditadas — se veia como "la comparacion no anda". Ahora, si ambas tienen drill-down, se agrega una segunda tabla con los mismos cuatro indicadores del resumen de nivel 1 (nivel de servicio, USD/tn, sobrecosto por restricciones, ocupacion pico), calculados con /dashboard/ y /cost-explorer/constraints/ que ya se usaban en otro lado — ningun dato nuevo, ninguno inventado.
- corridas/[runId]/costo: se agrega "Apertura por material" (by-dimension producto, mismo patron que el circuito de al lado). No habia en ningun lado del tablero una apertura de costo por producto a nivel corrida completa (solo existia dentro de almacenaje, acotada a ese costo).

Probado

Se armo un segundo paquete de auditoria real (mismos datos de ejemplo, run_id distinto, costos escalados) para poder probar en local el caso que reporto el usuario: dos corridas auditadas, ninguna con KPIs de barrido. Contra ese par, end-to-end con Playwright headless: la tabla de KPIs de barrido se ve completa con "sin dato" donde corresponde, la tabla de respaldo con los 4 indicadores aparece con numeros reales, y la cascada dibuja el bridge completo (total A, un paso rojo/verde por etapa en orden logistico, total B). Apertura por material verificada contra E-00-R0 real (UREA 64%, MAP 36%). Sin errores de consola.

102 tests de backend en verde (sin cambios de backend), ruff limpio, typecheck/lint/build de frontend en verde.

author: phuttimatebenchanakatkul
body:
Rebuilds the "create a food" screen users land on when a scanned barcode has no match, and closes a barcode-normalization gap found while reviewing it.

## What changed

**The create-food screen.** It was a flat list of fields ending in a native `prompt()` chain for extra serving sizes. `prompt()` dialogs read as coming from the browser rather than the app, and can't offer a unit picker. Now:

- Nav row with a back chevron and title, replacing the bottom button pair
- Emoji picker and serving-size editor collapse behind a tap instead of always being open
- Barcode gets its own row with a clear button, so a misread digit is fixable in place
- Serving weight uses the same amount+unit control (g / oz / mL) the rest of the app already uses for logging, converted to grams on submit
- "+ Add another serving size" is an inline form with that same control, no `prompt()`
- Numeric inputs clear on focus and restore their default on blur if left empty, so typing a value no longer starts with backspacing one

The primary serving name is now fixed at "1 serving" — it names the thing the macros above it describe, so it was never meaningfully editable. Extra serving sizes keep free-text names, since distinguishing them is the whole point.

**Barcode normalization.** Retail barcodes are numeric, but only `barcode_scanner`'s own paths enforced that. `/api/custom-foods` and `/api/lookup-barcode` accepted JSON directly with just `.strip()`, so any non-browser caller could store or query `"885-099"` verbatim. Two silent failures came out of that: a dirty stored barcode never string-matches the clean value a real scan produces, so the saved food stops resolving and the user is sent back to "create this food yourself" for a product they already created; and the duplicate-barcode 409 guard compares exact strings, so the same product stores twice under two spellings. Extracted the duplicated stripping into `digits_only()` and applied it at both endpoints.

## Tests

281 pytest (+8), 169 vitest (+15). Both suites green post-merge.

Coverage audit: **90%** of changed code paths and user flows, across two generation passes. Covered: unit conversion feeding `servingGrams`, add-serving-size validation (empty / zero / negative / non-numeric all no-op), barcode digit-stripping on both the client live-scan and server paths, emoji picker toggle + selection, serving editor toggle + live summary, barcode clear button, remove-serving splice, gram-rounding on display, `wireNumericClearOnFocus` focus/blur, quick-log render shape, and the two API endpoints' normalization.

Remaining gap: the quick-log full submit-success path (needs a fetch mock).

## Review

Pre-landing review dispatched 4 specialists plus an adversarial pass.

- **Fixed:** the API normalization gap above (found by the adversarial pass), plus two maintainability dedups — `digits_only()` in `barcode_scanner.py` and `sanitizeBarcodeDigits()` in the template's JS, replacing copy-pasted regexes on both sides.
- **Fixed:** the barcode value rendered into an HTML attribute using `escapeHtml()`, which escapes `< > &` but deliberately not quotes — correct for a text node, exploitable in a quoted attribute, where one `"` closes `value="..."` and the rest parses as markup. Reachable via the `not_found` echo from `/api/lookup-barcode`. Introduced by this branch's redesign; swapped to `escapeAttr()`, which this file already defines and uses elsewhere. Regression tests on both sides, verified to fail against the old call.

## Notes

No VERSION/CHANGELOG entry — this repo doesn't use that convention.

author: maharana2006-tech
body:
## Summary

Adds first-ever test coverage for the client-wizard **Mapping step** in
`ClientEditorPage.tsx` — both `MappingDraftStep` (create-mode staged-draft
form) and `ClientShippingMappingTab` (edit-mode delegate).

- **18 vitest cases** — 10 positive, 6 negative, 1 edit-mode smoke, 1
  cross-cutting fan-out check.
- Every network service is mocked at module level; nothing hits fetch.
- The wizard's sequential-lock is bypassed by seeding a per-user
  localStorage draft with `activeStep: 'mapping'` — the wizard reads this
  once on mount, so tests focus on the Mapping form's own behavior
  instead of clicking through 4 upstream steps.

### Positive coverage
- Empty state + "Add mapping" button visible when no drafts staged.
- Clicking Add opens the inline form (shipviaCd input, platform picker, service select).
- Typing lowercase `p80` normalizes to `P80` in the input.
- Carrier-service dropdown only lists services whose carrier matches the staged carrier draft; disabled catalog rows filtered out.
- Filling all fields + Add-to-list appends a row with shipviaCd chip + service name; row has a `Remove <CODE>` button.
- Multiple drafts stage with unique ids.
- Remove button deletes the row (and restores empty state when last).
- Platform-account label reads `· required` with no staged carrier / `· optional` with ≥1.
- Draft persistence: pre-populated drafts render on remount.

### Negative coverage
- Empty shipviaCd after blur → `Order Ship Via is required.`
- Separator-only shipviaCd (`--`) → `must include at least one letter or digit`.
- Spaces in shipviaCd (`A B`) → `Only letters, digits, '-' and '_' are allowed`.
- Zero carriers staged → service select placeholder reads `Add a carrier account first —`.
- Add-to-list button is `aria-disabled=true` when required fields empty.
- Clicking Add-to-list on empty form surfaces both errors and never appends a row.

### Cross-cutting
- Edit mode: `ClientShippingMappingTab` renders inside `#client-editor-panel-mapping` when the wizard loads a persisted client.
- `handleCreate` mapping-draft fan-out: two staged drafts round-trip through draft hydration and both render — the wizard consumes the same `mappingDrafts` state that the fan-out loop iterates.

### Bugs found
None material. Two cosmetic-only observations noted in the smoke doc
(Cancel does not clear the form state; validator runs on raw input),
both pre-existing behavior — no wizard-tests-bug issues filed.

### Files

- `multiship-react/src/components/ClientEditorPage.mapping.test.tsx` — 18 vitest cases
- `docs/wizard-tests/mapping-smoke.md` — QA manual checklist

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/components/ClientEditorPage.mapping.test.tsx` — 18/18 pass locally
- [x] `npx eslint src/components/ClientEditorPage.mapping.test.tsx` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint .` full frontend lint — no regressions
- [ ] CI green on this branch

author: josephjoshua
body:
## 问题
透明大页（THP）在部分 unmap/`mprotect` 时需要把一个存活的 2 MiB 大块降级为 512 × 4 KiB 叶子，之后可在同一 VA 上重新提升回 2 MiB。当前 `page-table-generic` 只能映射/拆除大块，缺少「拆分」原语：无法在保留大块底层数据帧的前提下，用一个更细粒度的子表原地替换它。#1990（buddy `split_pages`）与后续的 THP 内核特性都依赖这个页表侧原语，此前它并不存在，导致上层无法落地。

## 依赖（前置 PR）
本 PR 栈叠在 **#2009** 之上，复用其确立并测试过的 `clear -> flush -> free`（break-before-make）顺序。本分支前两个提交（`0d2a7f742`、`8b2775c51`）属于 #2009；请先合入 #2009，或将本 PR 视为其后续，合入后本 PR 会 rebase 使 diff 仅剩拆分提交。因为拆分是新增能力，其「在基线上必然失败」表现为：拆分 API 在 #2009 基线上并不存在（无法编译），而新增用例锁定了 #2009 的 break-before-make 顺序与「重提升无泄漏」不变量。

## 改动
- `frame.rs`：新增 `split_huge_page_recursive`，沿 present-independent 的 `huge()` 标记走到大块所在层级（因此 `mprotect(PROT_NONE)` 造成的 not-present 大块同样可拆分），按「大块基址 + 每子项 stride」逐项构造子表，再 `clear -> T::flush(Some(vaddr))` 打断旧大块，最后安装新子表指针。
- `table.rs`：公开单帧不透明预留类型 `ReservedTable`（`alloc_intermediate_table` 产生、`split_huge_page_with`/`dealloc_intermediate_table` 消费；子页表恒为一帧，多帧 reservation 在类型层面不可构造，避免泄漏/错误布局）；`peek_huge_block`（不改状态地定位大块）；`split_huge_page_with`（调用方预留 frame 的变体，任何错误路径都会释放该预留 frame）；`split_huge_page`。
- `lib.rs`：在 `PageTableEntry::huge()` 上补充契约文档——识别 present 大块在所有格式上都为真；识别 *not-present* 大块是 format-dependent（CPU 页表保留描述符，nested/second-stage EPT/NPT 将空权限项清零故返回 unmapped），这是 walk 与 not-present 拆分依赖的性质。
- `scripts/test/std_crates.csv`：将 `page-table-generic` 纳入 std 测试白名单，使新增 host 集成测试进入 CI。

## 逻辑
1. 拆分入口通过 `huge()`（结构性、与 present 无关）区分「大块」与「子表指针」，从而统一处理存活大块与 not-present 大块（后者数据帧必须保留，绝不释放）。
2. 先在预留 frame 上把 512 个叶子按 `block_paddr + i * child_stride` 填好并复制大块的 config/flags；此时旧大块仍然有效。
3. `clear -> flush` 打断旧大块，制造一个短暂的 not-present 窗口（break-before-make，避免 TLB 中同时存在大块与子表两种翻译），随后 `new_table` 安装子表指针。
4. 失败路径（当前项并非大块）释放预留 frame 且不 flush（预留 frame 从未安装、从不 live）。

## 测试
`memory/page-table-generic/tests/huge_split.rs`（host，4 个用例全部通过）：
- `split_2m_then_unmap_then_repromote_leaves_no_frame_leaked`：2M -> 拆分 -> 512×4K -> unmap -> 同 VA 重新提升 2M，断言成功且无页表帧泄漏（对应 #2009 修复的「残留空表 -> `AlreadyMapped`」回归）。
- `split_not_present_2m_block_preserves_the_data_frame`：对 `PROT_NONE` 大块拆分，数据帧从不交还分配器（tracking 分配器对外来 free 会 panic）。
- `split_emits_one_flush_and_frees_nothing`：成功拆分恰好一次 break-before-make flush、零释放。
- `failed_split_rolls_back_reserved_table_without_flushing`：对普通 4K 叶子拆分失败时，预留表恰好释放一次且从不 flush。
- `not_present_block_on_a_zeroing_format_degrades_to_not_mapped`：用模仿 EPT/NPT（空权限项编码为全零）的 nested PTE 断言窄化后的契约——present 大块在任意格式仍可拆分，not-present 大块得到 `peek == None` 且 `split == NotMapped`（不 panic、不泄漏）。

本地验证：`cargo test -p page-table-generic` 全绿；`cargo fmt --all -- --check` 通过；`cargo clippy -p page-table-generic --lib` 无告警；`cargo test --manifest-path scripts/axbuild/Cargo.toml`（std 白名单解析 + profile 断言）通过。

body:
## Summary

- Bind Compose management and Grafana ports to host loopback by default; network-wide publication is now explicit.
- Run the Compose service with a read-only root filesystem and bounded tmpfs while keeping all persistent state in the existing data volume.
- Keep Prometheus and Grafana installations immutable and root-owned while the application runs as UID/GID 10001.
- Add an optional resource overlay with configurable CPU, memory, and PID limits.
- Hash-pin container Python build tools and runtime wheels, build without dependency resolution drift, and verify the installed application version.
- Upgrade verified native defaults to Prometheus 3.13.2 and Grafana 13.1.3 for every supported OS/architecture definition.
- Add a pinned Trivy gate for fixed HIGH/CRITICAL findings with target-scoped, documented, expiring exceptions for findings still present in the latest official native releases.
- Add GitHub-OIDC Cosign signing for published multi-architecture release digests and document digest-pinned deployment and verification.
- Strengthen the live container test with forced SIGKILL, persisted-state recovery, read-only-root and ownership assertions, final graceful shutdown, and orphan checks.

## Operator-visible changes

Compose now publishes 9721 and 3000 on 127.0.0.1 by default because authentication is disabled. Set SBK_DASHBOARD_PUBLISH_HOST=0.0.0.0 only for deliberately protected network access. The optional compose.resources.yaml overlay defaults to 4 GiB, 2 CPUs, and 512 PIDs and is not applied automatically. Existing persistent data requires no migration.

## Validation

- ruff check src tests scripts
- mypy src scripts/sbk_dashboard_launcher.py
- PYTHONPATH=src python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -q: 195 tests passed
- coverage run -m pytest -q and coverage report: 195 passed, 78 subtests, 74 percent total coverage
- git diff --check

- Base, development, and resource-overlay Compose configurations validated

- Clean Linux AMD64 image build passed
- Trivy v0.74.0 scan passed with zero unsuppressed HIGH/CRITICAL findings; all 18 reviewed exceptions are path-scoped and expire 2026-09-30

- Hardened AMD64 container smoke passed with synthetic IPv4/IPv6 exporters
- Real SBK 10.5 container integration passed using host.docker.internal:19718/metrics, including target-up, dashboard generation, SIGKILL recovery, persistence, and final child-process cleanup
- No test containers, volumes, networks, listeners, or benchmark files remain

## Release notes

Tagged publication continues to build one control plane with its two native child processes for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. It now emits SBOM/provenance attestations and keylessly signs the shared manifest digest. Docker Desktop behavior on macOS/Windows and native ARM runtime execution were not claimed from this Linux validation environment.

Closes #24. Refs #3。M1-02 切片二：Go 权威分类规范化解析器。

## What's inside

- **新包 `apps/control/internal/classification`**（纯库，无 IO 依赖，仅标准库）：`Normalize(labels)` 输出 `(Workflow, Kind, Rigor)` 三维分类，或带结构化 `Reason{Code, Message}` 列表的无效结果。
- **规范化规则**（对齐 `docs/architecture/issue-types-goals-and-definition-of-done.md` 与 17 标签契约）：
  - workflow 恰好一个（CONTROL / DELIVERY / OPERATION）；
  - DELIVERY 恰好一个 deliveryKind（FEATURE / BUG / TECHNICAL / DOCUMENTATION）；CONTROL 恰好 `type:milestone-control`；OPERATION 的 `type:operation` 可省略；
  - rigor 恰好一个（LITE / STANDARD / HIGH_RISK）；
  - 标签大小写与首尾空白归一；workflow 中性标签（duplicate / wontfix 等）忽略。
- **fail closed 与全量可判定原因**：缺失维度（MISSING_WORKFLOW / MISSING_KIND / MISSING_RIGOR）、互斥冲突（MULTIPLE_WORKFLOW / MULTIPLE_KIND / MULTIPLE_RIGOR）、跨工作流错配（KIND_WORKFLOW_MISMATCH）、未知前缀标签（UNKNOWN_LABEL）全部无效并携带可读原因。kind 校验为三个互不短路的独立判定：基数（多个 type: 标签，与 workflow 无关）、可判定缺失（唯一 workflow 要求 kind，或所有候选 workflow 都要求）、可判定错配（某个 kind 与所有候选 workflow 都不兼容；workflow 完全缺失时三个工作流均为候选，任何受支持 kind 都有归属，故不报）。多个错配 kind 在同一条 reason 的消息中逐一点名。
- **测试覆盖（#24 AC-2 的"全部"）**：合法组合穷举 7 种 workflow-kind 组合 × 3 种 rigor = 21 个子用例；失败组合 25 个子用例（含 workflow 歧义与 kind 基数并存时的组合回归、兼容性沉默边界）；另有中性标签、大小写归一、消息可读性测试。合计 46 个表驱动子用例、5 个顶层测试函数。
- **测试顺序说明**：初版 RED 为包未实现时的编译失败（会话内真实发生，无持久化产物，不补造）；两轮修复的 RED 分别为 3 个 workflow 歧义漏报用例、3 个兼容性短路过用例在旧 head 上的真实失败。

## 边界（对应 #24 Non-Goals）

- 不修改 TS 原型；不做 Go 服务接线与 UI；浏览器验证随 Go 服务接入 UI 后进行（#3 DoD-2 留在 #3 层跟踪）。
- 无 API 变更，不触及 `protocol/openapi.yaml`（ADR 0001 契约优先约束）。

## Verification

- `gofmt -l` 无输出；`go vet ./...`、`go test ./...`、`go build ./...` 全绿。
- `pnpm check` 全绿（31 测试 + build，未触碰 TS）。
- CI 的 Go job 自动纳入新包。

author: fernandofilipuzzi-utn
body:
Realiza nueve de los diez criterios de aceptación de la transición `d` → `e` del roadmap. Registro sin elegir contraseña, habilitación, bloqueo, rehabilitación, baja con confirmación, y reseteo de la credencial.

LA PROVISORIA LA PRODUCE EL SISTEMA Y NADIE LA ESCRIBE. Doce caracteres, sin los que se confunden al dictarla, sin ningún parámetro de entrada: no se deriva del correo, del nombre ni de la fecha. Mil generaciones sin repetir. En el almacén va derivada; el claro se muestra una vez y no se guarda.

INV-08 se sostiene en la superficie: ninguna de las cuatro operaciones procede sobre la cuenta de administrador, y hay prueba que fuerza la petición.

RN-15: resetear no es una transición de la máquina de estados. Procede sobre una cuenta bloqueada y sobre una pendiente sin cambiarles la situación, leída del almacén antes y después.

RN-13 con dientes: la marca de cambio pendiente corta el acceso incluso con un acceso firmado obtenido ANTES del reseteo. La guardia es un intermediario y no un filtro por punto, porque el defecto a impedir es olvidarse de un punto.

La confirmación de la baja la exige también la superficie HTTP, no sólo la pantalla: RN-07 la hace condición de la operación, y sin eso una petición forzada borraría una cuenta y todos sus trabajos sin confirmación.

CRITERIO 10 NO CUMPLIDO Y NO DECLARADO CUMPLIDO: que la cuenta reseteada conserve todos sus trabajos no es verificable hasta la etapa `e`, porque los trabajos no existen. Se mide sólo la mitad que hoy tiene sustancia.

137 pruebas verdes (eran 73); 0 advertencias; los tres guiones de la etapa `c` siguen CONFORMES; 46 tablas sin filas rotas. El intake no se tocó.

Cuatro decisiones quedan elevadas al Product Owner, ninguna bloqueante.

author: charlietle
body:
§7f(f). `storage.Appender` (deferred since Phase 5 "to the phase that first has a caller"), `initAppender`,
`Head.Appender`/`appender`, `initTime`, `sampleType`, `appendBatch`, `headAppender.Append`,
`AppendSTZeroSample`, the appender's `getOrCreate` with both validations, `getCurrentBatch`'s decision table,
`GetRef`, `log()`, `Commit`, `appenderCommitContext`, `commitFloats`, `handleAppendableError`,
`unmarkCreatedSeriesAsPendingCommit`, `Rollback`, and `labels.HasDuplicateLabelNames`.

40 differential cases through the real `tsdb.Head`, each asserted in the three places a committed sample lands:
the accessors, the WAL records byte for byte, and the chunk files after `Close` m-maps the tail. A corpus with
only the accessors would pass on a port that never wrote a byte. 74 controls: 65 broke, 9 survived, 0 SKIP.

The corpus found a real defect. Upstream's `Rollback` ends with `return a.log()` AFTER truncating the batches,
so the samples are dropped but the series records are still written — "Series are created in the head memory
regardless of rollback." The port had read the first forty lines of the function and stopped; two rollback
cases were the only mismatches on the first run, both a missing 28-byte series record. Quirk 190.

Quirk 189: a REJECTED append can still initialise the Head, because `initAppender.Append` calls `initTime(t)`
before any validation. One bad sample permanently changes which appender the next caller gets.

One divergence: `appendSTZeroSample` returns Go's `(ref, error)` pair rather than throwing, because it is the
one appender method whose error carries a non-zero ref. Same treatment as `memSeries.appendable`, and the
fixture is what forced it — the port threw and lost the ref.

Closing the sweep's first-run survivors (50/74) taught the corpus four things: two appenders have to OVERLAP to
reach `commitFloats`' second `appendable` check; a duplicate label NAME cannot come from a map; `headMaxt` is
visible only through the OOO window; and the compaction-window floor MOVES, so a sample appendable early in a
program is out of bounds later. The nine remaining survivors are argued in the sweep's tail — the largest
family being metrics-only code, since `memSeries.append` rejects anything the second check would have.

author: amt911
body:
A 2025.12 ISO against 2026.08 repos hit the **gcc-libs split**: any install that drags new dependencies in conflicts with files the ISO's old `gcc-libs` still owns (`libgcc: /usr/lib/libgcc_s.so.1 exists in filesystem`). It killed the release path silently, then the build fallback loudly.

Every install into the **live session** now passes `--overwrite '*'`: the session is disposable, the flag never touches the install target (pacstrap runs its own world), and on a current ISO it changes nothing. The fallback message also stops claiming "no published package found" when the real reason — printed right above it — was a conflict.

If there are changes to other lines you didn't make deliberately, it's possible that your IDE made the changes with a utility like prettier.

author: werb210
body:
### Motivation
- Merchant Growth requires that a lender configured for email can also have a Google Sheet row appended, but the previous single if/else dispatch prevented running both flows for the same lender.
- The change extracts the Google Sheet append into a shared, idempotent helper so the sheet append can run either as the primary submission method or alongside an email delivery.

### Description
- Extracted the Google Sheet delivery logic into `async function appendLenderSheetRow(ctx, l, deps)` and reused it from both the `email` and `google_sheet` branches of `dispatchToSelected`.
- Preserved and centralised the idempotency claim by inserting into `lender_sheet_dispatches` with `ON CONFLICT (application_id, lender_id) DO NOTHING` so retries cannot duplicate rows.
- Built the real, column-ordered sheet row via `merchantGrowthSheet.js` and invoked the Google adapter, returning `{ ok, deliveredTo, error }` to the caller.
- When an email is sent and a lender has `google_sheet_id`, the sheet append runs after the email and the overall dispatch is marked failed if the sheet append fails; successful dual deliveries concatenate destinations into a single `deliveredTo` string.
- Removed the duplicated sheet logic and added an optional injection seam `deps.loadGoogleAdapter` (used by the helper) to make the Google adapter load stub-able in tests.
- Added a regression test file `src/services/lenders/__tests__/dualDispatch.v1.test.ts` that checks dual-dispatch guards, shared helper usage, idempotency SQL, real row construction, and pre-dispatch fraud enforcement.

### Testing
- Ran `npm install` which completed successfully.
- Ran typecheck with `npx tsc --noEmit` which completed successfully.
- Ran unit tests with `npx vitest run src/services/lenders` and the test run succeeded (`Test Files 3 passed`, `Tests 13 passed`).
- Verified no whitespace or diff issues with `git diff --check` which produced no errors.
