author: diogoammendes
body:
## Descrição Esta PR adiciona a funcionalidade de distribuição de lucros configurável, permitindo que os utilizadores escolham entre dois modos de distribuição: ### Modos de Distribuição 1. **Proporcional ao investimento** (padrão) - Os lucros são distribuídos proporcionalmente ao investimento de cada utilizador - Exemplo: Se um utilizador investiu 60% e outro 40%, os lucros são divididos 60/40 2. **Equitativa (50/50)** - Os lucros são distribuídos igualmente entre todos os utilizadores - Independentemente do valor investido, cada utilizador recebe uma parte igual ### Alterações Implementadas - ✅ Novo modelo `SystemSettings` para armazenar as configurações do sistema - ✅ Campo `distribution_mode` com opções PROPORTIONAL e EQUAL - ✅ Atualização da função `_compute_ledger` para aplicar o modo selecionado - ✅ Atualização da função `_compute_settlement` para aplicar o modo selecionado - ✅ Interface na página de acerto de contas para alterar o modo (apenas administradores) - ✅ View `UpdateDistributionModeView` para processar mudanças de configuração - ✅ Registo do modelo no Django Admin - ✅ Testes completos para ambos os modos de distribuição - ✅ Documentação atualizada em `docs/architecture.md` ### Como Usar 1. Navegue para a página **Acerto de contas** (`/acerto/`) 2. No topo da página, verá o modo de distribuição atual 3. Utilizadores com privilégios de administrador podem alterar o modo usando o dropdown 4. O sistema aplica imediatamente o novo modo a todos os cálculos de lucro ### Migração de Base de Dados Esta PR inclui uma nova migração: `0005_add_system_settings.py` - Após fazer merge, execute: `python manage.py migrate` - A configuração padrão será "Proporcional ao investimento" ### Testes Adicionada nova classe de testes `DistributionModeTests` que valida: - ✅ Distribuição proporcional no ledger - ✅ Distribuição equitativa no ledger - ✅ Distribuição proporcional no settlement - ✅ Distribuição equitativa no settlement
  

Greptile Summary

This PR adds a singleton system setting and administrator-facing selector for proportional or equal profit distribution, then applies that mode to dashboard ledger and settlement calculations. - Adds the SystemSettings model, migration, and Django admin integration. - Adds an authenticated, privilege-checked endpoint and settlement-page selector for changing the mode. - Updates ledger and settlement calculations and adds coverage for both modes. - The equal-mode calculation currently divides gross revenue rather than preserving principal and dividing profit.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR should not merge until equal mode preserves each user's principal and distributes only profit equally. Equal mode currently derives entitlements from gross receipts, so unequal investors receive unequal final profits and the settlement page recommends transfers that contradict the selected distribution contract. **Files Needing Attention:** operations/views.py, operations/tests.py

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | operations/views.py | Adds mode-aware ledger and settlement calculations plus the update endpoint; equal mode incorrectly equalizes gross revenue and produces wrong settlement transfers for unequal investments. | | operations/models.py | Adds the distribution-mode setting and a consistent pk=1 accessor. | | operations/migrations/0005_add_system_settings.py | Creates the SystemSettings table with proportional mode as the default. | | operations/tests.py | Covers both modes but asserts equal gross entitlements without checking whether resulting transfers actually equalize profit. | | templates/operations/settlement.html | Adds the administrator selector and displays the active distribution mode. |

Flowchart

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Administrator selects distribution mode] --> B[SystemSettings] B --> C[_compute_ledger] B --> D[_compute_settlement] C --> E[Dashboard attribution] D --> F[Fair entitlement per user] F --> G[Recommended transfers] ```

author: jmylchreest
body:
You asked what the benefit was. Investigating that turned up something better than either half I'd described: **the `require_confirmation` policy effect did not work at all.**

## The bug

`Executor.policyAllow` returned `ErrRequireConfirm`. The agent turned every executor error into a tool error string:

```go
result, err := a.cfg.Executor.Invoke(ctx, invReq)
if err != nil {
    inv.Error = err.Error()
    return inv, "", nil      // no confirmation, ever
}
```

So a `require_confirmation` rule behaved as a **deny with a confusing message, delivered to the model** rather than to the operator who wrote the rule expecting to be asked.

It looked fine because the *budget* path sets `NeedsConfirmation` and works. `docs/architecture/agent-loop.md` has always said *"If require_confirmation, pause turn and ask the channel; resume when user replies"* — one of the two producers did that, the other didn't, and nothing seeded a `require_confirmation` rule by default so it was never exercised.

Both dispatch paths now route it to the channel — `Executor.Invoke` and the skill path's own `CheckPolicy` — carrying the rule's own reason rather than the sentinel wrapper, which tells the operator nothing they don't know.

*(Worth distinguishing from `docs/configuration/reference.md`, which documents confirmation being deliberately **not** offered for cross-owner reads: two of the three call sites have no user in front of them. That's a different, correct decision — this is `tool:exec`.)*

## And approvals are no longer one-shot

`PromptDecision` was `Pending|Approved|Denied|TimedOut` — no scope — so the same operation prompted forever. That's the failure mode that matters: a confirmation answered a dozen times stops being read, and an operator who switches confirmations off to stop the nagging has lost the protection entirely.

Telegram now offers **Approve for this chat** alongside Approve. The executor checks the grant before prompting, so every dispatch path honours it — builtins, skills, MCP.

- **Per conversation and per operation.** In a group chat, the person tapping Approve is approving for that chat, not for every chat they're in.
- **Keyed off the request-context turn identity**, not the callback payload. A callback is attacker-shaped input; the same rule ownership already follows.
- **In memory, deliberately.** A restart ends the continuity the user was reasoning about, and a grant that outlives what they were looking at is one they didn't knowingly give.
- **Budget confirmations keep Approve/Deny only.** There's no operation to remember, and a button that silenced future budget warnings is the last thing an operator wants on that prompt.

## No permanent "always" here

The policy engine already evaluates (subject, action, resource) with `allow` as an effect, so a permanent approval **is** an allow rule — after which this check never fires, because `Evaluate` returns allow first. A second permanent store beside it would be two things deciding one question and eventually disagreeing. Left for a follow-up that adds the policy-write path from the channel; `policySvc.AddRule` is already used in-process for seeding, so it's small.

## Testing

`TestRequireConfirmationReachesTheCaller` drives the real policy engine and the real executor, because the bug lived in the seam between them: a `require_confirmation` rule must produce `ErrRequireConfirm`, a grant must suppress the next ask, and a *different* conversation must still be asked. Run with the grant check disabled, it fails with `the conversation was asked again after approving`.

Plus the scoping properties: grants don't leak across conversations or across operations, anonymous turns can't record or match one, and a nil store grants nothing.

Gates: build, vet, gofmt, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` 36 ok / 7 no-tests.

## Things I removed from my own first draft

An `ApprovalScope` type and a `SessionApprovals.Forget` — both would have been dead code. The callback parses verbs directly, and there's no clear-conversation command for `Forget` to hang off. The requirement that a future forget command must drop that conversation's grants is recorded as a note on the type instead.

author: mattkindy
body:
## Summary

First piece of the #326 second half. Each summary now records which project files its own file imports, so a checker working from summaries alone can rebuild the module graph:

```json
{
  "location": { "file": "src/server/handlers/connections.ts" },
  "metadata": {
    "moduleImports": ["src/contract/index.ts", "src/server/http.ts", "src/server/stores.ts"]
  }
}
```

Scoping a Lambda runtime by its `Handler` entry means computing that entry file's import closure at check time, and check reads summaries from disk with no compiler behind it. The graph has to travel with the summaries.

## What changed

- The adapter stamps `metadata.moduleImports` on every summary after assembly: compiler-resolved import and export-from targets of the summary's own file, project files only, sorted, absolute at that point.
- The CLI makes the paths relative in the same loop that relativizes `location.file`, so both use one root.
- `readModuleImports` in behavioral-ir parses the field back out; the metadata bag stays an open record, so there is no schema change beyond the new reader.
- The extraction cache's schema version moves from 4 to 5, so warm caches re-extract instead of serving summaries without the field.

## Risk and what to check

**Overall risk: 🟡 Caution** (legend: 🔴 Critical, 🟡 Caution, 🟢 Safe)

- 🟡 A new metadata field on every summary with imports; flagging per the standing rule on additive fields, object if unwanted. Summary files grow by the import lists.
- 🟡 One forced re-extract per project from the cache version move.
- 🟢 No behavior reads the field yet; the closure scoping lands separately.

## Test plan

- An adapter test extracts a two-file project and asserts the importer's summary records the imported file.
- A behavioral-ir test covers the reader, including refusing a non-array.
- The behavioral-ir, adapter, and CLI suites pass, plus repo typecheck, lint, and the coverage gate.
- On a corpus service, all 26 summaries record their imports with project-relative paths.

author: rodrigoadomes-star
glitchfox
body:
### Problem

`handlerKeyframe` blocks in `cons.WriteTo()` waiting for a keyframe, with no reference to the request context:

```go
if err := stream.AddConsumer(cons); err != nil { ... }

once := &core.OnceBuffer{}
_, _ = cons.WriteTo(once)   // blocks
b = once.Buffer()

stream.RemoveConsumer(cons) // never reached
```

If the HTTP client goes away first, or the source never produces a keyframe at all, `WriteTo` never returns and `RemoveConsumer` is never called. The consumer stays in the stream's list forever, so `stopProducers()` never fires and the upstream producer connection is held open indefinitely.

### Why it matters

Easy to hit with sources that can't reliably deliver a keyframe to a consumer attaching mid-GOP. Each aborted request then leaks another consumer, and because the leaked consumers keep the producer alive, the next request is slower — so the failure compounds.

On a battery powered camera the held-open session prevents the device from sleeping. I found this on an Aqara G410 doorbell, where Home Assistant's 10s image timeout aborted `/api/frame.jpeg` repeatedly and left the HomeKit session pinned open with `bytes_recv` static — the doorbell was streaming nothing and never sleeping, flattening the battery.

Observed on the same hardware, one aborted request each:

| | consumers afterwards |
|---|---|
| unpatched | 1, still attached 24s later |
| patched | 0 |

### Fix

Watch `r.Context()` and stop the consumer when the client drops, so `WriteTo` unblocks and the existing `RemoveConsumer` call is always reached. This mirrors the existing pattern in `internal/mp4/mp4.go`, comment included.

### Test

`TestKeyframeHandlerReleasesConsumerOnClientDisconnect` uses a producer that offers an H264 track then never sends anything, and cancels the request context while the handler waits. It fails against current master (handler never returns, consumer stays attached) and passes with the fix.

Refs #1733, #896

body:
## 背景

Mac 上の bridge セッション `daily-hack-blog2` が OAuth 失効で応答しなくなり、会話の文脈を別のセッションから読む手段が無かった。クラウドセッションから Mac へは SSH が届かないため、**Git に載せて渡す**のが唯一の確実な経路になる。

実際にこの PR の仕組みで 1143 メッセージを回収し、中断地点（依頼4 の DRY_RUN 中・2026-08-15 10:31Z）を特定できた。

## 変更点

### `scripts/export-session-log.mjs`（新規）

`~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` を Markdown に整形し、`session-log/{label}` ブランチへ push する。**Claude のログインは不要**なので、認証が切れて会話できなくなったセッションのログでも取り出せる。

| オプション | 意味 |
| --- | --- |
| `--list` | 履歴一覧。既定では「いま居るリポジトリで動いたセッション」に絞る |
| `--latest` | 絞り込んだ中の最新を選ぶ |
| `--each` | 候補を全件書き出し、索引付きで `docs/session-logs/{label}/` にまとめる |
| `--push` | 使い捨ての worktree でコミットして push する |

実際の運用で踏んだ落とし穴を、そのまま設計に反映してある。

- **プロジェクト名では当たらない。** `~/.claude/projects/` のディレクトリ名は cwd をハイフンに潰したもの（`-Users-ny-projects-anta-baka-x-blog`）なので、名前ではなく **cwd で判定**する。
- **利用者の作業ツリーとブランチを動かさない。** 使い捨ての worktree で detach したままコミットし、`HEAD:refs/heads/{branch}` へ送る。未コミット変更を持ったままでも実行でき、途中で失敗しても別ブランチに置き去りにされない。リモートに同名ブランチがあればその続きに積む。
- **スクリプトはリポジトリ外に置いて実行できる。** `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` でリポジトリを解決するため、`/tmp` から動かしてもよい。
- API キーらしき文字列（`sk-ant-` / `xoxb-` / `ghp_` / `AKIA` / JWT 等）は `[REDACTED]` に置換する。

未コミット変更を持ったまま、かつ手元が同名ブランチに居る状態で push まで通ることを、使い捨てのローカルリポジトリで再現テストして確認済み。

### ドキュメント

- `docs/session-log-export.md`（新規）— Mac 側・クラウド側それぞれの手順
- `docs/session-recovery.md` — 復旧手順を素の `claude` ではなく `claude --resume {会話ID}` に修正。素で起動すると別セッションになり文脈が繋がらない
- `docs/x-growth-play.md` — 実効値を 2picks 是正後（4 fires × 2 picks = 8 件/日・月 $1.00）に更新。`influencers.json` 7 件が条件に 1 件も合わず 8 件を選び直した経緯を追記。DRY_RUN の結果（検知と 15 分判定は正常・生成パスは未検証・plist 未作成で未ロード）も明記
- `docs/session-handoff.md` — #170 の内容を採用しつつ、bridge セッションのログが Mac に残ることと取り出し方を追記
- `.gitignore` — `docs/session-logs/` は `session-log/{label}` ブランチに置くもので、main には入れない

## 確認したこと

- `markdownlint-cli2 docs/*.md` — 0 issues（既存の見出し前空行欠落も直した）
- `#168` `#170` と同じ領域を触るため、main をマージして重複しない形で解決済み

author: buddhika75
body:
## What

Fixes #22997 — on the native-SQL GRN costing page (`pharmacy_grn_costing_native.xhtml`), both the regular item list's "Comments" field and the Bill Expenses section's "Description" field were silently dropped on every Save.

## Root cause

`GrnCostingNativeSqlController`/`GrnCostingNativeSqlService`'s native-SQL save path writes each `BillItem` row (line items and expense rows) via a plain-POJO DTO (`GrnLineData`) → hand-written `INSERT`/`UPDATE` SQL. `BillItem.descreption` (DB column `DESCREPTION` on `billitem`) had no field on the DTO at all, and neither `saveLine()` nor `saveExpenseLine()` included that column in their SQL — so whatever the user typed never reached the database, even though it looked correct in the UI until the next reload.

Same bug class as #22892 (Batch No / Date of Expiry silently dropped by the same native-SQL save path for the same reason) — same fix shape, same file.

## Fix

- `GrnLineData`: added a `description` field (correctly spelled; the DTO does not repeat the entity's legacy `descreption` typo).
- `GrnCostingNativeSqlController`: wired `BillItem.getDescreption()` into the DTO in both `populateLineData()` (shared by `toLineData()`/`toApproveLineData()` — regular items) and `toExpenseLineData()` (Bill Expenses).
- `GrnCostingNativeSqlService`: added the `DESCREPTION` column to all four native SQL statements (`saveLine` INSERT/UPDATE, `saveExpenseLine` INSERT/UPDATE), renumbering bound parameters accordingly.

The legacy entity-based `GrnCostingController`/`pharmacy_grn_costing_with_save_approve.xhtml` was not touched — it saves via `billItemFacade.edit()`/`.create()`, which already persists the full entity including `descreption`, and has no equivalent bug.

## Verification

Tested end-to-end on local Payara (Main Pharmacy department, GRN invoice 15861, PO `MP/PO/25/051368`):

1. Reopened an existing unfinalized GRN, entered an item "Comments" value and added a Bill Expense with a "Description" value, then Saved ("GRN Saved" confirmed).
2. Confirmed in the local DB that both values landed in `billitem.DESCREPTION`.
3. Reopened the same GRN again from "To Finalize GRNs" — both values now display correctly after a fresh reload from the DB:

![GRN reopened showing saved Comments/Description](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/hmislk/hmis/images/22997-grn-description-comment-saved.png)

(Also confirmed the GRN-level "Comment" field — `bill.comments` — was already saving correctly, so no regression there.)

Closes #22997

author: devinjameson
body:
## Summary

The Subscription DOM-event helpers promised that `event.preventDefault()` inside their `toMessage` mapper "works as expected". That claim is false when the listener is passive, and browsers register `wheel`, `mousewheel`, `touchstart`, and `touchmove` listeners as passive by default on exactly the targets these helpers steer people toward: `window`, `document`, `document.documentElement`, and `document.body`. Separately, two examples and the DragAndDrop component called `preventDefault()` inside `Stream.mapEffect`, which runs a turn after the dispatch, so the call was dead code.

This PR, in one commit:

- **Corrects the docs** in the `fromEvent` / `fromEventFilterMap` TSDoc, the Subscriptions page, the side-effects best-practices page, and the Mount TSDoc parenthetical. Each now states the passive exception, names the affected event types and targets, and shows the `options: { passive: false }` fix. Two additional false claims found during the sweep (the Subscriptions page and the best-practices page recommending `Stream.mapEffect` for `preventDefault`) are corrected too.
- **Adds `Subscription.fromEventPreventDefault`**, mirroring `h.OnKeyDownPreventDefault`: `Option.some(message)` means handled, and the runtime calls `preventDefault()` and emits the Message inside the dispatch; `Option.none()` leaves the default intact. It defaults `passive` to `false` and throws a diagnostic error when the config passes `passive: true` explicitly. Additive; `fromEvent` and `fromEventFilterMap` signatures are unchanged.
- **Adds the oxlint rule `foldkit/no-prevent-default-in-stream-operator`**, flagging `preventDefault()` inside callbacks passed to `Stream.map` / `mapEffect` / `filterMap` / `filter` / `tap`, with unit tests, real-oxlint fixtures, and registration in the repo lint config.
- **Fixes three live instances**: `examples/snake` (every keydown), `examples/pixel-art` (undo/redo shortcuts), and `@foldkit/ui` DragAndDrop keyboard-drag keys (Tab/Space/Enter/arrows), which the new lint rule caught. The website comparison snippet showing the old pixel-art pattern is updated to match.
- **Changesets**: `foldkit` minor, `@foldkit/ui` patch, `@foldkit/oxlint-plugin` minor.

## Verification

- Chromium (Playwright): confirmed the four event types are passive by default on `window`, `document`, `document.documentElement`, and `document.body` (so `documentElement` joined the documented target list), not on plain elements, and that `{ passive: false }` restores cancellation.
- Runtime check: confirmed a `Stream.mapEffect` mapper over `Stream.fromEventListener` runs after `dispatchEvent` returns, so the two suspected example bugs (and the DragAndDrop one) were real.
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm format:check`, changeset checks, foldkit (1820), ui (987), oxlint-plugin (337), snake, and pixel-art test suites, and the full pre-push pipeline (including website e2e) all pass.
- An independent review pass ran over the branch; its one substantive finding (the lint rule omitted `Stream.tap`, which the corrected docs name as equally late) is addressed, with `tap` covered by the rule, its unit test, and an invalid fixture.

## Notes

- The `passive: true` conflict throws when `fromEventPreventDefault` is called (config construction) rather than inside the acquire Effect: the config is immutable, so failing at the call site gives a synchronous stack at the offending code instead of a fiber defect at listener registration.

## Summary
Fixes 9 bugs found in a full bug-hunting pass over the monorepo, across 6 atomic commits:

- **Lockstep tick 0 never dispatched** — `MatchRelay.advance()` pre-incremented before broadcasting, so the multiplayer sim never advanced past a frozen state.
- **Stale `match` store state auto-completed the next campaign mission** — `GameRenderer.start()` deferred `setMatch(null)` past two awaits.
- **No runtime validation on the wire protocol envelope** — malformed client messages were relayed to every peer unchecked.
- **Match relay connection-lifecycle hardening**: protocol version never checked on join, late joiners never got a `start`/tick baseline, `stateHash` had no handler (desync detection was dead code), disconnects never broadcast `playerLeft`.
- **`DisarmingSystem` missing an `isAlive` guard** on a cross-tick stored entity reference, inconsistent with every other system in the engine.
- **`WebSocketTransport` had no `onclose`/`onerror` handling**, leaking an unbounded outbox on a dropped connection.

author: moshui-claude-code-tz[bot]
body:
链接 #178、#177、#176：本 PR 是阻断修复包，由 S-A-07 真实验收（biai-stage/Bot-Test）发现，三项均在本 PR 内解决，但不据此自动关闭 Issue（Draft PR，是否关闭由产品负责人在合并后决定）。基线 `epic/a-trusted-delivery@0e16b90`（原冻结候选 PR #174，因 #178 阻断失效）。

## 修复 A（#178，红线，核心）

**期望**：版本不可用/排队超时/心跳超时的队列收口必须写入唯一、可投递的用户终态（明确等待或失败），由 Gateway 完成同话题投递；不能只改 `task.status` 而遗漏 outbox；重启/重复处理时也不得重复投递。

**问题**：`src/lingxi/adapters/postgres_conversation.py` 里三条"系统代为收口"路径——`reclaim_stale` 心跳超时后判定不可再重试的终态分支、`reclaim_queued`（排队超时无人领取）、`fail_unavailable_versions`（目标 worker 版本连续不可用，`reclaim_queued`/`fail_unavailable_versions` 共用同一段代码 `_fail_queued`，因此实际是两处同构代码位置，逐一核对后确认没有第四处）——之前直接 `UPDATE task SET status='failed' ...` + 释放 `conversation.running_task_id`，完全绕开 `task_delivery_event` outbox。这正是 PR #170 描述里"三个系统声明超时路径不接入 outbox"的范围排除，本 PR 撤销这条排除。

**修复**：新增私有方法 `PostgresTaskQueue._write_system_terminal`，三条路径统一改为在已持有的行锁下：
1. 先写一条 `started` 事件（`content=None`，`worker_id` 用固定哨兵 `"system"` 标识"没有真实 worker 持有过这个任务"，不是伪造执行者）；
2. 再写 `terminal` 事件（`terminal_kind='failed'`，`error_kind` 分别为 `retry_exhausted`/`side_effect_uncertain`（reclaim_stale）/`queued_timeout`（reclaim_queued）/`worker_version_unavailable`（fail_unavailable_versions）；`content` 复用 `config/content.toml` 既有文案键 `worker.running_timeout`/`worker.side_effect_uncertain`/`worker.queued_timeout`/`worker.version_unavailable`——后两个键此前从未被任何生产代码渲染过，是 #151 outbox 改造遗留的孤儿键，本次是它们第一次真正投递）；
3. `task.status` 转入 `awaiting_delivery`（不是 `failed`）；**不释放 `conversation.running_task_id`**。

**话题释放语义**（Issue 明确要求"若某路径有特殊性需按最高原则设计并写明理由"）：不引入特殊语义，直接复用 #151/#152 既有约定——话题继续占用直到 Gateway 消费 outbox 调用 `confirm_delivery`（正常路径）或二十四小时到期由既有 `expire_undelivered_terminals` 兜底收敛为 `delivery_expired`（Gateway 不可用兜底路径）。这是唯一保证"用户必须收到明确终态且不重复"的设计：提前释放话题等于承认"这个任务已经有确定结果"，而此刻真正的结果（用户是否已经看到失败提示）还未知。

**为什么必须先写 `started` 再写 `terminal`（不是可省略的对称装饰）**：Gateway 消费循环 `apps/gateway/delivery.py` 的 `_handle_terminal` 只在 `stream.card_id is not None` 或 `stream.fallback_needed` 为真时才会建卡或走文本兜底；一个从未出现过 `started` 事件的任务两者都是假，`terminal` 事件会被无声消费（游标推进）但不产生任何外发——省略 `started` 会让"用户永远收不到终态"的窗口从"永不收口"缩小成"最长 24 小时才收口"，仍然是同一类缺陷换了个更晚的触发点。这个坑是在实现过程中读 Gateway 消费代码时发现并规避的，不是靠测试碰巧测出来。

**幂等**：`started`/`terminal` 各自用固定 `idempotency_key`（`terminal` 用与真实 worker 同形的 `f"{task_id}:terminal"`），复用既有 `append_delivery_event`/`write_terminal_event` 同一套 `_find_by_idempotency_key`/`_insert_new_event` 机制；housekeeping 轮询命中同一批任务时天然幂等（真库用例验证：`reclaim_queued`/`fail_unavailable_versions`/`reclaim_stale` 二次调用不产生第二条事件，见测试证据）。

## 修复 B（#177）

**期望**：worker 队列模式启动预检——`LINGXI_WORKER_WORKSPACE` 不存在或不可写时先尝试创建（`mkdir -p`），创建失败则以清晰的启动失败退出，绝不进入"每个回合泛化 `session_failed`"的运行状态。

**修复**：`src/lingxi/apps/worker/cli.py` 新增 `_ensure_worker_workspace`，在队列模式装配 `PostgresTaskQueue`/`WorkerService` 之前调用（放在宣告 `worker.queue.start` 之前，避免"先说已启动、又说启动失败"的误导顺序）：
- `config.workspace is None`（未显式配置）时跳过，不属于本次预检范围；
- 显式配置时：`Path(workspace).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`（只作用于这一个已配置路径本身，不派生/改写成别的路径）；创建失败（`OSError`）或路径存在但不是可写目录，记结构化日志事件 `worker.queue.workspace.unavailable`（`reason=create_failed|not_a_writable_directory`）并返回，`main()` 据此以 `EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR`（3）+ `config_error_report` 退出，不进入队列循环。

## 修复 C（#176，安全）

**期望**：Gateway 进程内对第三方 Lark SDK 的日志做凭据脱敏，覆盖 lark 相关 logger 与根 logger 传播路径，回归断言覆盖伪造凭据穿过过滤器与 gateway 装配真的安装了过滤器。

**根因确认**（读 `lark-oapi==1.7.1` 源码定位，未触达真实网络）：`lark_oapi/core/log.py` 固定 `logger = logging.getLogger("Lark")` 并直接给自己挂一个指向 `sys.stdout` 的 `StreamHandler`；`lark_oapi.ws.Client.__init__` 的 `log_level` 参数默认值是 `LogLevel.INFO`（本仓库未显式覆盖），构造时无条件 `logger.setLevel(log_level.value)`，把模块默认的 `WARNING` 收紧为 `INFO`；连接成功时 `logger.info("connected to {}", conn_url)` 因此被真正输出，`conn_url` 是飞书服务端签发的完整 URL，查询串带 `device_id`/`service_id`/`ticket` 等一次性凭据材料。

**修复**：
- `src/lingxi/core/execution/audit.py` 新增纯函数 `redact_query_parameter_values`：把文本里 `?key=value`/`&key=value` 形态的查询参数**值**统一替换为 `***`，不假设具体参数名单（宁可过宽，覆盖全部查询参数值，非仅"看起来像凭据"的键名）；与既有 `redact_free_text`（按关键词匹配赋值语句）是互补的两类脱敏，不重复实现。
- 新增 `src/lingxi/apps/gateway/log_redaction.py`：`CredentialQueryRedactingFilter`（`logging.Filter`，改写 `record.msg`/清空 `record.args`）+ `install_credential_redaction()`——两层安装：① 直接挂到 `"Lark"` 命名 logger（Logger 级 filter 在分发给任何 handler 之前就跑，同时盖住该 logger 自带的 stdout handler 与向 root 传播两条出口）；② 额外挂到当前 root logger 的每个 handler（Handler 级 filter 对任何传播到它的记录都生效，不依赖"第三方 SDK 固定叫这个名字"这个可能过期的假设，是处置要求"不能只依赖人工不查看日志"的落地）。
- `src/lingxi/apps/gateway/__init__.py` 的 `main()` 在 `logging.basicConfig()` 之后、任何可能触发连接的代码之前调用 `install_credential_redaction()`。

## 已知范围边界（明确不做）

- #175（文案）：等产品负责人定稿，未触碰。
- 未改卡片/投递协议语义：Fix A 完全复用 #151/#152 既有的 outbox/CardStream/DeliveryConsumer 机制，Gateway 侧代码零改动。
- 未新增迁移：三处修复都只使用既有 CHECK 约束已经允许的取值（`terminal_kind='failed'`、`task.status='awaiting_delivery'`），未扩展任何枚举，因此判断不需要新 revision，未跑 `check_migration_chain.sh` 之外的迁移改动。

**L1**（`PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"`，无 DSN）：1204 条全绿（较基线 +16：新增 `tests/test_worker_workspace_precheck.py` 6 条 + `tests/test_gateway_log_redaction.py` 10 条）。

**L2**（真实 PostgreSQL 16，容器 `lingxi-fixpack178-pg`，唯一命名，用后即删）：
- `tests/test_worker_queue_consumer.py::RealQueueTerminalTests` 三条改写/新增用例（`test_queued_without_worker_writes_an_honest_terminal_event_and_keeps_the_topic`/`test_unavailable_version_writes_an_honest_terminal_event_and_does_not_change_version`/`test_stale_safe_retry_then_exhaustion_writes_terminal_events_and_no_replay`）：均验证——`task.status` 转 `awaiting_delivery`（不是 `failed`）、话题不释放、`task_delivery_event` 恰好两行（`started`+`terminal`）、`terminal.content` 与 `default_content_catalog()` 渲染结果逐字相等（内容诚实）、二次调用 housekeeping 不产生第三行（幂等）、调用 `confirm_delivery` 后业务终态才真正收敛为 `failed` 并释放话题（闭环）。
- **负向验红**（对着 `epic/a-trusted-delivery@0e16b90`（修复前代码）单独跑过这三条新用例，真实红：`task.status` 断言拿到 `failed` 而不是 `awaiting_delivery`；对着修复后代码全绿）。

author: xhan97
body:
A one-word change per workflow that closes a real gap.

Both flags install exactly what `uv.lock` says, and neither modifies it. The difference:

- `--frozen` — sync without updating the lock, **skipping any consistency check**
- `--locked` — assert the lock is consistent with `pyproject.toml`, then sync

So `--frozen` will happily install a lock that no longer matches the declared dependencies.

## This is reachable today

Editing a dependency in `pyproject.toml` without running `uv lock` leaves CI installing the stale lock and passing green, with the declared and installed dependency sets silently disagreeing. There is no separate `uv lock --check` step in any workflow to catch it either.

Confirmed by adding an unlocked dependency to `pyproject.toml`:

```
uv sync --frozen : passes  ← the gap
uv sync --locked : fails   ← correct
```

## What does not change

Resolution stays pinned to the lockfile, so CI failures remain attributable to the change under test rather than to whatever upstream published overnight. That determinism is the reason to keep a lockfile in CI at all, and this preserves it.

Applied to all four workflows that sync: `pytest.yml`, `lint.yml`, `docs.yml`, `deploy-gh-pages.yml`.

Testing against fresh resolutions — what users actually get, rather than what the dev lockfile pins — is worth doing too, but belongs in a separate scheduled job rather than in the per-PR matrix, so that an upstream break cannot block merges. That is a follow-up.

## Summary
- CI workflow (lint/build/test) for all three apps — lint and the frontend/admin test steps are intentionally non-blocking (continue-on-error) because they surfaced substantial pre-existing debt unrelated to this change: ~470 backend lint errors, ~309 frontend lint errors, ~152 admin panel lint errors, and all frontend/admin test suites failing to load due to missing test dependencies (@testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom) that were never added to package.json.
- UAT deploy workflow, triggered automatically after CI succeeds on main: exact-commit git reset --hard, mandatory verified pg_dump backup before any migration (aborts deployment if the backup fails or can't be verified), atomic build swap for backend/frontend/admin with automatic rollback on failed health check, bounded-retry health checks. Concurrency-limited so two UAT deploys can never race, plus a server-side flock.
- Production deploy workflow: workflow_dispatch only, never auto-triggers, separate PROD_* secrets.
- Fixed a live bug found during the audit: UAT Nginx was proxying to ports (3052/3051) that didn't match the actually-running PM2 processes (3001/4001) - uat.valiarian.com and uatadmin.valiarian.com were returning 502. Already fixed directly on the server (Nginx config + reload), independent of this PR.
- Fixed an uncommitted hand-patch on the server (HOST default 127.0.0.1 -> 0.0.0.0 in src/index.ts) that the new git reset --hard deploy step would otherwise have silently wiped on first run.
- Added GET /health (DB connectivity check, no data echoed) since the existing /ping reflects request headers back and doesn't check the database.
- Committed package-lock.json for all three apps (previously gitignored) so npm ci is reproducible in CI.
- Added .env.example for all three apps (variable names only, no real values).
- Added ecosystem.config.js codifying the verified live PM2 config - kept at instances: 1 deliberately, since the backend runs two unconditional in-process timers (pending-order cleanup, premium-preorder expiry) with no distributed lock; more instances would duplicate order cancellations and Razorpay refunds.
- Added .gitattributes forcing LF line endings on shell scripts and workflow YAML so a Windows checkout can't corrupt files that need to run on the Linux deployment server.

## Test plan
- [x] bash -n on all new shell scripts
- [x] YAML syntax validated for all three workflow files
- [x] npm ci + npm run build verified locally for all three apps
- [x] Frontend/admin npm run lint run locally - confirmed pre-existing error counts cited above
- [x] Frontend/admin npm test -- --watchAll=false run locally - confirmed all suites fail to load due to missing dependencies (pre-existing)
- [x] Backend npm run build verified locally

- [ ] First actual UAT deployment via this pipeline - not yet run; recommend triggering manually once this PR is reviewed, watching the Actions log closely

### Problem
Resolves #61 where unpowered/previously-paired devices remained in the discovery cache indefinitely and were unintentionally added to Homey alongside chosen devices due to the pair wizard iterating over `window.found_devices`.

2. **`drivers/homeyduino/device.js`**: In `onDeleted()`, reset `paired: false` and unsubscribe the device so discovery timeout pruning (`_deleteAfterTimeout()`) cleans up offline removed boards.

author: roomote-roomote[bot]
body:
> ​<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:start -->Opened on behalf of @mrubens.<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:end --> Follow up by mentioning @roomote-roomote, in [the web UI](https://roomote.roomote.ai/task/1ev02n5fjf1ut?utm_source=github-comment&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=slack_app_mention), or in [Slack](https://roomote-dev.slack.com/archives/C0BDXC7FWBY/p1786810938712359).

## What changed

- Publish canonical `people/` cards from existing Roomote users and linked Slack, GitHub, source-control, Telegram, Discord, and Teams identities.
- Keep person slugs stable across profile renames, scrub standalone and embedded email addresses from Brain labels, and reconcile updates, removed aliases, and deleted members.
- Add member names alongside raw Slack user IDs, link exact Granola attendee matches to canonical person pages, and re-project historical meetings after identity changes.
- Expose gbrain's read-only `entity` lookup and document when agents should use it.

## Why this change was made

The Brain could retrieve activity about a person but had no canonical identity connecting names and provider handles across Slack, source control, and meeting notes. This made direct questions such as "who is this person?" noisy and unreliable.

## Impact

Agents can now resolve known deployment members through one privacy-safe identity card and connect their activity across supported sources. Identity changes also restart Granola's bounded backfill once so existing meeting pages converge without waiting for note edits. Postgres remains authoritative, no schema migration is required, and existing raw provider IDs remain available for exact matching.

author: saurabhav88
body:
## Summary
- Every transient overlay pill (warming-up, recording, warnings, passive chip, Bluetooth awareness, import status, hide) closes and asynchronously rebuilds the currently visible `NSPanel`. Dragging a pill mid-transition (e.g. its own 2s auto-dismiss timer, or an engine-readiness change) landed the close while AppKit's own native background-window drag still owned that panel, leaving a stuck duplicate on screen — reported and reproduced live twice (screenshots on the issue).
- Fix defers every one of these 9 identical-shape transitions while the mouse is down on the currently visible panel, coalescing queued requests so two transitions during one drag can't race each other once it ends.

author: jlumpkin5
body:
## Catching is not preventing

`audio_shape` works — it caught this in a live chapter of the post-deploy verification run:

```
*before the Steward, alone.*
```

which is exactly the artifact reported first and the reason the rule exists. But `writeChapter` rewrites **once** and ships the second draft whatever it says, so a marker the rewrite fails to remove still reaches the listener. A live eight-chapter run shipped one.

## Why deleting is the right instrument

A second model call is a weak guarantee against something a regex can simply delete. And deleting is safe here in a way it would not be for a prose defect: the asterisks carry nothing a narrator can pronounce, and the voice rules already require emphasis to live in word order. Removing the markup leaves exactly the words that were intended and takes away only the artifact.

The rule stays, and its role changes — it is now a detector for a defect that cannot reach the page. If it starts firing often, that means the model is straining against the instruction, which is worth knowing.

## Test

Asserts the words survive, and more importantly that things which merely *look* like emphasis are untouched: `snake_case_name`, `two * three`, a quoted `"5 * 4"`.

65 passing. Bundles clean.

**Optional for the demo** — the loop works without it. Requires `npm run functions:deploy` to take effect.

author: andrew3019
body:
Adds a `suggestions` plugin as a sibling of `report-bug`. Where `report-bug` catches "sb is broken", this catches "sb works and is costing me anyway": an agent that hits recurring friction mid-task files it, so the cost lands somewhere instead of dying in an `sb done` summary.

Built to the approved spec, which lands here too (`notes/suggestions-plugin-spec.md`).

**The bar, enforced in code.** A suggestion is refused — not filed with empty fields — unless it gives all three of `--friction` (what you actually hit), `--cost` (what it cost you), and `--recurs` (why it will happen again). Refusals name the missing flag.

**Commands.** `file`, `list`, `show <id>` for both audiences; `drop <id>` is human-only, so agents cannot bin their own or each other's suggestions.

**Binding.** Enabled in `defaults/plugins.toml` and bound under `all` in `defaults/presets.toml`, because an agent never told the verb exists will never use it. The always-on fragment is 522 chars against the 4000 cap.

**No dedup, no index, no surfacing.** Duplicates are the frequency signal. Nothing reads these yet — accepted knowingly in the spec, not overlooked.

Also updates the shipped docs from two plugins to three, and tightens the three `test_shipped_plugins` assertions that hard-coded "only report-bug ships" (still exact-equality on full lists).

Verified: full suite green (1231 passed), plus a live end-to-end run in a throwaway clone — filing, listing, prefix-show, and the human-only delete all behave. Independent spec-fidelity review found nothing blocking.

Unproven and stated: that agents file good suggestions, and that anyone reads them. Neither is testable here.

author: wrsmith108
body:
## Business Summary

**What shipped:** Fixed a production bug where the skill indexer's categorization step could throw a duplicate-key error and silently drop a skill's category assignments whenever two indexer runs (a backfill run and the regular cron, or two overlapping runs) touched the same skill at the same time. Categorization now tolerates that overlap instead of erroring.

**Quality bar:** Root-caused by tracing why the fix already existed on the edge-function side (under an earlier, differently-scoped ticket) but never made it into the code path GitHub Actions' production cron actually runs — a "sibling implementation drifted" gap, not a novel bug. Ported the already-proven fix rather than writing a new one. 10 regression tests added, independently confirmed to fail against the old code (6/10 fail) before passing against the fix. Typecheck, lint, format, and the full indexer test suite (1193 tests) all green; full pre-push suite (security scan, npm audit, all package tests) passed on push.

**Net result:** Fully shipped, no follow-up needed.

---

## Technical detail

**Root cause:** `scripts/indexer/indexer-runners.ts`'s `runCategorization()` (the Node twin the production `indexer.yml` cron actually runs via `npx tsx scripts/indexer/run.ts`) inserted each skill's category rows with a bare per-skill `.insert()`. Categorization Phase 5 has no scoping to "rows this specific run discovered" — `selectCategorizationRepoUrls()` deliberately draws from the whole "never categorized" pool — so any two concurrent phase-3 runs can independently select and categorize the same skill, and a bare insert turns that into a hard `23505` error on `skill_categories_pkey`. Production logs on 2026-08-15 showed a burst of these.

The Deno twin (`supabase/functions/indexer/indexer-runners.ts`) already fixed this exact race under SMI-5209 Wave 2 — collect every skill's category rows, then issue one batched upsert with `ignoreDuplicates: true` instead of N per-skill inserts — but that fix was never ported back to the Node twin, despite the Node twin's own header comment explicitly claiming to be "byte-near-identical" to the Deno twin.

**Changes:**
- `scripts/indexer/indexer-runners.ts` — restored batch-upsert parity with the Deno twin's SMI-5209 Wave 2 pattern.
- `supabase/functions/indexer/indexer-runners.ts` — brought up to the same standard: a failed stale-category `DELETE` was previously log-only and never surfaced to the run's own error report (now pushed into `errors[]`), and `onConflict: 'skill_id,category_id'` is now explicit on both twins' upsert calls rather than relying on `upsert()`'s implicit primary-key inference.
- `scripts/tests/indexer/indexer-runners.categorization.test.ts` (new) — ports the Deno twin's existing SMI-5209 batch-upsert test suite to the Node twin, plus two new cases (race-tolerance under a simulated concurrent-run conflict, delete-error surfacing).

No migration, no deploy step beyond the normal indexer cron picking up the merged code on its next run.

body:
Finding a report meant knowing the history. Thirty files sat flat in `docs/` with no grouping, **17 of them linked from nowhere** — including every shareable HTML report, which are exactly the files most likely to be wanted by somebody who did not write them.

## `docs/reports/`

The rendered deliverables now live together, with [their own README](https://github.com/tkhongsap/model-eval-harness/blob/docs/report-index/docs/reports/README.md) giving each one the question it answers and the command that regenerates it.

| Report | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `model-comparison.html` | The current headline — four models on `retention_v3` |
| `model-comparison-fragment.html` | Same page, for publishing as an Artifact |
| `model-comparison-metrics.json` | Every figure, machine-readable |
| `soak-test-report.html` | The 5-hour GPU soak |
| `experiment17-report.html` | E17, and Gemini's determinism collapsing |

**Only script-generated artifacts moved.** The written analyses stay in `docs/` — moving them would mean auditing cross-references through a 2,426-line `EXPERIMENTS.md`, plus `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `DEVLOG.md`, for no gain. The boundary is stated in the folder's README so the next file has an obvious home:

> A file belongs here when it is a rendered deliverable whose numbers came from somewhere else. It does not belong here if it carries model output verbatim.

The index is also honest about what cannot be rebuilt: **`experiment17-report.html` is hand-written** and no script regenerates it, so the table says that rather than implying a command that does not exist.

## Two things found while doing it

**1. The run behind the current headline was not in the run index.**

`20260815-124600Z-e18-tf-qwen38` is the Qwen3.8 run the entire four-model comparison rests on, and `RUNS.md` did not have it. That index exists precisely so a `run_id` quoted anywhere resolves on a clone holding none of the runs — which makes a missing row a real gap, not a cosmetic one. Regenerated: **66 runs**, `--check` now clean.

**2. The case explorer was documented nowhere.**

Its output is gitignored by design, so without a doc nothing recorded that it existed or how to get it back. [`docs/case-explorer.md`](https://github.com/tkhongsap/model-eval-harness/blob/docs/report-index/docs/case-explorer.md) now covers what it shows, the one command, the two self-checks, and why it is not committed.

## The data-safety boundary is unchanged

`out/` still holds every run directory and the case explorer, still gitignored, still the only copy. The reports regenerate from those runs in minutes — but **the runs themselves cannot be regenerated**: E17 established Gemini stopped being deterministic between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-14, so re-running the incumbent produces different outputs. `RUNS.md` preserves their provenance, not their contents.

That backup gap is real and is **not** addressed here — moving 78 MB of model output anywhere is a data-handling decision, not a cleanup.

## Verification

- **887 passed / 12 skipped** — unchanged
- Both generators re-run clean from the new paths, all four refusals passing, figures identical (**0.955 / 0.838 / 0.960**)
- `scripts/run_index.py --check` reports up to date

- Every doc under `docs/` is now reachable from `README.md`
- Nothing from `out/` is committed

author: co-dh
body:
Freyd writes the power transpose as `Λ`. The repo called it `A` because of an OCR error, not a
deliberate choice: `/home/dh/anki/typst-book/chapters/2.4/fix_ocr_2.4.py` lines 28-29 record that
MinerU misread `Λ` as plain, bold, and calligraphic `A` in roughly 50 places in §2.4, and the Lean
declaration was named after the misreading. The doc comments already wrote `Λ` in many places, so
the code and the prose around it disagreed.

## What changed

| commit | what | sites | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `853e3c6` | the 48 `A_*` / `*_A_*` lemmas → `Λ_*` | 313 | 41 |
| `8f47cf5` | `Freyd.Alg.A` → `Freyd.Alg.Λ` | 717 (716 uses + the definition) | 51 |
| `e1aba8c` | doc comments and prose | 374 comment lines | 51 |

`Λ` is U+039B: `isLetterLike` admits uppercase Greek U+0391–U+03A9 except `Π` and `Σ`, so it is a
legal Lean 4 identifier. `./scripts/cap lake build` is green (497 jobs) after every stage.

Both code passes ran through `scripts/lean-refactor rename-decl`, which is transactional at
repository scale — it stages every file, swaps them in together, and runs one capped whole-repository
build, restoring everything on failure.

## Left alone

`A` that is not the transpose: the English article ("A GREEDY algorithm"), objects and type variables
(`tree A`, `F A X`, `A ⟶ C`, `∃ A∈F`), the ambient allegory (`Map(A)`, `Spl(Cor(A))`, "a power
allegory `A`"), the opposite category `𝒮^(A°)`, coreflexive and idempotent relation variables named
`A`, the tabulation columns (`baseFibLift_A`, `colA`), the capitalization-tower prose (`A_i`,
`A_last`, `A_α`), and the `A<ch>_*` chapter-file naming scheme.

## Notes for review

- `rename-decl` matches its short name syntactically with no scope check, so it also renamed 83 bare
  `A` **binders** — objects in `S2_40`/`S2_41b`, `GlobalObj` in `S2_43`, type variables in
  `RelInterp`. Each was reverted line by line against a pre-rename snapshot, after confirming (by
  diffing the `rename-decl` report against the uses-only report) that no reverted line carries a real
  site. `S2_43`'s `A : GlobalObj 𝒜` had to be renamed out of the way for the pass to build at all —
  its `A.idx`/`A.obj` projections are not identifiers named `A`, so the fallback left them dangling —
  and was restored afterwards.
- `rel/AutoDeriveDP.lean:386` is a real use of the operator that the semantic pass does not see (the
  info trees do not record every occurrence). The syntax fallback caught it; it is renamed.
- The last commit is unrelated to the rename and fixes a pre-existing breakage: `Freyd.lean:138`
  imports `Freyd.S2_313`, but `Freyd/S2_313.lean` had never been added to the index, so `master`
  does not build from a clean checkout — only from a working tree that happens to hold the file.
  It is committed here. §2.313 is the division adjunction `•S ⊣ •/S` and names no power transpose,
  so no rename applies to it.

body:
## Why

Vercel renamed **Edge Config** to **Global Config**. Stores connected to a project from now on provision a `GLOBAL_CONFIG` environment variable instead of `EDGE_CONFIG`, and the legacy `@vercel/edge-config` SDK only reads `EDGE_CONFIG` by default. Without this change, connecting a freshly created store to this project would silently no-op instead of driving maintenance mode / the announcement banner - with no error to signal the mismatch.

## What Does This PR Do?

- Swap **`package.json`** dependency `@vercel/edge-config` → `@vercel/global-config` (official drop-in replacement).
- **`src/middleware.ts`**: import `get` from `@vercel/global-config`; the config-store presence check now looks for `GLOBAL_CONFIG` first, falling back to `EDGE_CONFIG` so stores/env vars connected before this change keep working unchanged.
- **`src/app/api/announcement/route.ts`**: same `GLOBAL_CONFIG` → `EDGE_CONFIG` fallback for the connection-string URL used to fetch the announcement banner payload.
- Updated **`src/middleware.test.ts`** and **`src/app/api/announcement/route.test.ts`** to cover the new `GLOBAL_CONFIG` path, plus regression tests asserting the legacy `EDGE_CONFIG` fallback still works.

author: anzalkhan16
body:
fixes #85606 

## Pull Request Description

This PR introduces a highly requested component variant: the **Dark Mode Interactive Filter Bar Header**. It provides a sleek, minimalist aesthetic designed for modern dark-themed interfaces. It discards heavy drop shadows in favor of subtle, semi-transparent borders and relies on high contrast accents (pure white text with a glowing blue indicator) to indicate state.

*Note: To comply with the strict repository CI pipeline (`submission-validator.yml`), this component variant has been submitted as a fully functional and documented example in `submissions/examples/dark-mode-filter-bar/`.*

---

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New animation / hover effect
- [x] 🧩 New component (Variant)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation improvement
- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix in an existing submission
- [ ] Other (describe below)

---

## Submission Checklist

> ⚠️ PRs that fail this checklist will be **closed without review**.

- [x] All changes are inside `submissions/` (e.g., `submissions/examples/your-feature-name/` or `submissions/docs/your-feature-name/`)
- [x] Includes `demo.html` — self-contained, opens in browser with no server
- [x] Includes `style.css` — raw CSS for the proposed feature
- [x] Includes `README.md` — what it does, how to use it, why it fits EaseMotion CSS
- [x] **No changes to `core/`**
- [x] **No changes to `components/`**
- [x] One feature per PR (no bundled unrelated changes)

---

## Feature Description

**What does this add?**

1. **Pure CSS State Management (`Zero JS`):** This component utilizes native HTML radio buttons grouped by the `name` attribute. By visually hiding the radio inputs but keeping them in the DOM flow, we use the `:checked` pseudo-class combined with the adjacent sibling combinator (`+`) to style the corresponding labels dynamically.
2. **Minimalist Dark Aesthetics:** Uses a deep surface color (`#1e1e1e`) with a delicate 8% opacity white border. The active state is indicated by brightening the text to pure white, adding a subtle 8% white background layer, and sliding up a crisp, glowing blue accent line at the bottom.
3. **Animated Accent Indicator:** The active indicator (`::after`) uses a targeted `@keyframes` animation (`ease-dark-slide-up`) to slide into view with a soft fade-in, creating a premium interaction feel without JavaScript.

**Accessibility & Responsiveness:**
- **Accessible Native Keyboarding:** The radio inputs are visually hidden using `opacity: 0` and absolute positioning rather than `display: none`. This allows them to receive native keyboard focus (tabbing and arrow keys), and a `:focus-visible` ring is dynamically applied to the fake label for clear focus indication (inset using `outline-offset` to keep the dark mode design clean).
- **Prefers-Reduced-Motion:** Deep integration with `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. The slide-up animation on the active indicator and all color transitions are safely stripped out for users with vestibular disorders.
- **Responsiveness:** By default, the filter bar acts as an inline-flex element. On very small screens (`< 480px`), it seamlessly switches to a flex-wrap layout to accommodate all options without breaking the viewport width.

---

## Demo

- [x] Demo added (`demo.html` works by opening directly in a browser)

---

## Browser Testing

- [x] Chrome
- [x] Firefox
- [x] Edge
- [ ] Safari *(optional but appreciated)*

---

## Notes for Maintainer

All submission rules have been strictly followed. Zero automated axe-core errors were detected during local testing, and hardware acceleration has been verified via Chrome DevTools rendering tabs.

author: lpezet
body:
Moves the default pin to **v1.10.1** and makes `sal` create the shape that release expects.

### What changed upstream

1.10.0 bakes `000_policy.py` and `001_allowlist.py` into the proxy image at `/opt/agent-proxy/addons/`, loaded **ahead of** the `/addons` mount a deployment provides. Their changelog says why: a consumer built a deployment with an empty `proxy/` — reasonable, since the bank supplies proxy addons and a fresh lab has installed none — and from inside the lab container got a real credential back.

```
curl http://cred-gateway/anthropic/cred   → 403     (the route is not exposed)
curl http://broker:8080/anthropic/cred    → {"type":"auth_token","value":"sk-ant-oat01-…"}
```

### Why this inverts a rule rather than adjusting one

- **Below 1.10.0, vendoring IS the control.** With no policy addon loaded the proxy forwards to the broker and the cred-gateway whitelist can be walked around entirely.
- **At or above, vendoring is not a smaller control but none.** The image's copy wins; the deployment's is skipped with a warning naming the file.

So each command that touches those files now asks which side of the line the release is on:

| command | below 1.10.0 | at or above |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | fetches and vendors both; refuses if it cannot | vendors nothing, and says so |
| `upgrade` | installs what the release ships | **deletes** what the lab vendored |
| `drift` | an unvendored addon is `MISSING` | a vendored one is a `note` |

`version.StackBakesAddons` is the single place that line is drawn. **A tag it cannot parse takes the vendoring branch** — a vendored copy at a release that bakes them is dead weight, a missing one below is a missing control, so that is the direction that fails closed. It is the same choice `scripts/check-drift.sh` makes for a pin that is not a release tag.

`MinimumStack` stays at 1.9.2: it marks the release below which a lab is unsafe, and a 1.9.2 lab vendors the addons and is not.

### One test changed meaning, not wording

A stack checkout with no addons directory used to be **refused** — "created but not safe yet" is not a state worth reaching. That assertion is still there, now pinned to `v1.9.2`, and it is joined by its opposite: at the default, the same hollow checkout is simply not a problem, because those files were never the deployment's to hold.

### Verified against the real releases

Not fixtures:

```
$ sal init                      # default
stack    v1.10.1 (75235129b95c)
addons   carried by the proxy image at v1.10.1, not vendored here
$ ls .../proxy/                 # empty

$ sal init --stack v1.9.2       # below the line
$ ls .../proxy/
000_policy.py  001_allowlist.py

$ sal upgrade --to v1.10.1
DELETE   000_policy.py (carried by the proxy image at v1.10.1)
DELETE   001_allowlist.py (carried by the proxy image at v1.10.1)
$ sal drift
summary     0 drift · 0 missing · 0 stale · 0 unowned
```

### Still open, and deliberately not here

`template/` — the stack's own deployment wiring, added in 1.10.0 partly because "a downstream tool had written its own service graph", which is this one. Adopting it needs [lpezet/secure-agent-lab#79](https://github.com/lpezet/secure-agent-lab/issues/79) (the observer's fixed host port collides across labs) and [#80](https://github.com/lpezet/secure-agent-lab/issues/80) (a profile, so a feature can be switched off without editing the wiring). When those land, `internal/compose/templates/` can go.

body: ## Problem Phase 3 already shipped the LaunchDarkly adapter. Nathan authorized the remaining vendor adapters to be built now. This PR lands the next one — `@pegma/flags-aws-appconfig` — and no others. ## Behavior `createAwsAppConfigFlagProvider` takes a host-injected AppConfig reader. The adapter translates an already-evaluated value, or a setting it can map without becoming a second targeting engine, into a `FlagResolution`. It does not import the AWS SDK, own a client singleton, or evaluate multi-variant rules / percentage splits. Documented AppConfig shapes only: - already-evaluated values, and ordinary string / JSON encodings → `TARGETING_MATCH` - an unconditional feature-flag object with `enabled: true` → `TARGETING_MATCH` - `enabled: false`, including a stored default variant with no `rule` → `DISABLED` - missing reader result → `DEFAULT_FALLBACK` - an enabled document that still carries `_variants` with a `rule` is rejected so the flags client can record `ERROR` Optional `awsAppConfigFlagValue` reads one stored flag from an `AWS.AppConfig.FeatureFlags` document or a retrieved flag map. Hosts that need variant evaluation do that in the injected reader (AppConfig Agent or `GetLatestConfiguration` with context) and return the already-evaluated value. ## Tests - Unit tests for value mapping, injected key mapping, unevaluated rules, reader errors, and no AWS SDK / `Date.now()` on the production path - Phase 1 conformance suite against a memory reader - Release inventory includes the new public package ## Docs Plan status is Phase 3 LaunchDarkly and AWS AppConfig in-tree, unpublished. author: mikevalstar
body:
A pass of small fixes and additions, one commit each.

## Fixes

- **The details panel no longer focuses the stars on open** (`d20ca82`). Radix's focus scope grabbed the first tabbable child — the `0.5` star radio — and its `onFocus` set the hover preview, so an unrated book showed a phantom half star. Programmatic focus doesn't match `:focus-visible`, so there was no ring to explain it. Not just cosmetic: an arrow key or Enter right after opening would have rated the book. Open-focus now goes to the panel itself.
- **Stale hover copy removed** (`b2ee54f`, `909a582`). The Hardcover mark still claimed a book in both libraries "appears twice", which stopped being true when works-grouping landed. Also fixed the same drifted claim in two code comments.

## Additions

- **Hardcover about / tags / moods** (`95a3a4a`). Three global preferences, all defaulting on via Zod (`.catch(true).default(true)`), so existing installs need no migration. Checked the real db before building this: 98 of 99 Hardcover descriptions are plain text with CRLF, zero Markdown — so no Markdown renderer was added, and the existing strip-and-split path picked up a CRLF fix instead. Hardcover files tags under four categories, so Genre+Tag render as **Tags** and Mood gets its own section; content warnings are deliberately dropped until someone decides how to present them.
- **Real brand marks** (`8a63b4e`). Calibre's official 256px PNG (their SVG is filter-heavy and smears at 12px) and Hardcover's `/logo.svg` with the viewBox trimmed to the mark's bounds. Both wear a lucide-shaped API so call sites were unchanged.
- **A link out to hardcover.app** (`fd076e2`). The slug was already stored, so no GraphQL change. Cloudflare 403s any direct probe of the URL, so the shape was confirmed against three independent live integrations instead. This also uncovered that `target="_blank"` was **dead in desktop mode** — `new-window-open` fires and nothing follows. Fixed in the Electrobun shell with an `openExternal` handler scoped to `http(s)`, which covers every future external link.

## Tooltips

- **One react-tooltip instance** (`99363fe`, ADR 0016). Replaces scattered native `title=` attributes and a lone Radix tooltip. A single `TooltipHost` in the app shell, targets opting in through a typed `tooltipProps()` helper — which matters because the library views are virtualized, so per-row tooltip components would mount and unmount constantly.
- **Header controls explained on hover** (`e07b22e`). Settings, theme toggle and the reader switcher. The theme label reflects the current state, and the avatar's tooltip is driven by whether there are other readers to switch to.

## Two judgement calls worth a second opinion

- The Hardcover link query no longer gates on the three content toggles, so a reader with all three off still gets the link — at the cost of one request. Reasoning: the link is about the *match*, not about whose prose wins.
- The panel's download button got no tooltip, since it already carries a visible "Download EPUB" label. One line to change if you'd rather it be uniform.

`typecheck`, `lint`, `build:web` and `docs:check` all clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: pthauvette
body:
Le dashboard finances, l'export XLSX et le rapport de taxes excluent tous `CANCELLED`/`FAILED` — du brut **et** de leurs remboursements, à dessein : une vente voidée n'est pas un revenu, et compter son remboursement la soustrairait deux fois.

Ce raisonnement suppose qu'une commande voidée a été **rendue**. Depuis #583 c'est faux dans le cas devenu normal : une soumission partie sans réponse laisse `FAILED` avec l'argent **conservé**, parce que la production est peut-être lancée. Plio détient du cash qu'aucun tableau ne compte, et l'écart ne se referme jamais seul — il n'y aura ni production comptée ni remboursement compté.

C'est le reste ouvert que j'avais nommé dans #583.

## Ce que fait le lot

Un encadré **avant** les KPI, qui dit ce que les tableaux du dessous ne comptent pas. **Aucune agrégation existante n'est modifiée** : rouvrir `CANCELLED/FAILED` casserait la sémantique « vente voidée » pour les vraies ventes voidées, qui sont la majorité. On ajoute le tableau manquant plutôt que de fausser celui qui existe.

## Trois défauts trouvés en revue, tous dans le sens qui sous-estime

| | Ce qui se passait |
|---|---|
| **Le repli éteignait l'alarme** | Délégation à `refundAmountCentsOf`, dont le repli rend le **total de la commande** quand `data` ne porte pas de montant. Un remboursement partiel de 200 $ sur 890 $ comptait 890 $ — les 690 $ détenus disparaissaient. Sur trois commandes, sans attendre la moindre montée en charge. **Le test censé le verrouiller le décrivait comme correct.** |
| **Frais d'annulation comptés comme un écart** | `cancel` rembourse `amountCents − cancelFeeCents` puis marque `FAILED`. Chaque annulation facturée laissait une ligne rouge qu'**aucune action ne peut fermer** — les frais sont dus. Et quand les frais couvrent toute la charge, il n'y a aucun remboursement Stripe : la commande entière s'affichait comme retenue. |
| **Le bruit n'était pas celui que je croyais** | Ce n'est pas l'annulation facturée, mais l'échec Sinalite **auto-remboursé intégralement** — le chemin `FAILED`-avec-`paidAt` le plus fréquent, qui n'a jamais de frais. J'avais affirmé que soustraire les frais suffisait ; c'était faux, et le reviewer l'a prouvé à l'exécution. |

Deux requêtes désormais : les commandes **sans aucun remboursement** (candidats par construction, aucun bruit possible — c'est là que vit le cas #583), puis celles qui en ont. Tri par **montant** : trier par date faisait périmer le plus ancien écart non réglé, l'inverse exact du commentaire écrit trois lignes plus haut.

## Le chiffre n'est pas un solde, et l'encadré le dit

`markRefundIssued` est appelé à la **création** du remboursement. Si Stripe le passe ensuite à `failed` — carte fermée, banque qui refuse le retour — l'argent revient chez Plio et rien n'amende l'événement : **il n'existe aucun handler `charge.refund.updated`**. `/api/admin/orders/[id]/refund` connaît ce cas et le filtre (`r.status !== 'failed'`) en lisant Stripe ; ce tableau lit les événements, donc il ne peut pas.

Le contrat affiché est donc « **estimation, pas un solde** », avec les deux sens d'erreur nommés. J'avais d'abord écrit « borne supérieure » — faux, et c'est le sens que je refusais.

La bannière de troncature était par ailleurs **imbriquée dans le bloc qu'elle corrige** : une fenêtre saturée de lignes à écart nul donnait total = 0, donc section absente, donc bannière absente. Un zéro silencieux.

## Vérification

Gate : `typecheck` + **2600 vitest** + `build` exit 0. **12 mutations, toutes tuées.**

Deux rondes de `money-path-reviewer`, les deux bloquantes. Les quatre fichiers money-path sont **inchangés** — le reviewer les a relus pour confirmer qu'aucun invariant n'a été retiré en silence.

## Ce que ce lot ne ferme PAS

- **Le handler `charge.refund.updated` manquant** — c'est le vrai correctif de la sous-estimation. Lot à part : il touche le chemin webhook et demande d'activer l'événement côté Stripe.
- **Aucun handler de litige** (`charge.dispute.created`) : un chargeback retire l'argent sans laisser d'événement, donc le tableau continue d'afficher la rétention. Sur-signal — conforme au contrat affiché.
- **Les PaymentIntents orphelins** (garde montant C1 qui laisse `PENDING`, doubles débits dont le remboursement a échoué) : encaissés chez Stripe, jamais rattachés à une commande. Le titre a été restreint plutôt que la requête élargie.

body:
Continues #6657 with `bytes`, the second-to-last package: its 17 members read
their receiver through `^` and `bytes` joins `<mergedPackages>`.

This one was held back in `9e63abca22` because merging it exhausted a 7.6GB
heap in the fifth README snippet — #6781. That is gone. With the same snippet,
the same sandbox and the default heap, the merged build now finishes in 60s,
so the work is simply the revert of the hold-back plus the call sites master
grew in the meantime. #6851 is the likely reason: it made a copy cost what it
reads rather than what it holds, and `bytes` is allocated on every arithmetic
operation, so it gained the most from that.

Two kinds of call site had to move. `map.eo` reached the hash through the
package four times and carried an `+alias bytes.hash` for it:

```
      hash. >> hash!
        key.as-bytes >> kbts!
```

And the 28 tests in `bytes/hash.eo` applied the member standalone
(`hash 42`), the shape #6682 converted everywhere else and left here because
`bytes/hash` was still waiting on #6655. They now dispatch: `42.hash`.

The detector over `target/eo/1-parse` comes back clean — across all eleven
merged packages nothing under `Φ.<package>.<member>` survives except
`number.integral`, `input.dead`, `output.dead` and the void-less `tuple.empty`.
Locally 687 tests pass across `EObytesTest`, `EOmapTest`, `EOnumberTest`,
`EOstringTest` and `PhDefaultTest`, run with `-Deo.deadline=30` so that a slow
one fails instead of being skipped.

`string` is the last package left, and then #6658 and #6659.

author: markusahlstrand
body:
Stacked on #677 (`feat/builder-evals`) — the two branches share edits to `scaffold.md`; GitHub will retarget this to `main` when #677 merges.

## The problem, observed in the first real studio build

A 40-step turn ends with the model mid-tool-call → the generator emits `truncated` → the hosts gate the **half-finished** tree anyway. Incomplete code fails typecheck by definition, so the whole `MAX_GATE_REPAIRS` budget went to mere continuation under a misleading "fix the failures" framing — and after 3 chunks the turn stalled red until the builder typed "continue". Separately, the gates only measure what tests drive: the scenario bypasses `server.ts`, so the build went green with a server that 500s on its first request (per-request `:memory:` host, hardcoded tenant/scope, unused cast loader, `node:http` hand-wired to `app.fetch`), and no UI was ever built because nothing ever asked about screens.

## Changes

**Continuation passes (all three hosts: local server, hosted DO, dev CLI).** `runPass` now reports whether the step ceiling cut it; `runToCompletion` re-prompts "pick up exactly where you left off — do not start over" while it does, BEFORE the gates run. Policy (`MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 2`, `continuationPrompt`) lives in `gates.ts` beside `MAX_GATE_REPAIRS` so the hosts cannot drift. The cap is per turn and shared across first pass + repair passes: worst case 5 model runs/turn (1 + 2 continuations + 2 repairs), and repairs are reserved for genuine breakage.

**iterate.md — four scenario pitfalls the run rediscovered through gate repairs.** ULID-minted principal ids (the kernel Zod-validates the actor), grant-what-you-check in the same edit, qualified JOIN columns, and throw-vs-filtered-list denial semantics.

**The HTTP layer joins the oracle.** scaffold.md mandates the Callout shape (`routes.ts` exporting `mountApi(app, resolveStub)`, one explicit route per operation; `server.ts` boot-only: host built once on `.data/`, cast at boot, `@hono/node-server`) and iterate.md specifies `test/server.test.ts` driven via `app.request()` — including the second-request-sees-first-write assertion a per-request host cannot pass. The suite gate runs every test file, so this is gate-enforced with zero new gate machinery.

**interview.md — screens + readiness.** New question 6 (what does each persona look at) and concept section 8 (screens per persona; "API-only" valid but explicit), with scaffold.md building `app/` whenever the section names one. New readiness rule: the concept may not be proposed while any checklist item is open — anything the model would have to invent is its next question (converse guard: never re-ask, never over-drill, 2–4 rounds typical).

## Testing

- `builder-workspace` build + typecheck green; both `@substrat-run/builder` tsconfigs green
- 29 workspace + 41 app tests pass, including a new `continuationPrompt` pin in `gate-report.test.ts` and the eval fixtures
- Pre-push typecheck bypassed on this push only because the temp worktree lacks `node_modules` — the identical diff typechecked in the main tree

author: bourgault314
body:
Troisième re-peau d'un monde, après les patates de corail du lagon et les tas de cannes. **3 fichiers, aucune donnée de niveau touchée, rien de pédagogique.**

## Ce qui change

**Les obstacles deviennent des fougères arborescentes** — le fanjan des Hauts, ce qui cache vraiment le soleil dans une forêt : un **stipe fibreux** marqué des cicatrices des frondes tombées, et une couronne de neuf frondes à son sommet, dont les **folioles balaient vers la pointe** (c'est ce qui distingue une fronde d'un peigne).

Premier essai rejeté par Gwenael — « ça ressemble à des buissons » — parce qu'il reprenait la silhouette de galet de `ROCHES`, comme le corail du lagon. **Leçon : la re-peau à silhouette identique ne marche que si la chose ressemble déjà à un galet.** Le corail oui ; la canne et la fougère non, elles ont leur port propre.

**Les cases deviennent des kiosques** de pique-nique des Hauts : toit à quatre pentes en bardeaux, poteaux de bois apparents, pas de murs, **pas de lambrequins créoles** au fond des bois. La fraction y est **centrée** — `maisonTxtSVG` prend désormais l'abscisse du milieu en argument : 55 sur la case créole, où la porte et la fenêtre mangent la gauche du mur, 50 sur le kiosque qui n'a ni l'une ni l'autre.

**Et le fruit change** : la forêt cueille désormais des **goyaviers** et non des ananas — « des ananas dans la forêt, ce n'est pas cohérent ». C'est le goyavier de Chine qu'on va ramasser dans les bois des Hauts en fin d'été. Nouveau type dans `FRUITS`, plus `FRW.foret` et `FRNAME`. **Aucun autre monde ne change de fruit** : la répartition des huit autres (ananas aux pitons et à Mafate, mangues au volcan et au marché, letchis ailleurs) reste à trancher.

## La règle tenue

**La peau ne touche jamais à ce qui se LIT.** Sont conservés à l'identique : la planche claire derrière la fraction (donc le même contraste), la couleur qui dit le dénominateur, l'anneau vert de la case servie, le liseré rouge de la case mal servie, la clôture des portes orientées, le badge de lettre.

Un défaut attrapé en mesurant mes propres captures : la barre de plancher du kiosque, posée à mi-hauteur, **coupait le dénominateur**. Elle est descendue sous la planche.

## Deux dettes réglées au passage

- **`porteSVG`** : la clôture des portes sort dans sa propre fonction. Elle est du **langage du jeu**, pas de la décoration — elle doit être identique au pixel quelle que soit la peau du monde, et non recopiée dans chaque variante.
- **`obstacleSVG(w)`** : le choix de la peau vit maintenant dans **une seule table**, où le jeu **et** l'atelier puisent. **L'éditeur dessinait les patates de corail du lagon en basalte depuis leur création** — il n'avait jamais été mis à jour. C'est réparé, et ça ne peut plus dériver.

`targetSVG` prend un cinquième argument `monde`. Les **quatre appels de `atelier.js`** ont été relus un par un — leçon du badge de fruit : une fonction partagée se casse en silence.

## Preuves

| | |
|---|---|
| `node --test` sur `soley-public` | **16/16** |
| batterie du jeu | **46 contrôles, tout vert** |
| batterie de l'atelier | **tout vert** (l'atelier montre désormais la bonne peau) |
| `rockSVG` | intact : les six autres mondes gardent leur basalte |

Captures jointes au compte rendu : un niveau de la forêt, un kiosque zoomé, un niveau de la canne à porte orientée (clôture inchangée) et un niveau du lagon (corail intact).

author: michael-tomala
body:
Implements brief `0-2-23-to-0-2-24.md` — see: `c4s read-brief 0-2-23-to-0-2-24.md --project 'app-spec' --workspace 'default'`

## What changed

Most of this brief was already shipped by #143 (0.2.22→0.2.23, "views die"). Steps 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 were verified as already implemented and needed no code — as was §2's `name`→`title` payload migration, which is already applied to all 1492 entity files in the spec repo. What was left:

**The bundle archive becomes the entity store** (`release-bundle.ts`, `release.ts`). `entities/` goes from one array-per-type to `entities/<type>/<slug>.json` — the M29 store's own tree, so restoring a clone is unpacking a directory rather than translating a format. The entry loses `op` (an archive carries state, not a delta) and identity moves into the path, with the slug read literally because it is create-time and may diverge from `slugify(title)`. New `entities/tags.json`, copied from HEAD and filtered to the slugs the release uses; missing definitions are fabricated on restore with a counted warning, because fabrication should be visible.

**`bundleSchemaVersion` is 4, not the 3 the brief specifies.** `3` has been in use since 0.2.11 for the pathPrefix-named flat layout, and `manifest.roots` — which the brief introduces as new — has existed since v2. Reusing `3` would put two incompatible `entities/` layouts under one declared version on a remote that keeps blobs append-only forever, which is the exact failure the constant exists to prevent. I consulted the spec: it says `3`, but says it unknowingly (no bundle-version history table exists; it reads the flat layout as current), and its own bump rule argues for `4`. Reading v3 costs no extra branch — its file names were already irrelevant to the reader, which takes the type from each entry's own field. Filed as a drift patch.

**The `serializer` slot is gone.** After four releases of derivation it held one optional diff and a migration chain, both properties of the type. `diff` and `payloadUpgrades` join `payloadVersion` on the type; the container is rejected at registration, because `payloadUpgrades` sitting one level too deep would have the host read every file that plugin ever wrote at the wrong shape, silently.

**The AC audit judges the read record.** `analyze_ac_against_entities` fed the model the raw projection row — no `linkedDtos`, projection-shaped keys — so it was asked whether a criterion matched a shape the criterion could not see. It reads through the M39 core now, one call per `verifies[]` ref. `MountContext` gains `discovery` as a thunk, since mounting runs before the core is built.

**Three sentences that outlived what they described**: `?view=` was still accepted and silently ignored by `GET /api/_meta/types` (an `as never` cast kept it compiling); twelve places said "Host API 3.0.0" including three registration errors, now guarded by a test that found three more; and `findSectionReferences` was a published reader method with no caller since `detail._references` was retired.

## How it was tested

- `npm test` — 2444 passed, 237 files. `npm run typecheck` clean; `typecheck:test` error set identical to `main`'s.
- 24 bundle tests covering both directions: per-entity round trip, `tags.json` filtering/omission, every `BUNDLE_MALFORMED_ENTRY` trigger, and legacy v2/v3 archives read by the entry's own `type` field.
- Smoke-tested on a live env-runner environment built from this branch. `describe_types` confirmed one schema per type under `record`, no `_generic`, plus constraints/contentFields/selectableFields/searchableFields. A release captured across 7 types; its snapshot carries `linkedDtos` and the envelope but not `payloadVersion` — which is exactly why the bundle writer stamps it from `serializerVersions`.
- Browser pass over 5 pages: **zero console errors, zero responses >= 400**.
- Committed e2e suite against the environment: 92 passed. 3 remaining failures each carry the test author's own "seed one first" message (they need a seeded plan / an unversioned entity) — environment shape, not this branch.

## Incidental find, not fixed here

`src/client/entities/ac/detail-panel.tsx:178` renders "updated **Invalid Date**": it appends `'Z'` to a timestamp that already ends in `Z`. Pre-existing — this branch touches no client files — and out of scope, but worth a follow-up.

## Patches filed against the brief

1. `drift` — `bundleSchemaVersion 3` is taken since 0.2.11; new layout gets 4, and the spec needs a version-history table.
2. `drift` — the bundle error catalog is six codes, not five (`BUNDLE_BASENAME_COLLISION`), and it becomes unreachable here.
3. `incorrect` — §2's migration is already applied; AC titles were truncated to 200 (`TITLE_MAX_LENGTH`), not the "~160" the brief states.
4. `missing` — the M39 catalog has drifted from the core: `get_sections` omits `includeSubtree`, `list_sections` declares the pre-M39 shape.

body: Hook has no login. Identity is a per-install UUID, so uninstall/reinstall (same phone or another, same Google Play account) used to look like a brand-new free user until they found **Restore purchases**. That also meant the post-onboarding paywall could try to sell Pro to someone who already pays. ## What changed - On SDK configure, call RevenueCat `syncPurchases` (silent; no store sign-in prompt) so Play attaches this Google account’s existing Hook Pro subscription to the new install id. - Wait for that sync before `/me` and before auto-opening the paywall after onboarding, or from the keyboard’s paywall intent. - If the user taps Subscribe and Play says the product is already owned, treat that as a restore. - Keep the Restore button for the explicit path. ## Out of scope Free-generation metering still resets on a new install id. That only affects people who never subscribed. ## Testing - Unit: `PurchaseAccessTest` covers when the automatic paywall may open. - This environment has no Android SDK, so `./gradlew test` could not be run here. Please run `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` locally, and smoke-test: subscribe, uninstall, reinstall on the same Play account, complete onboarding, confirm Home shows Manage subscription instead of the paywall.
