## Summary

- add `bezierExtremePoint` for direction-based extrema on a selected cubic Bezier segment
- add `bezierBulgePoint` for the maximum unsigned perpendicular distance from the segment chord
- share deterministic Bezier quadratic/root and candidate tie-break helpers across TypeScript and Rust

author: goodod0bedo
body:
Two things @brendan hit using v0.0.4.

## The crackle

> i had pressed stop on the tape section and i went to check the tabs that it was playing from and they were still playing so i paused them and a weird dissonant crackling started and didn't stop till i switched it to thru

**Reproduced before fixing**, which mattered — the measurement named the fault exactly:

| | outDb | DC offset |
|---|---|---|
| tape running | −13.46 | −0.0042 |
| stopped, sources silent | **−21.16** | **−0.0875** |
| after holding 6s | **−21.16** | **−0.0875** |

Identical to four decimal places. That's not audio, it's a frozen constant.

**Two faults, one cause.** `stop` drives the rate to ~0, freezing the read head, so `sample()` returns the same value forever — a DC offset, which buzzes rather than clicks. And once the 60s buffer fills, the oldest-clamp starts *dragging* that frozen head forward one jump per block, each held for 128 samples: a ~375 Hz staircase of unrelated samples. Pausing the tabs caused neither — it removed the live audio that was masking them.

**Fixed by making a stopped transport silent**, which is what real tape does; it doesn't hold the last sample. The worklet fades out over ~20 ms as `|rate|` falls below 0.02, well clear of genuine slow speeds. A DC-blocking highpass now sits between the tape and the output, with metering moved *after* it so what's measured is what's heard. Result: silence, `dc = 0.0000`, and audio returns at full level on resume.

The repro also caught a bug in its own test — `null > -50` is `0 > -50` in JS, so digital silence was quietly passing the "audio returns" check.

## Video mode was missing most of the app

> i couldn't help but notice that the tape controls are absent in video mode. thats a vital part of this app

An audit found it wasn't just the tape: **no transport** (which is why he had to go to the tabs to pause), no draggable rate, no pan, keep-pitch or remove, and no MIDI setup. It had been built as a viewing layout when it needed to be a playing one.

## The layout, and the space finding behind it

> i think the controls need to have more of a footprint... i think i want them outside the videobox

A 2×2 grid on a 16:9 screen gives cells that are **2:1 — wider than the 16:9 video inside them.** So side strips are nearly *free*, while every pixel of bottom strip costs the video both height and, through the aspect ratio, width.

So: tall vertical fader down the left, meter plus mute/solo/pitch/remove down the right, thin bottom holding title, transport, draggable rate and pan. **Level is vertical because that's what a fader is; pan is horizontal because pan is a left-and-right idea.**

Coloured borders per channel position — red, yellow, blue, white — on the cell itself with `gap: 0`, so they meet edge to edge and cost no extra space, as asked. Colour re-stamps when a channel is removed, matching the rule MIDI bindings already use.

**Tape and MIDI are *moved* into video mode rather than rebuilt**, so there is exactly one of each and the two modes cannot drift apart. Asserted, not assumed.

## Things only screenshots caught

- The `fullscreen / clean / midi` bar was **falling off the bottom of the screen** — `#video` was `100vh` while sitting below the topbar inside body padding. Those buttons were unreachable.
- The tape was eating a quarter of the height at list-mode spacing.
- The video box resolved to **zero width**: `aspect-ratio` with only `max-width`/`max-height` has no definite dimension to derive from. Height-driven now, and the 16:9 claim is asserted numerically at two window sizes rather than eyeballed.

## Verified

**86 checks** — 40 video, 23 MIDI, 18 panel, 5 crackle. Zip rebuilt with `pack.sh`: 13 files, 0.0.5, no signing key.

## Still unverified

Four *real* YouTube tabs in video mode, and CPU with four live streams — both need the toolbar click no test can perform.

author: shakibbinkabir
body:
`nt-staging-ci-deploy`'s state grant covered the **whole** bucket — `prod/core.tfstate` and `account/core.tfstate` included — while prod's own role was correctly scoped to `prod/core.tfstate*`.

## Why this landed before the prod apply, not after

Prod's state holds `random_password` values in **plaintext** — the Redis auth token and the `nt_app` role password. From the first prod apply this would have been a live path from the environment that runs on **every push to main**, from the least-privileged trust boundary we have, straight to production credentials.

Closing it once it is real is incident response. Closing it while it is still theoretical is a one-word change.

## The delta

Exactly one statement moved:

```
arn:aws:s3:::nt-tfstate-staging-252959251643/*
→ arn:aws:s3:::nt-tfstate-staging-252959251643/staging/*
```

`0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy`. Applied; staging then re-planned clean.

`nt-staging-ci-plan` is unaffected — it carries AWS-managed `ReadOnlyAccess` plus its own `refresh-secret-versions` inline policy, not this document.

## ⚠ Residual, recorded rather than glossed

That same `ReadOnlyAccess` includes account-wide `s3:GetObject`, and the role matches `role/nt-*` so the state bucket's deny admits it. **`nt-staging-ci-plan` can still read `prod/core.tfstate`.**

It cannot write, and it only assumes on pull-request events. But the honest statement is that prod state is readable by a staging principal until that managed policy is replaced by a scoped one — and swapping the managed policy on the role that gates every PR plan is its own change with its own blast radius. Tracked in `infra/README.md`.

author: clancey
body:
Tagging a release used to produce a version number and nothing else. The catalog carried a `releaseNotesUrl` that the app parsed and never showed, the catalog release body said "Published by tools/publish.sh", and v1.0.8 and v1.0.11 shipped with no release page at all. A rider on a console saw "update to 1.0.12" with no way to learn what that meant — and no browser to go find out.

## What a tag produces now

Pushing `v1.0.12` yields, in order:

1. **Notes assembled from git history** — the commits between the previous tag and this one, with bookkeeping subjects (bumps, chores, WIP, merges) filtered out.
2. **`catalog.json` carries the notes as plain text**, alongside the APK.
3. **The catalog release body** gets the real notes instead of the placeholder.
4. **A GitHub Release on this repo**, like the hand-written v1.0.6 and v1.0.7 pages.
5. **`CHANGELOG.md` committed back to `main`.**
6. **The console shows the notes** in the self-update dialog.

## Hand-written notes win

`tools/changelog.sh` always generates something, but if `docs/release-notes/<version>.md` exists it is used verbatim. The v1.0.6 and v1.0.7 bodies are backfilled there, so `CHANGELOG.md` starts with real prose rather than a commit list — and they double as working examples.

## Two renderings

The generator emits markdown with PR links for GitHub, and flattened plain text for the console. The update dialog is a Flutter `AlertDialog` on a TV: `**bold**` and `[text](url)` would render as literal punctuation, so bullets become `•` and links are stripped.

This is also why notes travel *in* the catalog rather than behind `releaseNotesUrl`. A console has no browser; a URL is a dead end.

## Notes accumulate

The catalog jumped versionCode 9 → 12, so a console sitting on 9 never saw 10 or 11. `catalog.json` now carries a window of the last eight releases, and `CatalogEntry.notesNewerThan(installed)` narrows to everything the console skipped. A console with nothing installed sees only the newest entry — a backlog it never lived through is noise.

## Notes are decoration, not a safety boundary

`CatalogManifest.parse` normally rejects the whole document on any malformation. `releaseNotes` is the deliberate exception: bad entries are skipped. Refusing the catalog over bad prose would take down the console's only update path. Documented inline and in APPSTORE §4.1.

## Workflow details worth a look

- `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout — without it every release generates empty notes that look like "nothing changed" rather than a broken checkout.
- Notes are assembled **before** the build, so a mistake costs seconds instead of ten minutes of Gradle.
- The keystore re-lock moved earlier, right after signature verification. The new trailing steps would otherwise have extended the decrypted key's lifetime.
- The `CHANGELOG.md` commit runs in a fresh clone, never the build workspace, which holds the decrypted keystore. It's `continue-on-error` with a recovery recipe in the run summary — a changelog that missed its push is a paragraph to re-run, not a reason to show a red release.
- Explicit `permissions: contents: write`.

## Verification

- `tools/changelog.sh notes|json|regenerate|check` against real history, including the first-tag path and the override path
- Catalog injection simulated against a real clone of `stride-catalog`; the diff is confined to the stride entry and the catalog's own `verify.sh` passes
- `flutter analyze` clean, 95 Dart tests pass (3 new)
- 41 Kotlin tests pass (7 new), Android lint clean
- Shell syntax checked on every `run:` block; the embedded Python heredoc compiles

The first tagged release after this merges is the real end-to-end test of `gh release create` and the CHANGELOG push-back.

## Optional follow-up

The `releaseNotes` field is injected by this repo's workflow after `publish.sh` runs, because the catalog repo doesn't know about it. `stride-catalog`'s `verify.sh` is permissive about unknown keys so this works today, but a `--notes-body` flag on `publish.sh` upstream would be tidier.

author: joshuad2824-art
body:
Two things from the second round on the phone.

## The foot rode up with the keyboard

Sizing the app to the visual viewport had the side effect of parking the word count and edited time directly above the keyboard, in the way for the whole time you were typing. It's for looking at a finished page, not for writing one — so it gives its line back to the text while the keyboard is up, and comes back when the keyboard goes.

## The tools row was off the top again

The screenshot showed it: text sitting under the status bar, no tools row. iOS has a *second* way of moving the app out from under itself. As well as scrolling the document — which a fixed body stops — it scrolls the **visual viewport**, which it doesn't. The body stays pinned where it was and the top of the app ends up above the visible area, taking the tools with it.

So the app is now positioned at `visualViewport.offsetTop` as well as sized to `visualViewport.height`. It covers exactly what can be seen, no more and no less.

## Verification

Twenty-six checks, all passing. Seven are new. A real soft keyboard can't be summoned in a headless browser — I tried driving it through CDP and Chromium wouldn't shrink the visual viewport — so instead they feed the handler the numbers iOS reports when a keyboard opens (a 420px visual viewport, scrolled 96px down under an 844px layout viewport) and assert what the app does with them:

```
PASS  the foot is there with no keyboard
PASS  the app sizes to the visual viewport  — 420
PASS  the app follows the viewport offset  — 96
PASS  the foot gets out of the way
PASS  the tools row is still on screen  — y=136
PASS  the foot comes back
PASS  the tools row returns to rest  — 40 → 40
```

That proves our reaction is right. It cannot prove iOS reports what I think it reports — that part is still only settleable on the phone, and it's the thing to watch when this lands.

author: rambaarde
body:
Wrapping a custom launcher worked — but only if you knew to name it, and the people most likely to have one are the least likely to read that far. For anyone who does not type `claude` directly, the hotkey just appears not to exist.

## Summary

- **`aps install` now reads your rc file** for launchers. A definition counts when its name pairs an agent with a word meaning *begin a session*: `claude-start`, `codex-run`, `start-claude`. Functions and aliases both.
- **Requiring that second word is the point.** Matching any function containing an agent's name also catches one-shot helpers — a note wrapper, a log tailer — and wrapping one puts a pty and a keyboard interceptor around a command that finishes in a second. Missing a launcher costs one explicit name; wrapping the wrong thing costs trust.
- **Our own block is excluded from the scan** — every alias in it contains an agent's name and the word `run`, so reading it back would wrap the wrapper.
- README documents this with a neutral placeholder, not any particular launcher name.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 53/53, two new cases: launchers found vs. one-shot helpers and unrelated functions rejected, and our own block never re-scanned
- [x] Run against a real `.zshrc`: found the two genuine launchers and correctly rejected a `*-note` helper that the first, broader heuristic had matched
- [x] Verified the generated block for that machine wraps both binaries and both launchers, guarded by `APS_WRAPPED`

author: jetnity
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Nimmt die Endpunkte der alten Produktwelt außer Betrieb. Von 77 Route Handlern bleiben 16, alle vier Cron-Jobs sind entfernt. Elf Commits, funktional getrennt.

Der wichtigste Teil ist nicht die Menge: **zwei Codepfade lösten ohne Nutzerbeteiligung kostenpflichtige DALL·E-3-Generierungen aus, und sechs Modell-Endpunkte waren vollständig ohne Authentifizierung öffentlich erreichbar.** Beides ist beseitigt.

## Kostenrisiken – vollständig beseitigt

**Pfad 1: der tägliche Cron.** `/api/copilot/auto` rief für bis zu 24 Regionen sequenziell `maybeGenerateCopilotUpload` auf, das über `copilot-upload-generator` und `copilot-image` DALL·E 3 erzeugt. Bei Portrait-Format entspricht das bis zu rund USD 1.90 pro Lauf. Zusätzlich war die Secret-Prüfung **fail-open**:

```ts
if (!CRON_SECRET) return true // wenn kein Secret gesetzt ist, nicht blocken (Dev)
```

Ohne gesetztes `CRON_SECRET` war der Endpunkt also öffentlich aufrufbar. Die beiden anderen Crons waren dagegen fail-closed.

**Pfad 2: eine öffentliche Seite – der schwerwiegendere Fall.** `app/search/page.tsx` löste beim Server-Rendering eine Generierung aus, sobald ein `region`- oder `city`-Parameter gesetzt war:

```ts
const generatorTarget = region || city || ''
if (generatorTarget) { try { await maybeGenerateCopilotUpload(generatorTarget) } catch {} }
```

Ein einfacher Aufruf von `/search?region=Bali` genügte. Ohne Authentifizierung, ohne Secret, ohne Rate Limit, ohne Obergrenze. Anders als beim Cron war hier nicht einmal ein Secret vorgesehen.

**Strukturell abgesichert.** Nach dem Entfernen beider Aufrufer blieb die Generierungskette als toter Code im Repository und ließe sich jederzeit erneut verdrahten. Deshalb sind `copilot-upload-checker`, `copilot-upload-generator` und `copilot-image` entfernt, ebenso der Block `maybeGenerateCopilotUpload`. `getCopilotSuggestions` bleibt erhalten, weil das Creator-Dashboard es nutzt und es ausschließlich lesend auf die Datenbank zugreift.

Ergebnis: **kein Codepfad löst mehr ohne Nutzerinteraktion einen kostenpflichtigen Modellaufruf aus.**

## Offene Modell-Endpunkte ohne Authentifizierung

Sechs der entfernten Endpunkte hatten keinerlei Auth-Prüfung. Der gravierendste:

`/api/generate-image` – öffentlich aufrufbare Bildgenerierung, abgesichert nur durch ein In-Memory-Rate-Limit von 20 Anfragen pro Minute und IP. Das ist pro Serverless-Instanz gezählt und durch IP-Wechsel umgehbar. Der Endpunkt schrieb Ergebnisse zusätzlich mit dem **Service-Role-Key** in den Supabase Storage.

Ebenfalls ohne Auth: `/api/generate-comment`, `/api/copilot/generate-cocreation`, `/api/storyboard`, `/api/media/title-suggest`, `/api/media/snippets`.

Das widerspricht [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) Regel 17. Nach ADR-0006 werden sie nicht abgesichert, sondern entfernt – das beseitigt das Risiko vollständig statt es zu verkleinern.

## Abhängigkeitsprüfung vor der Löschung

Vor jeder Entfernung habe ich den transitiven Abhängigkeitsgraphen der V2-Seiten aufgelöst (`/`, `/planen`, `/reisen`, `/reisen/[tripId]`, Login, Register, Layouts, Middleware).

**Ergebnis: 32 erreichte Dateien, null `/api/`-Aufrufe.** Die V2-Produktfläche hängt an keinem einzigen Endpunkt. Alle Aufrufer der entfernten Endpunkte sind Alt-Oberflächen.

Bei der Inventur ist außerdem aufgefallen, dass meine frühere Zählung von 76 Endpunkten unvollständig war: sie erfasste nur `route.ts` und übersah `app/api/og/story/[id]/route.tsx`. Tatsächlich waren es 77.

## Was entfernt wurde

| Gruppe | Anzahl | Inhalt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cron-Jobs | 4 | alle Einträge in `vercel.json` |
| Cron-Endpunkte | 3 | `copilot/auto`, `cron/publish-scheduled-posts`, `admin/cron/dns` |
| KI-/Modell-Endpunkte | 21 | Copilot, Story, Storyboard, generate-*, remix-image, media/ai/*, admin/copilot/*, publish/*, worker/render |
| Media und Video | 12 | Render, Transcode, Masken, Edits, Versionen, signierte URLs, Video-Jobs |
| Creator, Feed, Sessions | 13 | Analytics, Alerts, Publishing, Session-Speicherung und -Versionierung |
| Content | 4 | `blog/posts`, `content-type`, `inspiration`, `og/story/[id]` |
| Infrastruktur und Hilfsmittel | 8 | Infomaniak DNS und Mail, `dns/check`, `storage/ensure`, `uploads/signed-url`, `utils/gravatar` |

## Was bewusst bleibt

| Endpunkt | Begründung |
| --- | --- |
| `app/auth/refresh` | V2-Auth, Session-Erneuerung |
| `api/search/airports` | Flughafendaten, für Flüge in Phase 3 vorgesehen |
| `api/search` | hält die Alt-Suchseite funktionsfähig bis zur Alt-UI-Entfernung |
| `api/admin/payments/*` (5) | ADR-0010: behalten, nicht ausbauen |
| `api/admin/security/*` (8) | laut Vision Teil des späteren Admin-Umfangs |

Bei `app/search/page.tsx` habe ich bewusst nur den Generator-Aufruf und dessen Import entfernt, nicht die Seite. Das ist der minimale Eingriff, der den Kostenpfad stilllegt; die Seite selbst gehört zur Alt-UI und wird gemeinsam mit ihr entfernt. Nach ADR-0006 wird Alt-Code nicht modernisiert – ein aktiver Kostenpfad wird aber sofort stillgelegt.

## Abhängigkeiten

`ffmpeg-static`, `fluent-ffmpeg` und `@types/fluent-ffmpeg` entfernt: nach dem Wegfall der Render-Endpunkte gibt es im Quellcode keine Referenz mehr darauf. Zusammen rund 89 MB in `node_modules`.

Bewusst behalten: `hls.js`, `html2pdf.js` und `exifr` werden weiterhin dynamisch aus Alt-Komponenten importiert. `sharp` wird nicht direkt importiert, kann aber von Next.js für die Bildoptimierung genutzt werden – eine Entfernung wäre eine Verhaltensänderung und gehört nicht in diesen Schritt.

## Gastmodus-Entscheidung

Als ADR-0013 dokumentiert: ein Gast darf genau eine aktive Reise speichern, mehrere Reisen erfordern ein Konto. Damit ist der offene Widerspruch aus Phase 0 aufgelöst.

Die Umsetzung erfolgt **nicht** hier, weil in Phase 1.1 ausdrücklich keine zusätzlichen Funktionen entstehen sollen. Sie ist Phase 1.5 zugeordnet, gemeinsam mit der Migration Gast zu Konto. Der Code trägt weiterhin `MAX_GUEST_TRIPS = 20`; das ist als bekannte Abweichung dokumentiert. Nötig sind dort ein ehrlicher Hinweis auf das Konto statt stillem Überschreiben und ein definierter Übergang für Browser, die schon mehrere Gastreisen enthalten.

## Tests und Build

Aus frisch gelöschtem `node_modules`:

| Prüfung | Ergebnis |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | erfolgreich, 620 Pakete |
| `npm run check:setup:ci` | bestanden |
| `npm run typecheck` | fehlerfrei |
| `npm run lint` | 0 Fehler |
| `npm run build` | erfolgreich, exakt die 16 erwarteten Endpunkte |

Automatisierte Tests existieren weiterhin nicht; der Einstieg ist Phase 1.6.

## Datenbank

Keine Migration, keine Schemaänderung. Die entfernten Endpunkte haben Tabellen nur gelesen und geschrieben, nicht definiert.

Laufende Kosten sinken. Der tägliche Bildgenerierungs-Cron entfällt, und die beiden öffentlich missbrauchbaren Kostenpfade sind geschlossen. Keine neuen Kosten.

## Offene Risiken

1. **Alt-Oberflächen sind funktional beschädigt.** Media Studio, Creator Hub, Admin Copilot, Feed und Blog rufen entfernte Endpunkte auf und zeigen dort Fehler. Beabsichtigt; Entfernung als Schritt 1.1b eingeplant.

author: razzleberrytt
body:
> Stacked on #3180. Review that one first.

## What

`evidence_design_match`, `evidence_risk_of_bias`, and `evidence_consistency` drive the "why this grade?" card beside every evidence grade. The workbook never filled them — **all three empty on all 856 records** — so `EvidenceGradeRationale` rendered on **no page at all**.

The information needed already sat in `claims.json`, where each claim records the design of the study behind it. Now that #3180 gives those designs a canonical class, the rationale can be computed.

## How

`buildEvidenceRationale()` derives all three fields from study classes:

| Field | Derived from |
|---|---|
| Design match | Strongest recorded design across the profile's claims |
| Risk of bias | That design, with an override for studies flagging their own bias (`systematic_review_meta_analysis_high_bias`) |
| Consistency | Designs recording disagreement (`meta_analysis_mixed_result`) or a negative finding |

**Every field is null wherever the claims cannot support a judgement**, and the card renders "Not assessed" rather than hiding. An absent signal must not read as a clean bill of health.

Consistency deliberately requires **three** human studies before it will say "Consistent" — below that, "nothing disagreed" mostly means there was little to disagree with. That honesty costs coverage: 163 profiles can show design and bias, only 27 can also show agreement. Gating the card on all three fields would have rendered 27 cards, so it now gates on design + bias.

## Grade-vs-evidence validation

`gradeIsBackedByEvidence()` implements the grade-vs-study-count and grade-vs-study-type checks. It **reports rather than silently corrects**, because a missing human study is more often an unrecorded citation than a wrong grade.

On indexable profiles:
- **4 A/B grades with no human study on record** — `gotu-kola`, `schisandra`, `tribulus-terrestris`, `biotin`
- **4 Grade A profiles resting on a single human study** — `black-seed`, `tyrosine`, `lavandula-angustifolia`, `selenium`
- 68 more A/B grades have no claims recorded at all (data completeness, reported separately)

## Result

**Rationale cards renderable: 0 → 163.**

## Verification

- `vitest lib/__tests__/evidence-*.test.ts lib/__tests__/study-class.test.ts` — 47 passed
- Full suite: 32 failed / 1693 passed, against a clean-main baseline of 32 failed / 1679 passed — **same 32 pre-existing failures**, +14 new passing tests
- `tsc --noEmit` — 45 errors, identical to main
- `eslint` clean on all touched files
- Data diff verified field-level: 10 fields added, 5 updated, **no records added or removed**, indexable count unchanged at 445

body:
Both found by the documentation audit in #4100, which was scoped to prose and correctly stopped at code rather than editing it.

**`runner.py`** justified sending setup output as a `SetupOutput` frame by saying a new frame kind "would be a `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump — which, until the two ends negotiate, breaks every session on release". They negotiate now: the runner's `Hello` carries its range and both sides take the `max` of the common one. The caution is still right, for a reason the comment now states instead — `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` is a single element (`(2,)`), so a bump *refuses* a peer on the old version rather than degrading to it, and it would still break sessions in flight on release. The condition for affording a frame kind is therefore "the supported range is wide enough", which is checkable, rather than "once the two ends negotiate", which has already happened.

**`test_claude_bridge_e2e.py`** still named `runner.build_claude_environment`, deleted by #4083 in favour of `backend.child_environment`. (The same reference in the fullstack e2e is already fixed on the outbox branch.)

author: cplieger
body:
## Problem

The release, build-ability and scan builds all read the GHA layer cache, so a
Dockerfile package-upgrade layer stopped executing once it was cached and every
image kept shipping whatever packages were current when that layer was first
built. Nothing reported it: releases were green and the pinned base digests were
already the newest tags, so Renovate had nothing to bump.

Measured on `ghcr.io/cplieger/web-terminal-kiro:latest` (2026-08-16):

```text
image created:  2026-08-15T09:13:56Z   (v2.11.1)
apt layer:      2026-08-05T03:09:27Z   (11 days old, restored from cache)
```

It shipped `util-linux 2.41-5`, `unzip 6.0-29` and `jq 1.7.1-6+deb13u2` against
published Debian fixes `2.41.5-0+deb13u1`, `6.0-29+deb13u1` and
`1.7.1-6+deb13u3`. Across vibekit, web-terminal-kiro and web-terminal-server
that was ~354 open Trivy alerts.

`rebuild-stale.yaml` could not cover this. Its staleness clock resets on every
successful release run, so an actively released repo (vibekit ships several
times a day) never reaches the threshold, and a rebuild that did fire would
have hit the same cached layer.

## Change

All four build sites — the per-arch release build, both `ci.yaml`
build-ability gates, and the advisory scan build — resolve a `PKG_REFRESH`
build arg and pass it **only when the Dockerfile declares one**, so distroless
and scratch images draw no unconsumed-build-arg warning. The value is the UTC
date, so an opted-in package layer rebuilds at most once a day and later builds
the same day still hit cache.

The consumer half (`ARG PKG_REFRESH` referenced by the package layer) is
already on main in all ten affected image repos, so this PR activates a
mechanism that is waiting for it rather than introducing a coupled change. The
arg defaults to a constant, so a repo that never declares it is unaffected.

## Why the scan build needed it too

`security-scan.yaml` is a pure cache consumer, so without this it reported CVE
findings for a phantom image: a package set no published image actually ships.

## Notes

- `--no-cache-filter` was the obvious alternative and does not apply: Docker's
  docs require its arguments to be stage names, and the Debian images' final
  stages are unnamed.
- The provenance comment on the release build is corrected — `mode=max` embeds
  build-arg values and this workflow now passes one (a date, not a secret).

## Verification

`actionlint` and `yamllint` (repo settings) clean. The detection logic was
executed against every image Dockerfile in the fleet to confirm both branches:
declared arg yields a date, absent arg yields no build arg at all.

author: nikazzio
body:
## Perché

Ogni libro costava **due richieste per carta**: una per la pagina, una per la miniatura. Su un libro di 924 carte sono 1848 richieste a una biblioteca che risponde in modo irregolare — misurato su archive.org: la stessa richiesta va da 1 a 19 secondi.

La pagina la scarichiamo già. La miniatura si ricava da lì in qualche decina di millisecondi, senza chiedere niente a nessuno.

## Cosa cambia

**Libreria per le immagini.** `image`, puro Rust, `default-features = false` e i soli formati `jpeg` e `png`: nessuna dipendenza di sistema, le build per i tre sistemi restano come sono. Vive in `src-tauri/src/images.rs`, funzioni pure e provabili senza rete — decodifica, ridimensionamento al lato lungo conservando le proporzioni e **senza mai ingrandire**, ricodifica JPEG a qualità 80 (interna: è una scelta di resa, non una preferenza).

**Le miniature si ricavano.** Nel gestore, subito dopo la promozione della carta, dai byte già in memoria: stessa area di transito, riga `assets` con `kind = 'thumbnail'` e identificativo `<versione>:thumbnail:<carta>`, senza `remote_url` perché non l'ha servita nessuno. Decodifica e ricodifica in `spawn_blocking`, perché sono lavoro del processore e nel filo del runtime terrebbero ferma la coda.

**Se la miniatura non riesce, il libro non fallisce**: si scrive nel registro e si va avanti. Una carta già sul disco a cui manca la miniatura la fa ricavare rileggendo il file, una volta sola.

**Il lato lungo è configurabile**: predefinito **300 px**, ammessi 100-800, letto da `app_settings.thumbnail_long_edge` alla messa in coda. La schermata che lo cambia arriva con la politica di scaricamento (#422).

**Sparisce `source_thumbnails`**: tipo di lavoro, variante del gestore, messa in coda, traduzioni e prove. Il pannello torna a **una riga per libro**. L'area di transito torna una per digitalizzazione, con nomi diversi per carta e miniatura.

## Mappatura contro le decisioni

| Decisione | Cosa prescrive | Come è rispettata qui |
|---|---|---|
| **D6** (corretta il 2026-08-16) | le miniature vanno con il libro, restano fuori da «libera spazio» | si ricavano dalla carta appena scaricata; `kind = 'thumbnail'` resta fuori dal conteggio delle carte e da «libera spazio», che cancella solo `pages/`. Testo della decisione riscritto: diceva «si scaricano» |
| **D4** | il tetto è una politica, non si tenta niente alla cieca | invariato per le carte. Cade il primo dei tre livelli — «l'indirizzo che il manifesto dichiara già pronto» — che valeva per le sole miniature |
| **D7** | la disponibilità si conta dalle carte | le miniature non entrano nel conteggio: `kind` diverso, come prima |
| **D16-bis** | area di transito e validazione prima della promozione | la miniatura passa dalla stessa area di transito e dalla stessa validazione della carta |
| **D11** | classi di risorsa separate | il lavoro resta di classe rete; la parte che pesa sul processore gira fuori dal filo del runtime |

## Cosa mettere in conto

Le miniature esisteranno solo per le carte scaricate. Oggi non cambia niente, perché si scarica il libro intero; quando arriverà lo scaricamento della singola carta (D4), quel libro avrà le miniature solo di quelle. Per il resto si leggono online, che è il comportamento normale.

## Prove

- `cargo test`: 354 passate, `cargo clippy` senza rilievi, `cargo fmt` applicato;
- `vitest run`: 97 file, 832 prove passate;
- `npm run typecheck` pulito, `npm run lint` senza errori.

Prove nuove: il lato lungo diventa la misura chiesta in verticale e in orizzontale, un'immagine più piccola non viene ingrandita, una miniatura pesa molto meno della carta, byte che non sono un'immagine vengono rifiutati senza far cadere niente, carta e miniatura non condividono né identificativo né nome nell'area di transito.

## Da provare a mano

Scaricare un libro e verificare che nel pannello compaia **una riga sola**, e che nel deposito, accanto a `pages/2000/`, si riempia `thumbnails/` con immagini da 300 px sul lato lungo.

author: celestial0579
body: Closes #262 Auf deine Vorgabe „entscheide was das beste ist, nicht das einfachste" — deshalb **nicht** der naheliegende Referer-Filter in `public/uploads/.htaccess`. ## Warum nicht .htaccess Zwei Mängel, die beide erst im Betrieb auffallen: 1. **Er gilt nur für Apache.** Dieses Repo liefert ausschließlich `.htaccess` mit. Eine nginx- oder Caddy-Installation hätte damit *überhaupt keinen* Schutz, ohne dass das irgendwo sichtbar würde. 2. **Er ist in dieser Suite nicht prüfbar.** Sie fährt `php -S`, und das wertet `.htaccess` nicht aus. Ein Schutz, den keine Prüfung erreicht, fällt beim Umzug auf einen anderen Webserver oder bei verstellter Serverkonfiguration still aus — genau die Sorte Fehler, die dieses Repo schon zweimal als Lehre festgehalten hat. Die Entscheidung liegt deshalb im Anwendungscode: `/media/horse-image`, einmal, prüfbar, webserverunabhängig. ## Zwei Schichten, die sich gegenseitig decken **`Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`** ist der wirksame Teil — und im Issue gar nicht genannt. Er wird vom **Browser** durchgesetzt: Eine fremde Seite kann das Bild nicht per `` einbinden und kann das nicht umgehen. Das ist der entscheidende Unterschied zum Referer, den die einbettende Seite selbst bestimmt (`referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` genügt). **Die Referer-Prüfung** greift dort, wo CORP nicht greift: bei Clients, die CORP nicht kennen. Ein **leerer** Referer bleibt bewusst erlaubt — ihn zu blocken bräche direktes Aufrufen einer Bild-URL, Lesezeichen und jeden Browser, der den Referer grundsätzlich unterdrückt. Genau diese Lücke deckt CORP ab. Deshalb zwei Schichten und nicht eine. ## Warum keine signierten URLs Sie wären die dritte Möglichkeit und hier die falsche. Signierte, ablaufende URLs schützen **nicht-öffentliche** Ressourcen. Bei einem öffentlichen Katalog kosten sie Auffindbarkeit (Bild-Indexierung), Vorschaubilder in sozialen Netzen und die Verträglichkeit mit Addons — während CORP dasselbe Ziel ohne diese Kosten erreicht. Sie hätten außerdem alle vier offiziellen Addons gebrochen, die `image_url` direkt rendern. ## Nebenbefund, mit behoben **Als statische Datei war ein Foto unabhängig von `is_published` abrufbar.** Das Bild eines unveröffentlichten Pferdes lag offen, sobald jemand die URL kannte. Der Zufallsanteil im Dateinamen schützt vor Raten, nicht vor einer bekannten URL. Jetzt gelten dieselben Sichtbarkeitsregeln wie für die Detailseite. ## Kein Rückschritt beim Laden Bedingte Anfragen (`ETag`/`Last-Modified` → 304) und `Cache-Control` mit einem Jahr. Ohne sie wäre die Auslieferung über PHP genau der Rückschritt, den das Issue befürchtet. `readfile()` nach geleertem Ausgabepuffer, damit große Bilder nicht komplett im Speicher landen. ## Verträglichkeit Der gespeicherte Spaltenwert bleibt `/uploads/horses/` — er ist der Speicherort, nicht die Adresse. Die vier offiziellen Addons, die ihn direkt rendern (`galerie`, `merkliste`, `qr-code`, `verkaufsboerse`), funktionieren unverändert weiter und bekommen unter Apache über die ergänzte `.htaccess` ebenfalls CORP. **Sie umgehen dabei aber die `is_published`-Prüfung** — sie auf `App\Helper\MediaUrl::horseImage()` umzustellen ist ein eigener kleiner PR im Addons-Repo, den ich anschließe. ## Prüfung **Gegenprobe für jede Zusicherung einzeln geführt**, jeweils über den vollen Functional-Lauf: | Eingriff | Ergebnis | |---|---| | CORP-Header weggelassen | rot | | Fremden Referer durchgelassen | rot | | `is_published`-Prüfung entfernt | rot | | `realpath`-Prüfung entfernt | rot | | 304-Behandlung entfernt | rot | **Dabei ist eine Lücke im eigenen Test aufgefallen und behoben worden:** Beide Traversal-Fälle fing schon die Endungs-Positivliste ab — die `realpath`-Prüfung war damit gar nicht belegt. Gemerkt habe ich es daran, dass das gleichzeitige Abschalten beider Schutzmaßnahmen die Suite *abstürzen* ließ statt sie rot zu machen. Sie hat jetzt einen eigenen Fall: ein Symlink mit Bildendung, der aus dem Verzeichnis herauszeigt. | Suite | Ergebnis | |---|---| | Unit | 316 grün | | Integration | 67 grün | | Functional | 152 grün, 1531 Assertions | 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: kory-io
body:
## Problem

Long-lived machines accumulate daemon leftovers nothing reclaims. Measured on the maintainer's machine: **2695** dirs under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nestweaver/` (including all 1682 `daemon.spawnlock` files), **1885** under `~/.local/state/nestweaver/`, **264** under `/tmp/nw-sock-1000/` — ~1883 state dirs in three days. `gc_orphaned_state_dirs` swept only the persistent-state root; the runtime-dir root (the largest leak) and the `/tmp` socket-fallback dirs were touched by no path, and temp-database daemons never unlinked their dirs on clean shutdown.

## Fix

- `gc_orphaned_state_dirs` → `gc_orphaned_daemon_dirs`, sweeping **all three roots** (persistent state, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `/tmp` fallback) with a per-root report. Two-phase: candidates gathered from every root before any deletion; each instance identified once (state root's `daemon.log` boot line); one ownership test governs all of an instance's dirs.
- Ownership proof is kernel-attested, never the pidfile flock alone: the **database write lock** (`F_GETLK` names the holder) plus the pidfile flock as corroboration; `Unknown` fails closed. A live daemon's files are never reclaimed — asserted by an integration test that sweeps from a separate process against a **running** daemon and checks its socket still answers.
- `/tmp` squatting threat model preserved: the fallback root is ownership-checked (real dir, owned by euid — the shape `secure_fallback_sock_dir` already refuses) or skipped wholesale; foreign-owned entries left alone; the sweep constructs fallback paths directly and never calls `socket_path` per candidate.
- Clean shutdown of a **temp-database** daemon (the existing `is_temp_db_path` predicate) now unlinks its state/runtime/fallback dirs, so counts stop growing between sweeps. A flock probe on `daemon.spawnlock` vetoes removal mid-restart-handshake (a regression caught by the full suite, not by inspection).
- `daemon gc --help` now names exactly the roots it sweeps, and the output breaks removals down per root. `NESTWEAVER_SOCK_FALLBACK_DIR` (test support) documented in CLAUDE.md.

Fail-closed limitation, disclosed: entries whose state-dir `daemon.log` is already gone are unidentifiable and are reported but never reclaimed — the shutdown unlink stops future growth; the existing backlog needs an operator `rm`, not a guessing sweep.

## Tests

- Pre-fix demonstration: an orphaned runtime dir (with its spawnlock) survived the old sweep while its state-dir twin was reclaimed.
- daemon 277/277 (three consecutive runs), cli_test 90/90, daemon_test 50/50 serial, fmt/clippy clean.
- New coverage: three-root reclaim, live-holder spared under every root, squatted/symlinked/absent fallback root, temp-db unlink + spawnlock veto, real-DB keep, in-process clean-shutdown e2e (also fixed an env-swap test flake it exposed, via a crate-wide `TEST_ENV_LOCK`).

Backlog item: `gc-orphaned-state-dirs-and-socket-fallback-leaks` / "Runtime leftovers nothing reclaims" (MEDIUM). Two adversarial review rounds — no unsafe deletion path found; round 1's findings were honesty/precision (help text, race docs, dedupes).

author: diegoriccardi1234
body:
## v2.0.0 — the app stops being one person's tool

Sixteen commits. The release that started as a depersonalization pass ended up
closing three things nobody knew were broken.

### What it does now

- **It asks instead of guessing.** An empty search form used to resolve to the
  author's roles and city, then save them as *your* last search. Gone: terms and
  city come from your own profile, and with nothing to go on the scan refuses and
  says what it needs.
- **The archive is navigable** — five buckets with live counts, "showing X of Y",
  a From-mail filter, sub-tabs, six working densities.
- **The mailbox is a place, not a setting** — its own tab, a badge, and a review
  queue that survives restarts: one card per message, three answers, nothing
  decided for you.
- **It paces itself.** Three sources for every rate limit — what you typed, what
  it has measured on your key, what it ships with — and measurement wins, because
  a free tier belongs to a project and a key, not to a provider.
- **It says which provider to use**, from its own evidence first. A closed free
  tier is never suggested (Cerebras' closes tomorrow). Where it does not know
  whether a free tier trains on your prompts, it says so and links their terms.
- **Two providers more**, both measured through the app's own probe before being
  added: Cloudflare Workers AI (10.000 Neurons/day, 1.2s, clean JSON) and OVHcloud
  (EU-hosted, optional key).
- **Every new verdict names the model that wrote it.**

### Three bugs found while closing it

- `app/data/provider_limits.json` — the file the whole rate-limit feature reads —
  was matched by `.gitignore`'s `data/` rule and had never been committed, and
  `JobFinder.spec` did not copy it into the bundle either.
- The rate-limit panel was dead UI: imported, never called.
- The limit learner could never fire in production: `usage_log.error_type` held the
  exception class name while the learner matched the classified cause.

And `scripts/seed_demo.py` defaulted to the **real archive**, so `--force` would
have wiped a year of applications to make screenshots.

### Verification

- 985 unit tests, mypy strict, ruff, i18n parity (1000 keys × 5 locales)
- Playwright: 26 passed, plus the demo specs re-run against `data/demo.db`
- Migration 029 applied to a copy of the real archive (498 rows): no score changed,
  second pass a no-op
- Cloudflare and OVH exercised end to end with real calls, not from a list

body:
## What changed

- adds a dedicated Day Explorer temporal runtime instead of expanding the core day loader
- rebuilds the ±3-day neighborhood as a miniature week with compact signals for sleep, work, movement, active categories, and positive/negative day markers
- replaces the old same-date cards with a metric-focused cross-year comparison
  - Sleep · Work · Movement · Diary selector
  - selected metric bars aligned across years
  - automatic highest/lowest labels
  - click any year to open that actual day
- upgrades the year scrubber with 12 month-level archive coverage indicators
  - shows public record counts by month
  - current month is highlighted
  - clicking a populated month jumps to its first available public record
- explicitly labels the current archive year comparison as YTD
- changes the standouts copy to say it compares against the recorded portion of the selected year
- preserves the existing core Day Explorer runtime for selected-record loading, summary/context, standouts, record detail, URL state, copying, and keyboard navigation

## Why

Pass 1 clarified the hierarchy. Pass 2 makes the page's temporal idea legible at a glance:

- horizontal time: what surrounded this day?
- vertical time: what did this date look like in other years?
- annual position: where does this date sit in the recorded year?

The goal is not more metrics. It is stronger navigation through time.

## Architecture

`dayExplorerRuntime.ts` remains the owner of the selected day and core record rendering. The new `dayExplorerTemporalRuntime.ts` observes successful selected-day changes and independently renders the temporal views from the canonical daily API. This keeps the new interactions isolated from the already-large core runtime.

## Scope

No AI, correlations, diary exposure, or new private data. No Stats changes. No global Header changes.

## Validation

Branch is based directly on the deployed #173 merge commit `53311f9c98a0e861a2c74a1dcbb93f388c2572b0` and is zero commits behind. Opening this draft PR triggers the repository Astro build against the exact branch head.

author: surgeservicesllc
body:
## What this closes

Rows 4 and 29 — the final **FAIL-ABSENT** entries in the Phase 2D scorecard. Both close as structure, proven by tests, with their live halves named honestly.

## The general binding

`lib/connections/connection-credential.ts` — `resolveConnectionCredential(client, projectId, capability)` generalizes the three-step binding every provider shares: route the capability to exactly one authorized connection (or a named refusal), read that connection's `secret_reference`, dereference it server-side. Provider wrappers exist so call sites name what they ask for, but none can shortcut a step. `deployment-credential.ts` becomes a thin wrapper over it; its four tests pass unchanged.

## Row 4 — Supabase databases

`resolveDatabaseCredential(client, projectId, "read" | "migrate")` routes `database.read` / `database.migrate`. Proven: two projects resolve two Supabase connections to two different credentials in one process, and **read access never implies migrate** — schema changes are the higher privilege, and inferring it from read authorization would be the router guessing. Honestly noted in the scorecard: nothing in the tree operates on an external project database yet (the app's own control-plane client is not a workload target) — this is the doorway such a module must use, not one anything walks through today.

## Row 29 — graph-node identity

`lib/graph/connection-bridge.ts` routes a MODEL node's `inference.advisory` identity through the router. DETERMINISTIC and ANCHOR nodes **provably never touch the registry** — the test asserts the client is not called — mirroring `assertNodeMayCallProvider` on the provider side. Kept separate from the deliberately pure `provider-bridge.ts` because provider selection and identity selection are different decisions.

## Verification

- `connection-credential.test.ts`: 5 new tests (two-databases proof, read≠migrate, MODEL routing, non-MODEL never consults, legacy transparency).
- `deployment-credential.test.ts` + `deploy-vercel.test.ts`: unchanged behavior through the refactor, 30/30.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint 0 errors. No migration; pins and runbook untouched.

## Score movement

Phase 2D: **≈79% → ≈81%**, and structurally complete: **23 PASS · 12 PARTIAL · 0 ABSENT · 1 BLOCKED**. Every remaining gap is a live half (second real account, real Vercel/Supabase connection rows, a first live graph run, the 2A execution switch — all owner decisions or owner-blocked) or the ambient-worker-session rows, whose resolution is a worker-architecture decision rather than a missing binding.

## Risk

GREEN: TypeScript-only, additive, no schema change; the deployment path is a behavior-preserving refactor proven by its unchanged tests.

body:
Six code scanning alerts covering DOM-based XSS and cleartext storage of sensitive data in `localStorage`. All user-controlled values that were being interpolated directly into `innerHTML` are now HTML-escaped, and phone numbers are no longer persisted in browser storage. ## Changes ### Cleartext PII storage (`Avery/memory.js`) - Removed `phone` field from the object written to `localStorage` in `saveCustomerProfile()` ### DOM XSS — chat message (`backup_pre_reorg/script.js`) - Added `escapeHtml()` helper; applied to chat message text before `innerHTML` injection ### DOM XSS — request list template (`backup_pre_reorg/script.js`, `js/script.js`) - All user-sourced request fields (`company`, `contact`, `service`, `budget`, `description`, `email`, `message`, `priority`, `status`, `createdBy`, `requestType`) now passed through `escapeHtml()` before being interpolated into `innerHTML` templates ### DOM XSS — tracking status page (`pages/tracking-status.html`) - Added inline `escapeHtml()`; applied to `trackingId`, `status`, `pickupAddress`, `deliveryAddress`, `serviceLevel` ### DOM XSS — pickup confirmation (`js/pickup.js`) - Added `escapeHtml()`; applied to tracking number, request ID, addresses, and the Google Maps URL in the confirmation template **Example of the pattern applied throughout:** ```js // Before container.innerHTML = `

${trackingId}

${status}

`; // After container.innerHTML = `

${escapeHtml(trackingId)}

${escapeHtml(status)}

`; ``` No false positives — all 6 alerts were genuine vulnerabilities.

author: ackey1007fw-coder
body:
最新 `origin/main`（`56ae5f9`）から新規ブランチ。着手前に前提を確認済み: `api/mily-radio-status.js` / `src/data/radio.ts` / `TodayDashboard.tsx` / `api/mily-schedule.js` すべて存在（PR #11・#8）。

**最重要原則の実装**: 「予定開始から3時間以内」だけでは絶対に「配信中」と表示しません。本物の「ただいまSHOWROOMで配信中！」は **status API の `is_live === true` を取得できたときだけ**です。profile の `current_live_started_at` / `started_at` / `live_id` / `is_onlive` から LIVE を推測しません（テストで担保）。`next_live` と AGE schedule JSON は予定専用です。

## 1. 共有 room resolver — `server/mily-showroom.js`

`resolveMilyRoom()` / `fetchShowroomStatus()` / `fetchNextLive()` を提供。`api/mily-schedule.js` はこれを利用する形に変更し、**既存 export は再エクスポートで完全維持**（probe / watch / 既存テストが壊れないことをテストで検証）。

Codex 指摘の反映:

| 指摘 | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| `/r/<key>` も最初の一致で即採用しない | key 候補・id 候補を**すべて**本人確認してから判定 |
| 一意のときだけ採用 | `pickUniqueRoom()` が roomId で重複排除し、**1件のときのみ**返す |
| 複数一致は不採用 | 本人名の room が2つ以上なら曖昧として `null` |
| 未解決結果を6時間キャッシュしない | 成功（本人確認済み）だけ 6h キャッシュ。**未解決・失敗は一切キャッシュしない** |
| HTTP 失敗をキャッシュしない | 同上（次回すぐ再試行できる） |
| env fallback も本人確認 | `MILY_SHOWROOM_ROOM_ID` も profile 照会 → 本人名検証 → `pickUniqueRoom` を通す |

room ID はコードにも UI にも新規ハードコードしていません（テストで `573253` / `circle2026_0734` の混入を検知）。

## 2. `/api/mily-live` 仕様

schedule（分単位）と live（数十秒）でキャッシュ要件が違うため分離。`/api/mily-schedule` にライブ判定を混ぜていません（テストで `is_live` 非混入を検証）。

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "roomUrl": "...",
  "live": { "state": "live|offline|unknown", "liveId": null, "startedAt": null, "observedAt": "ISO" },
  "next": { "state": "scheduled|none|unknown", "at": "ISO" }
}
```

- **live 判定は `status.is_live` のみ**。取得失敗 / 不正JSON / 型不一致 / **応答 room_id が本人 room と不一致** → `unknown`
- `unknown` を offline にも live にも変換しない
- `next_live` の epoch は**秒・ミリ秒の両方を安全に正規化**して ISO で返す（UI 側で `"8/16(日) 20:30〜"` のような文字列を正規表現解析しない設計）
- `Cache-Control: s-maxage=12, stale-while-revalidate=12` / AbortController + 8秒 timeout / **GET・OPTIONS 以外は 405**

## 3. poll / stale 失効設計

`src/lib/realtimeStore.ts` + `src/lib/useMilyRealtimeStatus.ts`。ActivityBanner と TodayDashboard が**別々に poll しません**（モジュールスコープの store を共有）。

- 初回即時取得 → **前回完了後に次回を予約**（`setInterval` の無条件連打をしない）
- 進行中の fetch があれば join（重複 fetch 禁止）
- hidden 中は停止、`visibilitychange` / `focus` / `online` で即取得
- ライブは 60秒間隔・ラジオは 180秒間隔
- **`observedAt` が90秒以上古い LIVE は `unknown` へ失効**。API 障害時に前回の「配信中！」を残しません（取得失敗時は値ごと破棄）

## 4. `useStreamSchedule` 改善

モジュールスコープの Promise を永続保持していた問題を修正。**5分 TTL・成功だけキャッシュ**し、失敗はキャッシュしないので次回利用時に再試行できます。TodayDashboard / StreamSchedule の既存表示は維持。予定由来の「配信中の時間帯」と、実ライブの「ただいまSHOWROOMで配信中」は**別物として明確に分離**（テストで担保）。

## 5. ラジオ状態の分離

`/api/mily-radio-status` と `src/data/radio.ts` を source of truth として利用（再実装なし）。

- 番組状態: `PROGRAM_WINDOW` / `PROGRAM_TODAY` / `IDLE` / `UNKNOWN`
- 本人出演: `APPEARANCE_CONFIRMED` / `LISTED_PERSONALITY` / `UNKNOWN`
- `milyAppearanceConfirmed` は現状 null のため、**「みりぃ出演中！」等は表示しません**（番組が放送中である、までしか言わない）

## 6-9. ActivityBanner / 優先順位 / 文言

`src/components/ActivityBanner.tsx` を skip link の後・Header の前に配置（**非 sticky / 非 fixed**、MobileActionDock と非競合）。状態決定は純粋関数 `deriveBannerState()` に分離。

優先順位: **1.** SHOWROOM_LIVE → **2.** RADIO_PROGRAM_WINDOW → **3.** 今日の未来予定のうち開始が早い方 → **4.** 同時刻は SHOWROOM → **5.** NONE。SHOWROOM が `unknown` のときはライブ扱いせずラジオ予定を出します。**開始時刻を過ぎても実ライブ未確認なら「配信中」へ昇格しません**（未来時刻のみ表示）。

## 10. TodayDashboard の重複抑制

ActivityBanner が同じ配信（実ライブ / 同一 slot）を出している間は、TodayDashboard の「次回配信」行を出しません。両者は同じ store と同じ `deriveBannerState` を参照するので、構造は複雑になっていません。

## 11-12. デザイン / Accessibility

SHOWROOM LIVE のみ赤系、SHOWROOM 予定は sage、FM は apricot と識別。1行・`min-h-11`・320px でも横スクロールなし。pulse は LIVE のドットのみ＋`motion-safe:` 限定。**色だけで状態を伝えない**よう「配信中 / 放送中 / 予定」のテキストラベルを併記。`role="status"` `aria-live="polite"` `aria-atomic="true"`、focus 移動なし、外部リンクは `rel="noopener noreferrer"` ＋「新しいタブで開きます」。

## 14. 実ネットワーク probe 結果

[Actions run](https://github.com/ackey1007fw-coder/mily-fan-site/actions/runs/31914219508)（2026-08-15T23:14 UTC = 8/16 08:14 JST 実測）:

```
1. resolveMilyRoom → roomId 573253 / circle2026_0734
   roomName: 🔥2次最終日🩵三橋莉子🍅✨ #ミスサークル2026   ← 本人名で検証
   source: entry-page / sns: x・instagram・tiktok（mily 名義のみ）
2. SHOWROOM status → { state: "offline", liveId: null, startedAt: null }
   （is_live が false を返したので offline。unknown ではない）
3. next_live → { state: "scheduled", at: "2026-08-16T11:30:00.000Z" }
   （= JST 8/16 20:30。epoch を ISO へ正規化できている）
4. /api/mily-live → ok:true, live.state "offline", observedAt 付き
5. /api/mily-radio-status → todayScheduled:true, inScheduledWindow:false,
   onAirConfirmed:false, milyAppearanceConfirmed:null（日曜の放送前）
```

実測時点の期待表示: 実ライブ offline かつラジオ 10:00 開始前 → **RADIO_PROGRAM_TODAY**（「今日10:00〜 みりぃの担当番組『湘南シーサイドサークル』」）。ラジオ 10:00 のほうが SHOWROOM 20:30 より早いため、優先順位ロジックどおりです。

room ID はこの報告にのみ記載し、コードには固定していません。

## 13. テスト結果

`pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm test`（**151件 pass**、うち新規34件）/ `pnpm build` / `pnpm guard` すべて成功。

SHOWROOM: is_live true / false / 欠落 / 不正型 / profile 専用フィールドから推測しない / 候補0・1・複数 / 別人 room / env fallback の別人拒否 / 失敗を非キャッシュ / next_live 秒 epoch・ミリ秒 epoch・null・不正値。
poll: 90秒で LIVE 失効 / 重複 fetch しない / 完了後にのみ次回予約 / 失敗時に前回値を破棄 / hidden・visibilitychange・focus・online の結線。
Radio: NOW ON AIR 確認済み / 時間帯のみ / 当日開始前 / 非放送日 / 取得失敗で放送中と断定しない / 本人出演を断定しない。
優先順位: LIVE×window / 予定×window / 予定×予定（早い方）/ 同時刻は SHOWROOM / unknown×ラジオ予定 / 開始時刻超過を昇格しない。
JST: UTC 日付変更またぎ / 年越し。
UI: 配置（skip link 後・Header 前）/ 非 sticky / role=status / 色以外の状態ラベル / reduced motion / room ID 非露出 / TodayDashboard の重複抑制 / poll 共有 / schedule API の export 維持。

## Vercel Preview

PR 作成後に Vercel bot が Preview URL をコメントします（`/api/mily-live` で実レスポンスを確認できます）。

## Codex review

レビュー要求（`@codex review`）はオーナーが投稿します。エージェントは投稿しません。
接続エラーはレビュー成功として扱いません。

author: guidoginesi
body:
Primer tramo del agente que va a proponer respuestas a las consultas: traer el manual y decidir qué parte de él se le puede mostrar a un colaborador.

## El problema

El Manual RRHH de Pow son 165 secciones en un Google Doc. **Mezcla lo que le corresponde al colaborador con material interno**, y las tres secciones más largas son justamente las sensibles:

| Sección | Tamaño |
|---|---|
| Involuntaria (despido) | ~4.800 tokens |
| Protocolo de Violencia Laboral | ~2.100 |
| Sanciones Disciplinarias | ~2.000 |

Más los estándares de compensación, el bono por performance y el presupuesto de RRHH. Un agente con el manual entero puede citarle a alguien las bandas salariales.

## Cómo sincroniza

Un Apps Script pegado al documento (`google-addon/manual.gs`) empuja las secciones a `POST /api/addon/manual`, con el `ADDON_SECRET` que ya usa el add-on de salas — no hace falta cargar nada nuevo en Vercel.

Se empuja desde el Doc en vez de leerlo desde la app para no montar una service account de Google ni tener que publicar un documento que tiene el procedimiento de despido adentro. De yapa, el script lee la estructura real de encabezados y no un renderizado en texto.

Cada importación es un diff: nuevas, modificadas, jubiladas. **Lo que desaparece se jubila, no se borra** — si una respuesta citó una sección, hay que poder explicar de dónde salió.

## La marca de audiencia

Es lo que hace que esto sea seguro de conectar a un agente:

- Cada sección **nace en `SIN_DEFINIR` y no se cita hasta que una persona la habilite**. Falla cerrado: lo que el Doc sume mañana tampoco se cita solo.
- **Sobrevive a las reimportaciones.** Se decide 141 veces; no se puede perder porque alguien corrigió una coma.
- Si el texto cambia después de revisarse, la sección **vuelve a pedir revisión** (`actualizado_at` > `audiencia_definida_at`).

## La pantalla

`/admin/configuracion/manual`, con card en Configuración. Sin módulo nuevo.

Las 141 secciones agrupadas en 44 capítulos. **"Aceptar la propuesta" trabaja por capítulo respetando las excepciones**: en *Bajas de Personal* manda renuncia a colaborador y despido a solo HR en una sola acción. Así la revisión son ~44 decisiones y no 141.

Cada fila muestra la propuesta **y el porqué**, para que la decisión se discuta en la pantalla y no haya que abrir el código.

## La propuesta que trae

91 al colaborador, 47 internas, 3 sin regla (secciones vacías). El criterio: **se cita lo que le da derechos o instrucciones al colaborador; se guarda lo que describe cómo HR decide sobre él.**

De ahí las dos decisiones que van contra la intuición:
- **Renuncia sí, despido no.** Cómo renunciar es algo que puede preguntar; el procedimiento de despido es de una decisión que lo tiene de objeto.
- **El protocolo de violencia laboral es del colaborador**, con formulario de denuncia incluido. Un protocolo que la gente no puede leer no protege a nadie.

Tres quedaron opinables y las cerré por defecto porque es más fácil abrir después que desdecirse: *Incrementos de Sueldo*, *Bono anual por performance* y *Estándares de compensación*.

## Estado

- Migración **ya aplicada** en producción (`manual_sections`, `manual_imports`).
- Las 141 secciones **ya cargadas** con la propuesta, todas en `SIN_DEFINIR`.
- Typecheck y build limpios. API gated: 401 sin sesión en GET y PATCH.
- Verificado en local por Guido.

## Después de mergear

1. Instalar el Apps Script en el Doc (Extensiones → Apps Script), con `APP_URL` y `ADDON_SECRET` en las propiedades del script.
2. Revisar las 141 en la pantalla.

author: xiaoyxue
body:
## Summary

**#247 S7** — the PBR pass reads the mesh's own vertices instead of a second copy.

`PbrVertex` was `{ position, normal, uv, tangent }` — 48 bytes, of which **20 (position + uv) re-stored what the mesh's `Vertex` buffer already held**. Every mesh carried **80 B/vertex across two buffers**, and the two records collided on `@location(1)`: *color* in `mesh.wgsl`, *normal* in `pbr.wgsl`.

Split the **derived** half off rather than duplicating the **authored** one:

```
BEFORE                                        AFTER
pbr:  slot 0  PbrVertex   pos·normal·uv·tan   pbr:  slot 0  Vertex        ← the same buffer
              (0,1,2,7)              48 B                   pos·color·uv (0,1,2)      32 B
      slot 1  InstanceRaw (3..6)     64 B           slot 1  InstanceRaw  (3..6)       64 B
                                                    slot 2  ShadingVertex normal(8) tangent(9)  28 B
80 B / vertex, position+uv stored twice        60 B / vertex, stored once
```

Slot 0 is now literally the buffer the filled, wireframe, textured, shadow and picking pipelines already read.

## 📈 Measurement (the issue's own rule)

RTX 3090, **release**, 512×512, 600 frames, medians of 5 trials, **alternating prebuilt before/after binaries in one session** so GPU clock drift hits both arms (a rebuild-between-runs A/B was discarded — its variance exceeded the effect):

| meshes (3 185-vertex spheres, all `Shaded`) | before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.314 ms | 0.320 ms |
| 16 | 0.407 ms | 0.407 ms |
| 64 | 0.692 ms | 0.680 ms |

The extra `set_vertex_buffer` per shaded draw costs **nothing measurable**. The win is memory, and it is exact rather than benchmarked:

| | per vertex | 34 817-vertex bunny |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 80 B | 2.656 MiB |
| after | **60 B** | **1.992 MiB** (−25 %) |

The harness was temporary and is not committed.

## Correctness

All **7 goldens bit-identical**, including both PBR tone-map variants and the environment-light sky/reflection one — the shading math is untouched; only where its inputs come from changed. That is the check that matters here: normals and tangents moved buffers *and* shader locations.

Not done (and why, from the review): **lazy** derivation of the shading buffer. `MeshStore` deliberately drops the CPU `Mesh` after upload, so deferring would mean retaining it — ~32 B/vertex of RAM to save 28 B/vertex of VRAM, only for never-shaded meshes.

## ✅ Verification

| Gate | 🪟 Windows | 🐧 Linux/Nix |
|------|:---:|:---:|
| 🎨 `cargo fmt --all --check`                     | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 📎 clippy workspace `-D warnings`                | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🕸️ clippy wasm32 (lib)                           | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🧪 `cargo test --workspace` (221 core + …)       | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🔀 `decoder_parity` (2)                          | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🖼️ `golden_render` (7/7, GPU, **bit-identical**) | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🧪 GPU-gated `trd-core -- --ignored` (24)        | 🤝 | ✅ |
| 🌐 tsc / biome (`nix flake check`)               | 🤝 | ✅ |

## 🤝 Handoff — 🪟 Windows

- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` · `cargo test --workspace`
- [ ] `cargo test -p trd-core -- --ignored` (24 + 7 goldens — the PBR ones are the load-bearing check)
- [ ] `examples\render.ps1 -CLI -Pbr -Metallic 0.0 -Roughness 0.35 -Env assets\envmap\uffizi-large.hdr …` on the coca-can, and `cargo run -p trd-gui-app -- --pbr --env …` — normal-mapped shading is what moved slots
- [ ] browser: `-Web -CanvasRenderer -Pbr` — the wasm path compiles the same WGSL with the new locations

> Expected: all green, goldens bit-identical; the can still reads as a deep-red dielectric with sharp label normals.

Closes the last slice of #247. Follows #255 (S5), #253 (S6), #252 (S4), #250 (S3), #249 (S2), #248 (S1).

author: aalonx
body:
The greeter's locale-bar capsule had its keyboard icon jammed against the left cap.

## `padding: 4px` is not the bug

4 is the **derived** concentric inset — outer pill `32/2 = 16` minus the dropdown button's clamped pill `24/2 = 12` — and it is exactly right for the two dropdowns inside, whose hover fill has to sit evenly within the outer pill.

It is the wrong number for the only child in that capsule that **paints no fill**. A dropdown's glyphs sit `4 + 8 = 12px` in, behind its own `padding: 3px 8px`; the bare icon's ink sat at 4, with nothing between it and the cap's curve. Three times the clearance on one end.

The 8px goes on the **icon**, not on the container's `padding-left`: the container's number is derived and correct, and putting the correction on the bare child means reordering that row cannot lose it.

## Measured, not eyeballed

`scripts/dev/lock-probe.js` grew a **LOCALE BAR** block — the capsule and each child's box, where the ink starts and ends, and a `-locale.png` crop of the capsule.

⚠️ That crop is what makes the photometry honest. Measured out of the full-surface PNG, the **scrim's gradient** sits under the capsule and every luminance threshold lies about where the ink is. Crop the widget, then measure.

| | ink ← left cap | ink → right cap |
|---|---|---|
| before | **4px** | 17px |
| after | **12px** | 17px |

## Why 12 and not 17

The right end measures 17px and that number was deliberately **not** matched. GTK's `▾` does not fill the padding it sits in, so 17 is an accident of a glyph rather than a chosen inset; aiming at it would push a dense 12px square out to where a light triangle happens to land.

What 12 **is** derived from: the clearance the ink already has from the *straight* edges. A 12px glyph in a 32px capsule sits `(32 − 12) / 2 = 10px` off top and bottom — so 12 at the cap is marginally more at the curve, which is what a cap wants, since the arc falls away above and below the ink's own height.

## Both surfaces looked at

Greeter-only widget, but the stylesheet is shared, so the lockscreen was rendered too: it builds no locale bar, and its card (280×219) and power bar (279×32) are unchanged.

## Skill

`design-system.md` gets the general rule next to the inset formula — which presumes a child that *has* a radius. Bare ink is not covered by it, the correction belongs on the ink, and the opposite end's measured clearance is not the target. The `lock-probe.js` section records the new block and the scrim trap.

author: tassoossat
body:
E7.6 - a new room-derive tool: click inside walls already drawn and get their enclosed floor + ceiling, the opposite direction from room-stamp (which generates a brand new rooms own walls).

Why this scope - skipped E7.4 (opening tools) since door generation was just explicitly taken out of scope for wall-brush this session; E7.6 does not actually need doors to function (it derives floor/ceiling from a closed wall loop, not from openings), so it was reordered ahead per the owners own call.

Algorithm - every wall (including corner-welded and crossing-split ones from VTT-WALL-CORNER-WELD) is an edge between its two bottom corner nodes. Face-tracing a planar graph is the standard way to extract bounded regions from a straight-line graph, but getting its winding convention right by construction is easy to get backwards - sidestepped that by trying both directions of every wall as a starting edge and keeping whichever closed loop actually contains the click point (point-in-polygon), picking the smallest if more than one qualifies.

What changed
- room-derive-tool.ts - the algorithm (wallSpans/buildAdjacency/traceFace/pointInPolygon/polygonArea) plus the tool itself, onClick only
- tool-types.ts/tool-registry.ts/construction-hotbar.tsx/tabletop-entry.tsx - wired in exactly the pattern every other tool already uses
- No Rust change - reuses the existing generic addSurface path via applyIrregularTerrainPatch, same as the irregular-terrain tool

Scope decision, documented inline - no previewFor. ConstructionTool.previewFor never receives a ToolContext (every other tools ghost is pure pointer geometry), but this tools geometry is a live graph query. A hover ghost is a real, worthwhile follow-up, but it needs widening that signature first - a cross-cutting change touching every tool, not scoped to this one.

Verification
- New test/room-derive-tool.test.mjs (3 tests): a closed 4-wall square derives the correct floor/ceiling node cycles, a click outside any wall loop derives nothing, an open (unclosed) wall chain never derives a room even right next to a click
- node --experimental-strip-types --test test/architecture-boundaries.test.mjs test/room-derive-tool.test.mjs - 7/7 passing
- tsc - no new errors in any file this task touched (same pre-existing @grafting/* module-resolution gap as VTT-WALL-CORNER-WELD, confirmed unrelated)

Part of the wider close-out-Epic-7 plan - VTT-WALL-CORNER-WELD (E7.3) merged as #115. Next up per the plan: VTT-ROOF-RESEARCH (E7.7, a research/decision step, no code) or VTT-STAIRS-TOOL (E7.8), to be decided with the owner.

author: ibboabdoli-ai
body:
## Graph diagnosis
- Entry node: Super Admin Company Directory manual low-confidence refresh.
- Immediate failure: after a successful batch, the client can receive a rejected Server Action request and falls into the generic fatal catch path.
- Root-cause path: browser batch loop → Server Action invocation → full candidate scan → Official Facts/publication gate → route refresh. The UI was also issuing an extra `router.refresh()` after every batch and the helper rescanned the full backlog twice per batch.
- Preserved invariants: Super Admin authorization, 95% threshold, Bolagsverket pacing/429 cooldown, fail-closed publication gate, no direct publication writes.

## Patch
- Retry transient Server Action failures with bounded backoff before stopping.
- Remove per-batch route refresh; refresh once when the run finishes/stops.
- Reuse the already-loaded candidate snapshot to calculate remaining work instead of running the same full low-confidence scan twice per batch.
- Add regression contract coverage.

## Blast radius
Small: manual Super Admin Directory refresh only. No auth, schema, cron, publication-gate, billing, or tenant behavior changes.

## Validation
CI/CodeQL/Build/E2E required before merge.

body:
## Bug

A plugin kernel can eagerly materialize `Enumerable.Range(0, int.MaxValue).ToFrozenDictionary(...)` during static initialization. The analyzer accepts this compiler-clean shape without `DBXK001`, allowing caller-sized host-heap allocation before sandbox memory, fuel, and audit controls apply.

## Red test

Adds `tests/DotBoxD.Kernels.Tests/PluginAnalyzer/Core/Security/Reachability/Allocation/Surprise/Linq/PluginAnalyzerForbiddenApiEnumerableToFrozenDictionaryReachabilityTests.cs`. It compiles an `IEventKernel<string>` retaining a static `FrozenDictionary<int, int>` materialized with `ToFrozenDictionary()` and requires a `DBXK001` diagnostic naming `System.Linq.Enumerable.ToFrozenDictionary`.

## Expected failure

The focused test currently fails at `Assert.Single` because the analyzer reports zero `DBXK001` diagnostics for the `ToFrozenDictionary` invocation.

## Duplicate check

- Search terms: `[surprise-red-test]`, `ToFrozenDictionary`, `FrozenDictionary`, `DBXK001`, `ForbiddenCollectionCapacityPolicy`, `System.Collections.Frozen`, `LINQ materialization`, and `allocation`.
- Open PRs inspected: `#1113` (`ToFrozenSet`), `#1109` (`ToList`), and all open bug-labeled/red-test PRs; none covers unbounded `Enumerable.ToFrozenDictionary` materialization.
- Recent open `sweep:lens` comments inspected: `#145`, `#146`, `#148`, and `#149`; `#145` contains this run's `ToFrozenDictionary` dispatch, and no earlier cross-lens dispatch overlaps it.

## Validation

- Passed: `dotnet restore DotBoxD.slnx`
- Passed: `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true dotnet build DotBoxD.slnx -c Release --no-restore`
- Failed as expected: `dotnet test tests/DotBoxD.Kernels.Tests/DotBoxD.Kernels.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PluginAnalyzerForbiddenApiEnumerableToFrozenDictionaryReachabilityTests"`

No production implementation changes are included.

author: syuya2036
body:
#448 と #446 のうち**方針が固まった 4 件**をまとめて対応する。残りは各 issue に残す。

Closes #457

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **スタック PR。** base は `main` ではなく #445（`claude/workflow-retention-gc`）。`gc.rs` と migration 0064 の上にしか載らないため。マージ順は **#439 → #445 → 本 PR**（`ops.rs` の `resume_failed` は #439 も触るので競合し得る）。
>
> **0064 を適用済みの開発 DB は作り直しが必要。** 本 PR 系列で 0064 のコメントを直しており、sqlx の checksum 検証が `VersionMismatch(64)` になる（0064 は未マージなので本番影響なし）。

## 1. GC を `workflow.enabled` から独立して起動する（#448-1・実バグ）

`HistoryGcWorker` の起動も日次投入も `spawn_workflow_runtime` の中にあり、`workflow.enabled=false` で `wire_workflow` が早期 return するとどちらも動かなかった。過去にワークフローを使っていたデプロイが機能を無効化すると、**既存履歴が保持期限を過ぎても永久に残る**。保持はプライバシー/コンプライアンス側の義務で、「新規 run を受け付けるか」とは独立した責務。

日次投入を `HistoryGcWorker` のループへ移し、ワーカーを enabled ゲートの手前で spawn する。投入判定は `maintenance_schedule` の `FOR UPDATE` ＋ 24h チェックで多重起動安全なので、スケジューラの単一リーダーである必要がない。tick との結合も減る。

あわせて `purge_expired_history`（全テナント横断）を `pub(crate)` に落とし、公開入口を対象テナントが引数に現れる `purge_tenant_history` だけにした。保守ジョブに `AuthContext` は載らない（実行主体が存在しない）ので、境界をコメントではなく可視性で担保する。

## 2. テナント保持日数の設定経路（#448-2）

`tenant.workflow_retention_days` は列だけあって読み書きの経路が無く、raw SQL 以外に既定の 90 日を変える手段が無かった。`PUT /admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/workflow-retention` を `set_tenant_autonomous_policy` と同型（provisioner トークン・`validate_tenant_id`・`TenantStore` のセッター）で追加する。

範囲は 1〜3650 日。**下限が 1 日でよいのは** `effect_journal` の削除条件が所有 run 行の不在であり、run 行は terminal になるまで消えないため（保持を `run_timeout_sec` の上限 30 日より短くしても実行中 run の副作用記録は消えない）。上限は打ち間違いの検出用で、90 のつもりで 9000 と入れると GC が事実上無効化される。

## 3. index/vacuum の運用手順を集約する（#448-5）

「デプロイ前に手で `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` する」手順が 2 本、`VACUUM FULL` 手順が 1 本あり、いずれも migration コメントにしかなかった（＝その migration を読んだ人にしか届かない）。`docs/guides/db-maintenance.md` へ集約する。

## 4. resume の猶予を `lease_secs` から導出する（#446-1）

固定 35 秒は `WorkerConfig.lease_secs` の既定 30 を前提にしていたが、設定値なので 120 等にできる。その場合、旧 worker が有効リースを保持したままの 85 秒間に別 worker が再 claim できる。fencing があるのでデータは壊れないが「外部副作用を併走させない」という猶予の意図は破れる。

`RunStore` に構築時 `lease_secs` を持たせる（引数追加ではない）。この猶予は呼び出しごとの都合ではなく store が守る耐久プロトコルの不変条件（猶予 > リース）なので、1 箇所で担保できる形にする。

## 検証

Docker が無い環境のため compose 起動は不可。代わりに **axum ルータを通る HTTP テスト**で新エンドポイントを検証した（`auth_flow.rs` の `admin_tenant_lifecycle_end_to_end` を拡張）。UI 変更は無し。

| ゲート | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | ✅ |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` | ✅ |
| `check-file-size.sh` / `check-migration-versions.sh` / compose port | ✅ |
| `cargo test --workspace`（実 PG16・新規 DB） | ✅ 41 バイナリ緑。`shiki-chat autonomous_it` のみ **MinIO 未起動**で失敗（`create_bucket: dispatch failure`・本 diff と無関係） |
| `pnpm install` / `gen:api` / `lint` / `next build` | ✅ |
| `cargo machete` / `cargo deny` | ローカル未インストール。**本 diff は `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` を一切変更していない**ので論理的に無影響（CI で実走） |

新エンドポイントの HTTP 層検証:

- `204` で値が永続する
- 範囲外 `0` / `-1` / `3651` と桁溢れ `4000000000` / `-4000000000` がすべて `400`
- 拒否されたリクエストが既存値を壊さない
- provisioner トークン要求は既存の `admin_requires_provisioner_azp` と `route_table` の宣言的 PEP が担保

`export-openapi` で新規 path・schema・`provisioner_token` security の登録を確認。

## パフォーマンス

**A. 静的観点（独立エージェント）で P1 が 1 件**。journal GC の削除条件は「期限切れ かつ 所有 run が不在」なので、生存 run に属する期限切れ行は消せないまま index の先頭に残る。カーソルが無いと毎バッチその先頭群を頭から舐め直し、1 GC の総走査が O(消せない行数 × バッチ数) に膨らむ。カーソル化した。

実測（PG16・生存 run 5 万・消せない journal 20 万行・消せる孤児 1 万件）:

| | 1 バッチの実行時間 | バッファ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| カーソル無し | 2,128 ms | 808,868 |
| カーソル有り（2 バッチ目以降） | **82 ms** | **1,170** |

**B. 相対回帰**: `resume_failed` の SQL はプラン不変（PK Index Scan・`$3` バインドで interval も正しく 125s）。

**C. 絶対観測**: 日次投入の判定は 3 バッファ / 0.055 ms。投入頻度は「リーダーが 5 秒ごと」→「全レプリカが 60 秒ごと」に変わり、12 レプリカ未満なら総クエリ数は**減る**。

## ドキュメント整合

- **issue 番号の取り違えを修正**（#439→#438・#445→#444・#443→#442）。リポジトリの慣行は issue 番号
- `db-maintenance.md` に前提 migration（0062/0063 は未マージ）の但し書き
- `engine.md` §11.4 に resume 猶予の不変条件を追記（正本に記述が無かった）
- 「`run_timeout_sec` 30 日 < 保持 90 日だから衝突しない」を、保持が 1 日まで縮む前提へ更新（`engine.md` §12.2・`gc.rs`）
- `wire_workflow` の rustdoc に「GC は enabled に依らず起動する」を追記
- `DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS` を re-export し、API 側の既定 `30` リテラルを単一ソース化
- `tenant-ops.md` に保持期間設定の項と `db-maintenance.md` への相互リンク
- 掲載した SQL はすべて実 PG16 で実行して確認（`job_queue` に `last_error` 列は無く DLQ 側にあることも実行して判明・修正済み）

## 独立レビュー

会話文脈を持たない 4 エージェント（不変条件/認可・パフォーマンス・ドキュメント整合・正確性）に diff だけを渡した。**P1 認可バイパス・テナント越境は 0 件。**

**対応した指摘**

| 指摘 | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| journal GC がバッチごとに再走査（実測 P1） | カーソル化（上記） |
| resume 猶予が resume 時刻起算で、旧 worker 死亡後も満額待つ | `greatest(now(), updated_at + 猶予)` で cancel 時刻起算に。回帰テスト追加 |
| 1 テナントの GC 失敗が全テナントを止める | テナント単位で継続し、失敗件数を `GcReport` に載せて最後に Err へ畳む |
| 保持日数の範囲検証が呼び出し側の約束 | setter 内で検証。`2_000_000_000` が CHECK を通り `timestamp out of range` で GC 全体を落とすことを実測 |
| 桁溢れが 422 になりドキュメントの「範囲外は 400」と食い違う | `i64` で受けてハンドラで 400 に畳む |
| migration 0064 の編集は checksum を壊す | 編集を 0064 を導入した #445 側へ移し、本 PR は 0064 に触らない |
| 日次投入テストが `FOR UPDATE` を外しても通る | 並行呼び出し込みに統合。台帳とキューを先頭で初期化して再実行可能にした |

**見送った指摘（根拠）**

- **`purge_tenant_history` を `pub(crate)` にせよ（本番呼び出し元が 0 件）** — これは「破壊的操作は対象テナントを引数に持つ」という本 PR の方針そのものの体現で、テナント横断版を閉じた代わりの入口。テスト専用機能フラグを 1 本のために足すより、テナント境界が型に現れる公開 API を 1 つ持つ方が設計として一貫する。
- **`RunStore::new` の `lease_secs` を必須引数にせよ** — 呼び出し 49 箇所中 47 がテストで、全テストに定数を書かせる割に本番構築点は 1 箇所しかない。現構築点は `WorkerConfig` と同じ `config.workflow.lease_secs` を渡しており不整合は無い。加えて cancel 時刻起算にしたことで、猶予不足の窓自体が縮んだ。
- **`wire_workflow` の中に保守ランタイムを置くのは責務違反** — 独立性はコメントだけが支えている、という指摘は正しい。ただし `main.rs` は無条件に呼んでおり、切り出しは `wire_maintenance` という新しい配線層を作る判断になるため #448 に残す。

**フォローアップ issue へ回すもの**（PR 作成後に切る）

- テナント設定変更（`workflow-retention` と既存の `autonomous-policy` の両方）に `audit_log` が残らない（NFR-6）。不可逆な削除の引き金なので追跡できるべきだが、既存エンドポイントにも同じ穴があり、両方まとめて直すのが筋
- GC の visibility timeout heartbeat（#448-3）。カーソル化で所要時間が桁で縮んだので優先度は下がった。なお「DLQ に落ちると GC が恒久停止」という指摘は**誤り**で、日次投入は前回ジョブの結果を見ないため翌日新しいジョブが積まれる
- 削除対象のあるテナントだけを走査する事前絞り込み（空振り 1 テナントあたり run 側 0.029 ms）

author: iperception
body:
Adds **reading** support for 835 remittance advice: loop resolution, inspector naming, and three balancing checks. No payments table, no CSV export, no Limited Data Set — those are deliberately left for later.

## Why this one does not follow the PACDR pattern

PACDR's rule was *detected → do more, never do differently*, and it held because `005010X298` is structurally the same transaction as the 837P. It does not hold here. A probe of a hand-written 835 through the current build found the tree **actively wrong**, not merely incomplete:

- `LX` opened a group labelled **"Line 1"** — in an 835 it opens loop 2000, a grouping of *claims*.
- `NM1*82` opened **"Rendering provider"** and swallowed both `SVC` loops *and* `PLB`, a transaction-level segment that must never sit inside a claim.

So for an 835 the 837 anchors are switched **off** and replaced, gated on `ST-01` per transaction. What survives from PACDR is the gating discipline: a file with no 835 in it runs exactly the code it ran before, and a mixed interchange resolves each transaction correctly. 835 loop ids are deliberately kept out of `ENTITY_LOOPS`/`ANCHOR_LOOPS` — the omission is load-bearing, and makes the 837 fallback inert by construction.

## The three checks

All warnings, never errors, each standing down rather than guessing when a figure is absent or unreadable.

| Level | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Line | `SVC-02` − adjustments in that 2110 = `SVC-03` |
| Claim | `CLP-03` − every `CAS` on the claim = `CLP-04` |
| Transaction | `BPR-02` = Σ `CLP-04` − Σ `PLB-04` |

**The last one reads backwards on purpose:** a *positive* `PLB-04` *reduces* what the payer pays. It is the line most likely to be "corrected" into a bug, so it carries three separate treatments — a comment at the subtraction, `docs/835-validation.md` explaining why, and a test named for the convention. The test asserts the finding's **detail text**, not just that a finding fires: a flipped sign still produces a finding, only with the wrong number in it, so a pass/fail-only test would not catch the regression. Verified by flipping the sign and watching the suite go red.

Reversals (`CLP-02 = 22`) balance under the same rules with **no `CLP-02` gate anywhere**. The fixture's second claim is a reversal carrying negative amounts throughout.

## Also fixed, found in review

- **A dropped segment.** An 835 `N1` whose qualifier was not `PR`/`PE` returned without pushing a leaf, so the segment vanished from the tree *and* from the interchange's own count — invisible to every existing assertion, since a missing segment breaks no structure. Now falls through to a plain leaf as `NM1` already did, pinned by a test that fails on the one-word revert.
- **The Checks panel** told an 835 user that each claim's `CLM-02` reconciled — on a file with no `CLM` in it — while saying nothing about the three checks that actually ran.
- **The Outline** gave an 835 no per-claim navigation. It matters because the rail also scopes find & replace, and for the legal no-`LX` remittance the whole file collapsed to a single unselectable node.

## Verification

All 8 browser suites and the 11 Python tests pass. Tree 142→167, validate 74→93, deid 123→126, claims 106→108, outline 60→65; `parity` untouched at 77 and unaffected by construction — everything new inside the engine markers is reachable only from `validateDocument`, which parity never calls.

Existing 837P and PACDR assertions are **unchanged** — none was edited to make anything pass.

## Sources

The X12 TR3 is paywalled and was not read, and no companion guide was used for this pass. What is asserted is limited to loop ids, segment ids, element positions and the balancing arithmetic the transaction's own definition implies. Every unconfirmed item is either cut (`Σ SVC-03 = CLP-04`) or stands down (debit and zero-payment transactions). The fixture is wholly invented.

author: fagiteemmanuel4-bit
body:
💡 What: Added composite indexes (`idx_roasts_user_created` and `idx_roasts_ip_user_created`) on the `roasts` table and replaced `date(created_at) = date('now')` with index-friendly `created_at >= date('now')`.

🎯 Why: The previous rate limit and history queries performed un-indexed full table scans because wrapping `created_at` in `date()` prevented SQLite from using indexes. History queries also required creating temporary B-Trees for sorting.

📊 Impact: Converts full table scans (`SCAN roasts`) into O(log N) covering index range searches (`SEARCH roasts USING COVERING INDEX`) and eliminates `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` overhead for user history loading.

🔬 Measurement: Verified with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` in `tests/test_optimization.py` and ran unittest suite.
