body: ## Status: paused, awaiting input This PR is paused per an explicit request to stop further "build from scratch" work until the real Hostinger Horizons source (EVELIA logo, images, sections, original design, React components) is confirmed available. Opening this PR now so the completed work is visible and reviewable, and nothing is lost while we wait. ### What was verified (Phase 1, before any code was written) The repository (`vaiofordigital-byte/Evelia`) was audited exhaustively, more than once, including after this pause request: - All branches (`main` is the only one prior to this PR's branch), all commits (one: "Initial commit"), all refs, forks (none), and sibling repositories on the same GitHub account (none named/described as a Horizons/Evelia export). - The only tracked file before this work began was a one-line `README.md` (`# Evelia`). No `package.json`, no `src/`, no components, no images, no fonts, no PocketBase schema/data — nothing else. This is documented in detail in [`MIGRATION_PLAN.md`](../blob/cursor/evelia-wp-woocommerce-theme-e606/MIGRATION_PLAN.md), written and committed **before** any theme file was created, per the mandatory Phase 1 process. ### What's needed to proceed with a true "convert the original Horizons project" migration Please push the real source into this repository (e.g., to `main` or a new branch) so it can be analyzed and converted per the original brief. Specifically: - The Horizons React/Vite project source (components, pages, styles/design tokens, assets folder). - The EVELIA logo and brand imagery. - Any PocketBase schema/export if the ecommerce data model should be preserved. ### What exists on this branch right now (paused, not merged) Since no source existed, work proceeded on the documented fallback path: a complete, original, production-ready WordPress + WooCommerce theme (`Evelia`) built from scratch, with **zero hardcoded brand identity** — every visual/content element (colors, logo, copy, images, section order) is store-owner-editable via a custom Theme Options screen, specifically so it can absorb the real Horizons design later with minimal rework if/when that source is provided. Highlights: - Full WP theme structure, WooCommerce integration (variable products, related/upsell/cross-sell, reviews, quick view, wishlist), luxury-skincare product fields (ingredients/benefits/how-to-use/skin type/before-after), Arabic RTL support, Saudi Business Verification seal integration. - A dependency-free "Theme Options" admin engine (not the native Customizer) built to handle hundreds of settings without the freezing/lag typical of Customizer-heavy themes. - Verified on a real, disposable WordPress + WooCommerce install (WP-CLI + MariaDB): installed from an actual built zip, activated, browsed every page type and admin screen with `WP_DEBUG_LOG` on — zero PHP notices/warnings/fatals. Passes the official WordPress **Theme Check** plugin. - Full details in [`CHANGELOG.md`](../blob/cursor/evelia-wp-woocommerce-theme-e606/CHANGELOG.md) and [`README.md`](../blob/cursor/evelia-wp-woocommerce-theme-e606/README.md). No further theme-building changes will be made on this branch until the real source is provided and reviewed, or until proceeding with the from-scratch build is explicitly reconfirmed.

author: sehkone
body:
Adds `Validate E2E Run Scope` to the `check` job, after `Validate E2E Leftover Check` and before `Install cargo-audit`, and corrects the two documentation places that said the validator runs in no CI workflow.

`scripts/validate-e2e-run-scope.sh` was the per-run E2E identity's only guard, and nothing but `scripts/preflight/run-all.sh` invoked it — a control that depends on remembering. None of what it asserts is observable from the E2E matrix: each runner gets one run on an empty host, so a derivation that started colliding, a marker that stopped being written, or a sweep that began reaching past the runs it recorded would all leave every arm green.

The step adds no toolchain setup, no service and no cache. The validator redirects its marker directory and its hosts lock into its own `mktemp -d`, and stubs `docker` on `PATH`, so it cannot touch the runner's `/etc/hosts` or anything another job holds.

## Documentation

`docs/en/e2e-ci.md` and `docs/ko/e2e-ci.md` both stated the validator "is a local check ... not run by any CI workflow", and listed it under local-only extras. Those sentences are now false, so each was rewritten to say where it runs and what it needs, and the entry moved from the local-only table into the CI-equivalent one.

No `CHANGELOG.md` entry: CI and test-harness only, so a user of the last release cannot observe it. No Rust code changed and no E2E code path is touched, so the Docker preflight scripts were not run locally — CI's matrix covers them.

## Test plan

- [x] `./scripts/validate-e2e-run-scope.sh` exits 0 on this tree, reporting 45 `ok:` lines, in 3.2s measured on a non-root host — and the same on a detached worktree of `origin/main` (exit 0, 45 `ok:`, 3.4s), which is the clean checkout the issue asks about.
- [x] A break in the guarded behaviour turns the step red, checked on two separate guards and reverted after each, leaving `git status` clean.
    - Hosts lock default in `scripts/impl/lib/run-scope.sh` changed from `/etc/hosts` to a path of the harness's own: exit 1, `FAIL: the default hosts lock is '/tmp/broken-lock' rather than /etc/hosts; a lock at a path of the harness's own can be swapped for another inode between the check and the open, and one under $TMPDIR is not even machine-wide`.
    - Pid-liveness filter dropped from `hosts_lock_label` (`run_pid_is_alive "$pid" || return 0` removed): exit 1, `FAIL: the refusal named a dead run's label as the holder: ... (pid 4194305, a run that was killed)`.
- [x] The `check` job's step order is `... Validate E2E Leftover Check`, `Validate E2E Run Scope`, `Install cargo-audit`, `Run Security Audit`, and the step declares only `run:` — no toolchain setup, service or cache.
- [x] The four validators already in `check` are unchanged, and no job is added or reordered — the workflow diff is three added lines.
- [x] `./scripts/check-docs.sh` passes (`mkdocs build --strict` plus the theme assertions); `markdownlint-cli2` reports 0 issues and `biome ci --error-on-warnings .` is clean.
- [x] No `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
- [x] Full CI passes on this pull request — all 18 checks green. The new step took **2s** on the runner (`Validate E2E Run Scope`, 23:19:01 -> 23:19:03), less than the `Validate E2E Leftover Check` step above it.
- [x] The step runs and passes on a docs-only push. No single run can show this from here — the branch changes `.github/workflows/**`, which the change filter counts as code — so it was checked against two real runs instead of argued from the workflow alone. That the `check` job runs in full on a docs-only push is observed on [run 30968767229](https://github.com/aicers/bootroot/actions/runs/30968767229) (PR #791, which touched only two files under `docs/`): `Change Filter` resolved `docs_only=true`, `Unit & CLI Smoke` and every E2E matrix arm skipped, and `Quality Check` still ran to success with each of its validator steps green. That the new step passes inside that job is observed on this pull request's own run. The step cannot distinguish the two cases: it declares no `if:`, and it reads `scripts/impl/lib/run-scope.sh` and `src/commands/compose_project.rs` out of the full checkout rather than anything about the diff.

Closes #857

author: navigreen311
body:
Measured on every step against real Postgres in CI.

| | failed / 139 |
| --- | --- |
| Postgres, before | **55** |
| Postgres, after | **20** |
| in-memory, before | 27 |
| in-memory, after | **19** |

Postgres now fails nothing the in-memory store passes, bar one test.

## What was wrong

**1. Nothing seeded the foreign-key parents.** The suite was written against a `Map`, which enforces no referential integrity, so no test ever inserted the `users` and `projects` rows its ids referenced — 42 FK violations. The ids are not new: `STUB_OWNER_ID` from the controllers and the deterministic UUIDs from #69. They just needed rows.

**2. Test files ran in parallel against one shared database.** Fine while each suite owns a private `Map` — each worker gets its own module instance. Against Postgres, one file's `beforeEach` cleanup deleted rows another file had created microseconds earlier, and the symptom was a read returning 404 for a row whose write returned 201. Serialised when `DATABASE_URL` is set.

**3. Seventeen async service calls were never awaited.** `sceneService.create`, `shotService.create`, `projectService.create`, `shotService.lock` — the tests read `.id` and `.title` off a Promise and got `undefined`, and fire-and-forget writes had not landed when the request under test arrived. **Eight of the failures previously attributed to the #21 envelope mismatches were this**, which is why in-memory also dropped 27 → 19.

Unhandled rejections had been swallowing real FK errors, so fixing the awaits briefly *raised* the count before the seeding caught up — visible in the run history.

## Three service bugs the Map was hiding

- **`shotService.create` never supplied `shotNumber`**, a required `Int` with no database default. Shot creation against Postgres could not succeed at all. Now derived from the count within the scene, which is the only thing the column can mean.
- **`receiptService` wrote to Postgres and read from the `Map`.** All four read paths queried memory, so a receipt written to the database could never be read back. Invisible without a database, because then both halves used the `Map`.
- **`createReceipt` never wrote `projectId`**, which the in-memory path takes from `details.projectId`. `receipts.project_id` was always NULL, so `getReceiptsByProject` could only return an empty list.

## Two fixture defects

- `scenes-shots.test.ts` uses `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` as its `PROJECT_ID` while other suites use the same UUID as a user id. Different tables, so it needs a row in each.
- `styleRef: 'cinematic-dark'` against `shots.style_ref @db.Uuid` — the same class as #69, on a column the `Map` never type-checked.

## The one remaining Postgres-only failure

`GET /api/v1/receipts/project/:projectId`. `createReceipt` wraps its Prisma call in a bare `catch {}` that falls back to the in-memory store, so when the insert fails the write goes to memory while the read now goes to the database, and the list comes back empty. **The silent catch is the actual defect** — it converts a database error into an invisible divergence between write and read. I did not fix it here because doing so blind would mean guessing at the underlying error rather than measuring it; left on #73 with this diagnosis.

The other 19 are the pre-existing response-envelope mismatches in #21, failing identically in both stores.

## Seeding notes

Raw SQL with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so it works whatever shape the generated client is in and a re-run is free. Two bugs of my own along the way, both now commented in the file: `updated_at` is `@updatedAt`, so the column is NOT NULL with no database default and raw SQL must supply it; and the cleanup must cast the *column* to text, not the literal to uuid, because `receipts.user_id` is TEXT while the rest are `@db.Uuid`.

A failing seed used to abort all twelve suites and leave a report containing zero tests — which reads exactly like a clean pass. It now says what happened.

Closes #73

author: turneraroundauto-hub
body:
## Summary

**Part 1 — overlay self-noise (original commit).** The `?v=16` scroll ground-truth watcher caught nothing on the next real jump; instead the overlay filled with `#marqueeDiag Δy±132.0, input=true` noise. Root cause: `#marqueeDiag` is `position:fixed`, and mobile browsers shift fixed elements as their own address-bar chrome hides/shows during scroll — the Layout Instability observer was watching the whole page, including its own diagnostic panel, and reported that self-repositioning as if it were an app bug. Fixed by filtering out any layout-shift source node that is `#marqueeDiag` itself.

**Part 2 — second video + overlay retention fix (added commit).** A second real screen recording independently reproduced the same finding as an earlier one: a precise **-26px single-frame shift** at ~2.2s after load — same magnitude, same early timing, cross-validated. Re-analysis corrected the earlier characterization: the jump does **not** self-correct, it's a **permanent** offset (checked 50-80 frames past the event in both recordings, no recovery). The wrap-distance theory is ruled out by the numbers (`roloMarqueeOneSetW` ≈ 356px, needs 6-12s to reach at the marquee's speed; both anomalies happen at ~2.2-2.6s).

The real reason neither diagnostic screenshot showed anything: the overlay's single shared 20-entry cap let continuous routine layout-shift noise evict the one rare, real, notable entry before anyone thought to screenshot it — `marqueeDiagCheck`'s own logic should already catch a bare 26px jump like this. Fixed by splitting the overlay into two independent lists: notable events (rare, 40-slot cap, effectively never evicted) and routine layout-shift noise (high-frequency, 10-slot cap).

**Still no confirmed root-cause mechanism for the jump itself** — this PR fixes two real bugs in the diagnostic tooling that likely explain every "caught nothing" report so far, not the underlying jump.

## Test plan
- [x] Directly mutated `#marqueeDiag`'s own height/padding — confirmed zero self-sourced lines reach the rendered overlay; confirmed a real, unrelated forced shift is still caught
- [x] Full-resolution lossless frame-by-frame analysis of a second video (91fps, 4.56s) — confirmed the same -26px anomaly at ~2.2s, cross-validating the first video's finding
- [x] Re-analyzed both videos against far-earlier reference frames — confirmed the shift is permanent (deviation holds at -26 to -28px for 50-80+ frames after the event, no recovery)
- [x] Computed `roloMarqueeOneSetW` (~356px) and time-to-first-wrap (6-12s) — ruled out the wrap-distance theory before shipping anything based on it
- [x] Simulated the video's exact finding, then flooded the overlay with 30 subsequent routine shift events — confirmed the notable entry survives
- [x] `app.js` syntax check clean
- [x] `app.js` and `index.html` both bumped to `?v=18` per the cache-busting rule

author: grokify
body:
Reconsidered the repo/module naming after weighing it purely on communication/adoption grounds: VisionSpec (paired with VisionStudio) is the memorable product/methodology brand worth optimizing for at this stage, following the Swagger-era playbook (brandable name drives early adoption and thought leadership; a neutral standards-committee name is a later-stage move for multi-vendor governance neutrality, which isn't the situation here). The formal JSON-Schema-backed contract this repo defines is "the VisionSpec Specification" — same brand, "Specification" suffix disambiguating the schema/contract layer from the engine, mirroring "Swagger" / "Swagger Specification".

No downstream consumer has ever pulled a tagged release under the specification-workflow-spec module path (the v1.0.0 tag was deliberately held pending), so this corrects course before the first real release rather than reversing a shipped one.

Also fixes tools/prism-sync's own module declaration, which needed no change in the forward direction (it already carried the specification-workflow-spec path, inherited from sws) but is now stale against the reverted parent path.

davy-faugere
body:
Sur une fenêtre étroite, le bouton **Importer** sortait de la carte et la page défilait horizontalement.

## Cause

`.projbar select{flex:1}` **sans `min-width:0`**. Un élément flex a `min-width:auto` par défaut : il refuse de rétrécir sous la largeur de son contenu. Avec un nom de projet long — « Compétences (3 fichiers, 1 dossier) » — le select imposait sa largeur et poussait toute la barre hors du cadre.

C'est le piège flexbox classique, et il ne se voyait pas tant qu'aucun projet n'avait un nom long.

## Correction

`min-width:0` + base `flex:1 1 200px` : le select rétrécit, et si la place manque vraiment la barre passe à la ligne (`flex-wrap`) au lieu de déborder. Même garde-fou posé sur le champ de saisie, exposé au même piège.

## Au passage

« 1 dossiers » → « 1 dossier ».

sw v29.

- purge stored mobile post images when the owner deletes the post

`POST /api/mobile/posts` as `multipart/form-data`

author: aosullivan
body:
Makes the world lighter, with earth colours underfoot and a real sky — from a lit-landscape reference: pale cyan horizon, blue-grey snowy ranges, a gold dithered track over green turf, water reading blue.

The moonlit night is untouched. It becomes one of two keys rather than the only one, and renders **bit-identically** to `main` — same sha over a six-vista sheet, fresh process each side.

## What a key is

`LOOK.night` and this branch's `LOOK.daylight` were two spellings of one question — what light is the world under — so they collapse into `LOOK.key: "off" | "sky" | "meadow" | "moonlit" | "day"`.

A region's weather under a key is nothing but its eight ULAplus anchors, four soil and four sky. `applyNightSky` already swapped the sky ones; `applyKey` swaps the ground ladder too, deriving both exactly as `table()` derives them at load — `groundLadder()` is lifted out so the two build it one way and cannot drift. Daylight is therefore four soil words and four sky words per region and nothing else; the turf bridges, the interleaved rungs and every downstream ramp follow for free.

## What makes it read

- **The ground keeps no ink.** The day mat walks `main`'s own all-soil span, shared with the moonlit night behind `allSoilMat()`. Green marks growth, never ground — the rule that stops a lush biome reading as a lawn, and it holds at either hour. An earlier pass ended the ramp on `G`/`BG` and measured 37% of the moor as one saturated green; ending a rung lower is the whole fix.
- **Distance blends toward haze, not toward the dark.** Air is not empty: the far moor is paler *and* flatter, and the blend quiets its noise for free.
- **Far ranges fill solid in the sky's own zenith rung** under a broken white cap. A distant hill is nearer the colour of the sky above it than anything on the ground — this single change did most of the work.
- **Polarity inverts where it has to.** Near ridge, skyline copse and the skyline-ring silhouettes go dark-on-bright: they stand where the sky is palest, so what reads at 4–10px is the opposite of what read against navy. The pool becomes open water; swept yards, the pilgrim path and the hermit's bed margins take turned earth, because black is not a surface the sun can produce.
- **Stars and moon give way to a sun** on the same bearing, so the glade and slope lighting maths never learns which one is up there.
- The sky spends its rungs evenly enough that the pale band is a third of it rather than a fringe.

`N` toggles the key in game, alongside `C` for CRT and `V` for shades.

## Verification

- `key: "moonlit"` renders bit-identically to `main` across spawn, moor, dead wood, greenwood, keep and grove.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.
- 9.85 ms/frame by day, 10.68 by night, against the 16.7 budget.
- Driven live at `/rpg` through the CRT glass, both keys, no console errors.

author: tsondru
body:
Closes #163. Closes #161.

First two items of the leverage queue.

## #161 ships with Katz, **not** eigenvector centrality

The issue asked for eigenvector centrality. **It is undefined on this object.**
A step-graded evolution DAG has nilpotent adjacency, so spectral radius 0 and no
dominant eigenvector: rustworkx returns `Ok(None)` at the defaults, and forced
to converge it reports a *sink indicator* — the branching junctions the issue
wants to score come out at ≈ 0, the exact opposite of the intended reading.

Katz is the owner-picked remedy, and the substitution is **pinned by a test
rather than asserted in prose** (`katz_floors_the_root_where_eigenvector_centrality_degenerates`):

| leg | assertion |
|---|---|
| eigenvector at defaults | `Ok(None)` — a silent non-result |
| eigenvector forced to 100k iters | root `< 1e-2`, leaves `> 0.5` — a sink indicator |
| `multiway_katz` | root `= 1/√(1 + 3·1.1²) ≈ 0.4647 = β/‖x‖`, every child strictly above |

So a future refactor cannot quietly regress to the degenerate behaviour. The
"why Katz" rationale lives in the rustdoc *and* the CHANGELOG, so neither a
doc reader nor a changelog reader can think #161 shipped as filed.

**Betweenness was unaffected by the eigenvector problem** and ships as specified.

### API added (all behind the existing `rustworkx` feature, no new deps)

```rust
impl<S, T> MultiwayEvolutionGraph<S, T> {
    pub fn to_petgraph(&self) -> (DiGraph<MultiwayNodeId, ()>, Vec<MultiwayNodeId>);
}
pub fn multiway_betweenness<S, T>(g: &MultiwayEvolutionGraph<S, T>, normalized: bool)
    -> HashMap<MultiwayNodeId, f64>;
pub fn multiway_katz<S, T>(g: &MultiwayEvolutionGraph<S, T>, alpha: Option<f64>,
    max_iter: Option<usize>, tol: Option<f64>) -> Option<HashMap<MultiwayNodeId, f64>>;
```

`Cargo.lock` is unchanged — `rustworkx-core` was already a dep of this crate.

## #163 widens topologies at the **branchial** level

The issue said to widen `arb_branched_graph`. That isn't possible:
`MultiwayEvolutionGraph` is constructible only through `add_root`/`add_fork`, so
an arbitrary topology cannot be injected at the evolution level. The insertion
point is `BranchialGraph`, whose `nodes`/`edges` are public — which still serves
the three existing proptests, because they assert *branchial* properties.

Seven pinned-seed fixtures (sparse/dense Erdős–Rényi, Barabási–Albert, 3-regular,
path, Petersen, 4×6 grid) via `rustworkx-core` as a **dev-dependency**, plus a
`branchial_bench`. Per #33, generators supply **topology only**; numeric fixtures
stay on the byte-identity-pinned `catgraph-testutil` LCG.

⚠ **The existing λ₂ proptest would have gone vacuous on these fixtures** — it
guards on `is_fully_connected()`, true only for Kₙ, so reusing it would have
skipped the assertion on every new topology *and still shown green*. The new
sibling guards on `connected_components() == 1`, and a non-vacuity test pins
that the fixture set really does escape the complete-graph regime.

## Housekeeping

Four stale `(#10)` dep-comment cites repointed at `catgraph-physics/README.md`
(#10 is closed; it was the feature-gate work). The issue named one location and
a later audit named another — both had drifted, since #220 removed the ultragraph
block.

## Review findings — six, all applied

The most consequential was a real portability bug, not a nit:

1. **`multiway_betweenness` was the crate's first rayon call site and wasn't
   gated by `parallel`.** `--no-default-features --features rustworkx` would
   spawn rayon work on a build whose whole point is single-threading, and on a
   no-threads wasm target rayon's pool init fails **at runtime** — only for
   graphs ≥ 50 nodes. Threshold is now `usize::MAX` when `parallel` is off.
2. **The determinism claim overpromised.** Canonical ordering fixes the *index
   assignment*, but rustworkx accumulates Brandes partials from rayon workers,
   so f64 summation order varies and scores are not bit-pinnable on the parallel
   path. Documented, with the build that is. (Plus an off-by-one: `>= 50`, not
   "above 50".)
3. **`to_petgraph` silently drops dangling edges**, contradicting its own doc —
   so on such a graph the centralities run over a different topology than
   `edge_count()` reports. Documented.
4. **The DAG grading is a convention, not an invariant** — `add_merge_edge`
   permits a back-edge, which breaks nilpotency and can diverge Katz to a
   misleading `None`. Documented as "suspect α before `max_iter`".
5. **`multiway_katz` returned `None` for an empty graph** (`0.0 < 0.0` never
   converges), disagreeing with `multiway_betweenness`. Short-circuited + pinned.
6. **Both new proptests tolerated a missing key** on exactly the fixtures where
   isolated nodes first appear — `prop_assert_ne!` passes against `None`, and
   `unwrap_or(0)` satisfies `core <= degree` for free. Presence now asserted first.

## Gates

`fmt` · `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` · `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" doc` ·
`metadata --locked` · `test --workspace` → **1933 passed, 0 failed**.

Plus, because finding 1 is about exactly that build:
`-p catgraph-physics --no-default-features --features rustworkx` → **171 passed**,
`--no-default-features` → green, and `cargo check -p catgraph-physics --target wasm32-wasip1` → green.

## Problem
find_best_price latency regression — SG 16s, US 25s. Root cause: high-cardinality FTS terms (nike, iphone, samsung) match millions of rows and timeout even with enable_seqscan=off at 20s statement_timeout.

- SG iphone: was 10s timeout → now ~4.5s
- SG samsung: was 10s timeout → now ~4.5s

author: tamnd
body:
Continues #17. Covers the goreleaser, govulncheck and release-notes boxes. Does **not** tag: that is a separate, deliberate step.

### The release notes were two releases stale

The `release.header` still said goodread "routes around the Goodreads WAF through open endpoints so search and shelves keep working". That is now flatly untrue. Both surfaces are disallowed by `robots.txt` and neither is read without `--no-robots`.

Replaced with handwritten v0.3.0 notes: the book/work distinction, robots obeyed structurally, the graph, the resumable crawler, the MCP server, and a breaking-changes section naming every flag and command that moved. GoReleaser puts the generated changelog between the header and the footer, so the release page reads as a person explaining what changed with the commit list underneath rather than as a commit list on its own.

The header is rewritten per release rather than kept generic. That sounds like a chore until you notice this one went two releases without anybody reading it.

### govulncheck at the tag, not only the branch

`ci.yml` runs it on pushes to main and on PRs, which covers the branch. It does not cover the tag. A tag can be cut from a commit that was green a week ago, and the vulnerability database has moved since.

It now runs in the release job too, against the exact tree that is about to be published, before goreleaser starts.

### Which immediately found six

That is the point of adding it, so this PR fixes them rather than deferring.

Five were the standard library in `go1.26.5`, all fixed in `go1.26.6`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| GO-2026-6218 | `net/url` |
| GO-2026-6090 | `crypto/tls` |
| GO-2026-6088 | `encoding/xml` |
| GO-2026-5972 | `encoding/asn1` |
| GO-2026-5026 | `net/http`, reached from `Client.doGet` |

The release job's `setup-go` had no `check-latest`, so the runner's cached toolchain can be a patch or two behind and every standard library CVE fixed in between ships in the binary. It is set now, on both jobs in this workflow, which is what `ci.yml` already did.

The sixth, GO-2026-5970 in `golang.org/x/text` v0.38.0, is reached through `fang` and is bumped to v0.39.0.

Local `govulncheck ./...` is now clean apart from the five that need go1.26.6, which CI will have.

### Also

Dropped "fast, friendly" from the nfpm, OCI label, cask and scoop descriptions. It was doing no work.

The container example in the header is `book 2767052` rather than `search "dune"`, since `search` is a worse first impression now than it was.

### Not in this PR

Tagging `v0.3.0`, and pulling and running the published image. Both are outward-facing and want a deliberate go-ahead, so they stay on #17.

`gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test ./...` and `goreleaser check` are clean.
